products.name: gads_report
products.description: NERC Generating Availability Data System (GADS) monthly performance report records submitted for each generating unit. Captures reporting period, equivalent availability factor (EAF), equivalent forced outage rate (EFOR), equivalent planned outage factor (EPOF), net generation (MWh), capacity factor (%), total outage hours by cause code, and NERC submission status. SSOT for NERC GADS compliance and generation fleet benchmarking.
products.reference: NERC GADS (Generating Availability Data System) Reporting

attributes.name: gads_report_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Generating Availability Data System (GADS) Report ID
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the NERC GADS monthly performance report record. Primary key for the GADS report entity.

attributes.name: control_area_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to grid.control_area. Business justification: NERC GADS reporting includes balancing authority context for regional reliability benchmarking and forced outage rate analysis.

attributes.name: gads_generating_unit_id
attributes.description: Foreign key reference to the generating unit for which this GADS report is submitted. Links to the generation asset registry.

attributes.name: generating_unit_id
attributes.description: FK to generation.generating_unit.generating_unit_id — NERC GADS reports are submitted per generating unit. Without this FK, GADS compliance records cannot be linked to the unit they report on, breaking NERC compliance.

attributes.name: obligation_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.obligation. Business justification: GADS reporting is mandatory NERC obligation for bulk electric system reliability tracking. Direct link required for compliance tracking, audit evidence, regulatory submissions, and demonstrating adher

attributes.name: primary_generating_unit_id
attributes.description: FK to generation.generating_unit.generating_unit_id — NERC GADS reports are submitted per generating unit. Without this FK, GADS performance metrics cannot be associated with the reported unit. Critical for NERC compliance.

attributes.name: available_hours
attributes.description: The total number of hours during the reporting period that the unit was capable of service, whether or not it was actually in service. Includes service hours plus reserve shutdown hours.

attributes.name: capacity_factor_pct
attributes.description: The ratio of actual net generation to the maximum possible generation if the unit operated at full nameplate capacity for the entire reporting period. Calculated as (Net Generation MWh / (Nameplate Capacity MW * Period Hours)) * 100.

attributes.name: cause_code_group
attributes.description: The high-level NERC GADS cause code category for the most significant outage event during the reporting period (e.g., boiler, turbine, generator, electrical, external). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: boiler|turbine|generator|electrical|balance_of_plant|external|fuel_supply|environmental|other — promote to reference product]

attributes.name: comments
attributes.description: Free-text field for additional context, explanations of unusual performance, or notes regarding data quality issues. Supports regulatory compliance documentation.

attributes.name: commercial_operation_date
attributes.description: The date the generating unit entered commercial service. Used to determine unit age and applicable GADS reporting requirements.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this GADS report record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking.

attributes.name: data_source_system
attributes.description: The name of the operational system from which the GADS performance data was extracted (e.g., OSIsoft PI, ABB Ability Symphony Plus, plant DCS). Used for data lineage and quality assurance.

attributes.name: equivalent_availability_factor_pct
attributes.description: The percentage of time the unit was available to generate at full capacity, accounting for both full and partial outages. Key NERC GADS performance metric calculated as (Available Hours - Equivalent Forced Outage Hours - Equivalent Planned Outage Hours) / Period Hours * 100.

attributes.name: equivalent_forced_outage_rate_pct
attributes.description: The percentage of time the unit was unavailable due to forced outages, accounting for both full and partial forced deratings. Key NERC GADS reliability metric calculated as Equivalent Forced Outage Hours / (Service Hours + Equivalent Forced Outage Hours) * 100.

attributes.name: equivalent_planned_outage_factor_pct
attributes.description: The percentage of time the unit was unavailable due to planned outages, accounting for both full and partial planned deratings. NERC GADS metric calculated as Equivalent Planned Outage Hours / Period Hours * 100.

attributes.name: forced_outage_hours
attributes.description: The total number of hours the unit was unavailable due to unplanned events requiring immediate removal from service, including equipment failures and emergency conditions.

attributes.name: forced_outage_rate_pct
attributes.description: The percentage of time the unit was on full forced outage. Calculated as Forced Outage Hours / (Service Hours + Forced Outage Hours) * 100. Differs from EFOR by excluding partial deratings.

attributes.name: gross_generation_mwh
attributes.description: The total gross electrical energy in megawatt-hours (MWh) produced by the unit during the reporting period, before deducting station service and auxiliary loads.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this GADS report record was most recently updated. Used for change tracking and audit trail purposes.

attributes.name: maintenance_outage_hours
attributes.description: The total number of hours the unit was unavailable due to maintenance work that could be deferred beyond the end of the next weekend but requires removal from service within six weeks.

attributes.name: nameplate_capacity_mw
attributes.description: The maximum rated output of the generating unit in megawatts (MW) as specified by the manufacturer. Used as the denominator for capacity factor calculations.

attributes.name: nerc_unit_code
attributes.business_glossary_term: North American Electric Reliability Corporation (NERC) Unit Code
attributes.description: The unique NERC-assigned identifier for the generating unit. Used for regulatory reporting and cross-utility benchmarking.

attributes.name: nerc_validation_status
attributes.description: The outcome of NERC automated data validation checks applied to this report. Failed validations require correction and resubmission.

attributes.name: net_dependable_capacity_mw
attributes.description: The net capacity in megawatts (MW) that the unit can be relied upon to deliver during peak demand periods, adjusted for seasonal and operational constraints.

attributes.name: net_generation_mwh
attributes.description: The total net electrical energy in megawatt-hours (MWh) delivered by the unit to the grid during the reporting period, after deducting station service and auxiliary loads.

attributes.name: net_maximum_capacity_mw
attributes.description: The maximum net electrical output in megawatts (MW) that the unit can sustain over a specified period under normal operating conditions, accounting for station service loads.

attributes.name: number_of_forced_outages
attributes.description: The total count of discrete forced outage events during the reporting period. Used to calculate forced outage frequency metrics.

attributes.name: number_of_starts
attributes.description: The total count of unit synchronization events during the reporting period, including both successful and failed start attempts.

attributes.name: period_hours
attributes.description: The total number of hours in the reporting period. Typically 720 hours for a 30-day month or 744 hours for a 31-day month. Used as the denominator for availability calculations.

attributes.name: planned_outage_hours
attributes.description: The total number of hours the unit was unavailable due to scheduled maintenance, inspections, or overhauls that were planned in advance and approved by system operations.

attributes.name: primary_fuel_type
attributes.description: The predominant fuel source used by the generating unit during the reporting period. Used for fuel-specific performance benchmarking. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: coal|natural_gas|nuclear|hydro|wind|solar|oil|biomass|geothermal|other — 10 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: report_approval_date
attributes.description: The date on which this GADS report was reviewed and approved by authorized personnel before submission to NERC.

attributes.name: report_approver_name
attributes.description: The name of the authorized individual who approved this GADS report for submission to NERC. Used for internal compliance audit trail.

attributes.name: report_preparer_email
attributes.description: The email address of the individual who prepared this GADS report. Used for follow-up questions and validation issue resolution.

attributes.name: report_preparer_name
attributes.description: The name of the individual who prepared this GADS report. Used for internal audit trail and quality assurance purposes.

attributes.name: report_submission_date
attributes.description: The date on which this GADS report was submitted to NERC. Used to track compliance with NERC submission deadlines.

attributes.name: reporting_entity_name
attributes.description: The legal name of the utility or generation owner responsible for submitting this GADS report to NERC. May differ from the operating entity.

attributes.name: reporting_entity_nerc_code
attributes.description: The unique NERC-assigned identifier for the reporting entity. Used to aggregate performance data across multiple generating units owned by the same entity.

attributes.name: reporting_period_end_date
attributes.description: The last day of the monthly reporting period covered by this GADS report. Typically the last day of the calendar month.

attributes.name: reporting_period_start_date
attributes.description: The first day of the monthly reporting period covered by this GADS report. Typically the first day of the calendar month.

attributes.name: retirement_date
attributes.description: The date the generating unit was permanently retired from service. Null for active units. Determines the end of GADS reporting obligations.

attributes.name: service_hours
attributes.description: The total number of hours during the reporting period that the unit was in active service and synchronized to the grid, regardless of output level.

attributes.name: starting_reliability_pct
attributes.description: The percentage of attempted unit starts that were successful. Calculated as Successful Starts / Total Attempted Starts * 100. Applicable primarily to peaking and cycling units.

attributes.name: submission_status
attributes.description: The current status of this GADS report in the NERC submission and validation workflow. Tracks compliance with regulatory reporting requirements.

attributes.name: unit_type
attributes.description: The primary technology classification of the generating unit as defined by NERC GADS taxonomy. Determines applicable performance metrics and cause codes. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: fossil_steam|combined_cycle|combustion_turbine|nuclear|hydro_conventional|hydro_pumped_storage|wind|solar_pv|solar_thermal|biomass|geothermal — 11 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: validation_error_message
attributes.description: Detailed error or warning messages returned by NERC validation logic. Provides guidance for correcting data quality issues before resubmission.

products.name: plant_vendor_agreement
products.description: This association product represents the contractual relationship between a power generation facility and its suppliers/service vendors. It captures plant-specific procurement contracts, service level agreements, and vendor performance tracking. Each record links one power plant to one vendor with commercial terms, service commitments, and spend tracking that exist only in the context of this specific plant-vendor relationship.. Existence Justification: Power plants maintain contractual relationships with multiple vendors for different services (fuel supply, parts, maintenance, emergency response), and vendors serve multiple generation facilities across the utility's portfolio. Each plant-vendor relationship has its own contract terms, service level agreements, response time commitments, and spend tracking that vary by plant criticality, location, and vendor capability. This is an operational relationship actively managed by plant operators and procurement teams.

products.name: unit_crew_assignment
products.description: This association product represents the operational assignment of field crews to generating units for operations, maintenance, and outage work. It captures the assignment lifecycle, crew role, shift pattern, and certification requirements for NERC personnel qualification tracking. Each record links one generating unit to one crew with attributes that exist only in the context of this assignment relationship, supporting shift scheduling, outage planning, and regulatory compliance reporting.. Existence Justification: In energy utilities generation operations, generating units require multiple specialized crews rotating across shifts for 24/7 operations, planned maintenance, and outage execution. A single generating unit has multiple crews assigned simultaneously (e.g., day shift operators, night shift operators, maintenance crew, outage crew), and each crew is qualified to work on multiple generating units within the fleet. The business actively manages these assignments with specific roles, shift patterns, and NERC qualification tracking.

products.name: unit_certification_requirement
products.description: This association product represents the regulatory and operational certification requirements between generating units and workforce certifications. It captures which certifications are mandatory for personnel operating, maintaining, or accessing specific generating units based on unit type, voltage class, fuel type, and NERC CIP classification. Each record links one generating unit to one certification with attributes that define the requirement context, applicability rules, and compliance tracking metadata.. attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the generating unit for which this certification is required

attributes.name: created_date
attributes.description: Timestamp when this unit-certification requirement record was created in the system.

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: Date when this certification requirement became or will become effective for this generating unit. Used to track regulatory changes and phase-in periods for new requirements.

attributes.name: expiration_date
attributes.description: Date when this certification requirement expires or is superseded for this generating unit. Null if the requirement is ongoing. Used when unit modifications or regulatory changes eliminate a requirement.

attributes.name: last_updated_by
attributes.description: User ID or system identifier that last updated this requirement record.

attributes.name: last_updated_date
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent update to this requirement record.

attributes.name: mandatory_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this certification is absolutely mandatory (regulatory requirement) or recommended (best practice) for personnel working with this generating unit in the specified role.

attributes.name: nerc_cip_requirement_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this certification requirement is driven by NERC CIP (Critical Infrastructure Protection) standards for cyber security and physical access to bulk electric system assets. True when the generating unit is classified as a BES Cyber Asset and personnel require CIP-specific clearances.

attributes.name: regulatory_citation
attributes.description: Specific regulation, NERC standard, OSHA rule, or state PUC order that mandates this certification for this unit type or voltage class. Provides traceability for compliance audits.

attributes.name: required_for_role
attributes.description: The operational role or job function for which this certification is required when working with this specific generating unit. Determines which personnel must hold this certification based on their interaction with the unit.

attributes.name: requirement_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of this certification requirement. ACTIVE = currently enforced, PENDING = future requirement, SUPERSEDED = replaced by newer requirement, WAIVED = exception granted, GRANDFATHERED = existing personnel exempt.

attributes.name: unit_type_applicability
attributes.description: The generating unit technology types for which this certification is required. Comma-separated list (e.g., 'CCGT,COAL,NUCLEAR' or 'ALL'). Different unit types require different operator qualifications and safety certifications.

attributes.name: voltage_class_applicability
attributes.description: The voltage class range for which this certification requirement applies. Certain certifications (e.g., high voltage safety, arc flash) are only required when the generating unit operates at or above specific voltage thresholds.
attributes.references: Detection phase identified attribute as voltage_class

attributes.name: created_by
attributes.description: User ID or system identifier that created this requirement record.

products.name: facility_audit_scope
products.description: This association product represents the audit scope relationship between power_plant and audit. It captures the specific inclusion of a generation facility within a compliance audit's scope, including facility-specific findings, audit activities, and closure status. Each record links one power_plant to one audit with attributes that exist only in the context of this facility being audited.. Existence Justification: In energy utilities compliance operations, audits routinely cover multiple generation facilities (a NERC CIP audit may examine 10+ plants, an EPA inspection may cover all coal plants in a region), and each facility undergoes multiple audits over time (NERC reliability, FERC market behavior, state PUC, EPA environmental). The business actively manages facility-specific audit scope, tracks findings per facility, assigns facility coordinators, and closes findings independently per facility even within the same audit.
products.reference: Internal - M:N Association

attributes.name: facility_audit_scope_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for this facility-audit scope record. Primary key.

attributes.name: audit_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the compliance audit under which this facility is being examined

attributes.name: power_plant_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Facility Audit Scope - Power Plant Id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the generation facility included in the audit scope

attributes.name: audit_date
attributes.description: Date when audit activities were conducted at this specific facility (site visit, inspection, or evidence review). May differ from overall audit start/end dates when audit covers multiple facilities over time.

attributes.name: closure_status
attributes.description: Current closure status for this facility's portion of the audit. Tracks whether findings for this specific facility have been addressed and closed by the auditing body. Status can vary by facility within a multi-facility audit.

attributes.name: critical_findings_count
attributes.description: Number of critical or severe findings identified specifically for this facility during this audit.

attributes.name: facility_closure_date
attributes.description: Date when all findings and corrective actions for this specific facility were closed by the auditing body. May differ from overall audit closure date when facilities close at different times.

attributes.name: facility_coordinator_email
attributes.description: Email address of the facility audit coordinator for this facility-audit scope.

attributes.name: facility_coordinator_name
attributes.description: Name of the utility employee at this facility who coordinated audit activities, provided access, and gathered evidence for this facility's portion of the audit.

attributes.name: facility_penalty_amount
attributes.description: Monetary penalty assessed specifically for violations identified at this facility during this audit. Penalties are often assessed per facility based on facility-specific violations.

attributes.name: findings_count
attributes.description: Number of audit findings, violations, or observations identified specifically for this facility during this audit. Derived from child finding records but denormalized for reporting.

attributes.name: included_in_scope_flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this facility was ultimately included in the final audit scope. Facilities may be initially listed but excluded during scoping phase.

attributes.name: lead_auditor_name
attributes.description: Name of the auditor from the auditing body who led the audit activities at this specific facility. May differ from the overall audit lead auditor when audit teams are divided across multiple facilities.

attributes.name: scope_added_date
attributes.description: Date when this facility was added to the audit scope. Tracks when the facility-audit relationship was established.

attributes.name: scope_description
attributes.description: Detailed description of what aspects of this specific facility are included in the audit scope (e.g., 'NERC CIP-002 through CIP-009 compliance for critical cyber assets', 'EPA Title V air emissions permit compliance', 'Generation unit 1 and 2 only'). Scope varies by facility even within the same audit.

attributes.name: scope_removed_date
attributes.description: Date when this facility was removed from the audit scope, if applicable. Null if facility remains in scope.

products.name: plant_crew_assignment
products.description: This association product represents the Assignment between power_plant and crew. It captures the operational assignment of field crews to generation facilities for operations, maintenance, environmental compliance, security, and emergency response work. Each record links one power_plant to one crew with attributes that define the assignment period, crew function, assignment priority, and emergency response role. Critical for resource planning, mutual aid coordination, regulatory staffing compliance (NERC CIP personnel requirements), and outage work scheduling.. Existence Justification: In energy utilities generation operations, power plants require multiple specialized crews assigned simultaneously for different functions (operations, maintenance, environmental compliance, security, outage work). Crews are routinely assigned to multiple plants within a generation fleet, particularly in regions where plants are geographically clustered. The business actively manages these assignments with specific start/end dates, primary vs. backup designations, emergency response roles, and NERC CIP compliance tracking.
products.reference: Internal - M:N Association

attributes.name: plant_crew_assignment_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the plant-crew assignment record. Primary key.

attributes.name: assigned_by_employee_id
attributes.description: Reference to the plant manager or operations supervisor who authorized this crew assignment. Used for audit trail and assignment approval workflow.

attributes.name: crew_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the field crew assigned to the generation facility

attributes.name: power_plant_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Plant Crew Assignment - Power Plant Id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the generation facility where the crew is assigned

attributes.name: assignment_end_date
attributes.description: Date when the crew assignment to the generation facility ended or is planned to end. Null for ongoing assignments. Critical for tracking temporary assignments during outages or mutual aid deployments.

attributes.name: assignment_notes
attributes.description: Free-text notes about the assignment including special instructions, temporary restrictions, or coordination requirements with other crews.

attributes.name: assignment_start_date
attributes.description: Date when the crew assignment to the generation facility became effective. Used for resource planning and historical tracking of crew deployments.

attributes.name: assignment_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the crew assignment. Active assignments are used for dispatch and cost allocation. Suspended assignments indicate temporary unavailability (e.g., crew deployed elsewhere).

attributes.name: cost_allocation_percentage
attributes.description: Percentage of crew labor costs allocated to this plant assignment. Used when a crew is split across multiple facilities. Sum of percentages across all assignments for a crew should equal 100%.

attributes.name: crew_type
attributes.description: Classification of the crew function for this specific assignment. A crew may serve different functions at different plants. Determines work authorization, safety protocols, and regulatory compliance requirements.

attributes.name: emergency_response_role
attributes.description: Defines the crew's role in emergency response scenarios at this facility. Critical for NERC CIP compliance, emergency action plan (EAP) execution, and mutual aid coordination during grid emergencies.

attributes.name: nerc_cip_compliance_verified_date
attributes.description: Date when crew members' NERC CIP personnel risk assessments were verified for this specific facility. Required for crews working in CIP-designated critical cyber assets or physical security perimeters.

attributes.name: primary_assignment_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this is the crew's primary plant assignment (true) or a secondary/backup assignment (false). Primary assignments determine home base for crew scheduling and cost allocation.

attributes.name: work_authorization_level
attributes.description: Level of access and work authorization the crew has at this specific facility. Varies by NERC CIP security zone, plant type, and crew certification level. Determines which work orders can be assigned.

domains.name: customer
domains.description: SSOT for all customer identity, account, and relationship data across residential, commercial, and industrial segments. Manages customer profiles, service agreements, premises, contact information, premise-to-account linkages, credit classifications, and multi-channel engagement history within CIS platforms (SAP IS-U, Oracle CC&B). Supports NEM participants, BTM customers, and DER-enrolled accounts. Central reference for all downstream billing, metering, and demand response domains.

Captures the authoritative account record for residential, commercial, and industrial customers including account number, account type (residential/commercial/industrial), account status, account status history (with change timestamps, reason codes, and initiating events), credit class, move-in/move-out dates, service territory, rate category, NEM participation flag, BTM flag, DER enrollment status, CIS source system identifier, regulatory jurisdiction, parent account reference for consolidated billing and corporate hierarchy, and account group classification (consolidated billing, corporate parent, franchise, municipal aggregation, CCA). SSOT for all downstream billing, metering, and demand response domains. Supports lifecycle tracking of activation, suspension, disconnection, reconnection, write-off, and reactivation events.

attributes.description: Grouping classification that determines billing consolidation and hierarchy rules. Consolidated billing groups multiple premises under one bill; corporate parent denotes the apex of a corporate hierarchy; municipal aggregation and Community Choice Aggregation (CCA) denote aggregated load programs; franchise denotes accounts under a specific franchise territory agreement.

attributes.name: ami_enrolled

attributes.name: autopay_enrolled
attributes.description: Indicates whether this account is enrolled in automatic payment (AutoPay), where the bill amount is automatically debited from the customer's bank account or charged to a payment card on the due date. Reduces collections risk and improves cash flow.
attributes.references: SAP IS-U FI-CA Payment Method; Oracle CC&B Auto Pay; NAESB WEQ; PCI DSS

attributes.name: billing_cycle_code
attributes.description: Code identifying the billing cycle (meter reading and bill generation schedule) assigned to this account. Determines the monthly read date and bill due date. Managed in SAP IS-U Billing Order or Oracle CC&B Bill Cycle. Examples: BC01 (1st of month), BC15 (15th of month).
attributes.references: SAP IS-U Billing Order (ABRSPERR); Oracle CC&B Bill Cycle; State PUC Billing Rules

attributes.name: btm_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this account has Behind-the-Meter (BTM) generation or storage assets installed at the premise. BTM assets include solar PV, battery storage, and combined heat and power (CHP) systems that are not directly visible to the grid operator. Drives load disaggregation and DER management workflows.
attributes.references: FERC Order 2222; State PUC DER Rules; DERMS Integration; IEEE 1547

attributes.name: budget_billing_enrolled
attributes.description: Indicates whether this account is enrolled in a budget billing (levelized payment plan) program, where monthly bills are averaged over a 12-month period to smooth seasonal fluctuations. Affects bill calculation and settlement processes in SAP IS-U or Oracle CC&B.
attributes.references: SAP IS-U Budget Billing (ABSCHLAG); Oracle CC&B Budget Billing; State PUC Tariff

attributes.name: cis_account_key

attributes.references: SAP IS-U Contract Account (VKONT); Oracle CC&B Account ID; SOX Data Lineage; Enterprise MDM Policy

attributes.name: cis_source_system
attributes.description: Identifies the operational Customer Information System (CIS) from which this account record originates. Critical for data lineage, deduplication, and cross-system reconciliation in multi-CIS utility environments. Values: SAP_IS_U (SAP Industry Solution for Utilities), ORACLE_CCB (Oracle Customer Care and Billing), LEGACY_CIS (decommissioned legacy system).
attributes.references: SAP IS-U; Oracle CC&B; Enterprise Data Governance Policy; SOX Data Lineage

attributes.name: contract_end_date
attributes.description: Date on which the service agreement or contract associated with this account is scheduled to expire or terminate. Null for open-ended tariff service. For fixed-term commercial or industrial contracts and PPAs, this date triggers renewal or renegotiation workflows.
attributes.references: SAP IS-U Contract (VERTRAG); Oracle CC&B Service Agreement; FERC PPA; State PUC Tariff

attributes.name: contract_start_date
attributes.description: Date on which the service agreement or contract associated with this account became effective. For residential accounts this typically aligns with move_in_date; for commercial and industrial accounts this may reflect a separately negotiated contract effective date, Power Purchase Agreement (PPA), or special contract term.
attributes.references: SAP IS-U Contract (VERTRAG); Oracle CC&B Service Agreement; FERC PPA; State PUC Tariff

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this account record was first created in the source CIS system. Represents the audit creation time for data lineage and SOX compliance. Distinct from activation_timestamp which represents the business event of service energization.
attributes.references: SAP IS-U Contract Account Creation Timestamp; Oracle CC&B Account Created Date; SOX Internal Controls; GDPR Article 30

attributes.name: credit_class
attributes.description: Credit risk classification assigned to the account based on payment history, credit bureau data, and internal scoring. Governs deposit requirements, payment plan eligibility, and collections treatment. Managed within SAP IS-U FICA or Oracle CC&B Collections module.
attributes.references: SAP IS-U FI-CA Credit Management (FKKCR); Oracle CC&B Credit Review; State PUC Credit and Deposit Rules; SOX Internal Controls

attributes.name: deposit_amount

attributes.references: SAP IS-U FI-CA Security Deposit (FKKDEP); Oracle CC&B Deposit; State PUC Deposit Rules; SOX

attributes.name: ev_charging_enrolled

attributes.name: last_bill_date

attributes.name: last_payment_date

attributes.name: last_status_change_timestamp

attributes.name: last_updated_timestamp

attributes.name: life_support_equipment

attributes.name: move_in_date

attributes.name: move_out_date

attributes.name: open_balance

attributes.name: paperless_billing

attributes.name: preferred_contact_channel
attributes.description: Customer's preferred channel for receiving utility communications including bills, outage notifications, and program offers. Drives multi-channel engagement routing in CRM and outage notification systems (OMS). Aligns with customer consent preferences.

attributes.name: preferred_language

attributes.name: rate_category

attributes.name: regulatory_jurisdiction
attributes.description: Two-letter US state code (ISO 3166-2 subdivision) identifying the state Public Utility Commission (PUC) with regulatory authority over this account. attributes.name: renewable_energy_plan

Examples include 100% renewable, green power option, or Renewable Energy Certificate (REC) purchase programs. Supports Renewable Portfolio Standard (RPS) compliance tracking. attributes.name: service_territory_code
