attributes.description: Type of ATC calculation based on the time horizon: day-ahead, hour-ahead, real-time, monthly, or seasonal study.

attributes.name: cbm_mw
attributes.description: Capacity Benefit Margin: the amount of transmission transfer capability reserved for Load-Serving Entities to access generation from interconnected systems to meet generation reliability requirements. Measured in megawatts.

attributes.name: comments
attributes.description: Free-text field for additional notes, explanations, or context related to this ATC calculation, such as special operating conditions or unusual circumstances.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this ATC calculation record was first created in the system. Audit trail for record creation.

attributes.name: ems_snapshot_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the EMS real-time or historical snapshot used as input data for the ATC calculation. Represents the system state at a specific point in time.

attributes.name: etc_mw
attributes.description: Existing Transmission Commitments: the sum of all firm transmission service reservations, grandfathered rights, and other committed uses of the transmission system. Measured in megawatts.

attributes.name: ferc_reporting_flag
attributes.business_glossary_term: Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) Reporting Flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this ATC calculation is subject to FERC reporting requirements under OATT compliance (True) or not (False).

attributes.name: firm_atc_mw
attributes.business_glossary_term: Firm Available Transfer Capability (ATC) in Megawatts (MW)
attributes.description: ATC available for firm transmission service reservations, which have the highest priority and are not subject to curtailment except under emergency conditions. Measured in megawatts.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this ATC calculation record was last updated or modified. Audit trail for record changes.

attributes.name: limit_type
attributes.description: Type of transmission system limit that constrains the ATC: thermal (line/transformer rating), voltage (bus voltage limit), stability (transient or dynamic stability), or other.

attributes.name: limiting_contingency
attributes.description: Description or identifier of the transmission contingency (e.g., line outage, transformer outage) that limits the transfer capability for this path in this study.

attributes.name: limiting_facility
attributes.description: Name or identifier of the transmission facility (line, transformer, flowgate) that reaches its thermal, voltage, or stability limit first, constraining the ATC value.

attributes.name: nerc_reliability_region
attributes.business_glossary_term: North American Electric Reliability Corporation (NERC) Reliability Region
attributes.description: NERC regional entity responsible for reliability coordination and compliance for this transmission path: WECC, ERCOT, MRO, NPCC, RF, SERC, SPP, or TRE. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: WECC|ERCOT|MRO|NPCC|RF|SERC|SPP|TRE — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: non_firm_atc_mw
attributes.business_glossary_term: Non-Firm Available Transfer Capability (ATC) in Megawatts (MW)
attributes.description: ATC available for non-firm transmission service reservations, which are lower priority and subject to curtailment when firm service is needed. Measured in megawatts.

attributes.name: oasis_posting_timestamp
attributes.business_glossary_term: Open Access Same-Time Information System (OASIS) Posting Timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the ATC value was posted to the OASIS system for public access by transmission customers.

attributes.name: oatt_service_type
attributes.business_glossary_term: Open Access Transmission Tariff (OATT) Service Type
attributes.description: Type of transmission service under OATT for which this ATC is calculated: network integration service, point-to-point firm service, or point-to-point non-firm service.

attributes.name: operator_adjustment_mw
attributes.description: Manual adjustment applied by the transmission operator to the calculated ATC value based on operational judgment, real-time conditions, or reliability concerns. Measured in megawatts.

attributes.name: operator_adjustment_reason
attributes.description: Explanation or justification for any manual operator adjustment applied to the ATC value, documenting the operational or reliability rationale.

attributes.name: posting_status
attributes.business_glossary_term: Open Access Same-Time Information System (OASIS) Posting Status
attributes.description: Status of the ATC value posting to OASIS: pending (not yet posted), posted (published to OASIS), revised (updated after initial posting), or withdrawn (removed from OASIS).

attributes.name: rto_iso_region
attributes.business_glossary_term: Regional Transmission Organization (RTO) or Independent System Operator (ISO) Region
attributes.description: Name or code of the RTO or ISO region responsible for this transmission path and ATC calculation (e.g., PJM, MISO, CAISO, SPP, ERCOT, NYISO, ISO-NE).

attributes.name: scada_data_quality
attributes.business_glossary_term: Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) Data Quality
attributes.description: Quality indicator for the SCADA telemetry data used in the ATC calculation: good (reliable), suspect (questionable), stale (outdated), or unavailable (missing).

attributes.name: sink_ba_code
attributes.description: Code or identifier of the sink Balancing Authority to which power is being transferred on this transmission path.

attributes.name: source_ba_code
attributes.description: Code or identifier of the source Balancing Authority from which power is being transferred on this transmission path.

attributes.name: study_case_code
attributes.description: Identifier of the power flow or contingency analysis study case used as the basis for the ATC calculation. Links to the EMS or planning system study case.

attributes.name: study_horizon_end
attributes.description: Ending timestamp of the time horizon for which ATC is calculated. Defines the validity period of the ATC value.

attributes.name: study_horizon_start
attributes.description: Beginning timestamp of the time horizon for which ATC is calculated (e.g., start of the hour or day-ahead period).

attributes.name: trm_mw
attributes.description: Transmission Reliability Margin: the amount of transmission transfer capability reserved to ensure that the interconnected transmission network is secure under a reasonable range of uncertainties in system conditions. Measured in megawatts.

attributes.name: ttc_mw
attributes.description: Total Transfer Capability: the maximum amount of electric power that can be transferred over the transmission path in a reliable manner while meeting all reliability criteria. Measured in megawatts.

attributes.name: uncertainty_margin_mw
attributes.description: Additional margin reserved to account for uncertainties in load forecast, generation dispatch, or system conditions not captured in TRM. Measured in megawatts.

attributes.name: validation_status
attributes.description: Status of the ATC calculation validation process: validated (passed all checks), pending_review (awaiting engineer review), failed (did not pass validation rules), or override (validation failure overridden by operator).

attributes.name: validation_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the ATC calculation was validated and approved for posting to OASIS.

products.name: transmission_service_request
products.description: Transactional record of a request for transmission service under OATT — point-to-point (PTP) or network integration transmission service (NITS). Captures request identifier, service type, requestor entity, source and sink points, requested capacity (MW), service start and end dates, priority, queue position, study requirements, approval status, and FERC docket reference. SSOT for OATT transmission service queue management.
products.reference: FERC OATT Pro Forma / NAESB WEQ

attributes.name: transmission_service_request_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the transmission service request under OATT (Open Access Transmission Tariff). Primary key for the transmission service request record.

attributes.name: load_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to forecast.load. Business justification: Transmission service requests require load forecasts for system impact studies to assess whether requested capacity can be accommodated under forecasted system conditions. OASIS study process uses loa

attributes.name: primary_transmission_ems_node_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Point of Receipt PNode (Pricing Node) ID
attributes.description: Pricing node identifier for the point of receipt, used for LMP (Locational Marginal Price) settlement and congestion management in RTO/ISO markets.

attributes.name: requestor_counterparty_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to trading.counterparty. Business justification: Transmission service requestors are trading counterparties. Unified counterparty management enables credit exposure aggregation across transmission reservations and energy trades for the same entity,

attributes.name: transmission_service_agreement_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the executed transmission service agreement (TSA) resulting from this approved request. Links the request to the binding service contract.
attributes.references: OATT Pro Forma Tariff Attachment A, FERC Order 888

attributes.name: ancillary_services_required
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of ancillary services required to support the transmission service (e.g., scheduling, system control, reactive supply, regulation, frequency response, operating reserve, energy imbalance).
attributes.references: OATT Pro Forma Tariff Schedule 2-6, FERC Order 888

attributes.name: approval_date
attributes.description: Date when the transmission service request was formally approved by the transmission provider, granting transmission rights to the requestor.
attributes.references: OATT Pro Forma Tariff Section 17, FERC Order 888

attributes.name: approved_capacity_mw
attributes.description: Amount of transmission capacity approved by the transmission provider in megawatts (MW). May differ from requested capacity based on ATC (Available Transfer Capability) and system impact study results.
attributes.references: OATT Pro Forma Tariff Section 19, NERC MOD-001

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this transmission service request record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and data lineage.
attributes.references: SOX Internal Controls, Data Governance Standards

attributes.name: denial_date
attributes.description: Date when the transmission service request was formally denied by the transmission provider due to insufficient ATC, reliability concerns, or other OATT-compliant reasons.
attributes.references: OATT Pro Forma Tariff Section 17, FERC Order 888

attributes.name: denial_reason
attributes.description: Detailed explanation for denial of the transmission service request, citing specific OATT provisions, ATC constraints, or reliability standards that preclude approval.
attributes.references: OATT Pro Forma Tariff Section 17, NERC Reliability Standards

attributes.name: estimated_upgrade_cost_usd
attributes.business_glossary_term: Estimated Network Upgrade Cost (USD - United States Dollar)
attributes.description: Estimated cost in US dollars for transmission system network upgrades required to accommodate the requested service, as determined by the facilities study.
attributes.references: OATT Pro Forma Tariff Section 19.2, FERC Order 2003

attributes.name: facilities_study_status
attributes.description: Status of the facilities study required to identify transmission system upgrades or network modifications needed to accommodate the requested service.
attributes.references: OATT Pro Forma Tariff Section 19.2, NERC FAC Standards

attributes.name: ferc_docket_number
attributes.business_glossary_term: FERC (Federal Energy Regulatory Commission) Docket Number
attributes.description: FERC docket reference number for any related transmission service dispute, complaint, or tariff filing associated with this request.

attributes.name: ftr_allocation_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the approved transmission service includes allocation of Financial Transmission Rights for hedging congestion costs in RTO/ISO markets.
attributes.references: FERC Order 681, RTO/ISO FTR Allocation Rules

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this transmission service request record was last updated. Tracks the most recent change to any field in the record.
attributes.references: SOX Internal Controls, Data Governance Standards

attributes.name: modified_by_user
attributes.description: Username or identifier of the system user who last modified this transmission service request record. Used for audit and accountability.

attributes.name: nerc_reliability_region
attributes.business_glossary_term: NERC (North American Electric Reliability Corporation) Reliability Region
attributes.description: NERC regional entity responsible for reliability coordination and compliance oversight for this transmission service (e.g., WECC, ERCOT, MRO, NPCC, RF, SERC, SPP, TRE). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: WECC|ERCOT|MRO|NPCC|RF|SERC|SPP|TRE — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: NERC Regional Entities, NERC Functional Model

attributes.name: network_upgrade_required_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether transmission system network upgrades are required to accommodate the requested service. True if facilities study identified necessary system enhancements.
attributes.references: OATT Pro Forma Tariff Section 19.2, FERC Order 2003

attributes.name: point_of_delivery_name
attributes.description: Name of the sink point or substation where power will be delivered from the transmission system for point-to-point service. May reference a PNode or substation.
attributes.references: OATT Pro Forma Tariff Section 13, NERC TLR

attributes.name: point_of_receipt_name
attributes.description: Name of the source point or substation where power will be received onto the transmission system for point-to-point service. May reference a PNode or substation.
attributes.references: OATT Pro Forma Tariff Section 13, NERC Transmission Loading Relief (TLR)

attributes.name: priority_level
attributes.description: OATT priority ranking for the transmission service request. Lower numbers indicate higher priority. Firm service typically has priority 1-6, non-firm service 7.
attributes.references: OATT Pro Forma Tariff Section 13.2, FERC Order 888

attributes.name: queue_position
attributes.description: Sequential position of this request in the transmission service queue, determined by submission timestamp. Used for first-come-first-served processing under OATT rules.

attributes.name: redirect_rights_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the transmission customer has the right to redirect the point of receipt or point of delivery during the service period, subject to ATC availability.
attributes.references: OATT Pro Forma Tariff Section 22, FERC Order 888

attributes.name: request_number
attributes.description: Externally-known business identifier for the transmission service request, typically formatted as TSR-YYYYMMDD-NNNN. Used for OATT queue management and FERC reporting.
attributes.references: FERC Order 888, OATT Pro Forma Tariff

attributes.name: request_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the transmission service request in the OATT queue. Tracks progression from submission through study, approval, or denial. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: SUBMITTED|UNDER-STUDY|CONDITIONALLY-APPROVED|APPROVED|DENIED|WITHDRAWN|SUPERSEDED — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: OATT Queue Management Standards, NAESB WEQ-001

attributes.name: request_submitted_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the transmission service request was formally submitted to the transmission provider. Determines queue position and priority under OATT first-come-first-served rules.

attributes.name: requested_capacity_mw
attributes.description: Amount of transmission capacity requested in megawatts (MW). Represents the maximum power transfer capability sought under the transmission service agreement.
attributes.references: OATT Pro Forma Tariff Section 13, NERC MOD Standards

attributes.name: requestor_contact_email
attributes.description: Email address of the primary contact for transmission service request communications and notifications.

attributes.name: requestor_contact_name
attributes.description: Name of the primary contact person at the requesting entity for this transmission service request.

attributes.name: requestor_contact_phone
attributes.description: Phone number of the primary contact for urgent transmission service request communications.

attributes.name: resale_allowed_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the transmission customer is permitted to resell or reassign the transmission service capacity to a third party under OATT resale provisions.
attributes.references: OATT Pro Forma Tariff Section 23, FERC Order 888

attributes.name: rollover_rights_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the transmission customer has rollover rights to renew the transmission service at the end of the service period under OATT right-of-first-refusal provisions.
attributes.references: OATT Pro Forma Tariff Section 2.2, FERC Order 888

attributes.name: rto_iso_region
attributes.business_glossary_term: RTO/ISO (Regional Transmission Organization / Independent System Operator) Region
attributes.description: Name of the RTO or ISO region where the transmission service is requested (e.g., PJM, MISO, CAISO, SPP, ERCOT, NYISO, ISO-NE). Used for market coordination and FERC reporting.

attributes.name: service_end_date
attributes.description: Requested end date for the transmission service. Defines the termination of the service period. Null for open-ended or evergreen NITS agreements.

attributes.name: service_start_date
attributes.description: Requested start date for the transmission service. Defines the beginning of the service period for capacity reservation and scheduling rights.

attributes.name: service_type
attributes.description: Type of transmission service requested: PTP-FIRM (Point-to-Point Firm), PTP-NON-FIRM (Point-to-Point Non-Firm), NITS (Network Integration Transmission Service), or SECONDARY (Secondary Network Service).

attributes.name: study_completion_date
attributes.description: Date when all required transmission service studies (system impact and facilities studies) were completed and results delivered to the requestor.
attributes.references: OATT Pro Forma Tariff Section 19, NAESB WEQ-001

attributes.name: study_required_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether a system impact study or facilities study is required to evaluate the transmission service request. True if studies are needed to assess grid reliability impacts.
attributes.references: OATT Pro Forma Tariff Section 19, NERC TPL Standards

attributes.name: system_impact_study_status
attributes.description: Status of the system impact study required to evaluate whether the requested transmission service can be provided without adversely affecting system reliability.
attributes.references: OATT Pro Forma Tariff Section 19.1, NERC MOD-032

attributes.name: withdrawal_date
attributes.description: Date when the transmission service request was voluntarily withdrawn by the requestor before approval or denial.

products.name: transmission_service_agreement
products.description: Master record for executed transmission service agreements under OATT including associated billing and invoicing. Captures agreement identifier, customer entity, service type (PTP/NITS), contracted capacity (MW), source and sink points, term start and end dates, rate schedule reference, billing determinants, FERC filing status, amendment history, and invoice records (invoice identifier, billing period, billed capacity in MW-months, energy throughput in MWh, ancillary service charges, total amount due, invoice date, due date, payment status). SSOT for transmission customer contractual entitlements and transmission revenue billing within the OATT commercial lifecycle, distinct from retail billing domain.
products.reference: FERC OATT Transmission Service Agreement

attributes.name: transmission_service_agreement_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the transmission service agreement. Primary key for this entity.

attributes.name: billing_service_agreement_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to billing.billing_service_agreement. Business justification: Each transmission service agreement (OATT contract) has a corresponding billing service agreement for invoicing and AR management. Real business process: transmission revenue billing creates invoices

attributes.name: generator_fuel_supply_contract_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Generator Fuel Supply Contract Id (Foreign Key)
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to supply.fuel_supply_contract. Business justification: Network transmission service agreements for generators must reference fuel supply contracts to validate transmission capacity reservations align with fuel delivery capabilities, scheduling constraints

attributes.name: receivable_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.receivable. Business justification: Service agreements generate receivables for transmission capacity charges billed monthly to customers. Links transmission commercial operations to accounts receivable management and revenue recognitio

attributes.name: regulatory_filing_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.regulatory_filing. Business justification: Long-term firm transmission service agreements require FERC Section 205 rate filings for approval. Service agreements with non-standard terms or rates trigger mandatory regulatory filings and docket t

attributes.name: transmission_customer_id
attributes.description: Reference to the transmission customer entity that is party to this agreement.

attributes.name: agreement_number
attributes.description: Externally-known unique business identifier for the transmission service agreement, typically formatted as TSA- prefix followed by alphanumeric code.

attributes.name: agreement_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the transmission service agreement.

attributes.name: amendment_count
attributes.description: Total number of amendments executed against this transmission service agreement since original execution.

attributes.name: ancillary_services_included
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of ancillary services included in this transmission service agreement (e.g., scheduling, system control, reactive supply, regulation, frequency response, energy imbalance, operating reserve).

attributes.name: billing_cycle
attributes.description: Frequency of billing for this transmission service agreement.

attributes.name: collateral_amount_usd
attributes.business_glossary_term: Collateral Amount in United States Dollars (USD)
attributes.description: Amount of financial collateral required in USD, if applicable.

attributes.name: collateral_required_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether financial collateral is required from the transmission customer for this agreement.

attributes.name: contract_document_reference
attributes.description: Reference to the physical or electronic contract document storage location (e.g., document management system identifier, file path).

attributes.name: contracted_capacity_mw
attributes.description: Maximum transmission capacity in megawatts (MW) contracted under this agreement.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this transmission service agreement record was first created in the system.

attributes.name: credit_rating
attributes.description: Credit rating of the transmission customer at the time of agreement execution, used for credit assessment and collateral requirements.

attributes.name: energy_charge_rate_usd_per_mwh
attributes.business_glossary_term: Energy Charge Rate in United States Dollars per Megawatt-Hour (USD/MWh)
attributes.description: Energy transmission charge rate in USD per megawatt-hour (MWh) for actual energy throughput.

attributes.name: executed_date
attributes.description: Date when this transmission service agreement was formally executed by all parties.

attributes.name: ferc_docket_number
attributes.business_glossary_term: Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) Docket Number
attributes.description: FERC docket number assigned to the regulatory filing for this transmission service agreement.

attributes.name: ferc_filing_date
attributes.business_glossary_term: Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) Filing Date
attributes.description: Date when this transmission service agreement was filed with FERC for regulatory approval.

attributes.name: ferc_filing_status
attributes.business_glossary_term: Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) Filing Status
attributes.description: Status of FERC regulatory filing for this transmission service agreement.

attributes.name: last_amendment_date
attributes.description: Date of the most recent amendment to this transmission service agreement.

attributes.name: last_amendment_description
attributes.description: Brief description of the most recent amendment to this transmission service agreement.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this transmission service agreement record was last modified in the system.

attributes.name: monthly_capacity_charge_usd
attributes.business_glossary_term: Monthly Capacity Charge in United States Dollars (USD)
attributes.description: Monthly capacity reservation charge in USD based on contracted MW capacity.

attributes.name: nerc_reliability_region
attributes.business_glossary_term: North American Electric Reliability Corporation (NERC) Reliability Region
attributes.description: NERC reliability region applicable to this transmission service agreement. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: WECC|ERCOT|MRO|NPCC|RF|SERC|TRE|SPP — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-form notes or comments regarding this transmission service agreement for internal reference.

attributes.name: oatt_tariff_version
attributes.description: Version of the OATT tariff under which this transmission service agreement was executed.

attributes.name: payment_terms_days
attributes.description: Number of days from invoice date within which payment is due.

attributes.name: priority_ranking
attributes.description: Priority ranking for curtailment purposes, with lower numbers indicating higher priority. Firm service typically has priority over non-firm.

attributes.name: rate_schedule_reference
attributes.description: Reference to the applicable OATT rate schedule governing pricing for this transmission service agreement.

attributes.name: responsible_account_manager
attributes.description: Name of the account manager or business relationship owner responsible for this transmission service agreement.

attributes.name: rollover_rights_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the transmission customer has rollover rights to renew this agreement at expiration.

attributes.name: rto_iso_region
attributes.business_glossary_term: Regional Transmission Organization (RTO) or Independent System Operator (ISO) Region
attributes.description: RTO or ISO region in which this transmission service agreement operates (e.g., PJM, MISO, CAISO, ERCOT, SPP, NYISO, ISO-NE).

attributes.name: service_subtype
attributes.description: Subtype classification of transmission service indicating priority and curtailment rights: firm (guaranteed), non-firm (interruptible), or conditional firm.

attributes.name: service_type
attributes.description: Type of transmission service under OATT: PTP (Point-to-Point Transmission Service) or NITS (Network Integration Transmission Service).

attributes.name: sink_point_of_delivery
attributes.description: Designated point of delivery (POD) or sink location where power exits the transmission system under this agreement.

attributes.name: source_point_of_receipt
attributes.description: Designated point of receipt (POR) or source location where power enters the transmission system under this agreement.

attributes.name: term_end_date
attributes.description: Scheduled end date when the transmission service agreement expires. Nullable for open-ended or evergreen agreements.

attributes.name: term_start_date
attributes.description: Effective start date when the transmission service agreement becomes binding and service begins.

attributes.name: termination_date
attributes.description: Actual date when this transmission service agreement was terminated, if applicable.

attributes.name: termination_reason
attributes.description: Reason for termination of this transmission service agreement (e.g., customer request, non-payment, breach of terms, expiration).

products.name: ftr_position
products.description: Master record for Financial Transmission Rights (FTR) positions held by the utility or transmission customers as congestion revenue hedges. Captures FTR identifier, auction round and period, obligation or option type, source PNode, sink PNode, MW quantity, direction (prevailing/counter-flow), auction clearing price ($/MW), monthly settlement credits/charges, RTO/ISO market identifier, portfolio grouping, and expiration date. Supports congestion cost hedging strategy, day-ahead market settlement reconciliation, and ARR-to-FTR conversion tracking.
products.reference: FERC FTR / RTO FTR Auction Rules

attributes.name: ftr_position_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the FTR position record. Primary key for the FTR position master data.
attributes.references: FERC Order 888 - Open Access Transmission Tariff

attributes.name: energy_price_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to forecast.energy_price. Business justification: FTR positions are valued using energy price forecasts for mark-to-market accounting, portfolio risk assessment, and hedging strategy decisions. Treasury and trading functions require price forecasts t

attributes.name: ferc_market_report_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.ferc_market_report. Business justification: FTR positions and settlements must be reported in FERC Electric Quarterly Reports (EQR) per 18 CFR 35.41. Market participants report FTR auction results, holdings, and settlement credits quarterly.

attributes.name: ftr_holding_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to trading.ftr_holding. Business justification: FTR positions in transmission operations represent the same financial instruments managed as trading holdings. Energy utilities track transmission FTR positions that feed trading portfolio management

attributes.name: ftr_path_id
attributes.description: FK to transmission.path.path_id — FTR positions are defined between source and sink points that map to transmission paths. Required for congestion revenue hedging and settlement reconciliation.

attributes.name: hedged_ppa_contract_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to renewable.ppa_contract. Business justification: Renewable generators and their offtakers routinely acquire FTR positions to hedge congestion risk between generation source and delivery sink specified in PPAs. This is standard risk management practi

attributes.name: original_ftr_position_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Original Financial Transmission Right (FTR) Position Identifier
attributes.description: Reference to the original FTR position identifier if this position was created through reconfiguration or modification of an existing position. Null for positions acquired directly from auction.

attributes.name: primary_path_id
attributes.description: FK to transmission.path.path_id — FTR positions hedge congestion on specific source-sink paths. This FK connects financial hedges to physical network elements.

attributes.name: profit_center_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.profit_center. Business justification: FTR positions are financial instruments assigned to profit centers for P&L tracking, mark-to-market valuation, and financial performance reporting. Required for ISO market settlement reconciliation.

attributes.name: arr_conversion_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this FTR position was acquired through conversion of an Auction Revenue Right (ARR) allocation. ARRs are allocated to load-serving entities and can be converted to FTRs in annual auctions.
attributes.references: FERC Order 888 - Open Access Transmission Tariff

attributes.name: arr_identifier
attributes.description: Identifier of the ARR that was converted to create this FTR position, if applicable. Null for FTRs acquired directly through auction.
attributes.references: FERC Order 888 - Open Access Transmission Tariff

attributes.name: auction_clearing_price_per_mw
attributes.description: Price per MW at which this FTR position cleared in the auction, denominated in USD per MW for the contract period. Represents the upfront cost paid to acquire the FTR hedge.
attributes.references: FERC Order 888 - Open Access Transmission Tariff

attributes.name: auction_date
attributes.description: Date on which the FTR auction was conducted and this position was awarded.
attributes.references: FERC Order 888 - Open Access Transmission Tariff

attributes.name: auction_round
attributes.description: Identifier for the FTR auction round in which this position was acquired. Typically includes auction type (annual, monthly, reconfiguration) and period designation.
attributes.references: FERC Order 888 - Open Access Transmission Tariff

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this FTR position record was first created in the system.

attributes.name: cumulative_settlement_credit_usd
attributes.business_glossary_term: Cumulative Settlement Credit in United States Dollars (USD)
attributes.description: Total cumulative congestion revenue credits or charges for this FTR position since effective start date, denominated in USD. Used to track overall hedge performance.
attributes.references: FERC Order 888 - Open Access Transmission Tariff

attributes.name: effective_end_date
attributes.description: Date on which the FTR position expires and ceases to accrue congestion revenue. Typically aligned with auction period boundaries (end of month, end of planning year).
attributes.references: FERC Order 888 - Open Access Transmission Tariff

attributes.name: effective_start_date
attributes.description: Date on which the FTR position becomes effective and begins accruing congestion revenue credits or charges.
attributes.references: FERC Order 888 - Open Access Transmission Tariff

attributes.name: ferc_reporting_category
attributes.business_glossary_term: Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) Reporting Category
attributes.description: FERC reporting classification for this FTR position, used for regulatory compliance reporting under FERC Form 1 and FERC Electric Quarterly Reports (EQR).
attributes.references: FERC Form 1 - Annual Report of Major Electric Utilities

attributes.name: flow_direction
attributes.description: Direction of power flow for the FTR position. Prevailing flow aligns with typical congestion patterns; counter-flow opposes typical patterns and may have lower auction prices.
attributes.references: FERC Order 888 - Open Access Transmission Tariff

attributes.name: ftr_identifier
attributes.description: Externally-known unique identifier for the FTR position as assigned by the RTO/ISO market system. Used for market settlement reconciliation and external reporting.
attributes.references: FERC Order 888 - Open Access Transmission Tariff

attributes.name: ftr_type
attributes.description: Type of FTR position held. Obligation FTRs pay or charge the holder based on congestion price differences; Option FTRs only pay when positive, with no charge when negative.
attributes.references: FERC Order 888 - Open Access Transmission Tariff

attributes.name: hedge_strategy_code
attributes.description: Code identifying the hedging strategy or business purpose for acquiring this FTR position. Examples include load-serving hedge, generation hedge, merchant arbitrage, portfolio optimization.

attributes.name: holding_entity_name
attributes.description: Name of the legal entity or business unit that holds this FTR position. May be the utility itself or a transmission customer.
attributes.references: FERC Order 888 - Open Access Transmission Tariff

attributes.name: holding_entity_type
attributes.description: Classification of the entity holding the FTR position. Utility positions are held for internal hedging; transmission customer positions are held by external market participants.
attributes.references: FERC Order 888 - Open Access Transmission Tariff

attributes.name: internal_book_code
attributes.description: Internal accounting book or cost center code to which this FTR position is assigned for financial reporting and cost allocation.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this FTR position record was last updated in the system.

attributes.name: last_settlement_date
attributes.description: Date of the most recent settlement calculation for this FTR position. Typically monthly for ongoing positions.
attributes.references: FERC Order 888 - Open Access Transmission Tariff

attributes.name: monthly_settlement_credit_usd
attributes.business_glossary_term: Monthly Settlement Credit in United States Dollars (USD)
attributes.description: Total congestion revenue credit received for this FTR position in the most recent monthly settlement, denominated in USD. Positive values represent credits; negative values represent charges (for obligation FTRs only).
attributes.references: FERC Order 888 - Open Access Transmission Tariff

attributes.name: mw_quantity
attributes.description: Quantity of transmission capacity in megawatts covered by this FTR position. Determines the magnitude of congestion revenue credits or charges.
attributes.references: FERC Order 888 - Open Access Transmission Tariff

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text notes or comments regarding this FTR position, including hedging rationale, special conditions, or settlement exceptions.

attributes.name: on_peak_off_peak_designation
attributes.description: Time-of-use designation for the FTR position. On-peak FTRs cover weekday business hours; off-peak FTRs cover nights and weekends; 24-hour FTRs cover all hours.
attributes.references: FERC Order 888 - Open Access Transmission Tariff

attributes.name: portfolio_grouping
attributes.description: Business grouping or portfolio designation for this FTR position. Used to aggregate positions for risk management, hedging strategy analysis, and financial reporting.

attributes.name: position_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the FTR position. Active positions are in-force and subject to settlement; expired positions have reached their end date; settled positions have completed final financial settlement; cancelled positions were terminated before expiration.
attributes.references: FERC Order 888 - Open Access Transmission Tariff

attributes.name: reconfiguration_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this FTR position was acquired through a reconfiguration auction, which allows holders to modify existing positions mid-period.
attributes.references: FERC Order 888 - Open Access Transmission Tariff

attributes.name: rto_iso_market_code
attributes.business_glossary_term: Regional Transmission Organization (RTO) / Independent System Operator (ISO) Market Identifier
attributes.description: Identifier for the RTO or ISO market in which this FTR position was acquired and is settled. Examples include PJM, MISO, CAISO, ERCOT, NYISO, ISO-NE, SPP.
attributes.references: FERC Order 888 - Open Access Transmission Tariff

attributes.name: rto_iso_market_name
attributes.business_glossary_term: Regional Transmission Organization (RTO) / Independent System Operator (ISO) Market Name
attributes.description: Human-readable name of the RTO or ISO market.
attributes.references: FERC Order 888 - Open Access Transmission Tariff

attributes.name: sink_pnode_code
attributes.description: Identifier for the sink pricing node (withdrawal point) of the FTR path. Congestion revenue is calculated based on the Locational Marginal Price (LMP) difference between source and sink PNodes.
attributes.references: FERC Order 888 - Open Access Transmission Tariff

attributes.name: sink_pnode_name
attributes.description: Human-readable name of the sink pricing node for the FTR path.
attributes.references: FERC Order 888 - Open Access Transmission Tariff

attributes.name: source_pnode_code
attributes.description: Identifier for the source pricing node (injection point) of the FTR path. Congestion revenue is calculated based on the Locational Marginal Price (LMP) difference between source and sink PNodes.
attributes.references: FERC Order 888 - Open Access Transmission Tariff

attributes.name: source_pnode_name
attributes.description: Human-readable name of the source pricing node for the FTR path.
attributes.references: FERC Order 888 - Open Access Transmission Tariff

attributes.name: trading_hub_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether either the source or sink PNode is a major trading hub. Hub-based FTRs typically have higher liquidity and more predictable congestion patterns.
attributes.references: FERC Order 888 - Open Access Transmission Tariff

products.name: congestion_event
products.description: Transactional record of a transmission congestion event on a specific path or flowgate where physical power flow constraints cause economic dispatch deviations. Captures event identifier, affected path or flowgate, start and end timestamps, congestion direction, shadow price ($/MWh), curtailed MW, LMP differential between source and sink nodes, RTO/ISO market interval, binding constraint identifier, and remedial action taken (redispatch, TLR, curtailment). Used for congestion cost analysis, FTR settlement reconciliation, Transmission Loading Relief (TLR) tracking, and FERC reporting.
products.reference: LMP Congestion Component / FERC Order 888

attributes.name: congestion_event_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the transmission congestion event record. Primary key for the congestion event entity.

attributes.name: causal_outage_event_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to outage.outage_event. Business justification: Transmission outages frequently cause congestion events (flowgate binding, shadow prices). Linking congestion to the causal outage enables root cause analysis, market settlement dispute resolution, an

attributes.name: congestion_path_id
attributes.description: FK to transmission.path.path_id — Congestion events occur on specific transmission paths/flowgates. Required for congestion cost analysis, FTR settlement, and FERC reporting.

attributes.name: congestion_transmission_path_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the transmission path affected by congestion, representing the source-to-sink corridor where power flow is constrained.

attributes.name: contingency_element_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the contingency element (the element whose outage would cause the monitored element to exceed its limit), if the congestion is contingency-based.
attributes.references: NERC Transmission Planning Standards - Contingency Analysis

attributes.name: ems_event_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the corresponding event in the Energy Management System, used for cross-system event correlation and analysis.

attributes.name: energy_price_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to forecast.energy_price. Business justification: Congestion events are analyzed against energy price forecasts for FTR valuation, hedging strategy assessment, and portfolio risk management. Market operations teams use historical congestion patterns

attributes.name: ferc_market_report_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.ferc_market_report. Business justification: Congestion events, shadow prices, and LMP differentials are reportable market data in FERC EQR filings. ISO/RTO market participants report congestion costs and transmission constraint binding frequenc

attributes.name: flowgate_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the transmission flowgate or monitored facility experiencing congestion. A flowgate is a mathematical construct representing one or more transmission elements that may limit power flow.
attributes.references: NERC Interchange Distribution Calculator (IDC) - Flowgate Definition

attributes.name: ftr_holding_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to trading.ftr_holding. Business justification: Congestion events directly impact FTR settlement payouts. Trading desks link congestion events to FTR holdings to calculate actual vs expected hedge performance, required for mark-to-market valuation,

attributes.name: ftr_position_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the Financial Transmission Right position associated with the congested path, used for FTR settlement reconciliation.
attributes.references: FERC Order 888 - FTR Allocation and Settlement

attributes.name: profit_center_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.profit_center. Business justification: Congestion revenue and costs are allocated to profit centers for financial reporting and performance management. Supports ISO market settlement accounting and transmission revenue tracking.

attributes.name: source_pnode_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the source pricing node (PNode) at the origin of the congested transmission path, used for LMP calculation.

attributes.name: binding_constraint_code
attributes.description: Identifier of the specific binding constraint in the security-constrained economic dispatch that triggered the congestion event.

attributes.name: congestion_cost_usd
attributes.business_glossary_term: Congestion Cost in United States Dollars (USD)
attributes.description: Total congestion cost in USD for the event, calculated as the product of curtailed MW, event duration, and shadow price or LMP differential.

attributes.name: congestion_direction
attributes.description: Direction of the congestion on the transmission path: forward (source to sink), reverse (sink to source), or bidirectional (constrained in both directions).

attributes.name: congestion_end_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the transmission congestion event ended, marking the point at which the constraint was no longer binding or the event was resolved.

attributes.name: congestion_severity
attributes.description: Severity classification of the congestion event based on shadow price, curtailed MW, and duration: low, moderate, high, or critical.

attributes.name: congestion_start_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the transmission congestion event began, marking the point at which the flowgate or path became binding in the dispatch model.

attributes.name: constraint_type
attributes.description: Type of transmission constraint that caused the congestion: thermal (line rating), voltage (voltage limit), stability (transient or dynamic stability), interface (multi-element limit), or nomogram (multi-dimensional operating limit).
attributes.references: NERC Transmission Operations Standards - Constraint Classification

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the congestion event record was first created in the system, used for audit trail and data lineage tracking.

attributes.name: curtailed_mw
attributes.description: Amount of power in megawatts that was curtailed or redispatched to relieve the congestion on the affected flowgate or path.

attributes.name: element_rating_mw
attributes.description: Thermal or operational rating of the monitored transmission element in megawatts, representing the maximum allowable flow under the applicable rating methodology (normal, emergency, or seasonal).

attributes.name: event_cause
attributes.description: Primary cause of the congestion event: high demand, generation outage, transmission outage, renewable energy variability, loop flow, unscheduled flow, or market condition. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: high_demand|generation_outage|transmission_outage|renewable_variability|loop_flow|unscheduled_flow|market_condition — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: FERC Congestion Reporting - Root Cause Analysis

attributes.name: event_duration_minutes
attributes.description: Total duration of the congestion event in minutes, calculated as the difference between start and end timestamps.

attributes.name: event_number
attributes.description: Business identifier for the congestion event, typically assigned by the RTO/ISO or EMS system for external reference and reporting.

attributes.name: event_status
attributes.description: Current status of the congestion event in the event management lifecycle: active (ongoing), resolved (cleared), under review (post-event analysis), or escalated (requires higher-level intervention).

attributes.name: ferc_reportable_flag
attributes.business_glossary_term: Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) Reportable Flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether the congestion event meets FERC reporting thresholds and must be included in quarterly or annual transmission congestion reports.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the congestion event record was last modified, used for audit trail and change tracking.

attributes.name: lmp_differential_usd_per_mwh
attributes.business_glossary_term: Locational Marginal Price (LMP) Differential in United States Dollars (USD) per Megawatt-Hour (MWh)
attributes.description: Difference between sink LMP and source LMP, representing the congestion component of the price spread across the transmission path.

attributes.name: market_interval_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the RTO/ISO market interval (typically 5-minute or hourly) during which the congestion event occurred or was recorded.
attributes.references: FERC Order 2000 - RTO Market Interval Standards

attributes.name: market_type
attributes.description: Type of wholesale electricity market in which the congestion event occurred: day-ahead market (DAM), real-time market (RTM), intra-day market, or ancillary services market.

attributes.name: monitored_element_code
attributes.description: Identifier of the specific transmission element (line, transformer, or interface) that was monitored and became binding during the congestion event.
attributes.references: NERC Facility Ratings Standards - Monitored Element Registry

attributes.name: nerc_reliability_region
attributes.business_glossary_term: North American Electric Reliability Corporation (NERC) Reliability Region
attributes.description: NERC reliability region in which the congestion event occurred (e.g., WECC, ERCOT, MRO, NPCC, RF, SERC, TRE, FRCC).
attributes.references: NERC Reliability Standards - Regional Entity Designation

attributes.name: operator_notes
attributes.description: Free-text notes entered by transmission operators or market operators describing the congestion event, actions taken, and any special circumstances.

attributes.name: percent_of_rating
attributes.description: Percentage of the element rating at which the monitored element was operating during the congestion event, calculated as (flow / rating) * 100.

attributes.name: post_contingency_flow_mw
attributes.description: Projected power flow in megawatts on the monitored element following the contingency event, used in security-constrained dispatch.
attributes.references: NERC Transmission Operations - Contingency Flow Analysis

attributes.name: pre_contingency_flow_mw
attributes.description: Power flow in megawatts on the monitored element under normal (pre-contingency) conditions during the congestion event.

attributes.name: remedial_action_taken
attributes.description: Type of remedial action taken to relieve the congestion: economic redispatch, Transmission Loading Relief (TLR), load curtailment, voltage control, phase shifter adjustment, topology change, or none. products.name: outage_path_impact
products.description: This association product represents the operational impact event between transmission outages and transmission paths. It captures the specific effect each outage has on each affected transmission path, including ATC reductions, timing, and RTO notification requirements. Each record links one transmission outage to one impacted path with attributes that exist only in the context of this specific outage-path impact relationship. This is a core operational and compliance entity required for NERC reliability reporting and RTO/ISO coordination.. Existence Justification: In transmission operations, a single outage event (line trip, transformer failure, planned maintenance) simultaneously impacts multiple transmission paths by reducing their Available Transfer Capability, and each path experiences impacts from multiple different outages over time. RTOs and ISOs require utilities to report path-specific ATC impacts for reliability coordination and NERC compliance, making this a core operational relationship that transmission operators actively manage and monitor in real-time.

products.name: transformer_vendor_service
products.description: This association product represents the service and warranty relationship between power transformers and vendors. It captures the multi-vendor service ecosystem where a single transformer receives services from multiple specialized vendors (OEM for warranty, oil testing labs, bushing manufacturers, local contractors) and each vendor services many transformers. Each record links one power transformer to one vendor with warranty terms, service contract details, and service history that exist only in the context of this specific transformer-vendor relationship.. Existence Justification: In energy utilities transmission operations, a single power transformer receives specialized services from multiple vendors simultaneously: the OEM handles warranty and major repairs, oil testing laboratories perform dissolved gas analysis, bushing manufacturers provide component-specific maintenance, and local contractors handle routine servicing. Each vendor services many transformers across the utility's transmission network. The utility actively manages these multi-vendor service relationships, tracking warranty coverage, service contracts, maintenance schedules, and vendor performance on a per-transformer, per-vendor basis.

products.name: path_reservation
products.description: This association product represents the contractual reservation of transmission capacity on specific paths under OATT transmission service agreements. It captures the allocation of contracted MW capacity across transmission paths, priority rankings for curtailment, and effective periods for each path reservation. Each record links one transmission service agreement to one path with attributes that exist only in the context of this capacity reservation relationship. This is the SSOT for ATC calculation, TLR implementation, and OASIS posting compliance under FERC pro forma OATT requirements.. Existence Justification: In FERC-regulated transmission operations, a single transmission service agreement commonly reserves capacity across multiple transmission paths (e.g., a long-haul PTP agreement traversing multiple flowgates), and a single transmission path hosts capacity reservations from multiple customer agreements simultaneously. Transmission providers must actively manage these path-level reservations to calculate Available Transfer Capability (ATC), implement Transmission Loading Relief (TLR) during congestion, and post capacity availability to OASIS for regulatory compliance.

attributes.description: Zero sequence inductive reactance per unit length. Essential for fault current calculations and protection system design.

attributes.name: zero_sequence_resistance_ohms_per_km

attributes.description: Zero sequence resistance per unit length. Used in ground fault analysis and protective relay coordination studies.

products.name: load_zone
products.description: Master record for distribution load zones — logical groupings of network segments used for load balancing, volt-VAR optimization dispatch, demand forecasting, and capacity planning. Captures zone identifier, zone name, geographic boundary (GIS polygon), nominal load (MW/MVAr), peak demand (MW), associated feeders, voltage regulation targets, power factor targets, and DMS zone classification. Serves as the control zone for VVO dispatch actions and the planning unit for distribution capacity studies. SSOT for load zone definition in GE PowerOn ADMS.

attributes.name: load_feeder_id
attributes.description: FK to distribution.feeder.feeder_id — Load zones are associated with feeders. The description mentions 'associated feeders'. This is a many-to-many but the primary association is critical for load balancing operations.

attributes.name: load_zone_includes_feeder
attributes.description: FK to distribution.feeder.feeder_id — Load zones are logical groupings that include one or more feeders. This FK supports VVO dispatch zone definition and capacity planning by zone.

attributes.name: planning_engineer_employee_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: Load zones require planning engineers for capacity analysis, load forecasting, DER hosting capacity studies, and capital investment planning. Essential for distribution planning processes, capacity st

attributes.name: profit_center_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.profit_center. Business justification: Load zones represent service territories or planning areas that align with profit center structures for revenue and cost tracking by geographic/functional area. Essential for territorial profitability

attributes.name: capacity_mva
attributes.description: Total installed capacity of the load zone in megavolt-amperes, representing the maximum apparent power the zone infrastructure can support. Used for capacity planning and load transfer studies.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this load zone record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking.
attributes.references: SOX Compliance, Utility Data Governance Standards

attributes.name: customer_count
attributes.description: Total number of customer premises served by this load zone. Used for reliability index calculations (SAIDI, SAIFI, CAIDI) and outage impact assessment.

attributes.name: der_penetration_mw
attributes.description: Total installed capacity of distributed energy resources (solar PV, wind, storage, etc.) within the load zone, measured in megawatts. Used for DER hosting capacity analysis and grid integration planning.

attributes.name: dms_zone_classification
attributes.description: Classification of the zone within the DMS/ADMS for automation capabilities. VVO-enabled zones support Volt-VAR Optimization, FLISR-enabled zones support Fault Location Isolation and Service Restoration, manual zones require operator intervention, hybrid zones have partial automation, and advanced zones support full ADMS integration.

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: Date when the load zone configuration became or will become effective. Used for tracking zone boundary changes, capacity upgrades, and operational transitions.

attributes.name: expiration_date
attributes.description: Date when the load zone configuration expires or is scheduled for decommissioning. Null for active zones with no planned end date.

attributes.name: feeder_count
attributes.description: Number of distribution feeders associated with this load zone. Used for network topology analysis and load balancing.

attributes.name: flisr_enabled_flag
attributes.business_glossary_term: Fault Location Isolation and Service Restoration (FLISR) Enabled Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether FLISR automation is enabled for this load zone. True means automated fault detection, isolation, and restoration; false means manual switching operations.
attributes.references: GE PowerOn ADMS Technical Documentation, IEEE 1547

attributes.name: geographic_boundary_wkt
attributes.description: Geographic boundary of the load zone represented as a WKT (Well-Known Text) polygon. Used for spatial analysis, outage mapping, and GIS integration with Esri ArcGIS Utility Network.
attributes.references: OGC Simple Features Specification, Esri ArcGIS Standards

attributes.name: hosting_capacity_mw
attributes.description: Maximum amount of additional DER capacity the zone can accommodate without infrastructure upgrades or operational issues, measured in megawatts. Used for interconnection screening and DER integration planning.

attributes.name: last_capacity_study_date
attributes.description: Date of the most recent distribution capacity study performed for this load zone. Used to track planning cycle compliance and identify zones requiring updated analysis.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this load zone record was last updated. Used for audit trail, change tracking, and data synchronization across systems.
attributes.references: SOX Compliance, Utility Data Governance Standards

attributes.name: load_profile_type
attributes.description: Dominant customer class or load profile characteristic of the zone. Residential zones peak in evening, commercial zones peak mid-day, industrial zones have steady load, mixed zones have diverse profiles, and agricultural zones have seasonal patterns.

attributes.name: next_capacity_study_date
attributes.description: Scheduled date for the next distribution capacity study for this load zone. Used for planning resource allocation and ensuring regulatory compliance with capacity planning cycles.

attributes.name: nominal_load_mvar
attributes.description: Typical or average reactive power load of the zone under normal operating conditions, measured in megavolt-amperes reactive. Used for Volt-VAR optimization and power factor management.

attributes.name: nominal_load_mw
attributes.description: Typical or average real power load of the zone under normal operating conditions, measured in megawatts. Used for load balancing and capacity planning.

attributes.name: nominal_voltage_kv
attributes.description: Nominal operating voltage of the load zone in kilovolts. Typical distribution voltages range from 4.16 kV to 34.5 kV.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for operational notes, special considerations, or additional context about the load zone. May include information about unique load characteristics, planned projects, or operational constraints.

attributes.name: peak_demand_mw
attributes.description: Historical or forecasted peak real power demand for the zone, measured in megawatts. Critical for capacity planning and infrastructure investment decisions.
attributes.references: FERC Form 1, PUC Capacity Planning Requirements

attributes.name: peak_demand_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the peak demand was recorded or is forecasted to occur. Used for load profile analysis and demand response planning.

attributes.name: planning_area_code
attributes.description: Foreign key reference to the broader distribution planning area or service territory that contains this load zone. Used for regional capacity planning and resource allocation.

attributes.name: power_factor_target
attributes.description: Target power factor for the load zone, typically between 0.95 and 1.00. Used for Volt-VAR optimization dispatch and capacitor bank control to minimize reactive power losses.

attributes.name: reliability_caidi_minutes
attributes.business_glossary_term: Customer Average Interruption Duration Index (CAIDI) Minutes
attributes.description: Customer Average Interruption Duration Index for the load zone, measured in minutes per interruption. Calculated as SAIDI/SAIFI. Indicates average restoration time. Key reliability metric reported to PUC.

attributes.name: reliability_saidi_minutes
attributes.business_glossary_term: System Average Interruption Duration Index (SAIDI) Minutes
attributes.description: System Average Interruption Duration Index for the load zone, measured in minutes per customer per year. Key reliability metric reported to PUC. Lower values indicate better reliability.

attributes.name: reliability_saifi_count
attributes.business_glossary_term: System Average Interruption Frequency Index (SAIFI) Count
attributes.description: System Average Interruption Frequency Index for the load zone, measured as number of interruptions per customer per year. Key reliability metric reported to PUC. Lower values indicate better reliability.

attributes.name: scada_integration_status
attributes.business_glossary_term: Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) Integration Status
attributes.description: Level of SCADA system integration for real-time monitoring and control of the load zone. Fully integrated zones have complete telemetry and control, partially integrated zones have limited coverage, not integrated zones rely on manual operations, and planned zones are scheduled for integration.
attributes.references: NERC CIP Standards, OSIsoft PI Integration Standards

attributes.name: utilization_factor
attributes.description: Ratio of peak demand to installed capacity, indicating how heavily the zone infrastructure is utilized. Values approaching 1.0 indicate need for capacity expansion.

attributes.name: voltage_regulation_target_max_pu
attributes.business_glossary_term: Voltage Regulation Target Maximum Per Unit (pu)
attributes.description: Maximum acceptable voltage level for the zone expressed in per-unit (pu) of nominal voltage. Typically 1.05 pu per ANSI C84.1 Range A. Used by VVO algorithms to maintain voltage within acceptable limits.

attributes.name: voltage_regulation_target_min_pu
attributes.business_glossary_term: Voltage Regulation Target Minimum Per Unit (pu)
attributes.description: Minimum acceptable voltage level for the zone expressed in per-unit (pu) of nominal voltage. Typically 0.95 pu per ANSI C84.1 Range A. Used by VVO algorithms to maintain voltage within acceptable limits.

attributes.name: vvo_enabled_flag

attributes.name: zone_code
attributes.description: Business identifier for the load zone, typically a human-readable alphanumeric code used in operational systems and dispatch communications. Externally known identifier for the zone.

attributes.name: zone_name
attributes.description: Descriptive name of the load zone, often reflecting geographic area or substation association (e.g., 'Downtown West Zone', 'Substation 5 North').

attributes.name: zone_status
attributes.description: Current operational status of the load zone. Active zones are in service, inactive zones are temporarily out of service, planned zones are under construction, decommissioned zones are retired, and maintenance zones are undergoing scheduled work.

attributes.name: zone_type
attributes.description: Classification of the load zone based on its role in the distribution network hierarchy. Primary zones serve major load centers, secondary zones serve neighborhood clusters, tertiary zones serve smaller segments, and special zones serve unique loads (industrial parks, critical infrastructure).

products.name: distribution_switching_order
products.description: Transactional record capturing planned and emergency switching operations on the distribution network, including the full sequence of individual switching steps. Captures switching order number, order type (planned/emergency/FLISR-automated/load-transfer), initiating event reference, crew assignment, authorization approvals, safety clearances, and completion status. Each order contains an ordered sequence of switching steps, each with: step sequence number, target device, operation type (open/close/tag/untag), required pre/post device state, execution timestamp, operator ID, confirmed device state, and step completion status. Records pre-switch and post-switch network topology for each order. SSOT for all distribution switching operations including FLISR-automated sequences, load transfer operations, and step-level audit trail. Sourced from GE PowerOn ADMS switching management module.
products.reference: GE PowerOn ADMS Switching Management / IEEE 1547
