attributes.name: distribution_substation_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the distribution substation serving the affected feeder. Used for substation-level outage aggregation and reporting.
attributes.references: Esri ArcGIS Utility Network - Network Topology

attributes.name: employee_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the ADMS operator who intervened in the FLISR sequence, if operator override occurred. Null for fully automated events.

attributes.name: ems_alarm_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to grid.ems_alarm. Business justification: FLISR automation events trigger EMS alarms that grid operators monitor for real-time situational awareness, disturbance analysis, and NERC compliance reporting. Critical for integrated distribution-tr

attributes.name: event_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the parent outage event record in the Outage Management System (OMS) that this FLISR event is associated with. Links FLISR automation to broader outage lifecycle.

attributes.name: feeder_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the primary distribution feeder on which the FLISR event occurred. Used for feeder-level reliability analysis and SAIDI/SAIFI calculation.
attributes.references: Esri ArcGIS Utility Network - Network Topology

attributes.name: network_segment_id
attributes.description: FK to distribution.network_segment.network_segment_id — FLISR events identify a faulted segment. The description mentions 'faulted segment identified'. Critical for fault isolation logic and reliability reporting.

attributes.name: storm_event_id
attributes.description: Identifier linking this FLISR event to a declared storm event, if the fault occurred during a major weather event. Used for storm impact aggregation and mutual aid reporting.

attributes.name: caidi_contribution_minutes
attributes.business_glossary_term: Customer Average Interruption Duration Index (CAIDI) Contribution in Minutes
attributes.description: Calculated contribution of this FLISR event to the CAIDI reliability index, in minutes. Computed as total customer-minutes / customers affected. Measures average restoration time per affected customer.
attributes.references: IEEE 1366 - Electric Power Distribution Reliability Indices

attributes.name: communication_failure_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether communication failures with field devices occurred during the FLISR sequence. True if communication issues impacted automation; false otherwise.

attributes.name: customers_affected_initial
attributes.description: Number of customer meters that lost service when the fault occurred and before FLISR restoration actions. Used for SAIFI numerator calculation.
attributes.references: IEEE 1366 - Electric Power Distribution Reliability Indices

attributes.name: customers_affected_post_restoration
attributes.description: Number of customer meters that remain without service after FLISR restoration sequence completed. Represents customers on the isolated faulted segment awaiting manual repair.
attributes.references: IEEE 1366 - Electric Power Distribution Reliability Indices

attributes.name: customers_restored_count
attributes.description: Number of customer meters that had service restored by FLISR automation (initial affected minus post-restoration affected). Measures FLISR effectiveness in minimizing outage scope.
attributes.references: IEEE 1366 - Electric Power Distribution Reliability Indices

attributes.name: der_impacted_count
attributes.description: Number of Distributed Energy Resource (DER) installations (solar, storage, generators) affected by the FLISR event. Used for DER impact analysis and IEEE 1547 compliance reporting.

attributes.name: event_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the FLISR automation event. Tracks progression from initiation through completion or failure.

attributes.name: event_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the FLISR automation event was triggered by the Advanced Distribution Management System (ADMS). Represents the real-world moment the fault was detected and FLISR sequence initiated.

attributes.name: failure_reason
attributes.description: Detailed explanation of why FLISR automation failed or was aborted, if applicable. Captures system errors, communication failures, operator intervention reasons, or topology constraints.

attributes.name: fault_current_amps
attributes.description: Magnitude of fault current measured at the triggering fault indicator, in amperes. Used for fault severity analysis and protective device coordination validation.
attributes.references: IEEE C37.2 - Electrical Power System Device Function Numbers

attributes.name: fault_type
attributes.description: Classification of the fault condition that triggered FLISR. Permanent faults require manual repair; temporary faults may clear after isolation; transient faults clear on recloser operation.
attributes.references: IEEE C37.2 - Electrical Power System Device Function Numbers

attributes.name: flisr_algorithm_version
attributes.description: Version identifier of the FLISR algorithm logic deployed in ADMS at the time of this event. Used for performance trending and algorithm tuning analysis.

attributes.name: flisr_event_number
attributes.description: Business identifier for the FLISR event, typically generated by GE PowerOn ADMS. Used for external reference and operational tracking.

attributes.name: flisr_outcome_status
attributes.description: Final outcome classification of the FLISR automation attempt. Full success indicates all restoration actions completed; partial success indicates some customers restored; failed indicates no restoration achieved.

attributes.name: isolation_devices_operated
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of switching device IDs (reclosers, sectionalizers, automated switches) that were operated to isolate the faulted segment. Captures the isolation sequence executed by FLISR.
attributes.references: IEEE C37.2 - Electrical Power System Device Function Numbers

attributes.name: isolation_time_seconds
attributes.description: Elapsed time in seconds from fault detection to completion of fault isolation switching. Subset of total restoration time, measures speed of fault containment.
attributes.references: IEEE 1366 - Electric Power Distribution Reliability Indices

attributes.name: load_transferred_kw
attributes.description: Amount of electrical load in kilowatts transferred to alternate feeders during FLISR restoration. Used for load balancing analysis and feeder capacity validation.

attributes.name: major_event_exclusion_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this FLISR event qualifies for exclusion from reliability indices under IEEE 1366 Major Event Day criteria. True if excluded; false if included in normal reliability calculations.
attributes.references: IEEE 1366 - Electric Power Distribution Reliability Indices

attributes.name: operator_override_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether a human operator intervened to override or abort the automated FLISR sequence. True if operator action occurred; false if fully automated.

attributes.name: puc_reportable_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this FLISR event meets the threshold criteria for mandatory reporting to the state Public Utility Commission. True if reportable; false otherwise.

attributes.name: record_created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this FLISR event record was first created in the data system. Used for data lineage and audit trail.

attributes.name: record_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this FLISR event record was last modified in the data system. Used for data lineage and audit trail.

attributes.name: restoration_devices_operated
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of switching device IDs operated to restore service to de-energized segments downstream of the fault. Captures the restoration switching sequence executed by FLISR.
attributes.references: IEEE C37.2 - Electrical Power System Device Function Numbers

attributes.name: restoration_time_seconds
attributes.description: Elapsed time in seconds from fault detection to completion of FLISR restoration switching sequence. Critical metric for CAIDI calculation and FLISR performance benchmarking.
attributes.references: IEEE 1366 - Electric Power Distribution Reliability Indices

attributes.name: saidi_contribution_minutes
attributes.business_glossary_term: System Average Interruption Duration Index (SAIDI) Contribution in Minutes
attributes.description: Calculated contribution of this FLISR event to the SAIDI reliability index, in customer-minutes. Computed as (customers affected × duration) / total customers served. Critical for PUC reliability reporting.
attributes.references: IEEE 1366 - Electric Power Distribution Reliability Indices

attributes.name: saifi_contribution
attributes.business_glossary_term: System Average Interruption Frequency Index (SAIFI) Contribution
attributes.description: Calculated contribution of this FLISR event to the SAIFI reliability index. Computed as customers affected / total customers served. Critical for PUC reliability reporting.
attributes.references: IEEE 1366 - Electric Power Distribution Reliability Indices

attributes.name: scada_alarm_count
attributes.business_glossary_term: Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) Alarm Count
attributes.description: Number of SCADA alarms generated during the FLISR event. High alarm counts may indicate cascading issues or communication problems.

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: Identifier of the source system that generated this FLISR event record, typically GE PowerOn ADMS. Used for data lineage and multi-system integration scenarios.

attributes.name: switching_operations_count
attributes.description: Total number of switching device operations (open/close commands) executed during the FLISR sequence. Used for device wear analysis and maintenance planning.
attributes.references: IEEE C37.2 - Electrical Power System Device Function Numbers

attributes.name: topology_validation_status
attributes.description: Status of network topology validation performed by ADMS before executing FLISR switching. Invalid topology may prevent or abort FLISR automation.
attributes.references: Esri ArcGIS Utility Network - Network Topology

attributes.name: triggering_fault_indicator_code
attributes.description: Identifier of the fault indicator device (FCI or FPI) that detected the fault condition and triggered the FLISR automation sequence. Links to SCADA point or asset registry.
attributes.references: IEEE C37.2 - Electrical Power System Device Function Numbers

attributes.name: voltage_sag_percent
attributes.description: Percentage voltage drop observed during the fault condition, relative to nominal voltage. Indicates severity of power quality disturbance.

attributes.name: weather_condition
attributes.description: Prevailing weather condition at the time of the FLISR event, if available from weather data integration. Used for fault cause correlation and storm impact analysis. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: clear|rain|snow|ice|wind|lightning|fog|extreme_heat — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: NOAA - National Weather Service Data Standards

products.name: volt_var_action
products.description: Transactional record for Volt-VAR Optimization (VVO) control actions executed by GE PowerOn ADMS on the distribution network. Captures action timestamp, control zone, device operated (capacitor bank, voltage regulator, LTC transformer), setpoint before and after, voltage profile improvement (pu), reactive power reduction (MVAr), energy loss reduction (kWh), optimization objective (conservation voltage reduction/power factor correction), and execution mode (automatic/manual). SSOT for VVO operational action history. Supports CVR program performance measurement and energy loss reduction reporting.
products.reference: GE PowerOn ADMS Volt-VAR Optimization / IEC 61968

attributes.name: volt_var_action_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the Volt-VAR Optimization control action record. Primary key.

attributes.name: distribution_substation_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the distribution substation serving the control zone where the action occurred.
attributes.references: Esri ArcGIS Utility Network - Substation Registry

attributes.name: employee_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the system operator who initiated or approved the VVO action (for manual or advisory modes). Null for fully automatic actions.

attributes.name: feeder_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the distribution feeder circuit on which the VVO action was performed.
attributes.references: Esri ArcGIS Utility Network - Feeder Configuration

attributes.name: load_zone_id
attributes.description: FK to distribution.load_zone.load_zone_id — VVO actions are executed within a control zone. The description mentions 'control zone'. Critical for volt-VAR optimization tracking.

attributes.name: volt_load_zone_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the distribution control zone where the VVO action was executed. Links to the geographic/electrical zone managed by ADMS.
attributes.references: GE PowerOn ADMS - Control Zone Configuration

attributes.name: volt_var_device_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier of the distribution device operated during this action (capacitor bank, voltage regulator, LTC transformer, or other VVO-capable device).
attributes.references: Esri ArcGIS Utility Network - Asset Registry

attributes.name: volt_vvo_action_in_zone
attributes.description: FK to distribution.load_zone.load_zone_id — VVO actions are dispatched per control zone. This FK links operational actions to the load zone they optimize, supporting CVR program performance measurement by zone.

attributes.name: volt_vvo_action_targets_zone
attributes.description: FK to distribution.load_zone.load_zone_id — VVO control actions are dispatched per control zone. The load_zone FK identifies which zone the optimization action targets, enabling zone-level VVO performance analysis.

attributes.name: action_status
attributes.description: Outcome status of the VVO action execution: successful, failed, partial (some devices operated), aborted (cancelled mid-execution), or pending.
attributes.references: GE PowerOn ADMS - Action Status Codes

attributes.name: action_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the VVO control action was executed on the distribution network. Principal business event timestamp for this transaction.

attributes.name: action_type
attributes.description: Classification of the VVO action: voltage regulation, reactive power compensation, power factor correction, Conservation Voltage Reduction (CVR), energy loss reduction, or combined optimization.
attributes.references: IEEE 1547.8 - Recommended Practice for Establishing Methods and Procedures for VVO

attributes.name: affected_customer_count
attributes.description: Number of customer premises affected by the VVO action within the control zone.
attributes.references: GE PowerOn ADMS - Customer Impact Analysis

attributes.name: approval_required_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether operator approval was required before executing this VVO action (True/False).
attributes.references: GE PowerOn ADMS - Approval Workflow Configuration

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this VVO action record was first created in the system. Audit trail field.

attributes.name: cvr_factor
attributes.description: CVR factor achieved by the action: ratio of percent change in demand to percent change in voltage. Typical range 0.5 to 1.5.

attributes.name: demand_reduction_kw
attributes.description: Peak demand reduction achieved by the VVO action (typically through CVR), measured in kilowatts (kW).

attributes.name: der_active_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether Distributed Energy Resources (solar, wind, storage) were actively generating/discharging in the control zone during the VVO action (True/False).

attributes.name: der_impact_mw
attributes.description: Estimated impact of DER generation/discharge on the VVO optimization, measured in megawatts (MW). Null if no DER active.

attributes.name: device_name
attributes.description: Human-readable name or label of the device operated (e.g., 'CAP-BANK-12A-01', 'REG-SUBSTATION-5').

attributes.name: device_type
attributes.description: Type of distribution device operated: capacitor bank, voltage regulator, Load Tap Changer (LTC) transformer, switched capacitor, static VAR compensator, or other VVO-capable equipment.
attributes.references: IEEE C57.15 - Requirements for Load Tap Changers

attributes.name: energy_loss_reduction_kwh
attributes.description: Estimated energy loss reduction achieved by the VVO action over the optimization period, measured in kilowatt-hours (kWh).

attributes.name: execution_duration_seconds
attributes.description: Time taken to execute the VVO action from command initiation to device confirmation, measured in seconds.
attributes.references: GE PowerOn ADMS - Action Execution Metrics

attributes.name: execution_mode
attributes.description: Mode in which the VVO action was executed: automatic (ADMS-initiated), manual (operator-initiated), scheduled (pre-planned), or advisory (recommended but not executed).
attributes.references: GE PowerOn ADMS - Execution Mode Configuration

attributes.name: load_level
attributes.description: Distribution load level at the time of the VVO action: light, medium, heavy, or peak. Used for optimization performance analysis.

attributes.name: optimization_duration_seconds
attributes.description: Time duration over which the VVO optimization was calculated and applied, measured in seconds.
attributes.references: GE PowerOn ADMS - Optimization Cycle Configuration

attributes.name: optimization_objective
attributes.description: Primary objective of the VVO action: Conservation Voltage Reduction (CVR), power factor correction, loss minimization, voltage profile improvement, peak demand reduction, or multi-objective optimization.

attributes.name: power_factor_after
attributes.description: Power factor in the control zone after the VVO action (ratio of real power to apparent power, range 0.0 to 1.0).

attributes.name: power_factor_before
attributes.description: Power factor in the control zone before the VVO action (ratio of real power to apparent power, range 0.0 to 1.0).

attributes.name: power_factor_improvement
attributes.description: Improvement in power factor achieved by the VVO action. Positive value indicates power factor increased (closer to unity).

attributes.name: reactive_power_after_mvar
attributes.description: Reactive power flow in the control zone after the VVO action, measured in Megavolt-Amperes Reactive (MVAr).

attributes.name: reactive_power_before_mvar
attributes.description: Reactive power flow in the control zone before the VVO action, measured in Megavolt-Amperes Reactive (MVAr).

attributes.name: reactive_power_reduction_mvar
attributes.description: Reduction in reactive power flow achieved by the VVO action, measured in MVAr. Positive value indicates successful VAR reduction.

attributes.name: scada_command_code
attributes.business_glossary_term: Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) Command ID
attributes.description: SCADA system command identifier that initiated the device operation. Links to SCADA command log.

attributes.name: setpoint_after
attributes.description: Device setpoint value after the VVO action was executed. Units depend on device type.

attributes.name: setpoint_before
attributes.description: Device setpoint value before the VVO action (tap position for LTC/regulator, switch state for capacitor, VAR output for SVC). Units depend on device type.

attributes.name: setpoint_unit
attributes.description: Unit of measure for the setpoint values: tap position (integer), switch state (on/off), MVAr, kVAr, percent, or per-unit (pu).

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: Name of the source system that generated this VVO action record (e.g., 'GE PowerOn ADMS', 'OSIsoft PI', 'Manual Entry').

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this VVO action record was last updated. Audit trail field.

attributes.name: violation_description
attributes.description: Description of any voltage or operational violations detected (e.g., 'Voltage exceeded upper limit at node XYZ', 'Device operation count exceeded daily limit'). Null if no violations.

attributes.name: violation_detected_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether any voltage or operational violations were detected during or after the VVO action (True/False).

attributes.name: voltage_after_pu
attributes.description: Average voltage profile in the control zone after the VVO action, measured in per-unit (pu) relative to nominal voltage.

attributes.name: voltage_before_pu
attributes.description: Average voltage profile in the control zone before the VVO action, measured in per-unit (pu) relative to nominal voltage.

attributes.name: voltage_improvement_pu
attributes.description: Change in voltage profile achieved by the VVO action, measured in per-unit (pu). Positive value indicates voltage increase, negative indicates reduction (CVR).

attributes.name: weather_condition
attributes.description: Weather condition at the time of the VVO action (e.g., 'clear', 'rain', 'snow', 'high_wind'). Used for performance correlation analysis.

products.name: capacitor_bank
products.description: Master record for shunt capacitor banks installed on the distribution network for reactive power compensation and voltage support. Captures bank identifier, rated kVAr, voltage rating, number of steps, switching type (fixed/switched/automated), control mode (time/voltage/VAr/temperature), GIS location, feeder and phase assignment, SCADA point reference, installation date, and operational status. Managed through GE PowerOn ADMS for volt-VAR optimization.
products.reference: IEC CIM ShuntCompensator / GE PowerOn ADMS VVO Device

attributes.name: distribution_substation_id

attributes.name: feeder_id

attributes.description: Foreign key linking to supply.material_master. Business justification: Capacitor banks are procured volt-var control equipment requiring material master linkage for maintenance parts planning, replacement cost tracking, and equipment standardization. Supports power quali

attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.nerc_cip_asset. Business justification: SCADA-controlled capacitor banks in substations can be BES Cyber Assets requiring CIP compliance when they impact BES reliability. The scada_point_id and volt_var_optimization_enabled attributes indic

attributes.description: SCADA system telemetry point reference for real-time monitoring and remote control of the capacitor bank through the Distribution Management System (DMS) or Advanced Distribution Management System (ADMS).

attributes.name: technician_employee_id

attributes.name: acquisition_cost

attributes.name: ambient_temperature_rating_c

attributes.name: asset_condition_score

attributes.name: bank_name

attributes.name: bank_number

attributes.name: control_voltage_v

attributes.name: created_timestamp

attributes.name: latitude

attributes.name: longitude

attributes.name: notes

attributes.description: Identifier of the distribution substation that serves the feeder on which this device is located. Used for hierarchical network modeling and regional voltage management strategies.

attributes.name: fixed_asset_id

attributes.name: material_master_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to supply.material_master. Business justification: Voltage regulators and reactive power devices are physical assets requiring material master linkage for procurement tracking, spare parts management, lifecycle costing, and equipment standardization.

attributes.name: asset_criticality
attributes.description: Risk-based classification of the device importance to grid reliability and customer service. Critical devices serve large customer populations or critical infrastructure, high criticality devices impact significant load, medium and low criticality devices have localized impact. Used for maintenance prioritization and spare parts stocking.

attributes.name: bandwidth_voltage_kv
attributes.description: Voltage deadband or tolerance range within which the device will not initiate tap changes or switching operations, expressed in kilovolts. Prevents excessive switching due to minor voltage fluctuations. Typical values are 1.0 to 2.0 kV.

attributes.name: commissioning_date
attributes.description: Date when the device was tested, verified, and placed into active service. May differ from installation date if testing and acceptance procedures span multiple days. Used for warranty start date and performance baseline establishment.

attributes.name: communication_protocol
attributes.description: Communication protocol used for SCADA integration and remote control. DNP3 and Modbus are legacy protocols, IEC 61850 is the modern standard for substation automation, proprietary protocols are vendor-specific, and none indicates no remote communication capability.

attributes.name: control_mode
attributes.description: Operating control strategy for the volt-VAR device. Time-based uses scheduled switching, voltage-based responds to local voltage measurements, VAR-based responds to reactive power flow, temperature-based adjusts for ambient conditions, bandwidth control maintains voltage within a deadband, and remote SCADA enables centralized dispatch from ADMS.
attributes.references: IEEE 1547.8 Recommended Practice for Establishing Methods and Procedures

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this volt-VAR device record was first created in the system. Used for data lineage, audit trails, and record lifecycle tracking.

attributes.name: cvr_enabled_flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator of whether this device participates in conservation voltage reduction programs that intentionally lower distribution voltage to reduce energy consumption. True indicates the device is included in CVR dispatch strategies, false indicates exclusion from CVR operations.
attributes.references: IEEE 1547.8 Recommended Practice for Establishing Methods and Procedures

attributes.name: device_identifier
attributes.description: Externally-known unique identifier for the volt-VAR device, typically assigned by the utility and used in SCADA systems, field operations, and ADMS integration. May be asset tag, equipment number, or SCADA point reference.

attributes.name: device_name
attributes.description: Human-readable name or label for the volt-VAR device, often including location or feeder reference for operational identification.

attributes.name: device_type
attributes.description: Classification of the volt-VAR device by technology and function. Capacitor banks provide reactive power support, step regulators adjust voltage levels, LTC (Load Tap Changer) transformers provide dynamic voltage control, static VAR compensators offer fast reactive power injection, and synchronous condensers provide rotating reactive power reserves.

attributes.name: expected_useful_life_years
attributes.description: Estimated operational lifespan of the device in years, based on manufacturer specifications and utility experience. Used for depreciation schedules, capital planning, and asset replacement forecasting.

attributes.name: gis_feature_code
attributes.description: Unique identifier linking this volt-VAR device to its corresponding feature in the utility GIS system (Esri ArcGIS Utility Network). Enables spatial queries, network tracing, and integration between ADMS and GIS for topology-aware VVO.

attributes.name: installation_date
attributes.description: Date when the volt-VAR device was installed and commissioned on the distribution network. Used for age-based maintenance scheduling, depreciation calculations, and asset replacement planning.

attributes.name: last_maintenance_date
attributes.description: Date of the most recent preventive or corrective maintenance activity performed on the device. Used for maintenance interval tracking and reliability analysis.

attributes.name: last_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to this device record. Used for change tracking, data quality monitoring, and synchronization with upstream systems.

attributes.name: latitude
attributes.description: Geographic latitude coordinate of the device installation location in decimal degrees. Used for GIS mapping, spatial analysis, outage visualization, and field crew dispatch.

attributes.name: longitude
attributes.description: Geographic longitude coordinate of the device installation location in decimal degrees. Used for GIS mapping, spatial analysis, outage visualization, and field crew dispatch.

attributes.name: next_maintenance_date
attributes.description: Scheduled date for the next planned maintenance activity. Derived from maintenance plan intervals and last maintenance date. Used for work order generation and resource planning.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-form text field for operational notes, special instructions, configuration details, or historical context relevant to the device. Used by field crews, engineers, and operations staff for knowledge capture.

attributes.name: number_of_steps
attributes.description: Total number of discrete tap positions or switching steps available on the device. For step regulators and LTCs, this defines the granularity of voltage adjustment. Typical values range from 16 to 33 steps. For capacitor banks, this represents the number of switchable stages.

attributes.name: operational_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the volt-VAR device indicating availability for grid operations. In-service devices are actively controlled by VVO algorithms, out-of-service devices are temporarily unavailable, maintenance indicates scheduled work, testing indicates commissioning or validation, retired indicates permanent removal, and standby indicates reserve capacity.

attributes.name: ownership_type
attributes.description: Classification of asset ownership. Utility-owned devices are capitalized on the utility balance sheet, customer-owned devices (behind-the-meter DER) are not, third-party-owned devices may be under PPA or service agreements, and leased devices have specific accounting treatment.

attributes.name: phase_configuration
attributes.description: Electrical phase assignment of the volt-VAR device on the distribution circuit. Three-phase devices serve balanced loads, single-phase devices serve lateral taps, and two-phase devices serve open-wye or open-delta configurations. Critical for unbalanced load flow analysis. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: three_phase|single_phase_a|single_phase_b|single_phase_c|two_phase_ab|two_phase_bc|two_phase_ac — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: rated_capacity_kva
attributes.description: Nameplate apparent power capacity of the device in kilovolt-amperes (kVA). Applicable primarily to voltage regulators and LTC transformers. Used for thermal loading calculations and capacity planning.

attributes.name: rated_capacity_kvar
attributes.description: Nameplate reactive power capacity of the device in kilovolt-amperes reactive (kVAr). For capacitor banks, this is the total reactive power injection capability. For regulators and LTCs, this represents the maximum reactive power handling capability. Critical for VVO optimization calculations and grid planning.
attributes.references: IEEE 18 Standard for Shunt Power Capacitors

attributes.name: remote_control_enabled_flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator of whether the device can be operated remotely via SCADA or ADMS. True indicates remote control capability is active, false indicates local-only or manual operation. Critical for FLISR automation and real-time grid optimization.
attributes.references: IEC 61850 Communication Networks and Systems Standard

attributes.name: scada_point_reference
attributes.business_glossary_term: SCADA (Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition) Point Reference
attributes.description: SCADA system tag or point identifier used to monitor and control this device in real-time. Links the device to telemetry streams for voltage, current, tap position, and switch status. Essential for ADMS integration and remote operations.
attributes.references: IEC 61850 Communication Networks and Systems Standard

attributes.name: serial_number
attributes.description: Unique serial number assigned by the manufacturer to this specific device unit. Used for warranty claims, maintenance history tracking, and asset lifecycle management.

attributes.name: switching_type
attributes.description: Switching capability classification. Fixed devices are permanently connected, switched devices can be manually operated, and automated devices support remote control via SCADA or ADMS for real-time VVO and FLISR operations.

attributes.name: tap_range_percent
attributes.description: Total voltage adjustment range available through tap changing, expressed as a percentage of nominal voltage. Typical ranges are ±10% or ±5%. Used by VVO algorithms to determine available voltage control authority.

attributes.name: time_delay_seconds
attributes.description: Intentional delay period before the device responds to a control signal or voltage deviation, expressed in seconds. Prevents nuisance operations during transient conditions. Typical values range from 15 to 120 seconds.
attributes.references: IEEE 1547.8 Recommended Practice for Establishing Methods and Procedures

attributes.name: voltage_rating_kv
attributes.description: Nominal voltage level at which the device operates, expressed in kilovolts (kV). Typical distribution voltages include 4.16, 12.47, 13.2, 13.8, 23, 34.5 kV. Essential for network topology modeling and voltage compliance verification per ANSI C84.1.

attributes.name: voltage_setpoint_kv
attributes.description: Target voltage level that the device is configured to maintain, expressed in kilovolts. For voltage regulators and LTCs, this is the desired output voltage. For capacitor banks with voltage control, this is the threshold for switching. Updated by VVO optimization and CVR programs.

attributes.name: vvo_enabled_flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator of whether this device is actively participating in automated volt-VAR optimization algorithms executed by the ADMS. True indicates the device accepts remote control commands for voltage and reactive power management, false indicates manual-only operation.
attributes.references: IEEE 1547.8 Recommended Practice for Establishing Methods and Procedures

attributes.name: warranty_expiration_date
attributes.description: Date when the manufacturer warranty coverage ends. Used for maintenance cost forecasting and replacement planning decisions.

products.name: distribution_reliability_event
products.description: Transactional record for distribution reliability interruption events used to calculate IEEE 1366 reliability indices (SAIDI, SAIFI, CAIDI, MAIFI) for PUC reporting. Captures event identifier, event type (sustained/momentary/planned), cause code per IEEE 1366 Appendix (equipment failure/weather/animal/vegetation/scheduled/unknown), affected feeder and segment, number of customers interrupted, customer-minutes interrupted (CMI), event start and restoration timestamps, duration (minutes), major event day (MED) threshold flag, and IEEE 1366 2.5-beta exclusion flag. SSOT for PUC reliability reporting and IEEE 1366 index calculation. Supports annual reliability filings, worst-performing feeder analysis, and reliability improvement program tracking.
products.reference: IEEE 1366 / PUC Reliability Reporting / GE PowerOn OMS

attributes.name: distribution_reliability_event_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the distribution reliability interruption event. Primary key for IEEE 1366 reliability index calculation and PUC reporting.

attributes.name: distribution_substation_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the distribution substation serving the affected feeder. Used for substation-level reliability aggregation and asset performance correlation.

attributes.name: emergency_stock_event_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to supply.emergency_stock_event. Business justification: Major reliability events (storms, cascading failures) trigger emergency material deployment for restoration. Links outage events to emergency stock for cost allocation, FEMA reimbursement tracking, re

attributes.name: ems_alarm_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to grid.ems_alarm. Business justification: Distribution reliability events generate EMS alarms for grid operator awareness during major outages. Required for integrated outage management systems (OMS-EMS integration) and regulatory SAIDI/SAIFI

attributes.name: feeder_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the distribution feeder (primary circuit) affected by the reliability event. Used for worst-performing feeder analysis and targeted reliability improvement programs.

attributes.name: grid_reliability_event_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to grid.grid_reliability_event. Business justification: Major distribution reliability events escalate to grid-level reliability events for transmission-impacting outages. Required for NERC OE-417 reporting, major event day classification, and integrated r

attributes.name: network_segment_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to distribution.network_segment. Business justification: Reliability events (interruptions) occur on specific network segments. Currently reliability_event has segment_id as STRING, but this should be a proper FK to network_segment.network_segment_id for re

attributes.name: oms_event_id
attributes.description: Source system identifier from the Outage Management System (OMS) or ADMS. Used for cross-system reconciliation and audit trail back to operational systems.

attributes.name: regulatory_filing_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.regulatory_filing. Business justification: Reliability events are aggregated into IEEE 1366 reports and PUC performance filings. The puc_reportable_flag indicates filing requirement; linking events to filings enables automated report generatio

attributes.name: responding_crew_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to workforce.crew. Business justification: Reliability events track which crew responded for performance metrics, labor cost allocation, crew efficiency analysis, and storm restoration reporting. Essential for PUC reporting, mutual aid cost re

attributes.name: scada_alarm_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) Alarm ID
attributes.description: SCADA alarm identifier that triggered the reliability event detection. Used for SCADA integration validation and event correlation.

attributes.name: sectionalizing_device_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the specific protective device that operated during the event. Links to asset registry for device maintenance history and performance tracking.

attributes.name: storm_event_id
attributes.description: Foreign key reference to the storm event record if this reliability event was part of a larger storm or weather system. Enables storm-level reliability aggregation and mutual aid analysis.

attributes.name: cause_code
attributes.description: Root cause classification per IEEE 1366 Appendix categories: equipment failure, weather, animal contact, vegetation, vehicle accident, scheduled maintenance, unknown, or other utility-specific cause codes.

attributes.name: cause_description
attributes.description: Detailed narrative description of the root cause of the reliability event, including specific equipment failures, weather conditions, or external factors.

attributes.name: crew_arrival_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when field crew arrived at the fault location. Used to calculate crew travel time and on-site restoration duration.

attributes.name: crew_dispatch_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when field crew was dispatched to investigate and repair the fault. Used to calculate crew response time and restoration performance metrics.

attributes.name: critical_customer_affected_flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator whether any critical customers (hospitals, emergency services, water treatment, etc.) were affected by the interruption. Used for priority restoration and regulatory notification.
attributes.references: GE PowerOn ADMS Critical Customer Management

attributes.name: customer_minutes_interrupted
attributes.description: Total customer-minutes of interruption calculated as customers_interrupted × duration_minutes. Used to calculate SAIDI (System Average Interruption Duration Index) per IEEE 1366.

attributes.name: customers_interrupted
attributes.description: Total number of customer accounts experiencing service interruption during this event. Used to calculate SAIFI (System Average Interruption Frequency Index) per IEEE 1366.

attributes.name: customers_restored_by_flisr
attributes.description: Number of customers automatically restored by FLISR automation without manual crew intervention. Used to quantify FLISR benefit and avoided customer-minutes interrupted.

attributes.name: data_source_system
attributes.description: Name of the operational system that originated this reliability event record (e.g., GE PowerOn ADMS, OSIsoft PI, SAP IS-U). Used for data lineage and source system reconciliation.

attributes.name: duration_minutes
attributes.description: Total duration of the interruption event in minutes, calculated as the difference between restoration_timestamp and event_start_timestamp. Used for IEEE 1366 sustained vs. momentary classification.

attributes.name: energy_not_served_mwh
attributes.description: Total energy not delivered to customers in megawatt-hours (MWh) due to the interruption, calculated as load_interrupted_mw × duration_hours. Used for economic impact analysis and PUC reporting.

attributes.name: equipment_age_years
attributes.description: Age in years of the failed equipment at the time of the event. Used for asset health correlation and age-based replacement program justification.

attributes.name: equipment_failed
attributes.description: Type of distribution equipment that failed and caused the interruption (e.g., transformer, conductor, insulator, pole, underground cable). Used for asset failure analysis and replacement prioritization.

attributes.name: estimated_restoration_time
attributes.description: Initial estimated time of restoration communicated to customers and regulators when the event began. Used to measure ERT accuracy and customer communication effectiveness.

attributes.name: event_number
attributes.description: Business identifier for the reliability event, typically generated by the Outage Management System (OMS) or Advanced Distribution Management System (ADMS). Used for external reporting and cross-system correlation.

attributes.name: event_start_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the reliability event began (first customer interruption detected). Captured from SCADA, AMI, or customer call-in data via OMS/ADMS.

attributes.name: event_type
attributes.description: Classification of the interruption event per IEEE 1366 definitions: sustained (>5 minutes), momentary (≤5 minutes), or planned (scheduled maintenance outage).

attributes.name: exclusion_reason
attributes.description: Detailed explanation of why the event is excluded from IEEE 1366 reliability index calculations, if ieee_1366_exclusion_flag is true. References specific IEEE 1366 exclusion criteria.

attributes.name: fault_latitude
attributes.description: Geographic latitude coordinate of the fault location in decimal degrees. Used for spatial reliability analysis and vegetation management correlation.

attributes.name: fault_location_description
attributes.description: Textual description of the physical location where the fault occurred (e.g., street address, pole number, landmark). Used for crew dispatch and asset maintenance correlation.

attributes.name: fault_longitude
attributes.description: Geographic longitude coordinate of the fault location in decimal degrees. Used for spatial reliability analysis and vegetation management correlation.

attributes.name: flisr_operated_flag
attributes.business_glossary_term: Fault Location Isolation and Service Restoration (FLISR) Operated Flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator whether FLISR automation successfully operated to isolate the fault and restore service to unaffected customers. Used to measure FLISR effectiveness and MAIFI (Momentary Average Interruption Frequency Index) reduction.

attributes.name: flisr_operation_time_seconds
attributes.description: Time in seconds for FLISR automation to isolate the fault and restore service to unaffected segments. Used to measure FLISR performance and reduction in customer-minutes interrupted.

attributes.name: ieee_1366_exclusion_flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator whether this event should be excluded from IEEE 1366 reliability index calculations per standard exclusion criteria (e.g., loss of supply, prearranged interruption, customer-owned equipment failure).

attributes.name: load_interrupted_mw
attributes.description: Total electrical load in megawatts (MW) interrupted during the event, captured from SCADA or estimated from customer count and load profiles. Used for energy not served (ENS) calculations.

attributes.name: major_event_day_flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator whether this event occurred on a Major Event Day per IEEE 1366 2.5-beta method. Major Event Days are excluded from annual reliability index calculations to prevent catastrophic events from skewing performance metrics.

attributes.name: protective_device_type
attributes.description: Type of protective device that operated to isolate the fault (e.g., recloser, circuit breaker, fuse, sectionalizer). Used for protective device performance analysis and coordination studies.

attributes.name: puc_report_date
attributes.description: Date when the reliability event was reported to the Public Utility Commission, if puc_reportable_flag is true. Used to track regulatory reporting compliance.

attributes.name: puc_reportable_flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator whether this event must be reported to the state Public Utility Commission per regulatory requirements. Typically true for sustained interruptions affecting a threshold number of customers.

attributes.name: record_created_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this reliability event record was first created in the data warehouse. Used for data lineage and audit trail.

attributes.name: record_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this reliability event record was last modified. Used for change tracking and data quality monitoring.

attributes.name: repair_description
attributes.description: Detailed description of the repair work performed by field crew to restore service, including equipment replaced, temporary repairs, or permanent fixes.

attributes.name: restoration_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when service was fully restored to all affected customers. Used to calculate event duration and customer-minutes interrupted.

attributes.name: voltage_level_kv
attributes.description: Nominal voltage level in kilovolts (kV) of the distribution circuit affected by the event (e.g., 12.47, 13.2, 34.5). Used for voltage-class reliability analysis.

attributes.name: weather_condition
attributes.description: Weather conditions at the time of the event (e.g., thunderstorm, ice storm, high winds, lightning, normal). Used for weather-related reliability analysis and correlation with cause codes.

products.name: feeder_load_reading
products.description: Transactional record for interval load measurements at feeder head and key monitoring points on the distribution network, sourced from SCADA/OSIsoft PI historian or similar data historian. Captures reading timestamp, feeder or segment identifier, measurement point type (feeder head/midpoint/tie point), active power (MW), reactive power (MVAr), apparent power (MVA), current (A per phase), voltage (kV per phase), power factor, temperature, and data quality flag. SSOT for distribution-level load telemetry distinct from AMI meter interval data owned by the metering domain. Supports load balancing, capacity planning, peak demand analysis, volt-VAR optimization feedback, and normal/emergency rating calculations.
products.reference: OSIsoft PI Historian / SCADA ICCP / IEC 61968 MDM

attributes.name: feeder_load_reading_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the feeder load reading record. Primary key for this transactional measurement event.

attributes.name: distribution_flisr_event_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: FLISR (Fault Location, Isolation, and Service Restoration) Event ID
attributes.description: Identifier linking this reading to a FLISR automation event if the reading was captured during an automated switching sequence. Null if no FLISR event was active.
attributes.references: GE PowerOn ADMS - FLISR Module; IEEE 1547.4 Islanding Standard

attributes.name: event_id
attributes.description: Identifier linking this reading to an outage event if the reading was captured during or immediately after an outage. Null if no outage was active at reading time.
attributes.references: GE PowerOn ADMS - Outage Management System; OMS Event Registry

attributes.name: load_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to forecast.load. Business justification: Actual feeder load readings must be compared against load forecasts for accuracy measurement and model calibration. Essential for forecast accuracy tracking, MAPE calculation, model validation, and co

attributes.name: measurement_point_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the specific monitoring point on the feeder where the reading was captured (e.g., feeder head, midpoint sensor, tie point). Corresponds to SCADA tag or PI point identifier.
attributes.references: OSIsoft PI - Point Configuration; SCADA Tag Registry

attributes.name: primary_feeder_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the distribution feeder or circuit segment where the load measurement was taken. Links to the feeder asset in the distribution network topology.
attributes.references: GE PowerOn ADMS - Feeder Registry; Esri ArcGIS Utility Network

attributes.name: state_estimation_run_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to grid.state_estimation_run. Business justification: Feeder load measurements provide boundary condition inputs to transmission state estimators for distribution-transmission interface modeling. Essential for accurate voltage/power flow analysis and con

attributes.name: tertiary_feeder_id
attributes.description: FK to distribution.feeder.feeder_id — Feeder load readings are measurements taken at feeder head or monitoring points. The feeder FK is essential for associating readings with the correct feeder for load analysis and capacity planning.

attributes.name: active_power_mw
attributes.description: Real power measured in megawatts (MW) at the monitoring point. Represents the actual power flowing through the feeder segment at the reading timestamp. Used for load balancing and capacity planning.
attributes.references: IEEE 1459 - Power Definitions; NERC MOD Standards

attributes.name: ambient_temperature_celsius
attributes.description: Ambient temperature in degrees Celsius at or near the monitoring point. Used for thermal rating adjustments and equipment derating calculations under high-temperature conditions.
attributes.references: IEEE 738 - Conductor Thermal Rating; NERC FAC Standards

attributes.name: apparent_power_mva
attributes.description: Apparent power measured in megavolt-amperes (MVA) at the monitoring point. Represents the total power (vector sum of active and reactive power) and is used for equipment rating and capacity calculations.
attributes.references: IEEE 1459 - Power Definitions; ANSI C84.1 Voltage Standard

attributes.name: current_phase_a_amperes
attributes.description: Current measured on Phase A conductor in amperes at the monitoring point. Used for load balancing across phases and thermal limit monitoring.
attributes.references: IEEE C37.118 - Synchrophasor Measurements; ANSI C84.1

attributes.name: current_phase_b_amperes
attributes.description: Current measured on Phase B conductor in amperes at the monitoring point. Used for load balancing across phases and thermal limit monitoring.
attributes.references: IEEE C37.118 - Synchrophasor Measurements; ANSI C84.1

attributes.name: current_phase_c_amperes
attributes.description: Current measured on Phase C conductor in amperes at the monitoring point. Used for load balancing across phases and thermal limit monitoring.
attributes.references: IEEE C37.118 - Synchrophasor Measurements; ANSI C84.1

attributes.name: data_quality_flag
attributes.description: Quality indicator for the reading. Good indicates validated data; suspect indicates data outside normal range but not rejected; bad indicates failed validation; estimated indicates imputed value; missing indicates no data received. Aligns with VEE (Validation, Estimation, and Editing) processes.
attributes.references: OSIsoft PI - Data Quality Attributes; Oracle Utilities MDM VEE Rules

attributes.name: data_retention_category
attributes.description: Classification determining the retention period for this reading. Operational (1-2 years); regulatory (5-7 years per FERC/PUC requirements); historical (10+ years for trend analysis); archive (permanent retention for critical events).
attributes.references: FERC Data Retention Requirements; State PUC Regulations; SOX Compliance

attributes.name: data_source_type
attributes.description: Classification of the data acquisition method. SCADA realtime indicates live telemetry; historian archive indicates retrieved from PI or similar historian; manual entry indicates operator-entered value; estimated indicates calculated/imputed value.
attributes.references: OSIsoft PI - Data Source Classification; Data Governance Standards

attributes.name: der_generation_flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator (True/False) denoting whether DER generation (solar, wind, battery storage) was active on this feeder segment at the time of reading. Used for DER impact analysis and reverse power flow detection.
attributes.references: IEEE 1547 - DER Interconnection; DERMS Integration Standards

attributes.name: emergency_rating_mva
attributes.description: Emergency short-term thermal rating of the feeder segment in MVA. Represents the maximum load that can be carried for a limited duration (typically 15 minutes to 4 hours) during contingency conditions.
attributes.references: IEEE 738 - Conductor Thermal Rating; NERC FAC-008 Facility Ratings

attributes.name: estimation_method
attributes.description: Method used to estimate the reading value if actual data was missing or invalid. None indicates no estimation was performed; other values indicate the specific estimation algorithm applied per MDM VEE rules.
attributes.references: Oracle Utilities MDM - VEE Estimation Rules; Industry Best Practices

attributes.name: frequency_hz
attributes.description: System frequency measured in hertz at the monitoring point. Nominal value is 60 Hz in North America; deviations indicate grid stability issues and are monitored per NERC reliability standards.
attributes.references: NERC BAL Standards; IEEE C37.118 Synchrophasor Standard

attributes.name: loading_percentage
attributes.description: Percentage of normal rating currently being utilized, calculated as (apparent_power_mva / normal_rating_mva) * 100. Key metric for capacity planning and identifying overloaded feeders.
attributes.references: NERC MOD Standards; Utility Capacity Planning Guidelines

attributes.name: measurement_point_type
attributes.description: Classification of the monitoring location on the distribution network. Feeder head represents the substation exit point; midpoint and tie point represent intermediate monitoring locations; recloser, capacitor bank, and regulator represent device-level monitoring points.
attributes.references: GE PowerOn ADMS - Network Topology Model; IEEE 1547 DER Interconnection Standard

attributes.name: normal_rating_mva
attributes.description: Normal continuous thermal rating of the feeder segment in MVA under standard ambient conditions. Used to calculate loading percentage and identify overload conditions.
attributes.references: IEEE 738 - Conductor Thermal Rating; NERC FAC-008 Facility Ratings

attributes.name: peak_demand_flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator (True/False) denoting whether this reading occurred during a system peak demand period. Used for peak demand analysis and capacity planning studies.
attributes.references: Utility Load Forecasting Standards; PUC Peak Demand Reporting

attributes.name: pi_point_name
attributes.description: OSIsoft PI point tag name or equivalent historian tag identifier for this measurement. Provides traceability back to the source SCADA tag in the historian system.
attributes.references: OSIsoft PI - Tag Naming Convention; SCADA Integration Standards

attributes.name: power_factor
attributes.description: Ratio of active power to apparent power (dimensionless, range -1.0 to +1.0). Indicates the efficiency of power delivery and is a key input for volt-VAR optimization and capacitor bank control.
attributes.references: IEEE 1459 - Power Definitions; Utility Tariff Power Factor Requirements

attributes.name: reactive_power_mvar
attributes.description: Reactive power measured in megavolt-amperes reactive (MVAr) at the monitoring point. Critical for volt-VAR optimization and power factor management on the distribution network.
attributes.references: IEEE 1459 - Power Definitions; NERC VAR Standards

attributes.name: reading_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the load measurement was recorded by the SCADA system or data historian. Represents the actual event time of the observation, distinct from record creation time.
attributes.references: OSIsoft PI - Event Timestamp; IEEE C37.118 Synchrophasor Standard

attributes.name: record_created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this record was first inserted into the lakehouse silver layer. Distinct from reading_timestamp which represents the actual measurement event time. Used for data lineage and audit trail.
attributes.references: Data Governance - Audit Trail Standards; Databricks Lakehouse Best Practices

attributes.name: record_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this record was last modified in the lakehouse silver layer. Updated when VEE processes revise data quality flags or estimation values. Used for change tracking and audit trail.
attributes.references: Data Governance - Audit Trail Standards; Databricks Lakehouse Best Practices

attributes.name: reverse_power_flow_flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator (True/False) denoting whether power was flowing in the reverse direction (from customer premises back to substation) at the time of reading. Indicates high DER penetration or net export conditions.
attributes.references: IEEE 1547 - DER Interconnection; Distribution Grid Modernization Standards

attributes.name: scada_source_system
attributes.business_glossary_term: SCADA (Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition) Source System
attributes.description: Name or identifier of the SCADA system or data historian that originated this reading (e.g., OSIsoft PI, GE iFIX, Schneider ClearSCADA). Used for data lineage and troubleshooting.
attributes.references: OSIsoft PI - System Configuration; GE PowerOn ADMS Integration

attributes.name: validation_status
attributes.description: Status of the VEE (Validation, Estimation, and Editing) process for this reading. Validated indicates the reading passed all quality checks; pending indicates awaiting validation; failed indicates rejected by validation rules; bypassed indicates validation was skipped.
attributes.references: Oracle Utilities MDM - VEE Engine; NERC Data Quality Standards

attributes.name: voltage_phase_a_kv
attributes.description: Voltage measured on Phase A in kilovolts at the monitoring point. Critical for voltage regulation and ANSI C84.1 compliance monitoring.
attributes.references: ANSI C84.1 - Voltage Ratings; IEEE 1547 DER Standard

attributes.name: voltage_phase_b_kv
attributes.description: Voltage measured on Phase B in kilovolts at the monitoring point. Critical for voltage regulation and ANSI C84.1 compliance monitoring.
attributes.references: ANSI C84.1 - Voltage Ratings; IEEE 1547 DER Standard

attributes.name: voltage_phase_c_kv
attributes.description: Voltage measured on Phase C in kilovolts at the monitoring point. Critical for voltage regulation and ANSI C84.1 compliance monitoring.
attributes.references: ANSI C84.1 - Voltage Ratings; IEEE 1547 DER Standard

attributes.name: weather_condition
attributes.description: General weather condition at the time of reading. Used for correlating load patterns with weather events and for storm impact analysis. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: clear|cloudy|rain|snow|storm|extreme_heat|extreme_cold — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: NOAA Weather Data Integration; Utility Weather Analytics

products.name: der_interconnection_point
products.description: Master record for the physical point of interconnection (POI) where a Distributed Energy Resource connects to the distribution network. Captures POI identifier, DER type (solar PV/battery/EV charger/CHP/wind), nameplate capacity (kW), inverter type and settings, interconnection voltage level, feeder and segment assignment, GIS location, NEM eligibility, anti-islanding protection scheme, DERMS reference, IEEE 1547 compliance status, and interconnection agreement status. SSOT for DER physical connection points on the distribution network. Supports hosting capacity analysis, DERMS integration, reverse power flow monitoring, and state interconnection rule compliance (e.g., Rule 21, SB 700).
products.reference: IEEE 1547 / IEC CIM PowerElectronicsConnection / DERMS POI

attributes.name: der_interconnection_point_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Distributed Energy Resource (DER) Interconnection Point Identifier
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the physical point of interconnection where a DER connects to the distribution network. Primary key for the DER interconnection point master record.

products.name: switching_order_feeder_impact
products.description: This association product represents the operational impact relationship between distribution switching orders and feeders. It captures the specific role, sequence, and operational parameters for each feeder involved in a multi-feeder switching operation. Each record links one distribution switching order to one feeder with attributes that exist only in the context of this switching operation, including load transfer amounts, customer impact counts, isolation status, and restoration priority.. Existence Justification: In utility distribution operations, switching orders routinely coordinate actions across multiple feeders to perform load transfers, isolations, and network reconfigurations. A single switching order can impact 3-5 feeders simultaneously (e.g., isolating one feeder, transferring load to two backup feeders, and energizing a fourth). Conversely, each feeder participates in dozens of switching orders over its operational lifetime for maintenance, emergency response, and load balancing. The relationship carries substantial operational data including load transfer amounts, customer impacts, sequence coordination, and feeder-specific roles.
products.reference: Internal - M:N Association

products.name: feeder_zone_assignment
products.description: This association product represents the operational assignment between distribution feeders and load zones. It captures the many-to-many relationship where a single feeder can serve multiple load zones (feeder branches across zone boundaries) and a single load zone can be served by multiple feeders (for redundancy, load balancing, and reliability). Each record represents an active or historical assignment with load allocation percentages, circuit topology data, and customer distribution metrics used by DMS/ADMS for volt-VAR optimization dispatch and FLISR automation decisions.. Existence Justification: In utility distribution operations, feeders routinely serve multiple load zones as their circuits branch across geographic boundaries, and load zones are deliberately served by multiple feeders for redundancy, load balancing, and reliability. Distribution planners actively manage these assignments through switching operations, network reconfigurations, and seasonal load transfers. This is a core operational relationship tracked in DMS/ADMS systems for real-time control decisions.

products.name: substation_audit_coverage
products.description: This association product represents the audit coverage relationship between distribution substations and compliance audits. It captures which substations were included in which audits, the scope of examination for each substation, findings specific to that substation within the audit, and corrective action status. Each record links one distribution substation to one audit with attributes that exist only in the context of this specific substation-audit examination.. Existence Justification: In energy utilities compliance operations, a single audit (NERC CIP, PUC, EPA) routinely examines multiple distribution substations across the service territory, and each substation is subject to multiple audits over time from different regulatory bodies covering different compliance domains. The business actively manages audit coverage planning, tracks findings per substation per audit, and monitors corrective action status for each substation-audit combination.

products.name: substation_scenario_plan
products.description: This association product represents the planning relationship between distribution substations and IRP scenarios. It captures scenario-specific capacity expansion plans, upgrade schedules, and capital investment forecasts for each substation across different planning futures (base case, high growth, accelerated decarbonization). Each record links one distribution substation to one IRP scenario with year-by-year planning data that exists only in the context of that specific scenario-substation combination. Enables comparison of substation investment needs across alternative futures for regulatory IRP filings.. Existence Justification: In IRP planning, each distribution substation can appear in multiple scenario plans (base case, high growth, accelerated decarbonization), and each IRP scenario models capacity expansion needs for multiple substations across the service territory. Planning teams actively create and manage scenario-specific substation investment plans with year-by-year capacity additions, capital expenditure forecasts, and load projections that vary by scenario assumptions. This is an operational planning relationship, not an analytical correlation.
