attributes.description: Timestamp when this substation scenario plan record was last modified by planning staff.

attributes.name: load_forecast_mw
attributes.description: Forecasted peak load in megawatts (MW) for this substation in this scenario year, reflecting scenario-specific load growth assumptions (electrification, DER penetration, demand response).

attributes.name: plan_status
attributes.description: Lifecycle status of this substation plan within the scenario: draft (initial planning), under_review (stakeholder review), approved (included in final IRP), deferred (postponed to later year), cancelled (no longer needed).

attributes.name: planned_capacity_additions_mva
attributes.description: Planned transformer capacity additions or upgrades for this substation in this scenario year, measured in megavolt-amperes (MVA). Zero if no expansion planned.

attributes.name: planned_transformer_upgrades
attributes.description: Description of planned transformer bank upgrades or replacements for this substation in this scenario (e.g., 'Add third 10MVA transformer', 'Replace aging 33/11kV bank', 'None').

attributes.name: planning_notes
attributes.description: Free-text notes from planning engineers regarding assumptions, constraints, or alternatives considered for this substation in this scenario.

attributes.name: scenario_year
attributes.description: Planning year within the IRP scenario horizon for which this substation plan applies (e.g., 2025, 2030, 2035). Allows year-by-year capacity planning.

products.name: switching_order_material_requisition
products.description: This association product represents the material requisition relationship between distribution switching orders and materials. It captures the specific materials required for each switching operation, including quantities planned, quantities issued from inventory, staging locations, and material returns. Each record links one switching order to one material with attributes that exist only in the context of this specific requisition.. Existence Justification: In utility distribution operations, switching orders routinely require multiple different materials (poles, transformers, conductors, insulators, hardware, protective equipment), and the same materials are used across many different switching orders over time. The business actively manages material requisitions as operational records, tracking planned quantities, actual issuance from inventory, staging locations for crew pickup, and returns of unused materials after job completion.
products.reference: Internal - M:N Association

attributes.name: switching_order_material_requisition_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for this switching order material requisition record. Primary key.

attributes.name: distribution_switching_order_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Switching Order Material Requisition - Distribution Switching Order Id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the distribution switching order that requires this material

attributes.name: issued_by_employee_id
attributes.description: Foreign key reference to the warehouse or inventory employee who issued this material to the field crew. Used for accountability and audit trail.

attributes.name: material_master_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Switching Order Material Requisition - Material Master Id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the material master record for the required material

attributes.name: received_by_employee_id
attributes.description: Foreign key reference to the field crew member who received this material for the switching order. Used for chain of custody tracking.

attributes.name: issue_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this material was issued from inventory for this switching order. Used for inventory transaction tracking and crew logistics.

attributes.name: quantity_issued
attributes.description: Actual quantity of this material issued from inventory to the crew for this switching order. May differ from quantity required due to availability or field adjustments.

attributes.name: quantity_required
attributes.description: Planned quantity of this material required for the switching order, expressed in the material's base unit of measure. Determined during switching order planning phase.

attributes.name: requisition_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of this material requisition. Tracks progression from planning through issuance to return or consumption.

attributes.name: reservation_number
attributes.description: Inventory reservation identifier linking this requisition to the inventory management system. Used to reserve materials prior to physical issuance.

attributes.name: return_quantity
attributes.description: Quantity of this material returned to inventory after switching order completion. Unused materials are returned to maintain accurate inventory levels.

attributes.name: return_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when unused material was returned to inventory after switching order completion. Null if no return occurred.

attributes.name: staging_location
attributes.description: Physical location where this material is staged for pickup by the field crew executing the switching order. May be a warehouse, yard, or field staging area identifier.

attributes.name: unit_of_measure
attributes.description: Unit of measure for quantities in this requisition record. Typically matches the material's base unit of measure but may differ for operational convenience.

products.name: feeder_crew_assignment
products.description: This association product represents the operational assignment of field crews to distribution feeders for maintenance, inspection, vegetation management, and emergency restoration work. It captures the assignment lifecycle, responsibility type (primary maintenance crew, backup crew, vegetation management crew), coverage area within the feeder territory, and assignment dates. Each record links one feeder to one crew with attributes that exist only in the context of this assignment relationship. Critical for dispatch optimization in OMS/ADMS, storm restoration planning, crew workload balancing, and regulatory compliance reporting (vegetation management cycles, inspection frequency).. Existence Justification: In energy utility distribution operations, feeders require maintenance, inspection, and emergency restoration services from multiple specialized crews (line crews for electrical work, vegetation management crews for tree trimming, cable crews for underground sections), and each crew is assigned to multiple feeders within their service territory. The business actively manages these assignments with specific responsibility types (primary/backup), coverage areas, and assignment dates to optimize dispatch routing in OMS/ADMS, ensure regulatory compliance (vegetation management cycles), and coordinate storm restoration efforts. This is an operational assignment process, not an analytical correlation.
products.reference: Internal - M:N Association

attributes.name: feeder_crew_assignment_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for this feeder-crew assignment record. Primary key.

attributes.name: crew_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the field crew assigned to this feeder for maintenance, inspection, or restoration work.

attributes.name: employee_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the user or system process that created this assignment record. Used for audit trail and accountability.

attributes.name: feeder_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the distribution feeder being maintained or served by this crew assignment.

attributes.name: last_modified_by_user_employee_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the user or system process that last modified this assignment record. Used for audit trail.

attributes.name: assignment_end_date
attributes.description: Date when this crew assignment to the feeder ended or is planned to end. Null for active assignments. Used to track assignment lifecycle and crew rotation history.

attributes.name: assignment_start_date
attributes.description: Date when this crew assignment to the feeder became effective. Used to track assignment history and calculate crew tenure on feeder for knowledge continuity.

attributes.name: assignment_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the crew assignment. ACTIVE assignments are operational and used for dispatch. SUSPENDED assignments are temporarily inactive (crew on mutual aid deployment, equipment out of service). ENDED assignments are historical. PLANNED assignments are future-dated for crew rotation planning.

attributes.name: assignment_type
attributes.description: Classification of the crew's responsibility for this feeder. PRIMARY_MAINTENANCE crews handle routine maintenance and are first responders for outages. BACKUP crews provide coverage during peak periods or when primary crew is unavailable. VEGETATION_MANAGEMENT crews handle tree trimming cycles. EMERGENCY_RESTORATION crews are assigned during storm events. Determines dispatch priority and work order routing in OMS/ADMS.

attributes.name: average_response_time_minutes
attributes.description: Historical average time in minutes for this crew to respond to outage calls on this specific feeder, measured from dispatch to arrival. Used for restoration time estimation and crew assignment optimization. Varies by crew-feeder combination due to travel distance and familiarity with feeder topology.

attributes.name: coverage_area_description
attributes.description: Textual description of the geographic coverage area or feeder segments this crew is responsible for within the feeder territory. May reference mile markers, geographic boundaries, or circuit sections. Used when a feeder spans multiple crew territories or when specialized crews handle specific segments (e.g., underground vs overhead sections).

attributes.name: created_date
attributes.description: Timestamp when this assignment record was created in the system. Used for audit trail and data lineage.

attributes.name: dispatch_priority_rank
attributes.description: Numeric ranking for dispatch priority when multiple crews are assigned to the same feeder. Lower numbers indicate higher priority. Used by OMS/ADMS to route emergency work orders to the most appropriate crew based on assignment type, crew location, and current workload.

attributes.name: last_modified_date
attributes.description: Timestamp when this assignment record was last updated. Used for change tracking and data freshness assessment.

attributes.name: last_work_order_date
attributes.description: Date of the most recent work order completed by this crew on this feeder. Used to track crew activity levels, identify underutilized assignments, and ensure regular crew familiarity with feeder infrastructure.

attributes.name: primary_responsibility_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this crew has primary operational responsibility for the feeder (true) or is a backup/secondary assignment (false). Only one crew should have primary responsibility for a feeder at any time for a given assignment type. Used for dispatch routing and accountability.

attributes.name: work_order_count_ytd
attributes.description: Total number of work orders completed by this crew on this feeder in the current calendar year. Used for workload balancing, crew performance assessment, and assignment optimization.

domains.name: metering
domains.description: Advanced metering infrastructure including smart meters, interval data collection, AMI head-end systems, meter reading schedules, VEE (Validation, Estimation, and Editing) processes, TOU and CPP rate programs, and meter asset lifecycle. Manages meter-to-cash data flow, MDM integration via Oracle Utilities MDM, and raw/validated interval data streams feeding billing, demand response, and grid operations domains.
domains.references: ANSI C12.19, IEC 62056, Oracle Utilities MDM

products.name: meter
products.description: Master record for every physical metering device deployed or managed by the utility — smart meters (AMI), interval meters, demand meters, and legacy electromechanical units. Captures device identity (serial number, manufacturer, model), firmware version, meter form factor, voltage class, current rating, number of elements, register configuration, seal status, and AMI head-end system assignment. Includes embedded communication module attributes: module type (RF mesh/PLC/cellular), module serial number, MAC/IP address, signal strength baseline, module firmware version, communication protocol, assigned AMI network segment, and module status — supporting independent module replacement tracking without a separate entity. Also captures the active and historical programmed operational configuration: interval length setting (15/30/60 min), TOU rate program assignment, demand reset interval, load profile channels enabled, remote disconnect/reconnect capability, and configuration effective dates for versioning. SSOT for meter asset identity, communication endpoint, and device configuration within the metering domain; links to the asset domain for full lifecycle management.
products.reference: Oracle Utilities MDM — Device Master

attributes.name: meter_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the physical metering device. Primary key for the meter entity. System-of-record: Oracle Utilities MDM meter object.

attributes.name: fixed_asset_id

attributes.name: meter_ami_head_end_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to metering.ami_head_end. Business justification: Meters are enrolled in and managed by specific AMI head-end systems. The meter table currently has ami_head_end_system as a STRING attribute, which should be normalized to a FK relationship. This is a

attributes.name: obligation_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.obligation. Business justification: Meters must comply with regulatory obligations for accuracy (ANSI C12.20), testing frequency, certification. Supports compliance tracking, audit evidence, regulatory reporting on meter accuracy progra

attributes.name: to_ami_head_end_id
attributes.description: FK to metering.ami_head_end.ami_head_end_id — Each smart meter is assigned to an AMI head-end system for communication management. Required for data collection scheduling and network management.

attributes.name: tou_rate_program_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to metering.tou_rate_program. Business justification: Meters are configured with specific Time-of-Use (TOU) rate programs that define peak/off-peak periods, CPP event criteria, and interval data requirements. The meter table currently has tou_rate_progra

attributes.name: accuracy_class
attributes.description: ANSI accuracy classification of the meter (e.g., Class 0.2, Class 0.5, Class 1.0, Class 2.0). Lower numbers indicate higher precision. Determines acceptable measurement error tolerance and testing requirements.
attributes.references: ANSI C12.20 - Electricity Meters Accuracy Classes

attributes.name: ami_network_segment
attributes.description: Identifier of the AMI communication network segment or cell to which this meter is assigned. Used for network planning, troubleshooting, and load balancing across AMI infrastructure.

attributes.name: communication_module_serial
attributes.description: Unique serial number of the communication module. Tracked separately from meter serial to support independent module replacement without replacing the entire meter. Used for module-level warranty and troubleshooting.

attributes.name: communication_module_type
attributes.description: Technology type of the embedded or attached communication module enabling remote meter reading. RF Mesh uses radio frequency mesh networks; PLC uses power line carrier; Cellular uses mobile networks; Fiber uses optical networks; None for non-communicating meters.

attributes.name: communication_protocol
attributes.description: Application-layer protocol used for meter-to-head-end communication (e.g., ANSI C12.22, DLMS/COSEM, SEP 2.0, Modbus). Determines data format, security features, and interoperability with AMI systems.
attributes.references: ANSI C12.22 - Protocol Specification for Interfacing to Data Communication Networks

attributes.name: configuration_effective_date
attributes.description: Date when the current operational configuration (interval length, TOU program, demand reset, channels) became active. Used for configuration versioning and historical data interpretation. Critical for billing accuracy during configuration changes.

attributes.name: configuration_expiration_date
attributes.description: Date when the current operational configuration is scheduled to expire or be replaced. Nullable for open-ended configurations. Used for planned configuration change management and audit trails.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this meter record was first created in the MDM system. Used for data lineage, audit trails, and system integration reconciliation. Distinct from installation date.

attributes.name: current_rating_amps
attributes.description: Maximum continuous current the meter can measure in amperes. Typical values: 100A, 200A, 320A. Used to ensure meter capacity matches service load requirements.

attributes.name: demand_reset_interval_minutes
attributes.description: Programmed interval in minutes for resetting the demand register (e.g., 15, 30 minutes). Determines how frequently peak demand is calculated and recorded. Critical for demand billing accuracy.
attributes.references: ANSI C12.19 - Utility Industry End Device Data Tables

attributes.name: disconnect_switch_status
attributes.description: Current position of the remote disconnect switch for meters with disconnect capability. Connected indicates service is on; Disconnected indicates service is off; Armed indicates ready for remote command; Not Applicable for meters without disconnect.
attributes.references: ANSI C12.19 - Utility Industry End Device Data Tables

attributes.name: firmware_version
attributes.description: Version identifier of the embedded software running on the meter device. Critical for security patching, feature enablement, and compatibility with head-end systems. Tracked for firmware upgrade campaigns.

attributes.name: form
attributes.description: ANSI form designation describing the physical configuration and wiring arrangement of the meter (e.g., Form 2S, Form 12S, Form 16S). Determines socket compatibility and installation requirements.
attributes.references: ANSI C12.10 - Physical Aspects of Watthour Meters

attributes.name: installation_date
attributes.description: Date the meter was physically installed at its current service location. Used for age tracking, warranty calculations, and lifecycle management. Distinct from manufacturing date.

attributes.name: interval_length_minutes
attributes.description: Programmed interval duration in minutes for load profile data collection (e.g., 15, 30, 60 minutes). Determines granularity of consumption data for billing, demand response, and grid analytics. Configurable parameter tracked for versioning.
attributes.references: ANSI C12.19 - Utility Industry End Device Data Tables

attributes.name: ip_address
attributes.description: Assigned IP address for meters using IP-based communication protocols (cellular, fiber). Used for direct meter communication, remote diagnostics, and firmware updates. Confidential to prevent unauthorized access.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent update to any field in this meter record. Used for change tracking, data synchronization, and audit compliance. Updated automatically on any record modification.

attributes.name: lifecycle_status
attributes.description: Current state of the meter in its asset lifecycle. Installed indicates active deployment; In Stock indicates warehouse inventory; In Transit indicates shipment; Retired indicates end-of-life; Failed indicates defective; Under Test indicates lab testing.

attributes.name: load_profile_channels_enabled
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of load profile channels currently enabled for data collection (e.g., kWh Delivered, kWh Received, kVARh, Voltage, Current). Defines which measurement streams are actively recorded in interval data.
attributes.references: ANSI C12.19 - Utility Industry End Device Data Tables

attributes.name: mac_address
attributes.description: Hardware MAC address of the communication module network interface. Used for network device identification, AMI head-end provisioning, and communication diagnostics. Confidential to prevent network security risks.

attributes.name: manufacturer
attributes.description: Name of the company that manufactured the meter device (e.g., Landis+Gyr, Itron, Sensus, Elster, Aclara). Used for vendor management, warranty tracking, and firmware compatibility.

attributes.name: meter_type
attributes.description: Classification of meter technology and capability level. AMI Smart Meter supports two-way communication and remote operations; Interval Meter records time-series consumption; Demand Meter tracks peak demand; Electromechanical is legacy analog; Electronic is digital non-communicating; Prepaid supports prepayment programs.

attributes.name: model_number
attributes.description: Manufacturer model designation identifying the specific meter product line and capabilities. Used for configuration management, firmware updates, and technical specifications lookup.

attributes.name: module_firmware_version
attributes.description: Version identifier of the firmware running on the communication module, tracked separately from meter firmware. Critical for communication security patches and protocol updates.

attributes.name: module_status
attributes.description: Current operational status of the communication module. Active indicates normal operation; Inactive indicates disabled but functional; Failed indicates hardware failure; Replaced indicates module swap; Not Installed for non-AMI meters.

attributes.name: next_test_due_date
attributes.description: Scheduled date for the next required accuracy test or calibration. Calculated based on regulatory testing intervals (typically 5-15 years depending on meter type and jurisdiction). Used for test planning and compliance tracking.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for operational notes, special handling instructions, field observations, or historical context not captured in structured fields. Used by field technicians and operations staff.

attributes.name: number_of_elements
attributes.description: Count of independent metering elements within the device. Single-phase meters have 1 element; polyphase meters have 2 or 3 elements. Determines measurement capability for multi-phase services.

attributes.name: ownership_status
attributes.description: Legal ownership classification of the meter asset. Utility Owned is standard for most deployments; Customer Owned for customer-purchased meters; Leased for rental arrangements; Third Party for meters owned by service providers.

attributes.name: purchase_order_number
attributes.description: Purchase order number under which this meter was procured. Used for procurement tracking, warranty validation, and vendor management. Links to financial and supply chain systems.

attributes.name: register_configuration
attributes.description: Description of the meter register setup including number of dials, multiplier, and measurement units (kWh, kVARh, kW demand). Defines what consumption data the meter captures and how it is displayed.

attributes.name: remote_disconnect_capable
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether the meter has remote service disconnect/reconnect capability. True enables remote service control for collections, move-in/move-out, and emergency response. False requires manual field operations.
attributes.references: ANSI C12.19 - Utility Industry End Device Data Tables

attributes.name: removal_date
attributes.description: Date the meter was removed from service location. Nullable for currently installed meters. Used for lifecycle tracking, inventory management, and historical service point analysis.

attributes.name: seal_number
attributes.description: Unique identifier of the tamper-evident seal applied to the meter cover. Used to detect unauthorized meter access, tampering, and theft. Recorded during installation and verified during inspections.

attributes.name: seal_status
attributes.description: Current condition of the meter seal. Intact indicates no tampering; Broken indicates potential unauthorized access requiring investigation; Missing indicates seal loss; Not Applicable for meters without seals.

attributes.name: serial_number
attributes.description: Manufacturer-assigned unique serial number physically stamped on the meter device. Used for asset tracking, warranty claims, and field verification. SSOT for device identity.

attributes.name: service_point_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to metering.service_point. Business justification: A service point can host many meters; the many side (meter) gets a foreign key to the parent service_point. This eliminates the siloed service_point table and provides the needed inbound relationship.

attributes.name: signal_strength_baseline_dbm
attributes.description: Baseline communication signal strength measurement in dBm at time of installation or last network optimization. Used to detect communication degradation and plan network improvements. Typical range: -110 to -40 dBm.

attributes.name: test_date
attributes.description: Date of the most recent accuracy test or calibration performed on the meter. Used to track compliance with regulatory testing intervals and identify meters due for testing.

attributes.name: voltage_class
attributes.description: Nominal voltage rating for which the meter is designed and certified. Determines appropriate deployment location (residential 120/240V, commercial 277/480V, primary voltage for large industrial).

attributes.name: warranty_expiration_date
attributes.description: Date when the manufacturer warranty coverage expires. Used for warranty claim eligibility, replacement planning, and total cost of ownership analysis. Nullable if warranty terms are not date-based.

Captures service point identifier, premise address, GPS coordinates, service voltage level, load class (residential, commercial, industrial), distribution feeder and transformer association, network topology node, and AMI network segment. Distinct from the meter device itself: a meter point persists even when meters are swapped. SSOT for the measurement location concept in the metering domain.

attributes.business_glossary_term: Service Point Asset Registry Id (Foreign Key)
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to asset.asset_registry. Business justification: Service points reference physical infrastructure assets (poles, pad-mount equipment, service cabinets) where metering is installed. Field operations, outage restoration, and capital planning require l

attributes.name: cpp_eligible_flag

attributes.name: gps_longitude

attributes.name: interval_data_collection_flag

attributes.name: phase_configuration

attributes.name: rate_schedule_code

attributes.name: service_activation_date

attributes.name: service_address_line1

attributes.name: service_address_line2

attributes.name: service_city

attributes.name: service_point_number

attributes.name: service_point_status

attributes.name: tou_enabled_flag

attributes.name: vee_processing_flag

attributes.description: Indicates whether meter data from this point undergoes VEE processing for data quality assurance before billing and analytics.

products.name: meter_installation
products.description: Tracks the active and historical association between a meter device and a meter point — the physical installation record. Captures installation date, removal date, meter reading at installation (start index), meter reading at removal (end index), installation technician, seal numbers applied, multiplier/CT ratio in effect, and installation status. Enables meter-to-premise traceability for billing, VEE, and regulatory audit. Supports meter swap history and back-billing calculations.
products.reference: SAP IS-U — Device Installation / Oracle Utilities MDM — Installation

attributes.name: billing_end_date
attributes.description: Date when billing ends for this meter installation. Used for final bill calculation and account closure processing.

attributes.name: billing_start_date

attributes.name: created_timestamp

attributes.name: ct_ratio

attributes.name: end_reading
attributes.description: Meter register reading captured at the time of removal. Used to calculate final consumption and validate billing for the installation period.

attributes.name: installation_date
attributes.description: Date when the meter was physically installed at the meter point. Marks the start of the installation period.

attributes.name: installation_notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for technician notes captured during installation. May include site conditions, access issues, or special configuration details.

attributes.name: installation_number
attributes.description: Business identifier for the meter installation record. Used for external reference and work order tracking.

attributes.name: installation_reason_code
attributes.description: Business reason for the meter installation. Used for program tracking, cost allocation, and regulatory reporting.

attributes.name: installation_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the meter installation. Active indicates the meter is currently in service at the meter point.

attributes.name: installation_timestamp
attributes.description: Precise date and time when the meter installation was completed. Used for interval data alignment and VEE (Validation, Estimation, and Editing) processing.

attributes.name: installation_type
attributes.description: Classification of the installation based on its intended duration and purpose. Permanent installations are standard service; temporary installations support construction or events.

attributes.name: meter_location_code
attributes.description: Physical location classification of the meter at the premise. Used for field service routing, safety planning, and AMI (Advanced Metering Infrastructure) signal strength analysis.

attributes.name: multiplier
attributes.description: Multiplier factor applied to meter readings to calculate actual consumption. Used when Current Transformer (CT) or Potential Transformer (PT) ratios are in effect.

attributes.name: phase_configuration
attributes.description: Electrical phase configuration of the service. Single-phase for residential; three-phase for commercial and industrial customers.
attributes.references: IEEE C57.12.00 - General Requirements for Liquid-Immersed Distribution, Power, and Regulating Transformers

attributes.name: pt_ratio
attributes.description: Potential Transformer ratio in effect for this installation (e.g., 7200:120). Used in conjunction with CT ratio for accurate high-voltage metering.

attributes.name: rate_schedule_code
attributes.description: Rate schedule in effect for this meter installation. Determines pricing structure (flat, TOU, CPP) and billing determinants.

attributes.name: reading_uom
attributes.description: Unit of measure for the meter readings. Typically kWh (Kilowatt-Hour) for electric meters, therms or ccf for gas meters. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: kWh|MWh|kW|kVAh|kVArh|therms|ccf|mcf — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: register_count
attributes.description: Number of registers (dials) on the meter. Multi-register meters support TOU (Time of Use) and demand metering programs.

attributes.name: remote_disconnect_capable_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the meter has remote service disconnect/reconnect capability. Used for credit management and demand response programs.

attributes.name: removal_date
attributes.description: Date when the meter was removed from the meter point. Marks the end of the installation period. Null for active installations.

attributes.name: removal_notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for technician notes captured during removal. May include meter condition, seal integrity, or reasons for discrepancies in final readings.

attributes.name: removal_reason_code
attributes.description: Business reason for the meter removal. Used for asset lifecycle tracking, failure analysis, and warranty claims.

attributes.name: removal_timestamp
attributes.description: Precise date and time when the meter was removed. Used for final interval data cutoff and back-billing calculations.

attributes.name: seal_number_1
attributes.description: Primary tamper-evident seal number applied to the meter at installation. Used for security and regulatory audit purposes.

attributes.name: seal_number_2
attributes.description: Secondary tamper-evident seal number applied to the meter at installation. Provides additional security for high-value or critical installations.

attributes.name: service_amperage
attributes.description: Maximum service amperage rating at the meter point in amps. Determines meter sizing and load capacity.
attributes.references: NEC Article 220 - Branch-Circuit, Feeder, and Service Load Calculations

attributes.name: service_voltage
attributes.description: Nominal service voltage at the meter point in volts. Used for meter configuration, safety planning, and load analysis.
attributes.references: ANSI C84.1 - Electric Power Systems and Equipment Voltage Ratings

attributes.name: start_reading
attributes.description: Meter register reading captured at the time of installation. Used as the baseline for consumption calculations during this installation period.

attributes.name: test_date
attributes.description: Date when the meter was last tested for accuracy before or after installation. Used for regulatory compliance and quality assurance.
attributes.references: ANSI C12.1 - Electric Meters Code for Electricity Metering

attributes.name: test_result
attributes.description: Result of the most recent meter accuracy test. Passed indicates the meter meets accuracy standards; failed triggers meter replacement.
attributes.references: ANSI C12.20 - Electricity Meters Accuracy Classes

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: System timestamp when the meter installation record was last modified. Used for change tracking and data quality monitoring.

attributes.name: vee_profile_code
attributes.business_glossary_term: Validation, Estimation, and Editing (VEE) Profile Code
attributes.description: Reference to the VEE (Validation, Estimation, and Editing) rule set applied to interval data from this installation. Determines data quality thresholds and estimation algorithms.

products.name: interval_reading
products.description: Raw interval energy consumption and demand data collected from AMI smart meters at sub-hourly or hourly granularity (typically 15-min or 60-min intervals). Stores channel identifier, interval start timestamp, interval end timestamp, raw kWh or kW value, quality code (raw/estimated/substituted), data collection method (AMI push, manual, estimated), head-end system receipt timestamp, and collection run reference. This is the foundational time-series dataset feeding Oracle Utilities MDM VEE processing, billing, demand response, and grid operations. Immutable raw record — validated versions are stored in validated_interval_reading. High-volume transactional entity; typical utility processes millions of interval records daily.
products.reference: Oracle Utilities MDM — Interval Data / ANSI C12.19 Interval Data Table

attributes.name: interval_reading_id

attributes.name: interval_meter_id

attributes.name: meter_point_id

attributes.name: to_meter_id

attributes.name: channel_number
attributes.description: Channel identifier on the meter device. Multi-channel meters track multiple measurement types (kWh delivered, kWh received, kW demand, voltage, power factor). Typically 1-99.

attributes.name: collection_method
attributes.description: Method by which the interval data was collected. AMI_PUSH = meter initiated transmission, AMI_POLL = head-end system requested, MANUAL = field reading, ESTIMATED = system generated, SCADA = real-time system, IMPORT = bulk file load.
attributes.references: Oracle Utilities MDM - Collection Method Taxonomy

attributes.name: collection_run_code
attributes.description: Identifier of the batch collection run or polling cycle that retrieved this reading. Groups readings collected in the same operational batch for traceability and reprocessing.
attributes.references: Oracle Utilities MDM - Collection Run Entity

attributes.name: correction_reason_code
attributes.description: Code identifying the reason for manual correction or substitution of the original reading value. Examples: METER_ERROR, COMM_FAILURE, CUSTOMER_DISPUTE, DATA_QUALITY. Empty if no correction.
attributes.references: Oracle Utilities MDM - Correction Reason Taxonomy

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this interval reading record was first inserted into the MDM system. Audit field for data lineage and record creation tracking.
attributes.references: Oracle Utilities MDM - Audit Trail Standards

attributes.name: data_completeness_percentage
attributes.description: Percentage of expected interval data received for the associated collection period. 100.00 = complete, <100.00 = partial data. Used for data quality monitoring and VEE prioritization.
attributes.references: Oracle Utilities MDM - Data Quality Metrics

attributes.name: data_source_system
attributes.description: Name or identifier of the source system that provided this interval reading. Examples: AMI_HEAD_END, SCADA_HISTORIAN, MANUAL_ENTRY, BILLING_SYSTEM. Supports multi-source MDM environments.
attributes.references: Oracle Utilities MDM - Source System Registry

attributes.name: daylight_saving_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether daylight saving time was in effect during this interval. True = DST active, False = standard time. Critical for accurate time-of-use rate application and demand response event timing.

attributes.name: demand_response_event_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether a demand response event was active during this interval. True = DR event in progress, False = normal operation. Used for curtailment measurement and settlement.

attributes.name: estimation_method_code
attributes.description: Code identifying the estimation algorithm applied if the reading was estimated. Examples: LIKE_DAY, LINEAR_INTERPOLATION, AVERAGE_USAGE, ZERO_FILL. Empty for actual meter readings.
attributes.references: Oracle Utilities MDM - Estimation Algorithm Registry

attributes.name: interval_duration_minutes
attributes.description: Duration of the measurement interval in minutes. Common values: 15 (quarter-hourly), 30 (half-hourly), 60 (hourly). Supports variable interval lengths for different meter configurations.

attributes.name: interval_end_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp marking the end of the measurement interval. Defines the close of the accumulation period for this reading.

attributes.name: interval_start_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp marking the beginning of the measurement interval. Represents the real-world event time when the meter began accumulating energy for this interval. Typically aligned to 15-minute or 60-minute boundaries.

attributes.name: last_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent update to this interval reading record. Tracks modifications during VEE processing, manual corrections, or reprocessing events.
attributes.references: Oracle Utilities MDM - Audit Trail Standards

attributes.name: load_profile_segment
attributes.description: Customer load profile classification segment for this service point. Used for load forecasting, rate design, and demand response targeting. Examples: RESIDENTIAL_STANDARD, COMMERCIAL_SMALL, INDUSTRIAL_LARGE.

attributes.name: meter_read_status
attributes.description: Status of the meter read operation that produced this interval. SUCCESS = complete read, PARTIAL = incomplete data, FAILED = read failure, TIMEOUT = communication timeout, COMM_ERROR = network error.
attributes.references: Oracle Utilities MDM - Read Status Taxonomy

attributes.name: net_metering_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this service point is enrolled in net energy metering (solar or DER generation). True = NEM active, False = standard consumption-only metering. Affects billing credit calculations.

attributes.name: original_reading_value
attributes.description: Original raw reading value before any estimation, substitution, or manual correction. Preserved for audit trail and comparison with corrected values. Null if no correction occurred.
attributes.references: Oracle Utilities MDM - Audit Trail Standards

attributes.name: power_outage_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether a power outage was detected during this interval based on meter status flags or zero-consumption patterns. True = outage detected, False = normal operation.

attributes.name: quality_code
attributes.description: Data quality indicator for the raw interval reading. RAW = actual meter reading, ESTIMATED = calculated by estimation algorithm, SUBSTITUTED = replaced due to validation failure, EDITED = manually corrected, REJECTED = failed validation, MISSING = no data received.
attributes.references: Oracle Utilities MDM - VEE Quality Codes

attributes.name: rate_schedule_code
attributes.description: Rate schedule or tariff code in effect for this service point at the time of the interval. Used to determine applicable TOU (Time of Use) or CPP (Critical Peak Pricing) rates for billing.
attributes.references: Oracle Utilities CC&B - Rate Schedule Entity

attributes.name: reading_value
attributes.description: Raw numeric value of the interval measurement as collected from the meter. Represents energy consumption (kWh) or demand (kW) depending on channel configuration. Immutable raw value before VEE processing.

attributes.name: received_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the interval reading was received by the head-end system or MDM platform. Used for latency analysis and data freshness monitoring. Distinct from the interval measurement time.

attributes.name: reprocessing_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this interval reading has been reprocessed after initial load. True = reprocessed due to correction or VEE re-run, False = original processing. Supports data lineage tracking.

attributes.name: reverse_flow_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether energy flowed in reverse direction (customer generation exported to grid) during this interval. True = export/generation, False = import/consumption. Critical for NEM and DER settlement.

attributes.name: temperature_celsius
attributes.description: Ambient temperature at the service point location during the interval, if available from weather data integration. Used for weather normalization and load forecasting. Null if not available.

attributes.name: time_zone_offset
attributes.description: UTC offset for the interval timestamps in ISO 8601 format (e.g., -05:00, +00:00). Ensures correct temporal alignment across service territories and daylight saving transitions.

attributes.name: tou_bucket
attributes.description: Time-of-use pricing period classification for this interval based on rate schedule and timestamp. Determines the applicable energy rate tier for billing calculations.
attributes.references: NAESB WEQ-019 - TOU Rate Structure Standards

attributes.name: unit_of_measure
attributes.description: Unit of measurement for the reading value. kWh (kilowatt-hour) for energy consumption, kW (kilowatt) for demand, kVArh for reactive energy, kVAr for reactive demand, kVAh for apparent energy, kVA for apparent demand.

attributes.name: updated_by_user
attributes.description: User ID or system account that last modified this interval reading record. Supports audit trail and accountability for manual edits or system corrections.
attributes.references: SOX - Internal Controls for Data Modification

attributes.name: validation_exception_code
attributes.description: Code identifying the specific validation rule or exception that flagged this reading during VEE processing. Examples: HIGH_USAGE, NEGATIVE_VALUE, MISSING_INTERVAL, SPIKE_DETECTED. Empty if no exceptions.
attributes.references: Oracle Utilities MDM - VEE Exception Taxonomy

attributes.name: validation_status
attributes.description: Status of VEE (Validation, Estimation, and Editing) processing for this raw reading. PENDING = awaiting validation, VALIDATED = passed validation rules, FAILED = validation exceptions detected, BYPASSED = validation skipped.

attributes.name: voltage_level
attributes.description: Voltage classification of the service point where this interval was measured. LOW = residential/small commercial (<1kV), MEDIUM = commercial/industrial (1-35kV), HIGH = large industrial (35-230kV), TRANSMISSION = bulk power (>230kV).

products.name: validated_interval_reading
products.description: VEE-processed (Validation, Estimation, and Editing) interval data representing the authoritative, billing-quality energy consumption record for each meter point and interval. Stores validated kWh, kW demand, reactive power (kVAR), power factor, VEE rule applied, estimation method (if estimated), editor identifier, validation status (valid/estimated/edited/substituted), and VEE processing run reference. This is the SSOT for consumption data consumed by billing, demand response, and grid operations domains. Distinct from raw interval_reading by lifecycle stage and quality assurance.
products.reference: Oracle Utilities MDM — VEE Output / ANSI C12.19

attributes.name: billing_quality_flag

attributes.name: consumption_kwh
attributes.description: The validated energy consumption for this interval measured in kilowatt-hours. This is the authoritative billing-quality consumption value after VEE processing.

attributes.name: cpp_event_flag

attributes.name: created_timestamp

attributes.name: data_quality_score
attributes.description: A composite quality score (0-100) calculated by the VEE engine based on validation rules, estimation confidence, and data completeness. Higher scores indicate higher quality.

attributes.name: data_source_system
attributes.description: The originating system or channel from which the raw interval data was collected before VEE processing.
attributes.references: Oracle Utilities MDM - Source System Registry

attributes.name: demand_kw
attributes.description: The maximum instantaneous power demand recorded during this interval, measured in kilowatts. Used for demand-based billing and capacity planning.

attributes.name: edit_comment
attributes.description: Free-text notes provided by the editor explaining the context or justification for manual edits to this reading.

attributes.name: edit_reason_code
attributes.description: The business reason code explaining why this reading was manually edited. Examples include meter malfunction, data transmission error, or customer dispute resolution.
attributes.references: Oracle Utilities MDM - Edit Reason Reference

attributes.name: estimation_confidence_score
attributes.description: A numerical score (0-100) indicating the confidence level in the estimated value. Higher scores indicate greater confidence in the estimation accuracy.
