attributes.name: estimation_method
attributes.description: The algorithm or technique used to estimate this reading if the original data was missing or invalid. Set to 'none' for non-estimated readings.

attributes.name: exception_code
attributes.description: The specific exception rule code that was triggered during VEE processing. Examples include high-usage threshold breach, negative consumption, or data gap detection.
attributes.references: Oracle Utilities MDM - Exception Rule Reference

attributes.name: exception_flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator of whether this reading triggered any VEE exception rules requiring manual review. True indicates the reading requires analyst attention.

attributes.name: interval_duration_minutes
attributes.description: The length of the measurement interval in minutes. Common values include 15, 30, or 60 minutes depending on meter configuration and rate program requirements.

attributes.name: interval_end_timestamp
attributes.description: The precise date and time when this measurement interval ended. Defines the end boundary of the consumption period.

attributes.name: interval_start_timestamp
attributes.description: The precise date and time when this measurement interval began. Defines the start boundary of the consumption period.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this validated interval reading record was most recently updated or edited.
attributes.references: Oracle Utilities MDM - Audit Trail Standards

attributes.name: meter_read_type
attributes.description: Classification of how the meter reading was obtained: automatically via AMI, manually by field personnel, estimated by system, or provided by customer.

attributes.name: original_consumption_kwh
attributes.description: The raw, unmodified consumption value before VEE processing. Preserved for audit trail and comparison purposes. Null if no original value existed.

attributes.name: outage_flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator of whether a power outage was recorded at this service point during this interval. True indicates zero consumption due to service interruption.

attributes.name: power_factor
attributes.description: The ratio of real power to apparent power, ranging from 0 to 1. Indicates the efficiency of power usage and may trigger power factor penalties or credits.
attributes.references: IEEE 1459 - Definitions for Measurement of Electric Power

attributes.name: reactive_power_kvar
attributes.description: The reactive power component measured in kilovolt-amperes reactive. Used for power factor calculations and grid stability analysis.
attributes.references: IEEE 1459 - Definitions for Measurement of Electric Power

attributes.name: reading_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when the meter physically recorded this interval data. May differ from interval_end_timestamp in cases of delayed meter reads or backfill scenarios.
attributes.references: Oracle Utilities MDM - Reading Timestamp Convention

attributes.name: temperature_fahrenheit
attributes.description: The ambient temperature in degrees Fahrenheit recorded at the associated weather station during this interval. Used for load forecasting and weather normalization.

attributes.name: tou_period_code
attributes.description: The time-of-use pricing period classification for this interval (e.g., on-peak, off-peak, shoulder). Determines the rate tier applied for billing.

attributes.name: unit_of_measure
attributes.description: The measurement unit for the primary consumption value. Standardizes interpretation of numeric readings across different meter types and configurations.

attributes.name: validation_status
attributes.description: The quality status assigned by the VEE process indicating whether the reading is original valid data, was estimated, edited, substituted, flagged as suspect, or missing.
attributes.references: Oracle Utilities MDM - VEE Status Codes

attributes.name: vee_processing_timestamp
attributes.business_glossary_term: VEE (Validation, Estimation, and Editing) Processing Timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when the VEE process completed validation and transformation of this reading into its final billing-quality state.
attributes.references: Oracle Utilities MDM - Processing Audit Trail

attributes.name: vee_run_code
attributes.business_glossary_term: VEE (Validation, Estimation, and Editing) Run ID
attributes.description: Reference to the VEE processing batch run that produced this validated reading. Enables traceability of which VEE execution cycle processed this data.
attributes.references: Oracle Utilities MDM - VEE Processing Framework

attributes.name: voltage_volts
attributes.description: The average voltage level measured during this interval in volts. Used for power quality monitoring and voltage regulation analysis.
attributes.references: ANSI C84.1 - Electric Power Systems and Equipment Voltage Ratings

attributes.name: weather_station_code
attributes.description: Reference to the weather station used for temperature normalization and weather-adjusted load analysis for this service point location.

products.name: meter_read
products.description: Scalar (register-level) meter reading record and associated read scheduling — capturing both the cumulative register value at a specific point in time and the recurring schedule governing when reads are collected. For readings: stores read date, read time, register identifier, read value, read type (scheduled/special/final/initial), read source (AMR/AMI/manual/estimated), reader employee reference, and read quality flag. For scheduling: defines read cycle (monthly/bi-monthly/daily), read method (AMI automated/manual route), scheduled read date, route assignment, billing cycle alignment, schedule code, and active status. Drives field crew routing for manual reads and AMI polling schedules for automated collection. Feeds billing domain consumption calculation. Distinct from interval_reading (which is time-series) — this is the periodic scalar snapshot and its collection governance.
products.reference: SAP IS-U — Meter Reading / Oracle CC&B — Meter Read

attributes.name: meter_read_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the meter read record. Primary key. Role: TRANSACTION_HEADER (scalar meter reading event with lifecycle and scheduling governance).
attributes.references: Oracle Utilities MDM - Meter Reading Object

attributes.name: account_id
attributes.description: Reference to the customer account responsible for this service point. Enables customer-level consumption reporting.

attributes.name: ami_event_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier from the AMI head-end system for this read event. Used to correlate the scalar read with interval data and AMI system logs. Null for non-AMI reads.

attributes.name: billing_run_id
attributes.description: Reference to the billing run that consumed this meter read for invoice calculation. Null if not yet billed. Used for billing audit and revenue assurance.

attributes.name: control_area_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to grid.control_area. Business justification: Aggregated meter reads feed control area load profiles for interchange accounting and NERC reporting. Standard practice for balancing authority operations and compliance.

attributes.name: cycle_id
attributes.description: Reference to the billing cycle for which this read was captured. Links the read to the billing run and invoice generation process.

attributes.name: der_registry_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to renewable.der_registry. Business justification: Register-based reads from DER meters support NEM annual true-up calculations, monthly generation reporting, and capacity factor verification. NEM true-up process requires cumulative meter reads linked

attributes.name: meter_id
attributes.description: Reference to the physical meter device from which this reading was captured. Links to the meter asset registry.

attributes.name: premise_id
attributes.description: Reference to the service premise where the meter is installed. Enables geographic and customer aggregation of reads.

attributes.name: primary_meter_point_id
attributes.description: Reference to the logical service point (delivery point) associated with this meter read. Used for billing and consumption analysis.

attributes.name: rate_schedule_id
attributes.description: Reference to the rate schedule (tariff) in effect for this service point at the time of the read. Used to determine Time-of-Use (TOU) periods, Critical Peak Pricing (CPP) applicability, and billing determinants.

attributes.name: reader_employee_id
attributes.description: Reference to the employee (field technician or meter reader) who captured the reading. Null for automated AMI/AMR reads. Used for workforce productivity analysis and audit trails.

attributes.name: register_id
attributes.description: Reference to the specific register on the meter (e.g., kWh delivered, kWh received, kVArh). Multi-register meters have multiple read records per read event.

attributes.name: route_id
attributes.description: Reference to the meter reading route assignment for manual reads. Defines the geographic sequence and schedule for field crews. Null for automated reads.

attributes.name: to_meter_point_id
attributes.description: FK to metering.meter_point.meter_point_id — Scalar meter reads must reference the meter point where the read was taken. Essential for billing cycle consumption calculation.

attributes.name: vee_rule_id
attributes.description: Reference to the VEE (Validation, Estimation, and Editing) rule that processed this read. Links to the validation rule configuration for audit and troubleshooting.
attributes.references: Oracle Utilities MDM - VEE Rule Engine

attributes.name: average_daily_usage
attributes.description: Consumption divided by consumption days. Expressed in kWh per day or MWh per day. Used for customer usage profiling, demand response eligibility, and anomaly detection.

attributes.name: billed_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this meter read has been used in a billing run and invoice generation. True if billed; False if pending or unbilled. Used to prevent duplicate billing and support billing cycle reconciliation.

attributes.name: consumption_days
attributes.description: Number of days between the current read date and the previous read date. Used to normalize consumption for billing and to calculate average daily usage.

attributes.name: consumption_kwh
attributes.description: Calculated energy consumption for the period (current read value minus previous read value). Expressed in kilowatt-hours (kWh) or megawatt-hours (MWh). This is the billable quantity fed to the billing domain.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this meter read record was first created in the MDM (Meter Data Management) system. Used for data lineage and audit trails.

attributes.name: demand_kw
attributes.description: Peak demand recorded during the read period, expressed in kilowatts (kW) or megawatts (MW). Captured for commercial and industrial customers on demand-based rate schedules. Null for residential meters without demand registers.

attributes.name: demand_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the peak demand occurred during the read period. Used for Time-of-Use (TOU) and Critical Peak Pricing (CPP) rate application.

attributes.name: estimation_method
attributes.description: Algorithm or rule used to estimate the read value when actual read was unavailable. Examples: HIST_AVG (historical average), PREV_YEAR (same period prior year), PRO_RATA (prorated from partial period), ADL (average daily load). Null for actual reads.
attributes.references: Oracle Utilities MDM - VEE Estimation Rules

attributes.name: exception_code
attributes.description: Code identifying any exception or anomaly detected during read capture or validation. Examples: HIGH_USAGE, LOW_USAGE, ZERO_CONSUMPTION, NEGATIVE_CONSUMPTION, TAMPER, COMM_FAILURE. Used to trigger investigation workflows.

attributes.name: multiplier
attributes.description: Constant multiplier applied to the raw register reading to calculate actual consumption. Used for current transformer (CT) and potential transformer (PT) ratios on high-voltage meters. Default is 1.0 for direct-connected meters.

attributes.name: previous_read_date
attributes.description: Date of the prior valid read for this register. Used to calculate the consumption period length (days between reads) and validate read sequence.

attributes.name: previous_read_value
attributes.description: The register value from the prior valid read. Used to calculate consumption (current read minus previous read) and detect anomalies such as reverse flow or register rollover.

attributes.name: read_cycle_code
attributes.description: Code identifying the recurring read schedule pattern. Examples: M01 (monthly cycle 1), B15 (bi-monthly cycle 15), D (daily), W (weekly). Aligns with billing cycle and route planning.

attributes.name: read_date
attributes.description: The calendar date on which the meter reading was captured. Principal business event timestamp for billing cycle alignment and consumption period determination.
attributes.references: NAESB WEQ-015 - Meter Reading Business Practices

attributes.name: read_frequency
attributes.description: The recurring interval at which reads are scheduled for this meter. Monthly: standard residential. Bi-monthly: some residential jurisdictions. Daily: large commercial/industrial or AMI. On-demand: special reads only.

attributes.name: read_method
attributes.description: Technical method used to capture the reading. Optical: infrared port. RF: radio frequency. PLC: power line carrier. Cellular: mobile network. Visual: technician reads display. Handheld: portable reader device.

attributes.name: read_quality_code
attributes.description: Standardized code indicating the quality or exception condition of the read. Examples: OK (normal), EST (estimated), REV (reverse flow), OVF (overflow), PWR (power outage), TMR (tamper detected). Aligns with ANSI C12.19 quality flags.
attributes.references: ANSI C12.19 - Event Log and Quality Flags

attributes.name: read_reason_code
attributes.description: Business reason for the read event. Examples: BILL (billing cycle), MOVE (move-in/move-out), DISC (disconnect), RECON (reconnect), INSP (inspection), COMP (complaint investigation). Used for operational reporting and audit.

attributes.name: read_sequence_number
attributes.description: Business identifier for the meter read, often formatted as meter number plus read date. Used for external reference and audit trails.

attributes.name: read_source
attributes.description: Method by which the reading was obtained. AMI: Advanced Metering Infrastructure (two-way automated). AMR: Automated Meter Reading (one-way drive-by). Manual: field technician on-site. Estimated: calculated by VEE (Validation, Estimation, and Editing) process. Customer: self-reported. Remote: handheld or mobile device.
attributes.references: NAESB RMR - Retail Meter Reading Standards

attributes.name: read_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the meter read. Valid: passed VEE (Validation, Estimation, and Editing) and accepted for billing. Estimated: calculated value pending actual read. Suspect: flagged for review. Failed: read attempt unsuccessful. Pending_validation: awaiting VEE processing. Corrected: replaced by subsequent correction read.
attributes.references: Oracle Utilities MDM - VEE Status Workflow

attributes.name: read_timestamp
attributes.description: Precise date and time when the meter reading was captured, including time zone. Used for interval boundary alignment and AMI (Advanced Metering Infrastructure) event correlation.

attributes.name: read_type
attributes.description: Classification of the read event. Scheduled: routine billing cycle read. Special: off-cycle read for move-in/move-out or investigation. Final: account closure. Initial: new service activation. Test: commissioning or validation. Correction: replacement of erroneous prior read.
attributes.references: Oracle Utilities MDM - Read Type Classification

attributes.name: read_uom
attributes.description: Unit of measure for the read value. Common values: kWh (kilowatt-hour), MWh (megawatt-hour), kVArh (kilovolt-ampere reactive hour) for electric; CCF, MCF, Therms for gas; Gallons for water. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: kWh|MWh|kVArh|MVArh|kW|MW|kVA|MVA|CCF|MCF|Therms|Gallons — 12 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: NAESB WEQ-015 - Unit of Measure Standards

attributes.name: read_value
attributes.description: The cumulative register value captured at the read timestamp. For energy meters, typically kilowatt-hours (kWh) or megawatt-hours (MWh). This is the raw scalar reading before consumption calculation.
attributes.references: ANSI C12.19 - Utility Industry End Device Data Tables

attributes.name: register_digits
attributes.description: Number of digits on the meter register display. Used to detect register rollover (e.g., a 5-digit register rolls from 99999 to 00000). Typical values: 5, 6, 7.

attributes.name: register_rollover_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the register rolled over during this read period (current read value is less than previous read value due to register capacity limit). True if rollover detected; False otherwise.
attributes.references: Oracle Utilities MDM - VEE Rollover Detection

attributes.name: scheduled_read_date
attributes.description: The planned date for this meter read as defined by the read schedule. Used to measure on-time read performance and identify late or early reads.

attributes.name: tou_period
attributes.description: The TOU rate period for this register reading. On-peak: highest rate hours. Off-peak: lowest rate hours. Shoulder: mid-tier hours. Super-off-peak: ultra-low rate hours (e.g., overnight EV charging). Null for non-TOU registers.

attributes.name: tou_register_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this register captures Time-of-Use (TOU) segmented consumption (e.g., on-peak, off-peak, shoulder). True for TOU registers; False for cumulative registers. TOU meters have multiple read records per read event.

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this meter read record was last modified. Tracks VEE corrections, status changes, and data quality improvements.

products.name: vee_rule
products.description: Defines the business rules applied during the VEE (Validation, Estimation, and Editing) process in Oracle Utilities MDM. Each rule specifies the rule type (validation/estimation/editing), rule algorithm, threshold parameters (e.g., spike tolerance percentage, zero-consumption threshold), applicable meter types, priority order, effective date range, and regulatory basis. Governs data quality for billing-quality interval data. Reference entity managed by the metering operations team.
products.reference: Oracle Utilities MDM — VEE Rule Configuration

attributes.name: vee_rule_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Validation Estimation and Editing (VEE) Rule Identifier
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the VEE rule. Primary key for the VEE rule reference entity.

attributes.name: obligation_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.obligation. Business justification: VEE rules implement regulatory obligations for data quality, estimation limits, validation thresholds mandated by state PUC orders. Enables compliance mapping, regulatory justification for VEE algorit

attributes.name: algorithm_type
attributes.description: The computational algorithm or method used by the rule to validate, estimate, or edit meter data (e.g., threshold-based, statistical analysis, linear regression, interpolation). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: threshold|statistical|regression|interpolation|substitution|comparison|pattern_matching — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: applicable_meter_types
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of meter types to which this VEE rule applies (e.g., AMI electric, AMI gas, interval demand, TOU residential). Defines the scope of rule application within the meter population.

attributes.name: applicable_rate_schedules
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of rate schedule codes to which this VEE rule applies. Enables rate-specific validation and estimation logic for TOU and CPP programs.

attributes.name: applicable_service_types
attributes.description: Type of utility service to which this VEE rule applies (electric, gas, water, steam). Ensures rules are applied to appropriate commodity data streams.

attributes.name: approval_required_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether changes to this VEE rule require formal approval before activation. True for rules impacting billing or regulatory compliance.

attributes.name: approved_by
attributes.description: User identifier of the person who approved this VEE rule for production use. Applicable when approval_required_flag is true.

attributes.name: approved_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this VEE rule was formally approved for production use. Supports governance and compliance documentation.

attributes.name: audit_trail_enabled_flag
attributes.business_glossary_term: VEE Rule Audit Trail Enabled Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether detailed audit logging is enabled for this rule, capturing every application of the rule and its outcomes for compliance and troubleshooting.

attributes.name: billing_quality_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether data passing this VEE rule is considered billing-quality and suitable for revenue calculation. True if the rule ensures billing-grade accuracy.

attributes.name: confidence_threshold_percent
attributes.description: Minimum confidence level (as a percentage) required for estimated values to be accepted as billing-quality. Used in statistical estimation algorithms.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this VEE rule record was first created in the MDM system. Supports audit trail and data lineage.

attributes.name: effective_end_date
attributes.description: Date after which the VEE rule is no longer active. Nullable for open-ended rules. Supports rule lifecycle management and historical analysis.

attributes.name: effective_start_date
attributes.description: Date from which the VEE rule becomes active and is applied to meter data. Supports temporal rule management and regulatory compliance.

attributes.name: estimation_method
attributes.description: Specific estimation technique used when the rule type is estimation. Defines how missing or invalid interval data is calculated (e.g., linear interpolation, historical average, same-day-last-week). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: linear_interpolation|historical_average|same_day_last_week|same_day_last_year|regression|zero_fill|prior_value — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: exception_handling_action
attributes.description: Action taken when the rule detects a data quality exception: flag for review, automatically estimate, reject the data, route to manual review, or substitute with a default value.

attributes.name: execution_frequency
attributes.description: Frequency at which the VEE rule is executed against incoming or historical meter data (real-time, hourly, daily, weekly, on-demand).

attributes.name: last_modified_by
attributes.business_glossary_term: VEE Rule Last Modified By User
attributes.description: User identifier of the person who last modified this VEE rule record. Supports change tracking and accountability.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this VEE rule record was last modified. Supports audit trail and change management.

attributes.name: lookback_period_days
attributes.business_glossary_term: VEE Rule Lookback Period in Days
attributes.description: Number of days of historical data the rule examines for validation or estimation purposes. Used by statistical and pattern-matching algorithms.

attributes.name: lower_limit
attributes.description: Minimum acceptable value for validation rules. Interval data below this limit triggers a validation exception or editing action.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for additional notes, implementation guidance, or special considerations related to this VEE rule. Supports knowledge transfer and operational documentation.
attributes.references: Oracle Utilities MDM Business Practice Standards

attributes.name: owner_group
attributes.description: Business unit or team responsible for maintaining and governing this VEE rule (e.g., Metering Operations, Revenue Assurance, Data Quality Team).

attributes.name: priority_order
attributes.description: Execution sequence priority for the rule within the VEE processing engine. Lower numbers execute first. Determines the order in which multiple rules are applied to the same interval data.

attributes.name: regulatory_basis
attributes.description: Citation of the regulatory requirement, tariff provision, or PUC order that mandates or justifies this VEE rule. Supports compliance documentation and audit trails.
attributes.references: FERC Order 2222, State PUC Tariff Requirements

attributes.name: rule_category
attributes.description: Functional category of the rule indicating the specific data quality issue it addresses (e.g., spike detection, zero consumption validation, missing data estimation).

attributes.name: rule_code
attributes.description: Business identifier code for the VEE rule, used for external reference and system integration. Typically a short alphanumeric code following utility naming conventions.
attributes.references: Oracle Utilities MDM Business Practice Standards

attributes.name: rule_description
attributes.description: Detailed description of the VEE rule including its business logic, application context, and expected outcomes when applied to interval meter data.
attributes.references: Oracle Utilities MDM Business Practice Standards

attributes.name: rule_name
attributes.description: Human-readable name of the VEE rule describing its purpose and function within the meter data management process.

attributes.name: rule_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the VEE rule indicating whether it is actively applied to meter data processing or in a non-operational state.

attributes.name: rule_type
attributes.description: Classification of the rule within the VEE process: validation (checks data quality), estimation (fills missing data), or editing (corrects erroneous data).

attributes.name: threshold_unit
attributes.business_glossary_term: VEE Rule Threshold Unit of Measure
attributes.description: Unit of measure for the threshold value (e.g., kWh, MWh, percentage, count, standard deviations) providing context for threshold interpretation.

attributes.name: threshold_value
attributes.description: Numeric threshold parameter used by the rule algorithm to determine data quality exceptions. For example, spike tolerance percentage, maximum consumption limit, or minimum expected value.

attributes.name: upper_limit
attributes.description: Maximum acceptable value for validation rules. Interval data above this limit triggers a validation exception or editing action.

attributes.name: version_number
attributes.description: Version number of the VEE rule configuration. Incremented with each modification to support change tracking and rollback capabilities.

attributes.name: created_by
attributes.description: User identifier of the person who created this VEE rule record. Supports accountability and audit requirements.

products.name: vee_exception
products.description: Operational record of a VEE processing exception raised during interval data validation or estimation — capturing intervals that failed validation rules and required manual review, automatic re-estimation, or override. Stores exception type, severity, affected interval range (start/end timestamps), VEE rule triggered, auto-resolution status, manual reviewer identifier, resolution action taken (re-estimate/edit/accept/override), resolution timestamp, and exception disposition (resolved/escalated/waived). Supports MDM data quality workflows, operational dashboards for VEE pass rates, and regulatory audit trails for billing data integrity. Key metric: exception rate by rule type drives VEE rule tuning.
products.reference: Oracle Utilities MDM — VEE Exception Management

attributes.name: vee_exception_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Validation Estimation and Editing (VEE) Exception Identifier
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the VEE exception record. Primary key for the VEE exception entity.

attributes.name: account_id
attributes.description: Reference to the customer account associated with the meter and service point for this VEE exception. Used for customer impact analysis and billing hold workflows.

attributes.name: audit_finding_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.audit_finding. Business justification: VEE exceptions identified as audit findings when indicating systematic data quality issues or control deficiencies. Supports audit evidence collection, corrective action tracking, regulatory reporting

attributes.name: employee_id
attributes.description: Reference to the employee or system user who reviewed and resolved this VEE exception. Null if exception is still open or was auto-resolved without manual review.

attributes.name: event_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to outage.outage_event. Business justification: VEE analysts investigate whether missing/anomalous interval readings stem from power interruptions. Regulatory VEE reports require cross-referencing exceptions with outage events to justify estimation

attributes.name: meter_id
attributes.description: Reference to the meter that generated the interval data which triggered this VEE exception.

attributes.name: meter_point_id
attributes.description: Reference to the service point (delivery location) associated with the meter that generated the interval data for this exception. Used to link exceptions to customer accounts and premises.

attributes.name: primary_vee_rule_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Validation Estimation and Editing (VEE) Rule Identifier
attributes.description: Reference to the VEE rule that was triggered and caused this exception to be raised.

attributes.name: rate_schedule_id
attributes.description: Reference to the rate schedule (tariff) applicable to the service point at the time of the exception. Used to determine billing impact and priority for resolution, especially for Time-of-Use (TOU) and Critical Peak Pricing (CPP) customers.

attributes.name: to_interval_reading_id
attributes.description: FK to metering.interval_reading.interval_reading_id — VEE exceptions must reference the interval reading(s) that failed validation. Without this link, operators cannot identify and resolve data quality issues.

attributes.name: to_vee_rule_id
attributes.description: FK to metering.vee_rule.vee_rule_id — Each VEE exception must reference the VEE rule that triggered it. This is essential for exception resolution workflows and rule tuning.

attributes.name: vee_interval_reading_id
attributes.description: Reference to the specific interval data record that failed VEE validation and raised this exception.

attributes.name: auto_resolution_attempted
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether the VEE engine attempted automatic resolution of this exception through estimation algorithms. True if auto-resolution was attempted; False if exception was immediately flagged for manual review.

attributes.name: auto_resolution_successful
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether automatic resolution by the VEE engine was successful. True if the engine successfully estimated a replacement value that passed validation; False if auto-resolution failed and manual intervention is required.

attributes.name: billing_impact_flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this VEE exception affects customer billing. True if the affected interval data is used in billing determinants and the exception must be resolved before bill calculation; False if the exception is for non-billing data (e.g., operational monitoring, grid analytics).

attributes.name: corrected_value
attributes.description: Final corrected interval data value (in kWh or other unit of measure) after manual review and editing. This is the value that will be used for billing if the exception is resolved. Null if not yet corrected.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this VEE exception record was first created in the MDM system. Audit field for data lineage and record lifecycle tracking.

attributes.name: data_quality_score
attributes.description: Numeric data quality score (0.00 to 100.00) assigned to the interval data by the VEE engine, indicating confidence in the data accuracy. Lower scores trigger exceptions. Used for trending meter health and VEE rule tuning.

attributes.name: estimated_value
attributes.description: Estimated interval data value (in kWh or other unit of measure) calculated by the VEE engine to replace the invalid or missing original value. Null if estimation was not performed or failed.

attributes.name: estimation_method
attributes.description: Method used by the VEE engine or analyst to estimate the corrected interval value. Linear interpolation: average of adjacent intervals. Historical average: average of same interval from prior days. Similar day: value from comparable day (same day-of-week, season). Regression: statistical model. Manual entry: analyst-provided value. None: no estimation performed.

attributes.name: exception_disposition
attributes.description: Final disposition category of the VEE exception indicating how it was ultimately handled. Resolved: data corrected and validated. Escalated: sent to engineering or management for further investigation. Waived: accepted without correction per approved business rule or regulatory guidance.

attributes.name: exception_number
attributes.business_glossary_term: Validation Estimation and Editing (VEE) Exception Number
attributes.description: Business-facing unique exception number assigned to this VEE exception for tracking and audit purposes. Format: VEE-xxxxxxxxxx.

attributes.name: exception_raised_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the VEE exception was first raised by the MDM VEE engine during interval data validation processing. Represents the business event time of exception detection.

attributes.name: exception_severity
attributes.business_glossary_term: Validation Estimation and Editing (VEE) Exception Severity
attributes.description: Severity level of the VEE exception indicating business impact and urgency for resolution. Critical exceptions block billing; high exceptions require immediate review; medium and low exceptions are tracked for quality metrics; informational exceptions are logged for audit only.

attributes.name: exception_source_system
attributes.description: Source system that originated the interval data which triggered this VEE exception. Typically MDM (Meter Data Management) for AMI data, AMI head-end for direct meter reads, SCADA for grid operations data, manual entry for field reads, or billing system for estimated reads.

attributes.name: exception_status
attributes.business_glossary_term: Validation Estimation and Editing (VEE) Exception Status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the VEE exception. Open: newly raised and awaiting review. In Review: assigned to analyst for investigation. Resolved: corrective action taken and data corrected. Escalated: requires supervisor or engineering review. Waived: exception accepted without correction per business rule. Closed: final disposition recorded and exception archived.

attributes.name: exception_type
attributes.business_glossary_term: Validation Estimation and Editing (VEE) Exception Type
attributes.description: Classification of the VEE exception indicating the nature of the data quality issue: validation failure (data failed validation rule), estimation failure (unable to estimate missing interval), editing failure (manual edit rejected), missing data (no interval data received), suspect data (data flagged as questionable), or out of range (value exceeds expected bounds).

attributes.name: interval_count
attributes.description: Number of individual interval readings affected by this VEE exception. For 15-minute interval meters, a 1-hour exception would affect 4 intervals.

attributes.name: interval_end_timestamp
attributes.description: End timestamp of the interval data range affected by this VEE exception. Defines the end of the time window containing suspect or invalid data.

attributes.name: interval_start_timestamp
attributes.description: Start timestamp of the interval data range affected by this VEE exception. Defines the beginning of the time window containing suspect or invalid data.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this VEE exception record was last updated. Audit field for tracking changes to exception status, resolution actions, and data corrections.

attributes.name: original_value
attributes.description: Original raw interval data value (in kWh or other unit of measure) that triggered the VEE exception before any estimation or editing was applied.

attributes.name: regulatory_reportable_flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this VEE exception must be reported to regulatory authorities (e.g., state Public Utility Commission) as part of data quality and billing accuracy compliance reporting. True if reportable; False otherwise.

attributes.name: resolution_action
attributes.description: Action taken to resolve the VEE exception. Re-estimate: apply different estimation algorithm. Manual edit: analyst manually corrected the value. Accept original: original value accepted despite exception. Override: supervisor approved exception without correction. Escalate: sent to engineering for investigation. Waive: exception acknowledged but no correction required per business rule.

attributes.name: resolution_notes
attributes.description: Free-text notes entered by the analyst or system documenting the resolution action, rationale for the decision, and any additional context for audit purposes.

attributes.name: resolution_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the VEE exception was resolved (status changed to resolved, waived, or closed). Null if exception is still open or in review. Used to calculate exception aging and VEE team performance metrics.

attributes.name: reviewer_name
attributes.description: Full name of the analyst or system user who reviewed and resolved this VEE exception. Captured for audit trail and operational reporting.

attributes.name: threshold_value
attributes.description: Numeric threshold value defined in the VEE rule that was exceeded or violated, triggering this exception. For example, maximum expected consumption in kWh, or maximum percent deviation from historical average.

attributes.name: unit_of_measure
attributes.description: Unit of measure for the interval data values associated with this exception. Typically kWh (kilowatt-hour) for electric energy consumption, kW for demand, or gas volume units. products.name: ami_event
products.description: Operational event and investigation record generated by AMI smart meters and transmitted to the head-end system — covering the full spectrum of AMI-originated events and their investigation lifecycle. Event types include: tamper alerts (with detection method, tamper type such as cover removal/bypass/reverse installation/unauthorized reconnect, investigation status, confirmed theft indicator, estimated unbilled consumption, revenue recovery amount, and law enforcement referral status), power outage notifications (last gasp), power restoration notifications (first breath), communication failures, voltage sag/swell events, reverse energy flow detections, and firmware update events. Stores event type code, event timestamp, meter identifier, event severity, raw event payload, head-end receipt timestamp, downstream notification status, and for tamper/theft events: detection source (AMI alert, field inspection, VEE anomaly), case status, and closure date. SSOT for all AMI-originated events including tamper/theft investigation within the metering domain. Feeds outage management, grid operations, and revenue protection workflows. Supports non-technical loss reporting and PUC-mandated theft-of-service regulatory filings.

products.name: tou_rate_program
products.description: Defines Time-of-Use (TOU) and Critical Peak Pricing (CPP) rate program structures and manages meter point enrollments in those programs. For program definition: specifies program code, peak/off-peak/shoulder period definitions, seasonal schedules, CPP event trigger criteria, applicable customer segments, effective date range, rate period definitions, and regulatory approval reference. For enrollment: tracks meter point association via enrollment records with enrollment ID, enrollment effective date, program end date, enrollment channel (web/CSR/auto), opt-in/opt-out status, and program-specific meter configuration requirements triggered by enrollment. Owned by metering as the SSOT for rate period time definitions that govern interval data classification and enrollment lifecycle; pricing amounts are owned by the billing domain. Enables billing domain to apply correct TOU rate periods to validated interval data and supports demand response domain for CPP event targeting.

products.name: net_energy_metering
products.description: Master record for customer premises enrolled in Net Energy Metering (NEM) programs — tracking bi-directional energy flow measurement for customers with behind-the-meter generation (rooftop solar, battery storage). Captures NEM program type (NEM 1.0/2.0/3.0), interconnection approval date, export capacity (kW), generation technology type, inverter details, true-up period, banking balance (kWh credits), and regulatory tariff reference. Distinct from standard metering — NEM requires bi-directional meter configuration and special billing treatment including export credit calculations.
products.reference: CPUC NEM Tariff / Oracle CC&B — NEM Account

attributes.name: account_id

attributes.name: meter_id

attributes.name: meter_point_id
attributes.description: FK to metering.meter_point.meter_point_id — NEM enrollment must reference the meter point where bi-directional metering is configured. Essential for identifying NEM premises and applying special billing treatment.

attributes.name: net_meter_point_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to metering.meter_point. Business justification: Net Energy Metering (NEM) enrollment is tied to a specific service delivery point (meter_point) where the distributed energy resource (DER) system is physically interconnected. While net_energy_meteri

attributes.name: ppa_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to trading.ppa. Business justification: NEM customers with solar installations often have underlying power purchase agreements; tracking which PPA supplies the generation measured by the NEM meter is essential for compliance verification, s

attributes.name: premise_id
attributes.description: Reference to the customer premise enrolled in the NEM program. Links to the physical service location with behind-the-meter generation.

attributes.name: regulatory_filing_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.regulatory_filing. Business justification: NEM programs require periodic regulatory filings (annual reports on enrollment, generation, credits issued per state PUC requirements). Supports regulatory reporting obligations, rate case support, pr

attributes.name: application_date
attributes.description: Date the customer submitted the NEM interconnection application to the utility. Used to determine applicable tariff version and grandfathering provisions.

attributes.name: banking_balance_kwh
attributes.description: The cumulative net excess generation (kWh) banked as a credit within the current true-up period. Positive balance indicates customer has exported more than imported; negative balance indicates net import. Balance is carried forward month-to-month until true-up settlement.
attributes.references: Oracle Utilities MDM - NEM Credit Calculation, State PUC NEM Tariff Rules

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this NEM enrollment record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking.

attributes.name: eligible_for_rec
attributes.business_glossary_term: Eligible for Renewable Energy Certificate (REC) Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the generation system is eligible to generate Renewable Energy Certificates (RECs) under state RPS programs. True if eligible; False if ineligible or RECs have been contractually assigned to the utility.
attributes.references: State RPS Standards, NERC e-Tag Standard

attributes.name: enrollment_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the NEM enrollment. Pending indicates application submitted but not yet approved; Active indicates interconnection complete and bi-directional metering operational; Suspended indicates temporary hold; Terminated indicates customer-initiated cancellation; Expired indicates end of program eligibility period.

attributes.name: export_capacity_limit_kw
attributes.description: The maximum instantaneous power (kW) the customer is authorized to export to the grid. May be less than nameplate capacity due to grid constraints or inverter settings. Enforced by inverter configuration.
attributes.references: IEEE 1547 Interconnection Standard, Distribution System Impact Study

attributes.name: export_credit_rate_type
attributes.description: The methodology used to calculate the monetary credit for energy exported to the grid. Retail Rate (NEM 1.0) credits at full retail rate; Avoided Cost credits at utility's marginal generation cost; NEM 3.0 Export Rate uses time-varying export compensation rates; Wholesale Rate credits at market energy price.

attributes.name: generation_technology_type
attributes.business_glossary_term: Distributed Energy Resource (DER) Generation Technology Type
attributes.description: The type of behind-the-meter generation technology installed at the premise. Solar PV is the most common; other eligible technologies include wind turbines, fuel cells, biogas generators, micro-hydro, combined heat and power (CHP), and battery storage systems. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: solar_pv|wind|fuel_cell|biogas|micro_hydro|combined_heat_power|battery_storage — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: grandfathered_expiration_date
attributes.description: The date the grandfathered tariff protection expires and the customer transitions to the current NEM tariff. Null if not grandfathered or if grandfathering is perpetual.
attributes.references: CPUC Decision 16-01-044, State PUC Grandfathering Rules

attributes.name: grandfathered_tariff_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the customer is grandfathered under a prior NEM tariff version due to application date. True if grandfathered; False if subject to current tariff. Grandfathering typically lasts 20 years from PTO date.
attributes.references: CPUC Decision 16-01-044, State PUC Grandfathering Rules

attributes.name: has_energy_storage
attributes.description: Indicates whether the NEM system includes a battery energy storage system (BESS) for behind-the-meter storage. True if storage is present; False if generation-only. Storage systems may be subject to additional tariff rules and export limitations.

attributes.name: inspection_date
attributes.description: The date the utility conducted the field inspection of the generation system. Null if inspection is not required or has not yet occurred.

attributes.name: inspection_status
attributes.description: The status of the utility's field inspection of the installed generation system. Pending indicates inspection scheduled but not completed; Passed indicates system meets interconnection requirements; Failed indicates deficiencies found; Not Required for systems under simplified interconnection threshold.
attributes.references: IEEE 1547 Interconnection Standard, Internal Field Inspection Procedure

attributes.name: installer_company_name
attributes.description: The name of the contractor or company that installed the behind-the-meter generation system. Required for warranty claims and quality assurance tracking.

attributes.name: installer_license_number
attributes.description: The state-issued contractor license number of the installer. Required to verify installer is properly licensed and bonded per state electrical code requirements.
attributes.references: State Electrical Code, OSHA Safety Standards

attributes.name: interconnection_agreement_number
attributes.description: The unique identifier for the signed interconnection agreement between the customer and the utility. Governs technical and operational requirements for grid interconnection.

attributes.name: interconnection_approval_date
attributes.description: Date the utility approved the interconnection application and authorized the customer to energize the behind-the-meter generation system. Marks the start of NEM program participation.

attributes.name: inverter_manufacturer
attributes.description: The manufacturer of the inverter that converts DC power from the generation source to AC power for grid export. Required for equipment certification and warranty tracking.

attributes.name: inverter_model
attributes.description: The specific model number of the inverter installed. Must be on the utility's approved equipment list and comply with IEEE 1547 anti-islanding and voltage/frequency ride-through requirements.

attributes.name: inverter_serial_number
attributes.description: The unique serial number of the inverter unit installed at the premise. Used for warranty claims, equipment recalls, and field service tracking.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this NEM enrollment record was last updated. Used for audit trail and change tracking.

attributes.name: last_true_up_date
attributes.description: The date of the most recent annual NEM true-up settlement. Used to track true-up cycle and determine next true-up anniversary.

attributes.name: nameplate_capacity_kw
attributes.description: The rated maximum output capacity of the behind-the-meter generation system in kilowatts (kW). Used to determine interconnection study requirements and export limits.

attributes.name: nem_program_type
attributes.description: The specific NEM tariff program under which the customer is enrolled. NEM 1.0 provides full retail rate credit for exports; NEM 2.0 includes non-bypassable charges; NEM 3.0 uses export compensation rates; VNEM is Virtual Net Energy Metering for multi-tenant properties; NEM-ST is NEM with energy storage.
attributes.references: CPUC Decision 14-03-041, CPUC Decision 16-01-044, CPUC Decision 17-12-022

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for additional notes, special conditions, or operational comments related to the NEM enrollment. May include interconnection study findings, customer requests, or billing exceptions.

attributes.name: permission_to_operate_date
attributes.description: Date the utility issued Permission to Operate (PTO), authorizing the customer to begin exporting energy to the grid. Bi-directional metering and export credit calculations commence from this date.

attributes.name: rate_schedule_code
attributes.description: The tariff rate schedule applicable to this NEM customer. Determines import energy charges, export credit rates, and non-bypassable charges. Common NEM rate schedules include residential TOU and commercial demand rates.
attributes.references: State PUC Tariff Book, FERC Rate Schedule

attributes.name: rec_ownership
attributes.description: Identifies who retains ownership of the RECs generated by the system. Customer retains RECs unless contractually assigned to the utility or sold to a third party. Not Applicable if system is not REC-eligible.

attributes.name: storage_capacity_kwh
attributes.description: The rated energy storage capacity of the battery system in kilowatt-hours (kWh). Null if no storage is present. Used to assess demand response and grid services potential.

attributes.name: storage_power_rating_kw
attributes.description: The maximum charge/discharge power rating of the battery system in kilowatts (kW). Null if no storage is present. Determines instantaneous grid support capability.

attributes.name: system_installation_date
attributes.business_glossary_term: Distributed Energy Resource (DER) System Installation Date
attributes.description: The date the behind-the-meter generation system was physically installed at the premise. May precede Permission to Operate date. Used for warranty tracking and system age analysis.

attributes.name: tariff_reference
attributes.description: The specific tariff rule or schedule reference governing this NEM enrollment. Includes tariff book section, effective date, and any rider or special condition references. Used for regulatory compliance and billing validation.
attributes.references: State PUC Tariff Book, FERC Rate Schedule

attributes.name: termination_date
attributes.description: Date the NEM enrollment was terminated or expired. Null for active enrollments. Used to calculate final true-up and settle remaining kWh credit balance.

attributes.name: true_up_anniversary_month
attributes.description: The calendar month (1-12) in which the annual NEM true-up settlement occurs. Determines when banked kWh credits are reconciled and any remaining balance is settled or forfeited.

attributes.name: true_up_period_months
attributes.description: The number of months in the NEM billing cycle before a true-up settlement occurs. Typically 12 months. During the true-up period, excess generation credits are banked; at true-up, remaining credits are settled or forfeited per tariff rules.

products.name: remote_service_order
products.description: Operational record of a remote service action executed via AMI on a smart meter — including remote connect, remote disconnect, remote meter read on demand, load limiting activation, and firmware over-the-air (OTA) update commands. Captures order type, requested timestamp, execution timestamp, requesting system or user, execution result (success/failure/pending), failure reason code, and retry count. Supports meter-to-cash workflows (disconnect for non-payment, reconnect after payment) and field operations efficiency tracking.
products.reference: Oracle Utilities MDM — Remote Command / AMI Head-End Command Queue

attributes.name: remote_service_order_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the remote service order executed via Advanced Metering Infrastructure (AMI) on a smart meter.

attributes.name: account_id
attributes.description: Customer account identifier associated with the remote service order, used for meter-to-cash workflows.

attributes.name: ami_head_end_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to metering.ami_head_end. Business justification: Remote service orders (disconnect, reconnect, load limit, firmware update, on-demand read) are executed through specific AMI head-end systems. The remote_service_order table currently has ami_head_end

attributes.name: capital_project_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to asset.capital_project. Business justification: Remote service operations (mass disconnects/reconnects, load limiting) during grid modernization or construction projects require tracking against capital projects for cost allocation, project managem

attributes.name: cost_center_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.cost_center. Business justification: Remote connect/disconnect operations have associated costs (system usage, labor oversight) tracked by cost center. Required for customer operations cost allocation, efficiency metrics vs. truck rolls,

attributes.name: customer_service_request_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to customer.service_request. Business justification: Remote disconnect/reconnect operations are often initiated by customer service requests (non-payment, move-in/out, safety concerns). Supports customer service workflows, SLA tracking, and audit trails

attributes.name: cycle_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the billing cycle during which the remote service order was executed, used for meter-to-cash reconciliation and revenue assurance.

attributes.name: der_registry_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to renewable.der_registry. Business justification: Remote disconnect/reconnect commands for DER sites during emergency curtailment events, interconnection violations, or VPP dispatch. Emergency curtailment dispatch process requires remote service orde

attributes.name: dr_event_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the demand response event that triggered the remote service order, if the order is part of a load management or curtailment program.

attributes.name: employee_id
attributes.description: User identifier of the person who initiated the remote service order, if manually requested; null for system-initiated orders.

attributes.name: meter_point_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the service point associated with the meter receiving the remote service action.

attributes.name: remote_meter_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the smart meter on which the remote service action was executed.

attributes.name: scada_point_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to grid.scada_point. Business justification: Remote disconnect/reconnect commands coordinate with SCADA-controlled distribution switching for load management, demand response, and safety interlocks. Distribution automation integration requiremen

attributes.name: to_meter_id
attributes.description: FK to metering.meter.meter_id — Remote service orders (connect/disconnect/on-demand read) must reference the target meter device. Core operational link for AMI remote operations.

attributes.name: work_order_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the associated field work order if the remote service order was initiated as part of a broader field service activity (e.g., meter installation, maintenance).

attributes.name: actual_execution_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the remote service order was actually executed on the meter, recorded by the AMI head-end system upon completion.

attributes.name: ami_transaction_code
attributes.description: Unique transaction identifier assigned by the AMI head-end system for tracking the command execution at the network layer.

attributes.name: command_payload
attributes.description: Technical payload or command string sent to the meter by the AMI head-end system, stored for audit and troubleshooting purposes.

attributes.name: communication_protocol
attributes.description: Communication protocol used by the AMI network to transmit the remote service command to the meter (e.g., ZigBee, cellular, RF mesh, power line carrier, Wi-Fi).

attributes.name: completion_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the remote service order reached a terminal state (success, failed, cancelled, or timeout) and was closed in the system.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the remote service order record was first created in the system, supporting audit trail and data lineage requirements.

attributes.name: customer_notification_sent
attributes.description: Indicates whether a customer notification (email, SMS, IVR call) was sent prior to or after the remote service order execution, as required by regulatory or business policy.

attributes.name: customer_notification_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the customer notification was sent regarding the remote service order, used for regulatory compliance documentation.

attributes.name: disconnect_reason
attributes.description: Business reason for a remote disconnect order, supporting meter-to-cash workflows and regulatory compliance reporting (e.g., non-payment, customer request, safety hazard).

attributes.name: execution_result_code
attributes.description: Standardized code returned by the AMI head-end system indicating the outcome of the remote service order execution (e.g., SUCCESS, METER_OFFLINE, COMMAND_REJECTED, TIMEOUT).

attributes.name: failure_reason_code
attributes.description: Detailed code explaining why the remote service order failed, populated only when order_status is failed; used for root cause analysis and retry logic.

attributes.name: failure_reason_description
attributes.description: Human-readable description of the failure reason, providing additional context for troubleshooting and customer communication.

attributes.name: firmware_version_after
attributes.description: Target meter firmware version to be installed by the over-the-air (OTA) update, verified upon successful completion.

attributes.name: firmware_version_before
attributes.description: Meter firmware version installed before the over-the-air (OTA) update, used for version control and rollback tracking.

attributes.name: last_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the remote service order record was last modified, supporting audit trail and change tracking requirements.

attributes.name: load_limit_threshold_kw
attributes.description: Power threshold in kilowatts (kW) set for load limiting activation orders, restricting customer consumption to prevent overload or support demand response programs.

attributes.name: max_retry_count
attributes.description: Maximum number of retry attempts allowed for this remote service order before it is marked as permanently failed.

attributes.name: meter_reading_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the meter reading was captured at the meter during an on-demand read remote service order.

attributes.name: meter_reading_uom
attributes.description: Unit of measure for the meter reading value captured during on-demand read (e.g., kWh for energy, kW for demand, kVAh for apparent energy).

attributes.name: meter_reading_value
attributes.description: Meter register reading value captured during an on-demand read remote service order, used for billing validation or dispute resolution.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text notes or comments entered by users or systems regarding the remote service order, capturing additional context, special instructions, or resolution details.

attributes.name: order_number
attributes.description: Externally visible unique business identifier for the remote service order, used for tracking and customer communication.

attributes.name: order_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the remote service order: pending (queued), in progress (executing), success (completed successfully), failed (execution error), cancelled (user/system cancelled), or timeout (no response from meter).

attributes.name: order_type
attributes.description: Type of remote service action executed via AMI: remote connect, remote disconnect, on-demand meter read, load limiting activation/deactivation, or firmware over-the-air (OTA) update.

attributes.name: priority
attributes.description: Priority level assigned to the remote service order, determining execution sequence in the AMI command queue (critical for safety/emergency, high for revenue protection, normal for routine, low for bulk operations).

attributes.name: reconnect_reason
attributes.description: Business reason for a remote reconnect order, typically following payment receipt or resolution of the disconnect condition.

attributes.name: regulatory_compliance_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the remote service order execution complies with applicable Public Utility Commission (PUC) regulations for disconnect/reconnect procedures and customer notification requirements.

attributes.name: requested_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the remote service order was requested by the system or user, representing the business event initiation time.

attributes.name: requesting_system
attributes.description: Name or identifier of the source system that initiated the remote service order (e.g., CC&B, OMS, MDM, manual CSR entry).

attributes.name: response_payload
attributes.description: Technical response payload returned by the meter to the AMI head-end system, stored for audit and troubleshooting purposes.

attributes.name: retry_count
attributes.description: Number of times the remote service order has been retried after initial failure, used to track execution persistence and prevent infinite retry loops.

attributes.name: scheduled_execution_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the remote service order is scheduled to be executed on the meter, may differ from requested timestamp for planned actions.

attributes.name: signal_strength_dbm
attributes.description: Signal strength in decibels-milliwatts (dBm) measured at the time of remote service order execution, used to diagnose communication failures.

products.name: meter_test
products.description: Records the results of meter accuracy and performance tests conducted in the field or at a test laboratory — including periodic in-service tests, customer-requested tests, and post-complaint investigations. Captures test type (in-service/shop/referee), test date, test technician, test equipment used, accuracy result (percentage error), as-found and as-left readings, pass/fail determination, regulatory standard applied (ANSI C12.1), and any corrective action taken. Supports regulatory compliance with PUC meter testing requirements and back-billing adjustments.
products.reference: ANSI C12.1 — Electric Meters Code for Electricity Metering / SAP IS-U — Device Test

attributes.name: meter_test_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the meter test record. Primary key.

attributes.name: account_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to customer.account. Business justification: Meter accuracy test failures trigger billing adjustments that must be tracked to specific customer accounts. Supports revenue protection, regulatory compliance for meter accuracy standards, and custom

attributes.name: adjustment_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to billing.adjustment. Business justification: Failed meter tests trigger billing adjustments for inaccurate metering periods (regulatory requirement). This link directly connects test results to financial corrections, supports PUC audit trails, a

attributes.name: audit_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.audit. Business justification: Meter testing programs audited for compliance with testing frequency, accuracy standards, documentation requirements. Provides audit evidence for measurement accuracy programs, regulatory inspection s

attributes.name: cost_center_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.cost_center. Business justification: Meter testing activities are cost-accounted to specific cost centers (meter shop operations). Required for meter shop budgeting, labor cost allocation, and regulatory compliance testing cost tracking

attributes.name: customer_service_request_id
attributes.description: Reference to the customer service request that initiated the meter test, if applicable. Links to the customer service system for complaint tracking and resolution.

attributes.name: der_registry_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to renewable.der_registry. Business justification: Accuracy testing of bidirectional meters at DER installations for regulatory compliance and revenue assurance. Annual DER meter testing program requires test records linked to DER for compliance repor

attributes.name: employee_id
attributes.description: Reference to the technician or engineer who performed the meter test. Links to the workforce or employee registry for accountability and certification tracking.

attributes.name: environmental_permit_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.environmental_permit. Business justification: Meter test facilities require environmental permits for calibration equipment, hazardous waste disposal (mercury switches, electronic waste). Enables permit compliance tracking for test labs, regulato

attributes.name: inspection_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to asset.asset_inspection. Business justification: Meter testing is a specialized asset inspection activity. Utilities integrate meter test results (accuracy, condition ratings, defects) into asset health monitoring and condition-based maintenance pro

attributes.name: primary_meter_id
attributes.description: Reference to the meter that was tested. Links to the meter asset registry.
attributes.references: Oracle Utilities MDM - Meter Asset Management

attributes.name: to_meter_id
attributes.description: FK to metering.meter.meter_id — Meter test results must reference the meter device tested. Required for regulatory compliance (PUC meter testing requirements) and accuracy tracking.

attributes.name: work_order_id
attributes.description: Reference to the work order that authorized or triggered the meter test. Links to the work management system for scheduling, labor tracking, and cost allocation.

attributes.name: accuracy_percentage
attributes.description: Measured accuracy of the meter expressed as a percentage error. Positive values indicate the meter is running fast (over-registering); negative values indicate the meter is running slow (under-registering). Calculated as ((measured - actual) / actual) * 100.

attributes.name: as_found_reading
attributes.description: Meter register reading captured at the beginning of the test, before any adjustments or repairs. Represents the meter state as found in the field or upon receipt at the test facility. Measured in kilowatt-hours (kWh).

attributes.name: as_left_reading
attributes.description: Meter register reading captured at the conclusion of the test, after any adjustments, calibrations, or repairs. Represents the meter state after corrective action. Measured in kilowatt-hours (kWh).

attributes.name: billing_adjustment_amount
attributes.description: Calculated billing adjustment amount resulting from the meter test, measured in local currency. Positive values indicate customer credit (meter was over-registering); negative values indicate back-billing (meter was under-registering). Calculated based on accuracy error, consumption history, and regulatory back-billing limits.

attributes.name: billing_adjustment_required_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the test results require a billing adjustment (back-billing or credit). True if meter was found out of tolerance and billing correction is needed; false otherwise. Triggers downstream billing adjustment workflow.

attributes.name: corrective_action_code
attributes.description: Standardized code representing the corrective action taken. None indicates meter passed without adjustment; calibrated indicates meter was adjusted to meet accuracy standards; repaired indicates component-level repair; replaced indicates meter was swapped; sealed indicates new tamper seal applied; retired indicates meter removed from service.

attributes.name: corrective_action_taken
attributes.description: Description of any corrective action performed on the meter following the test. May include calibration adjustments, component replacement, seal replacement, or meter replacement. Empty if no action was required (meter passed as-found).

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this meter test record was first created in the system. Audit trail field for data lineage and compliance.

attributes.name: customer_notification_date
attributes.description: Date on which the customer was notified of the test results. Required for regulatory compliance when test results trigger billing adjustments or service actions.

attributes.name: customer_notified_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the customer was notified of the test results. True if notification was sent; false if not yet notified. Required for customer-requested tests and tests resulting in billing adjustments.

attributes.name: failure_code
attributes.description: Standardized code categorizing the failure mode. Examples include accuracy-out-of-tolerance, display-failure, communication-failure, mechanical-damage, tampering-detected, seal-broken, internal-component-failure. Empty if meter passed. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: accuracy_out_of_tolerance|display_failure|communication_failure|mechanical_damage|tampering_detected|seal_broken|internal_component_failure|environmental_damage|calibration_drift|manufacturing_defect — promote to reference product]

attributes.name: failure_reason
attributes.description: Detailed description of why the meter failed the test, if applicable. May include root cause analysis such as component wear, environmental damage, tampering, manufacturing defect, or calibration drift. Empty if meter passed.

attributes.name: power_factor
attributes.description: Power factor applied during the test, expressed as a decimal between 0 and 1. Represents the phase relationship between voltage and current. Unity power factor (1.0) represents purely resistive load; lagging power factor (e.g., 0.5 lag) simulates inductive loads common in industrial settings.

attributes.name: regulatory_report_submitted_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the test results have been included in regulatory reporting to the Public Utility Commission (PUC). True if reported; false if pending. Required for periodic meter testing compliance reports.
attributes.references: State PUC Meter Testing Reporting Requirements

attributes.name: regulatory_tolerance_percentage
attributes.description: The maximum allowable percentage error defined by the applicable regulatory standard. Meters exceeding this tolerance fail the test and require adjustment or replacement. Typical values range from ±2% to ±3% depending on meter class and jurisdiction.
attributes.references: ANSI C12.1, State PUC Meter Accuracy Requirements

attributes.name: test_cost
attributes.description: Total cost incurred to perform the meter test, including labor, equipment usage, and materials. Measured in local currency. Used for cost recovery and regulatory rate case support.

attributes.name: test_current_amperes
attributes.description: Current level applied during the meter test, measured in amperes. Test standards typically specify light load, full load, and heavy load current levels to validate accuracy across the meter's operating range.

attributes.name: test_date
attributes.description: The date on which the meter test was performed. This is the principal business event timestamp for the test.

attributes.name: test_duration_minutes
attributes.description: Total time required to complete the meter test, measured in minutes. Includes setup, test execution, and teardown. Used for labor costing and scheduling optimization.

attributes.name: test_equipment_code
attributes.description: Reference to the test equipment or meter test bench used to perform the test. Links to the asset registry for calibration tracking and equipment certification.

attributes.name: test_equipment_serial_number
attributes.description: Serial number of the test equipment used. Captured for traceability and to ensure test equipment is within its calibration period.

attributes.name: test_facility_code
attributes.description: Reference to the facility or service center where the test was performed. Links to the facility registry for location tracking and certification management.

attributes.name: test_load_kwh
attributes.description: The known reference load applied during the test, measured in kilowatt-hours. This is the standard energy quantity used to calculate meter accuracy by comparing the meter's measured value against this reference.

attributes.name: test_location
attributes.description: Physical location where the meter test was conducted. Field indicates in-situ testing at the customer premise; shop indicates utility service center; laboratory indicates independent testing facility; customer-premise indicates on-site testing; service-center indicates utility-operated test facility.

attributes.name: test_notes
attributes.description: Free-form notes captured by the test technician. May include observations about meter condition, environmental factors, customer interactions, or any anomalies encountered during testing.

attributes.name: test_number
attributes.description: Business identifier for the meter test, typically assigned by the testing system or laboratory. Used for external reference and tracking.

attributes.name: test_result
attributes.description: Overall pass/fail determination for the meter test based on regulatory accuracy thresholds. Pass indicates meter meets accuracy standards; fail indicates meter is out of tolerance; inconclusive means test could not produce a definitive result.

attributes.name: test_standard_applied

products.name: metering_dr_enrollment
products.description: This association product represents the enrollment relationship between a meter and a demand response program. It captures the operational enrollment lifecycle, participation tracking, and settlement data for each meter enrolled in each DR program. Each record links one meter to one DR program with enrollment-specific attributes including enrollment dates, status, enrolled capacity commitment, baseline calculation method override, participation performance metrics, opt-out history, and cumulative incentive payments earned. This is the SSOT for DR program enrollment administration, event dispatch eligibility, M&V settlement, and regulatory compliance reporting.. Existence Justification: In energy utilities operations, a single meter can simultaneously enroll in multiple demand response programs (e.g., ISO/RTO capacity market + utility peak-time rebate + behavioral DR campaign), and each DR program enrolls thousands of meters across the service territory. The business actively manages enrollments as operational entities with lifecycle status, capacity commitments, participation tracking, opt-out history, and settlement data. Enrollment is a recognized business concept with dedicated administration, event dispatch eligibility determination, M&V settlement processes, and regulatory compliance reporting obligations.
