attributes.description: Classification of the contingency analysis execution context. Real-time runs support live operations; study mode supports planning; post-event supports incident investigation.

attributes.name: base_case_mvar_mismatch
attributes.description: Total MVAR mismatch in the base case power flow solution before contingency evaluation. Indicates quality of reactive power balance in the state estimation input.

attributes.name: base_case_mw_mismatch
attributes.description: Total MW mismatch in the base case power flow solution before contingency evaluation. Indicates quality of the state estimation input. Should be near zero for valid analysis.

attributes.name: convergence_tolerance
attributes.description: The numerical convergence tolerance threshold used for power flow solutions in this contingency analysis. Smaller values provide higher accuracy but longer execution time.

attributes.name: corrective_action_description
attributes.description: Description of recommended or required corrective actions to address violations detected in the contingency analysis. May include generation redispatch, switching orders, or load curtailment.

attributes.name: corrective_action_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether corrective actions are required based on the violations detected. Triggers operator response procedures when true.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this contingency analysis run record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and data lineage.

attributes.name: data_source_system
attributes.description: Name of the source system that generated this contingency analysis run record. Typically the EMS application name and version for data lineage tracking.

attributes.name: ems_system_name
attributes.description: Name or identifier of the EMS system that executed this contingency analysis run. Supports multi-EMS environments and system integration tracking.

attributes.name: execution_duration_seconds
attributes.description: Total elapsed time in seconds for the contingency analysis execution from initiation to completion. Critical for monitoring EMS performance and real-time operational requirements.

attributes.name: last_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this contingency analysis run record was last modified. Tracks updates to operator acknowledgment, corrective actions, or status changes.

attributes.name: max_iterations
attributes.description: Maximum number of iterations allowed for power flow convergence in each contingency scenario. Prevents excessive computation time for non-converging cases.

attributes.name: n1_contingencies_evaluated
attributes.description: Number of single-element (N-1) contingencies evaluated in this run. N-1 represents loss of a single transmission element.
attributes.references: NERC TPL-001 Category B Performance Requirements

attributes.name: n2_contingencies_evaluated
attributes.description: Number of double-element (N-2) contingencies evaluated in this run. N-2 represents simultaneous loss of two transmission elements.
attributes.references: NERC TPL-001 Category C Performance Requirements

attributes.name: nerc_compliance_flag
attributes.business_glossary_term: North American Electric Reliability Corporation (NERC) Compliance Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this contingency analysis run meets NERC TPL compliance requirements for documentation and retention. Used for regulatory audit evidence.

attributes.name: non_converged_contingencies
attributes.description: Number of contingency scenarios that failed to converge within the iteration limit. Non-convergence may indicate severe system stress or numerical issues.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text notes or comments regarding this contingency analysis run. May include operator observations, special conditions, or analysis context.

attributes.name: operator_acknowledged
attributes.description: Indicates whether the system operator has reviewed and acknowledged the contingency analysis results and any violations detected.
attributes.references: NERC TOP Operator Situational Awareness Requirements

attributes.name: operator_acknowledgment_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the system operator acknowledged the contingency analysis results. Null if not yet acknowledged.

attributes.name: pi_historian_tag_prefix
attributes.description: Tag prefix used for storing this contingency analysis run results in the OSIsoft PI historian for operational analytics and post-event review.

attributes.name: run_status
attributes.description: Current execution status of the contingency analysis run. Tracks the lifecycle from initiation through completion or failure.

attributes.name: run_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this contingency analysis execution was initiated by the EMS system. Represents the real-world operational moment of the analysis.

attributes.name: scada_snapshot_timestamp
attributes.business_glossary_term: Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) Snapshot Timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the SCADA telemetry snapshot used as input to the state estimator that preceded this contingency analysis. Establishes data lineage for compliance.

attributes.name: solution_method
attributes.description: The power flow calculation method used for this contingency analysis execution. Full AC provides highest accuracy; linear DC provides faster performance for screening studies.

attributes.name: stability_violations_detected
attributes.description: Number of system stability violations detected including transient stability, voltage stability, or oscillatory stability issues.

attributes.name: thermal_violations_detected
attributes.description: Number of thermal overload violations detected where transmission line or transformer loading exceeds emergency ratings under contingency conditions.

attributes.name: total_contingencies_evaluated
attributes.description: The total number of contingency scenarios evaluated during this analysis run. Includes N-1, N-2, and other credible contingencies per NERC TPL standards.
attributes.references: NERC TPL-001 Transmission System Planning Performance Requirements

attributes.name: total_violations_detected
attributes.description: Total number of reliability violations detected across all contingencies evaluated. Includes thermal overloads, voltage violations, and stability issues.

attributes.name: voltage_violations_detected
attributes.description: Number of bus voltage violations detected where voltage levels fall outside acceptable operating limits under contingency conditions.

attributes.name: worst_case_contingency_description
attributes.description: Human-readable description of the worst-case contingency scenario, typically describing the element(s) lost and the resulting system impact.

attributes.name: worst_case_severity_index
attributes.description: Numerical severity index for the worst-case contingency, typically representing the magnitude of the most severe violation (e.g., percent overload or per-unit voltage deviation).

products.name: contingency_violation
products.description: Individual violation record produced by a contingency analysis run for a specific contingency case. Captures the contingency reference, violated element (line, transformer, bus), violation type (thermal overload % of rating, voltage limit exceedance kV), pre-contingency and post-contingency values, applicable rating (normal/emergency/extreme), and operator corrective action status. SSOT for real-time N-1 security violations used in NERC TPL and TOP reliability reporting.
products.reference: NERC TPL-001 Violation Record

attributes.name: contingency_violation_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the contingency violation record. Primary key for the contingency violation entity.
attributes.references: NERC TPL-001 Transmission System Planning Performance Requirements

attributes.name: contingency_analysis_run_id
attributes.description: Reference to the parent contingency analysis execution that produced this violation. Links to the specific analysis run timestamp and configuration.

attributes.name: contingency_id
attributes.description: Reference to the specific contingency scenario (N-1, N-2, etc.) that was simulated and resulted in this violation. Identifies the outage condition tested.
attributes.references: NERC TPL-001 Transmission System Planning Performance Requirements

attributes.name: control_area_id
attributes.description: Reference to the balancing authority responsible for the violated element. Identifies the operational control area where the violation occurred.
attributes.references: NERC BAL-001 Real Power Balancing Control Performance

attributes.name: distribution_substation_id
attributes.description: Reference to the substation where the violated element is located. Links the violation to physical infrastructure location.

attributes.name: emergency_stock_event_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to supply.emergency_stock_event. Business justification: Contingency violations requiring physical corrective action (not just redispatch) trigger emergency stock mobilization. Essential for tracking material deployment decisions, FEMA reimbursement eligibi

attributes.name: employee_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the system operator or dispatcher who acknowledged or acted on the violation. Used for audit trail and accountability.

attributes.name: scada_point_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) Point ID
attributes.description: SCADA telemetry point identifier for the violated element. Links the violation to real-time monitoring data in the SCADA system.

attributes.name: acknowledged_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the violation alarm has been acknowledged by an operator. True if acknowledged, false if still requiring attention.

attributes.name: acknowledged_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the violation alarm was acknowledged by an operator. Null if not yet acknowledged.

attributes.name: alarm_priority
attributes.description: Priority level assigned to the violation alarm in the EMS operator interface. Determines visual and audible alarm presentation to operators.

attributes.name: analysis_model_version
attributes.description: Version identifier of the power flow or stability model used for the contingency analysis. Ensures traceability of analysis results to specific model configurations.
attributes.references: NERC MOD-032 Data for Power System Modeling and Analysis

attributes.name: contingency_case_name
attributes.description: Human-readable name of the contingency scenario tested (e.g., 'Loss of Line 345-123', 'Generator Unit 5 Trip'). Provides operator-friendly identification of the simulated outage.
attributes.references: NERC TPL-001 Transmission System Planning Performance Requirements

attributes.name: contingency_probability
attributes.description: Estimated probability of the contingency event occurring (0.0 to 1.0). Used for risk-based contingency ranking and prioritization.
attributes.references: NERC TPL-001 Transmission System Planning Performance Requirements

attributes.name: corrective_action_description
attributes.description: Free-text description of the corrective actions taken or planned to mitigate the violation (e.g., 'Reduce generation at Unit 3 by 50 MW', 'Open breaker at Station A').

attributes.name: corrective_action_status
attributes.description: Current status of operator corrective actions to resolve the violation. Tracks the lifecycle of violation mitigation from detection to resolution.

attributes.name: corrective_action_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when corrective action was initiated or completed by the operator. Null if no action has been taken yet.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this violation record was first created in the system. Audit trail for record lifecycle tracking.

attributes.name: data_source_system
attributes.description: Name of the source system or application that generated this violation record (e.g., 'GE EMS', 'Siemens Spectrum PowerOn', 'OSI Monarch'). Used for data lineage and troubleshooting.

attributes.name: ems_system_name
attributes.description: Name of the EMS or contingency analysis application that generated the violation record (e.g., 'GE PSLF', 'Siemens Spectrum', 'OSI Monarch').

attributes.name: last_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this violation record was last modified. Tracks the most recent change to any field in the record.

attributes.name: limit_value
attributes.description: The applicable operating limit threshold that was exceeded (e.g., thermal rating in MW, voltage limit in kV). Defines the boundary of acceptable operation.
attributes.references: NERC FAC-011 System Operating Limits Methodology

attributes.name: nerc_category
attributes.business_glossary_term: NERC (North American Electric Reliability Corporation) Category
attributes.description: NERC TPL planning event category classification (P0 through P7) that this contingency represents. Defines the severity and likelihood of the contingency scenario. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: P0|P1|P2|P3|P4|P5|P6|P7 — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: NERC TPL-001 Transmission System Planning Performance Requirements

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-form text field for operator comments, analysis notes, or additional context about the violation. Used for post-event review and documentation.

attributes.name: operator_action_required
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether immediate operator intervention is required to mitigate the violation. True if corrective action is needed, false if informational only.

attributes.name: pi_tag_name
attributes.description: OSIsoft PI historian tag name for the violated element measurement. Enables integration with PI historian for post-event analysis and trending.

attributes.name: post_contingency_value
attributes.description: Simulated or calculated value of the monitored parameter after the contingency event. Represents the stressed system condition that triggered the violation.

attributes.name: pre_contingency_value
attributes.description: Measured or estimated value of the monitored parameter (MW loading, voltage kV, etc.) before the contingency event. Baseline condition for comparison.

attributes.name: rating_duration_minutes
attributes.description: Time duration in minutes for which the applicable rating is valid (e.g., 15-minute emergency rating, 4-hour emergency rating). Null for continuous normal ratings.

attributes.name: rating_type
attributes.description: Classification of the equipment rating that was violated. Identifies whether the violation is against normal, emergency, or extreme operating limits.

attributes.name: resolution_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the violation was resolved and the system returned to secure operating limits. Null if violation is still active.

attributes.name: risk_score
attributes.description: Calculated risk score combining violation severity, probability, and impact. Used for prioritizing violations in operator displays and reports.

attributes.name: time_to_violation_seconds
attributes.description: Simulated time in seconds from the contingency event initiation to the violation occurrence. Indicates how quickly the system degrades post-contingency.

attributes.name: unit_of_measure
attributes.description: Unit of measurement for the violation values (MW for thermal, kV for voltage, etc.). Provides context for interpreting pre/post-contingency and limit values.
attributes.references: IEEE Std 260.1 Standard Letter Symbols for Units of Measurement

attributes.name: violated_element_name
attributes.description: Human-readable name or designation of the violated grid element (e.g., 'Line 345kV Smith-Jones', 'Transformer T-123'). Provides operator-friendly identification.
attributes.references: NERC FAC-011 System Operating Limits Methodology

attributes.name: violated_element_reference
attributes.description: Reference to the specific grid element (transmission line, transformer, bus, generator) that experienced the limit violation in the post-contingency state.
attributes.references: NERC FAC-011 System Operating Limits Methodology

attributes.name: violated_element_type
attributes.description: Classification of the grid element that experienced the violation. Categorizes the equipment type for analysis and reporting purposes.

attributes.name: violation_magnitude
attributes.description: Absolute difference between the post-contingency value and the limit value. Quantifies the extent of the violation in native units (MW, kV, etc.).
attributes.references: NERC FAC-011 System Operating Limits Methodology

attributes.name: violation_percentage
attributes.description: Percentage by which the post-contingency value exceeds the limit. Calculated as ((post_contingency_value - limit_value) / limit_value) * 100. Used for relative severity assessment.
attributes.references: NERC FAC-011 System Operating Limits Methodology

attributes.name: violation_severity
attributes.description: Severity classification of the violation based on magnitude and operational impact. Used for prioritization of operator corrective actions.

attributes.name: violation_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the contingency violation was detected by the analysis engine. Represents the real-time or study timestamp of the violation occurrence.

attributes.name: violation_type
attributes.description: Category of the limit violation detected. Identifies whether the violation is thermal (loading), voltage (magnitude), or stability-related.
attributes.references: NERC FAC-011 System Operating Limits Methodology

attributes.name: voltage_level_kv
attributes.description: Nominal voltage level in kilovolts of the violated element. Used for categorizing violations by voltage class (transmission vs sub-transmission).

products.name: agc_signal
products.description: Time-series transactional record of Automatic Generation Control (AGC) regulation signals and Area Control Error (ACE) computations for the balancing authority control area. AGC attributes include generating unit reference, base point (MW), regulation raise/lower signal (MW), regulation reserve deployed (MW), and response rate (MW/min). ACE attributes (same time grain) include raw ACE (MW), filtered ACE (MW), 10-minute average ACE, CPS1/CPS2 compliance indicators, frequency bias setting (MW/0.1 Hz), actual system frequency (Hz), scheduled frequency (Hz), and net interchange deviation (MW). Sourced from OSIsoft PI historian AGC and ACE tags. SSOT for all AGC regulation and ACE compliance data — used for NERC BAL-001 CPS1/CPS2 compliance evidence, NERC BAL-003 frequency response obligation, frequency regulation performance tracking, and ancillary services settlement.
products.reference: NERC BAL-001 AGC / OSIsoft PI AGC Tags

attributes.name: agc_signal_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the AGC signal record. Primary key for the agc_signal product.

attributes.name: agc_control_area_id
attributes.description: Reference to the balancing authority control area issuing this AGC signal.

attributes.name: generating_unit_id
attributes.description: Reference to the generating unit receiving this AGC regulation signal.

attributes.name: obligation_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.obligation. Business justification: AGC operations directly implement NERC BAL-001 and BAL-002 standards for frequency control and CPS compliance. Each AGC signal execution must be traceable to the governing obligation for CPS1/CPS2 com

attributes.name: primary_control_area_id
attributes.description: FK to grid.control_area.control_area_id — AGC regulation signals and ACE computations are performed for a specific balancing authority control area. This link is required for NERC BAL-001 CPS1/CPS2 compliance reporting scoped to the correct B

attributes.name: scada_point_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) Point ID
attributes.description: The SCADA system point identifier associated with this AGC signal measurement.

attributes.name: to_control_area_id
attributes.description: FK to grid.control_area.control_area_id — AGC signals and ACE records (now merged) are computed for a specific balancing authority control area. This FK is essential for multi-area operations and NERC BAL compliance reporting.

attributes.name: trade_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to trading.trade. Business justification: AGC regulation deployment often fulfills ancillary service trades or regulation market awards. Linking enables real-time trade performance tracking, settlement quantity validation, and compliance veri

attributes.name: actual_frequency_hz
attributes.description: The actual measured system frequency in hertz (Hz) at the time of this AGC signal. Nominal frequency is 60.000 Hz in North America.

attributes.name: agc_mode
attributes.description: The operational mode of the Automatic Generation Control system at the time of this signal. Automatic mode means AGC is actively controlling generation; manual mode means operators are controlling generation manually.

attributes.name: ancillary_service_type
attributes.description: The type of ancillary service being provided by this AGC signal. Regulation services provide continuous balancing, while reserve services provide contingency response.

attributes.name: base_point_mw
attributes.description: The base generation setpoint in megawatts (MW) for the generating unit before AGC regulation adjustment.

attributes.name: cps1_compliant
attributes.description: Boolean indicator of whether this AGC signal interval meets NERC CPS1 compliance criteria. CPS1 measures the balancing authority's ability to follow its own generation schedule on a one-minute basis.

attributes.name: cps2_compliant
attributes.description: Boolean indicator of whether this AGC signal interval meets NERC CPS2 compliance criteria. CPS2 measures the balancing authority's ability to limit unscheduled power flows on a 10-minute average basis.

attributes.name: data_source_system
attributes.description: The name of the operational system from which this AGC signal record was sourced (e.g., OSIsoft PI, EMS, SCADA).

attributes.name: ems_system_name
attributes.description: The name of the Energy Management System that generated this AGC signal.

attributes.name: filtered_ace_mw
attributes.description: The filtered Area Control Error in megawatts (MW) after applying smoothing algorithms to remove noise and transient spikes.

attributes.name: frequency_bias_setting_mw_per_0_1_hz
attributes.description: The frequency bias setting in megawatts per 0.1 hertz (MW/0.1 Hz) used in the ACE calculation. Represents the balancing authority's expected MW response to a 0.1 Hz frequency deviation.

attributes.name: interconnection_name
attributes.description: The name of the North American electric interconnection to which this control area belongs. The four major interconnections are Eastern, Western, Texas (ERCOT), and Quebec.

attributes.name: nerc_region
attributes.business_glossary_term: North American Electric Reliability Corporation (NERC) Region
attributes.description: The NERC regional entity code responsible for reliability oversight of this control area (e.g., WECC, SERC, MRO, NPCC, RF, TRE).

attributes.name: net_interchange_actual_mw
attributes.description: The actual net interchange power flow in megawatts (MW) across all tie lines for the control area at this timestamp.

attributes.name: net_interchange_deviation_mw
attributes.description: The deviation between actual and scheduled net interchange in megawatts (MW). Calculated as (Actual Net Interchange - Scheduled Net Interchange).

attributes.name: net_interchange_scheduled_mw
attributes.description: The scheduled net interchange power flow in megawatts (MW) across all tie lines for the control area at this timestamp.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for additional comments, annotations, or operational notes related to this AGC signal event.

attributes.name: pi_tag_name
attributes.description: The OSIsoft PI historian tag name from which this AGC signal data was sourced. Used for traceability back to the SCADA system.

attributes.name: raw_ace_mw
attributes.description: The unfiltered Area Control Error in megawatts (MW) computed at the same time grain as the AGC signal. Raw ACE = (Actual Net Interchange - Scheduled Net Interchange) - (Frequency Bias Setting) × (Actual Frequency - Scheduled Frequency).

attributes.name: record_created_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this AGC signal record was first created in the data platform.

attributes.name: record_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this AGC signal record was last updated in the data platform.

attributes.name: regulation_direction
attributes.description: The direction of the regulation signal. Raise indicates the unit should increase generation, lower indicates decrease, neutral indicates no change.

attributes.name: regulation_reserve_deployed_mw
attributes.description: The amount of regulation reserve capacity deployed in megawatts (MW) in response to the AGC signal.

attributes.name: regulation_signal_mw
attributes.description: The AGC regulation signal in megawatts (MW) sent to the generating unit. Positive values indicate raise signal, negative values indicate lower signal.

attributes.name: response_rate_mw_per_min
attributes.description: The rate at which the generating unit responds to the AGC signal, measured in megawatts per minute (MW/min).

attributes.name: rto_iso_code
attributes.business_glossary_term: Regional Transmission Organization (RTO) or Independent System Operator (ISO) Code
attributes.description: The code identifying the RTO or ISO responsible for coordinating this control area's operations (e.g., PJM, MISO, CAISO, ERCOT, NYISO, ISO-NE, SPP).

attributes.name: scheduled_frequency_hz
attributes.description: The scheduled target system frequency in hertz (Hz). Typically 60.000 Hz for North American interconnections.

attributes.name: settlement_interval
attributes.description: The settlement interval number within the operating day, used for ancillary services market settlement. Typically 5-minute or 15-minute intervals.

attributes.name: signal_quality_code
attributes.description: Quality indicator for the AGC signal data. Good indicates reliable data, uncertain indicates questionable data, bad indicates invalid data, substituted indicates estimated or replaced data.

attributes.name: signal_timestamp
attributes.description: The precise timestamp when this AGC signal and ACE computation were recorded. Primary event timestamp for this transactional record.

attributes.name: ten_minute_average_ace_mw
attributes.description: The rolling 10-minute average of Area Control Error in megawatts (MW), used for NERC CPS2 compliance calculations.

attributes.name: unit_response_status
attributes.description: The status of the generating unit's response to the AGC signal. Indicates whether the unit is following the signal as expected.

products.name: ace_record
products.description: Time-series record of Area Control Error (ACE) computed by the EMS for the balancing authority control area. Captures UTC timestamp, raw ACE (MW), filtered ACE (MW), 10-minute average ACE (MW), CPS1 compliance indicator, CPS2 compliance indicator, frequency bias setting (MW/0.1 Hz), actual system frequency (Hz), scheduled frequency (Hz), and net interchange deviation (MW). SSOT for NERC BAL-001 CPS1/CPS2 compliance evidence and frequency regulation performance.
products.reference: NERC BAL-001 CPS1/CPS2 ACE

attributes.name: ace_record_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the ACE record. Primary key for the time-series ACE dataset.

attributes.name: control_area_id
attributes.description: Foreign key reference to the balancing authority control area for which this ACE value was computed.

attributes.name: obligation_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.obligation. Business justification: ACE measurements are the foundation of NERC BAL-001 compliance for balancing authorities. Every ACE record serves as evidence for CPS1/CPS2 compliance calculations. This link enables automated complia

attributes.name: scada_point_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) Point ID
attributes.description: SCADA system point identifier for the ACE calculation output. Links this record to the underlying SCADA telemetry infrastructure.

attributes.name: ace_10min_avg_mw
attributes.description: Rolling 10-minute average of ACE values in megawatts. Critical metric for NERC CPS2 compliance evaluation, which requires the 10-minute average ACE to remain within L10 limits.

attributes.name: ace_filtered_mw
attributes.description: Filtered Area Control Error value in megawatts after applying smoothing algorithms to remove noise and transient spikes. Used for AGC control actions.

attributes.name: ace_raw_mw
attributes.description: Raw unfiltered Area Control Error value in megawatts as computed by the EMS. Represents the instantaneous imbalance between scheduled and actual interchange plus frequency bias contribution.

attributes.name: actual_frequency_hz
attributes.description: Actual measured interconnection frequency in hertz at the time of this ACE calculation. Nominal frequency is 60.000 Hz for North American interconnections (Eastern, Western, Texas) and 50.000 Hz for other regions.

attributes.name: agc_enabled
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether AGC was enabled and actively issuing control signals to generating units at the time of this ACE measurement.

attributes.name: agc_mode
attributes.description: Operating mode of the AGC system at the time of this ACE measurement. Automatic mode indicates AGC is actively controlling generation; manual mode indicates operators are manually balancing; off indicates AGC is disabled; test indicates AGC is in test/simulation mode.

attributes.name: calculation_method
attributes.description: Method used to compute this ACE value. Standard indicates normal EMS calculation; backup indicates calculation by backup system; manual indicates operator calculation; estimated indicates interpolated or reconstructed value.

attributes.name: cps1_compliant
attributes.description: Boolean indicator of whether this ACE measurement contributes positively to CPS1 compliance. CPS1 measures the balancing authority's contribution to interconnection frequency error over a rolling 12-month period.

attributes.name: cps2_compliant
attributes.description: Boolean indicator of whether the 10-minute average ACE is within the L10 limit for this measurement period. CPS2 requires the balancing authority to maintain its 10-minute average ACE within specific bounds at least 90% of clock-10-minute periods.

attributes.name: data_quality_code
attributes.description: Quality indicator for this ACE measurement. Good indicates validated real-time data; suspect indicates potential data quality issues; bad indicates known invalid data; estimated indicates calculated/interpolated value; manual indicates operator-entered value.

attributes.name: data_source_system
attributes.description: Name or identifier of the source system that provided this ACE record (e.g., EMS vendor name, PI historian instance, SCADA system identifier).

attributes.name: disturbance_flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether a reportable disturbance event was occurring during this ACE measurement period. Disturbances may trigger special ACE evaluation rules under NERC standards.

attributes.name: ems_system_name
attributes.description: Name or identifier of the EMS system that computed this ACE value. Supports environments with multiple EMS instances or backup systems.

attributes.name: frequency_bias_setting_mw_per_0_1_hz
attributes.description: The frequency bias setting in megawatts per 0.1 Hz used in the ACE calculation for this measurement period. Represents the balancing authority's obligation to respond to frequency deviations. Negative value indicates the BA will increase generation when frequency drops.

attributes.name: frequency_deviation_hz
attributes.description: Difference between actual and scheduled frequency in hertz (actual minus scheduled). Positive values indicate over-frequency; negative values indicate under-frequency.

attributes.name: ime_mw
attributes.description: Interchange meter error correction term in megawatts applied to the ACE calculation to account for known metering inaccuracies on tie lines.

attributes.name: interconnection_name
attributes.description: Name of the North American interconnection to which this balancing authority belongs. Eastern, Western, and Texas (ERCOT) are the three major asynchronous interconnections in North America; Quebec operates as a separate interconnection.

attributes.name: l10_limit_mw
attributes.description: The L10 limit in megawatts for CPS2 compliance evaluation. Represents the maximum allowable 10-minute average ACE magnitude. Calculated as 1.65 times epsilon10 (the root-mean-square of the balancing authority's 10-minute average ACE over 12 months).

attributes.name: measurement_timestamp_utc
attributes.description: UTC timestamp when the ACE measurement was captured by the EMS. Represents the real-world event time for this ACE calculation cycle, typically at 4-6 second intervals per NERC requirements.

attributes.name: nerc_region
attributes.business_glossary_term: North American Electric Reliability Corporation (NERC) Region
attributes.description: NERC regional entity code for the balancing authority. WECC=Western Electricity Coordinating Council, TRE=Texas Reliability Entity, MRO=Midwest Reliability Organization, NPCC=Northeast Power Coordinating Council, RF=ReliabilityFirst, SERC=SERC Reliability Corporation, SPP=Southwest Power Pool, FRCC=Florida Reliability Coordinating Council. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: WECC|TRE|MRO|NPCC|RF|SERC|SPP|FRCC — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: net_actual_interchange_mw
attributes.description: Net actual interchange power flow in megawatts across all tie lines connecting this balancing authority to neighboring control areas. Positive values indicate net export; negative values indicate net import.

attributes.name: net_interchange_deviation_mw
attributes.description: Difference between net actual interchange and net scheduled interchange in megawatts (actual minus scheduled). A key component of the ACE calculation formula.

attributes.name: net_scheduled_interchange_mw
attributes.description: Net scheduled interchange power flow in megawatts for this measurement period, including all confirmed interchange transactions and dynamic schedules.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for operational notes, annotations, or explanations related to this ACE measurement. May include operator comments about unusual conditions, data quality issues, or special events.

attributes.name: pi_historian_tag
attributes.description: OSIsoft PI historian tag name for this ACE measurement point. Enables traceability to the real-time data historian for post-event analysis and compliance reporting.

attributes.name: primary_frequency_response_adjustment_mw
attributes.description: Adjustment term in megawatts applied to ACE during primary frequency response events to account for the balancing authority's contribution to arresting frequency decline or rise.

attributes.name: record_created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this ACE record was first inserted into the data historian or lakehouse. Distinct from measurement_timestamp_utc, which represents the real-world event time.

attributes.name: scheduled_frequency_hz
attributes.description: Scheduled interconnection frequency in hertz for this measurement period. Typically 60.000 Hz for North American grids, but may vary during time error correction periods.

attributes.name: state_estimator_solution_valid
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether the EMS state estimator had a valid converged solution at the time of this ACE calculation. Invalid state estimator solutions may affect ACE accuracy.

attributes.name: tie_line_meter_count

attributes.name: tie_line_meter_failures

attributes.name: time_error_correction_active
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether the interconnection was in time error correction mode during this measurement period. Time error correction adjusts scheduled frequency to correct accumulated time error.

products.name: interchange_schedule
products.description: Master and transactional record of energy interchange schedules between the balancing authority and neighboring control areas or counterparties. Captures schedule ID, counterparty entity (NERC registered), interchange direction (import/export), scheduled MW by hour, e-Tag reference number, NERC TAG ID, effective start/end timestamps, schedule type (firm/non-firm), curtailment status, and OASIS posting reference. products.reference: NERC BAL-002 / NAESB e-Tag

attributes.name: counterparty_id

attributes.name: energy_schedule_id

attributes.name: interchange_control_area_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the balancing authority control area that owns this interchange schedule.

attributes.name: primary_control_area_id
attributes.description: FK to grid.control_area.control_area_id — Interchange schedules define energy flows between control areas. The FK to control_area identifies which balancing authority is party to the schedule — required for NERC BAL-002 compliance.

attributes.name: regulatory_filing_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.regulatory_filing. attributes.name: transmission_path_id

attributes.name: approved_timestamp

attributes.name: created_timestamp

attributes.name: curtailment_status

attributes.name: data_source_system

attributes.name: effective_end_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the interchange schedule ends and energy flow ceases. Marks the conclusion of the scheduled interchange period.

attributes.name: effective_start_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the interchange schedule becomes effective and energy flow begins. Marks the start of the scheduled interchange period.

attributes.name: etag_reference_number
attributes.description: Electronic tag reference number assigned by the NERC tag authority for this interchange transaction. Links to the OASIS e-Tag system.

attributes.name: interchange_direction
attributes.description: Direction of energy flow relative to the balancing authority. Import indicates energy flowing into the control area; export indicates energy flowing out.

attributes.name: last_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this interchange schedule record was most recently modified. Tracks the latest change for audit and version control.

attributes.name: market_type
attributes.description: Classification of the market context for the interchange schedule. Day-ahead schedules are submitted in advance; real-time schedules are for immediate delivery; bilateral schedules are direct contracts between parties.

attributes.name: nerc_tag_reference

attributes.description: NERC-assigned tag identifier for the interchange schedule. Used for compliance reporting and audit trail.

attributes.name: notes

attributes.name: oasis_posting_reference

attributes.name: priority_level

attributes.name: ramp_rate_mw_per_minute

attributes.name: schedule_number

attributes.name: schedule_status

attributes.name: schedule_type

products.name: load_forecast
products.description: Operational load forecast records produced by the EMS load forecasting function for the control area. Captures forecast run timestamp, forecast horizon type (hour-ahead, day-ahead, week-ahead), target hour, forecasted system load (MW), weather-adjusted load (MW), temperature input (°F), humidity input (%), forecast model version, and actual load (MW) populated post-interval for accuracy tracking. Distinct from the long-term capacity forecast (owned by forecast domain) — this is the real-time/short-term operational load forecast used by AGC and dispatch.
products.reference: EMS Load Forecasting / NERC BAL-001

attributes.name: load_forecast_id
attributes.description: Primary key for load_forecast

attributes.name: control_area_id
attributes.description: FK to grid.control_area.control_area_id — Operational load forecasts are produced for a specific control area. This link scopes forecasts to the correct BA for AGC and dispatch coordination.

attributes.name: forecast_model_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to forecast.model. Business justification: Grid load forecasts should link to the forecast model used for accuracy tracking, model governance, and regulatory compliance. Model metadata (version, type, accuracy metrics) is essential for forecas

attributes.name: forecast_run_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to forecast.run. Business justification: Grid domain load forecasts should reference the forecast run metadata for traceability, model versioning, and forecast accuracy analysis. Operators need to know which forecast run produced the values

attributes.name: forecast_zone_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to forecast.zone. Business justification: Grid load forecasts are spatially scoped to forecast zones for geographic aggregation, weather correlation, and substation-level planning. Forecast zones enable hierarchical load forecasting from feed

attributes.name: load_control_area_id
attributes.description: Reference to the control area for which this load forecast was generated.

attributes.name: load_forecast_for_control_area
attributes.description: FK to grid.control_area.control_area_id — Load forecasts are produced for a specific control area. Required for AGC and dispatch operations scoping.

attributes.name: to_control_area_id
attributes.description: FK to grid.control_area.control_area_id — Operational load forecasts are produced for a specific control area. This FK scopes the forecast to the correct balancing authority boundary.

attributes.name: actual_load_mw
attributes.description: The actual measured system load in megawatts (MW) for the target interval, populated post-interval from SCADA telemetry for forecast accuracy tracking and model tuning.

attributes.name: agc_participation_flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this forecast is actively used by the Automatic Generation Control system for real-time generation dispatch and frequency regulation.

attributes.name: base_load_mw
attributes.description: The baseline load component in megawatts (MW) representing the minimum continuous demand independent of weather or time-of-day variations.

attributes.name: behind_the_meter_generation_mw
attributes.description: The estimated distributed energy resource generation in megawatts (MW) occurring behind customer meters (rooftop solar, battery storage) that reduces net load visible to the grid.

attributes.name: cloud_cover_input_percentage
attributes.description: The cloud cover percentage used as input to the load forecasting model, influencing solar radiation and temperature-driven load patterns.

attributes.name: confidence_level_percentage
attributes.description: The statistical confidence level of the forecast expressed as a percentage, indicating the model's certainty in the predicted load value.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this load forecast record was first created and persisted in the data platform.

attributes.name: data_source_system
attributes.description: The name of the source system or application that originated this load forecast record (e.g., EMS vendor name, forecasting module identifier).

attributes.name: day_type
attributes.description: The classification of the target day used in the forecast model to account for load pattern variations (weekday, weekend, holiday, or special event day).

attributes.name: demand_response_adjustment_mw
attributes.description: The expected load reduction in megawatts (MW) from active demand response programs during the target interval, subtracted from gross load to calculate net forecasted load.

attributes.name: ems_system_name
attributes.description: The name or identifier of the Energy Management System that generated this load forecast record.

attributes.name: forecast_error_mw
attributes.description: The difference between forecasted load and actual load in megawatts (MW), calculated as (actual_load_mw - forecasted_load_mw), used for accuracy metrics and model performance evaluation.

attributes.name: forecast_error_percentage
attributes.description: The forecast error expressed as a percentage of actual load, calculated as ((actual_load_mw - forecasted_load_mw) / actual_load_mw) * 100, used for model accuracy assessment.

attributes.name: forecast_horizon_type
attributes.description: The temporal horizon category of the forecast indicating the planning timeframe (hour-ahead for AGC, day-ahead for unit commitment, week-ahead for resource planning).

attributes.name: forecast_lower_bound_mw
attributes.description: The lower confidence interval bound for the forecasted load in megawatts (MW), representing the low-end estimate for minimum generation and reserve planning.

attributes.name: forecast_run_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when the forecast model was executed and this forecast record was produced by the EMS load forecasting function.

attributes.name: forecast_status
attributes.description: The lifecycle status of the forecast record indicating whether it is preliminary, final, revised, superseded by a newer forecast, or archived.

attributes.name: forecast_upper_bound_mw
attributes.description: The upper confidence interval bound for the forecasted load in megawatts (MW), representing the high-end estimate for reserve planning and contingency analysis.

attributes.name: forecasted_load_mw
attributes.description: The predicted system load in megawatts (MW) for the target interval as calculated by the EMS load forecasting model.

attributes.name: humidity_input_percentage
attributes.description: The relative humidity percentage used as input to the load forecasting model, influencing cooling load and weather-sensitive demand patterns.

attributes.name: last_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this load forecast record was last modified or updated, typically when actual load values are populated post-interval.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for operational notes, comments, or explanations regarding forecast anomalies, model adjustments, or special conditions affecting this forecast.

attributes.name: peak_indicator
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether the target interval is expected to be a system peak load period, used for resource adequacy and reserve planning.

attributes.name: pi_historian_tag
attributes.description: The OSIsoft PI historian tag name associated with this load forecast time series for integration with the real-time data historian and operational analytics.

attributes.name: revision_number
attributes.description: The sequential revision number for this forecast target interval, incremented each time a new forecast is issued for the same target timestamp.

attributes.name: scada_integration_flag
attributes.business_glossary_term: Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) Integration Flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this forecast record is integrated with SCADA telemetry for real-time actual load comparison and AGC feedback.

attributes.name: season
attributes.description: The meteorological season classification for the target interval, used to apply seasonal load pattern adjustments in the forecasting model.

attributes.name: target_timestamp
attributes.description: The specific date and time for which the load forecast applies (the future interval being forecasted).

attributes.name: temperature_input_f
attributes.description: The temperature value in degrees Fahrenheit used as input to the load forecasting model, typically representing the control area weighted average or key city temperature.

attributes.name: weather_adjusted_load_mw
attributes.description: The forecasted load in megawatts (MW) after applying weather normalization adjustments based on temperature, humidity, and other meteorological inputs.

attributes.name: weather_sensitive_load_mw
attributes.description: The portion of forecasted load in megawatts (MW) that is driven by weather conditions (heating, cooling, and weather-dependent industrial processes).

attributes.name: wind_speed_input_mph
attributes.description: The wind speed in miles per hour used as input to the load forecasting model, affecting heating and cooling load calculations.

products.name: generation_dispatch
products.description: Transactional record of economic dispatch and unit commitment instructions issued by the EMS to generating units within the control area. Captures dispatch timestamp, generating unit reference, dispatch MW setpoint, economic merit order rank, operating cost ($/MWh), ramp rate (MW/min), minimum/maximum operating limits (MW), dispatch type (economic/emergency/must-run), and operator override indicator. Supports NERC BAL compliance, fuel cost optimization, and generation operations coordination.
products.reference: EMS Economic Dispatch / Unit Commitment

attributes.name: generation_dispatch_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the generation dispatch instruction record. Primary key for the generation dispatch transaction.

attributes.name: control_area_id
attributes.description: FK to grid.control_area.control_area_id — Dispatch instructions are issued within a control area's generation fleet. FK to control_area is needed for BAL compliance and to scope dispatch to the correct balancing authority.

attributes.name: employee_id
attributes.description: The identifier of the system operator who issued or approved this dispatch instruction. Populated for manual dispatches or operator overrides.

attributes.name: fuel_supply_contract_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to supply.fuel_supply_contract. Business justification: Economic dispatch optimization requires fuel contract terms (pricing index, take-or-pay obligations, delivery constraints) to calculate operating costs and ensure contract compliance during unit commi

attributes.name: generating_unit_id
attributes.description: Reference to the generating unit receiving this dispatch instruction within the control area.

attributes.name: generation_control_area_id
attributes.description: Reference to the control area issuing this dispatch instruction.

attributes.name: generation_dispatch_within_control_area
attributes.description: FK to grid.control_area.control_area_id — Economic dispatch instructions are issued to generating units within a control area. Required for NERC BAL compliance scoping and dispatch optimization.

attributes.name: internal_order_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.internal_order. Business justification: Economic dispatch decisions often relate to specific internal orders for fuel procurement, emissions compliance projects, or ancillary service provision. Links operational dispatch to financial commit

attributes.name: ppa_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to trading.ppa. Business justification: Many generation dispatch instructions fulfill PPA delivery obligations. Linking enables real-time PPA compliance monitoring, settlement validation, and curtailment tracking. Essential for renewable en

attributes.name: scada_point_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) Point Identifier (ID)
attributes.description: Reference to the SCADA point used to monitor the actual output of the generating unit in response to this dispatch instruction.

attributes.name: trade_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to trading.trade. Business justification: Dispatch instructions often execute physical delivery obligations from bilateral energy trades. Operators need trade context for dispatch compliance verification, settlement reconciliation, and audit

attributes.name: actual_output_mw
attributes.description: The actual real power output in megawatts (MW) achieved by the generating unit in response to this dispatch instruction, as measured by SCADA telemetry. Nullable until the unit responds.
attributes.references: NERC BAL-001 Real Power Balancing Control Performance

attributes.name: agc_participation_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this dispatch instruction is part of an Automatic Generation Control (AGC) signal for real-time frequency regulation. True if AGC-controlled, false if manual or economic dispatch.
attributes.references: NERC BAL-001 Real Power Balancing Control Performance

attributes.name: ancillary_service_type
attributes.description: The type of ancillary service this dispatch instruction is providing, if applicable. None indicates energy-only dispatch. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: regulation_up|regulation_down|spinning_reserve|non_spinning_reserve|voltage_support|black_start|none — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: compliance_tolerance_mw
attributes.description: The acceptable deviation in megawatts (MW) between the dispatch setpoint and actual output for the unit to be considered compliant with the dispatch instruction.
attributes.references: NERC BAL-001 Real Power Balancing Control Performance

attributes.name: contingency_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this dispatch instruction was issued in response to a contingency event (transmission outage, generation loss, or other reliability event). True if contingency-related, false otherwise.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this dispatch record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking.

attributes.name: data_source_system
attributes.description: The name of the source system from which this dispatch record originated. Typically the EMS system name or SCADA integration platform.

attributes.name: dispatch_compliance_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the generating unit complied with the dispatch instruction within the required tolerance and timeframe. True if compliant, false if non-compliant. Used for NERC BAL compliance reporting.
attributes.references: NERC BAL-001 Real Power Balancing Control Performance

attributes.name: dispatch_mw_setpoint
attributes.description: The target real power output in megawatts (MW) that the generating unit is instructed to achieve. This is the primary dispatch instruction value.

attributes.name: dispatch_number
attributes.description: Business identifier for the dispatch instruction, typically generated by the Energy Management System (EMS) for operational tracking and audit purposes.

attributes.name: dispatch_reason_code
attributes.description: The operational reason code explaining why this dispatch instruction was issued. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: economic_optimization|frequency_regulation|voltage_support|congestion_management|reserve_activation|emergency_response|must_run_contract|renewable_curtailment|manual_override|load_following|spinning_reserve|non_spinning_reserve|black_start — promote to reference product]

attributes.name: dispatch_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the dispatch instruction: issued (sent to unit), acknowledged (received by unit), active (unit ramping or at setpoint), completed (instruction fulfilled), superseded (replaced by new instruction), or cancelled (instruction voided).

attributes.name: dispatch_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when the dispatch instruction was issued by the EMS to the generating unit. This is the principal business event timestamp for the dispatch transaction.
attributes.references: NERC BAL-001 Real Power Balancing Control Performance

attributes.name: dispatch_type
attributes.description: The classification of the dispatch instruction indicating the operational reason for the dispatch: economic (cost-optimized), emergency (reliability event), must-run (contractual or reliability requirement), regulation (frequency control), manual (operator override), or AGC (Automatic Generation Control).
attributes.references: NERC BAL-001 Real Power Balancing Control Performance

attributes.name: economic_merit_order_rank
attributes.description: The rank of this generating unit in the economic dispatch merit order at the time of dispatch, where 1 is the lowest-cost unit. Used for economic dispatch optimization and fuel cost minimization.

attributes.name: effective_end_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when the dispatch instruction expires or is superseded by a subsequent dispatch instruction. Nullable for open-ended dispatches.
attributes.references: NERC BAL-001 Real Power Balancing Control Performance

attributes.name: effective_start_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when the dispatch instruction becomes effective and the generating unit is expected to begin ramping to the target setpoint.
attributes.references: NERC BAL-001 Real Power Balancing Control Performance

attributes.name: emissions_rate_co2_lbs_per_mwh
attributes.business_glossary_term: Carbon Dioxide (CO2) Emissions Rate Pounds per Megawatt-Hour (MWh)
attributes.description: The carbon dioxide emissions rate in pounds per megawatt-hour (lbs/MWh) for this generating unit at the dispatch setpoint. Used for environmental compliance and carbon accounting.
attributes.references: EPA Clean Air Act Title IV

attributes.name: ems_system_name
attributes.description: The name or identifier of the Energy Management System (EMS) that issued this dispatch instruction. Used for multi-EMS environments and data lineage tracking.

attributes.name: fuel_type
attributes.description: The primary fuel type of the generating unit receiving this dispatch instruction. Used for fuel cost tracking and emissions reporting. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: coal|natural_gas|nuclear|hydro|wind|solar|biomass|oil|geothermal — 9 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: last_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this dispatch record was last modified. Used for audit trail and change tracking.

attributes.name: locational_marginal_price
attributes.description: The locational marginal price in dollars per megawatt-hour ($/MWh) at the generating unit's point of interconnection at the time of dispatch. Used for market settlement and economic dispatch optimization.
attributes.references: FERC Order 888 Open Access Transmission Tariff

attributes.name: market_settlement_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this dispatch instruction is subject to wholesale market settlement with the RTO/ISO. True if market-settled, false if bilateral or internal dispatch.
attributes.references: FERC Order 888 Open Access Transmission Tariff

attributes.name: maximum_operating_limit_mw
attributes.description: The maximum continuous operating output in megawatts (MW) for the generating unit. The dispatch setpoint must be at or below this limit.
attributes.references: NERC MOD-024 Generator Frequency and Voltage Excursion Monitoring

attributes.name: minimum_operating_limit_mw
attributes.description: The minimum stable operating output in megawatts (MW) for the generating unit. The dispatch setpoint must be at or above this limit when the unit is online.
attributes.references: NERC MOD-024 Generator Frequency and Voltage Excursion Monitoring

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for operational notes, comments, or special instructions related to this dispatch instruction. Used for operator communication and post-event review.

attributes.name: operating_cost_per_mwh
attributes.description: The marginal operating cost in dollars per megawatt-hour ($/MWh) for this generating unit at the time of dispatch. Includes fuel cost, variable O&M, and emissions costs. Used for economic dispatch calculations.

attributes.name: operator_override_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this dispatch instruction was manually overridden by a system operator, bypassing the automated economic dispatch algorithm. True if operator-initiated, false if system-generated.

attributes.name: pi_tag_name
attributes.description: The OSIsoft PI historian tag name associated with this dispatch instruction for time-series data archival and post-event analysis.

attributes.name: ramp_rate_mw_per_min
attributes.description: The maximum rate at which the generating unit can change its output in megawatts per minute (MW/min). Used by the EMS to calculate the time required to reach the dispatch setpoint.
attributes.references: NERC BAL-001 Real Power Balancing Control Performance

attributes.name: response_time_seconds
attributes.description: The elapsed time in seconds from when the dispatch instruction was issued to when the generating unit reached the target setpoint within compliance tolerance. Nullable until the unit responds.
attributes.references: NERC BAL-001 Real Power Balancing Control Performance

attributes.name: rto_iso_code
attributes.business_glossary_term: Regional Transmission Organization (RTO) or Independent System Operator (ISO) Code
attributes.description: The code identifying the RTO or ISO market in which this dispatch instruction was issued, if applicable. Examples: PJM, CAISO, ERCOT, MISO, NYISO, ISO-NE, SPP.

products.name: grid_switching_order
products.description: Operational record of a switching order — a formal, sequenced set of switching steps issued by the system operator to field crews for network reconfiguration, isolation, or restoration. Order-level attributes include switching order number, issuing operator, target substation and equipment, safety clearance reference, pre/post-switching network state, execution timestamps, and completion status. Step-level detail (grain: one row per step) captures sequence number, device identifier, action type (open/close/tag/verify), device pre/post-action status, executing crew member, execution timestamp, and step completion status. SSOT for switching order management including granular step-by-step audit trail used in NERC TOP compliance, outage coordination, and post-event review.
products.reference: NERC TOP-001 / GE PowerOn ADMS Switching Order
