attributes.name: data_source_system
attributes.description: Name of the source system that provided this operating limit data (e.g., EMS, DLR system, engineering study database). Used for data lineage, reconciliation, and troubleshooting.

attributes.name: element_name
attributes.description: Human-readable name of the transmission element (e.g., line name, transformer designation, interface name) for operator displays and reporting.

attributes.name: element_reference
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the transmission element (line, transformer, interface) to which this operating limit applies. References the network model element in the EMS system.

attributes.name: element_type
attributes.description: Classification of the transmission element type to which the operating limit applies. Determines the applicable limit categories and rating methodologies.

attributes.name: emergency_rating_mva
attributes.description: Emergency operating limit in MVA for the transmission element under post-contingency conditions. This higher rating is allowed for a limited duration (typically 15 minutes to 4 hours) following a system disturbance.

attributes.name: ems_model_version
attributes.description: Version identifier of the EMS network model in which this operating limit is defined. Critical for change management, model synchronization, and audit trails.

attributes.name: ems_system_name
attributes.description: Name of the EMS system (e.g., GE ADMS, Siemens Spectrum, ABB Network Manager) that manages and enforces this operating limit. Used for multi-EMS environments and data lineage tracking.

attributes.name: from_bus_name
attributes.description: Name of the originating bus or substation for transmission line or transformer elements. Defines the topology and network connectivity for EMS modeling.

attributes.name: last_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this operating limit record was last modified. Tracks changes to ratings, limits, or metadata for change management and audit purposes.

attributes.name: limit_type
attributes.description: Category of operating limit being defined: normal MVA rating, emergency MVA rating, voltage upper limit, voltage lower limit, stability limit in MW, or thermal limit in MW. Determines the constraint type enforced by EMS contingency analysis.
attributes.references: NERC FAC-008 Facility Ratings, NERC FAC-011 System Operating Limits

attributes.name: max_conductor_temperature_c

attributes.name: nerc_fac_002_study_reference

attributes.description: Reference identifier for the NERC FAC-002 facility interconnection study or FAC-008 facility ratings methodology study that established this operating limit. Provides traceability to engineering analysis and regulatory compliance documentation.

attributes.name: normal_rating_mva

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text notes providing additional context, special operating instructions, temporary limit adjustments, or engineering rationale for this operating limit. Used by operators and engineers for situational awareness.

attributes.name: operational_status
attributes.description: Current operational status of the transmission element and its associated operating limits. In-service limits are actively enforced by EMS; out-of-service limits are inactive due to equipment outages.

attributes.name: operator_code
attributes.description: Code identifying the transmission operator responsible for real-time operation and monitoring of this element and its limits. May differ from owner in joint-use or RTO-operated facilities.

attributes.name: operator_display_flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this operating limit is displayed on EMS operator screens and alarm systems. True means operators receive real-time visibility and alarms for limit violations.

attributes.name: owner_code
attributes.description: Code identifying the transmission asset owner responsible for the physical equipment and its ratings. Used for cost allocation, maintenance responsibility, and regulatory reporting.

attributes.name: pi_tag_name
attributes.description: OSIsoft PI historian tag name for archiving this operating limit time-series data. Enables historical trending, post-event analysis, and integration with asset performance analytics.

attributes.name: rating_method
attributes.description: Method used to determine the operating limit: static (fixed rating), seasonal (varies by season), ambient-adjusted (AAR based on weather), or dynamic (DLR with real-time conductor monitoring). Indicates the sophistication and real-time responsiveness of the rating.

attributes.name: rating_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this operating limit or dynamic rating was calculated or became effective. For dynamic ratings, this represents the real-time calculation timestamp. Critical for time-series analysis and operational decision-making.

attributes.name: rto_iso_code

attributes.name: solar_irradiance_w_per_m2

attributes.name: study_date

attributes.name: created_timestamp

attributes.name: data_source_system

products.name: contingency_element
products.description: This association product represents the participation of specific transmission and generation assets in NERC-mandated contingency analysis scenarios. It captures the element-specific attributes that exist only in the context of a contingency case definition, including removal sequence, pre/post-contingency loading conditions, and criticality ranking. Each record links one contingency scenario to one physical asset that is removed or affected in that scenario, supporting NERC TPL compliance evidence and EMS contingency analysis execution.. Existence Justification: In utility grid operations, contingency analysis scenarios (N-1, N-2) are defined by specifying which physical assets (transmission lines, generators, transformers) are removed from service and in what sequence. A single contingency case removes multiple assets (e.g., N-2 removes two elements), and each physical asset participates in multiple contingency definitions across different scenarios. Grid operators actively manage these contingency-asset associations as part of NERC TPL compliance, updating element sequences, criticality rankings, and monitoring thresholds based on seasonal conditions and system topology changes.

products.name: control_area_obligation
products.description: This association product represents the applicability and compliance tracking relationship between a balancing authority control area and a specific regulatory obligation. It captures which NERC reliability standards, FERC requirements, and other regulatory obligations apply to each control area, along with the compliance status, assessment history, and evidence location for that specific control area-obligation pair. Each record links one control area to one obligation with attributes that exist only in the context of this applicability determination and compliance tracking relationship.. Existence Justification: In energy utility operations, each balancing authority control area must comply with multiple NERC reliability standards (BAL-001 through BAL-006 for balancing, TOP standards for transmission operations, IRO standards for reliability coordination, MOD standards for modeling), FERC regulations, and state PUC requirements. Conversely, each regulatory obligation applies to multiple control areas across the utility's operational footprint. The business actively manages this relationship through compliance tracking workflows, audit preparation, evidence collection, and regulatory reporting processes.

products.name: contingency_monitored_element
products.description: This association product represents the operational relationship between transmission lines and contingency scenarios in NERC-compliant security analysis. Each record captures a specific transmission line's behavior under a defined contingency case, including whether the line is a monitored element, a limiting element, post-contingency loading levels, violation types, and severity indices. This data is essential for real-time EMS contingency analysis, NERC TPL compliance evidence, and operator situational awareness during N-1 and N-2 security assessments.. Existence Justification: In NERC-compliant transmission operations, each contingency scenario (N-1, N-2) must be analyzed against multiple transmission lines to identify thermal overloads, voltage violations, and stability issues. Conversely, each transmission line must be evaluated under multiple contingency scenarios to determine its vulnerability and limiting conditions. The EMS contingency analysis function actively manages this many-to-many relationship, tracking which lines are monitored vs. limiting elements per contingency, post-contingency loading levels, violation types, and severity indices.

products.name: trading_position
products.description: Real-time and end-of-day energy trading position record aggregated by book, commodity, delivery period, and delivery point. Tracks net long/short position in MWh or MMBtu, mark-to-market (MtM) value, unrealized P&L, and value-at-risk (VaR) exposure. Captures position valuation snapshots at configurable intervals for trend analysis and intraday risk monitoring. Includes LMP reference data: Locational Marginal Price records by PNode and market interval with energy component, congestion component, and loss component ($/MWh), market type (DAM/RTM/FMM), and ISO source — used for position valuation, settlement price verification, congestion analysis, and hedging strategy support. Sourced from OpenLink Endur position management module and ISO market data feeds. Supports intraday risk monitoring, end-of-day P&L reporting, MtM valuation time-series, and FERC market reporting.

products.name: ppa
products.description: Power Purchase Agreement master record with integrated delivery tracking for long-term bilateral contracts for the purchase or sale of electricity from generation assets, including renewable PPAs (wind, solar, hydro) and conventional source agreements. Captures contract identity: counterparty, contracted capacity (MW), energy volume (MWh), contract term, delivery point, pricing structure (fixed, indexed, LMP-based), REC bundling flag, and FERC filing reference. Tracks delivery performance at interval granularity: scheduled MWh, actual delivered MWh, curtailment volume, delivery point, interval start/end timestamps, and settlement status for each delivery period. Supports PPA performance tracking, curtailment reconciliation, invoice generation against contracted volumes, and FERC reporting. SSOT for PPA contract identity and all delivery records within the trading domain.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this delivery record was first created in the energy trading and risk management (ETRM) system. Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking.

attributes.name: currency_code
attributes.description: The ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for the settlement amount. Typically USD for North American energy markets.

attributes.name: curtailment_instruction_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when the curtailment instruction was issued by the ISO/RTO or grid operator. Used for compliance verification and dispute resolution.

attributes.name: curtailment_mwh
attributes.description: The quantity of energy in megawatt-hours (MWh) that was curtailed (not delivered) during this interval due to grid constraints, economic dispatch, or ISO/RTO instructions. Calculated as scheduled minus actual delivered.

attributes.name: curtailment_reason_code
attributes.description: The reason code explaining why energy was curtailed during this interval. Used for PPA performance analysis, force majeure claims, and curtailment credit reconciliation.
attributes.references: NERC Reliability Standards - Curtailment Cause Codes

attributes.name: data_quality_flag
attributes.description: Indicates the quality and reliability of the delivery data for this interval. Estimated or missing data may require subsequent true-up settlement runs.

attributes.name: delivery_interval_end
attributes.description: The timestamp marking the end of the delivery interval for which energy was scheduled and delivered under the PPA. Defines the close of the measurement period.

attributes.name: delivery_interval_start
attributes.description: The timestamp marking the beginning of the delivery interval for which energy was scheduled and delivered under the PPA. Typically aligned with ISO/RTO market intervals (5-minute, 15-minute, or hourly).

attributes.name: deviation_mwh
attributes.description: The net deviation in megawatt-hours (MWh) between scheduled and actual delivered energy. Positive values indicate over-delivery; negative values indicate under-delivery. Used for imbalance settlement.

attributes.name: dispute_flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this delivery interval is under dispute between the PPA counterparties. Triggers dispute resolution workflow and may delay final settlement.

attributes.name: dispute_reason
attributes.description: Free-text description of the reason for dispute on this delivery interval. May reference metering discrepancies, pricing disagreements, or curtailment credit disputes.

attributes.name: energy_charge
attributes.description: The energy component of the locational marginal price (LMP) charged or credited for this delivery interval. Represents the marginal cost of generation.

attributes.name: force_majeure_flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether a force majeure event (natural disaster, grid emergency, regulatory order) affected delivery during this interval. Used for contractual excuse and penalty waiver determination.
attributes.references: PPA Contract Terms - Force Majeure Provisions

attributes.name: invoice_date
attributes.description: The date on which the invoice containing this delivery interval was issued. Used for payment terms calculation and accounts payable tracking.

attributes.name: invoice_number
attributes.description: The invoice number under which this delivery interval was billed to the purchasing utility. Links delivery records to accounts payable and revenue management systems.

attributes.name: iso_rto_code
attributes.business_glossary_term: Independent System Operator (ISO) / Regional Transmission Organization (RTO) Code
attributes.description: The code identifying the ISO or RTO market in which this delivery occurred. Critical for market-specific settlement rules and regulatory reporting. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: CAISO|ERCOT|PJM|MISO|NYISO|ISO_NE|SPP — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: last_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this delivery record was last modified in the ETRM system. Tracks settlement run updates, dispute resolution, and data quality corrections.

attributes.name: lmp_price_per_mwh
attributes.description: The locational marginal price (LMP) in USD per megawatt-hour (MWh) at the delivery point for this interval, as published by the ISO/RTO. Used for market settlement and PPA performance benchmarking.

attributes.name: loss_charge
attributes.description: The marginal loss component of the locational marginal price (LMP) charged or credited for this delivery interval. Reflects transmission line losses between generation and load.

attributes.name: market_type
attributes.description: The type of energy market in which this delivery occurred. Day-ahead market (DAM) schedules are submitted one day prior; real-time market (RTM) reflects actual dispatch; bilateral contracts are direct counterparty agreements.

attributes.name: meter_reading_source
attributes.description: The source system or method used to obtain the actual delivered MWh measurement. SCADA provides real-time telemetry; revenue meters provide billing-quality data; ISO settlement data is the final authoritative source.

attributes.name: payment_due_date
attributes.description: The date by which payment for this delivery interval is due per the PPA payment terms. Used for cash flow forecasting and accounts receivable management.

attributes.name: rec_quantity
attributes.description: The quantity of renewable energy certificates (RECs) generated by this delivery interval, typically one REC per MWh of renewable energy delivered. Used for RPS compliance and environmental attribute tracking.

attributes.name: rec_serial_number
attributes.description: The unique serial number or identifier assigned to the renewable energy certificate(s) associated with this delivery interval, as registered in a REC tracking system (e.g., WREGIS, M-RETS, PJM-GATS).

attributes.name: scheduled_mwh
attributes.description: The quantity of energy in megawatt-hours (MWh) that was scheduled for delivery during this interval under the PPA contract. Represents the day-ahead or real-time schedule submitted to the ISO/RTO.

attributes.name: settlement_amount
attributes.description: The total settlement amount in USD for this delivery interval, calculated as actual delivered MWh multiplied by the contract price, adjusted for any curtailment credits or penalties per the PPA terms.

attributes.name: settlement_run_type
attributes.description: The type of settlement run that produced this delivery record. ISO/RTO markets typically perform multiple settlement runs (initial, recalculation, final) as metering and pricing data are refined.

attributes.name: settlement_status
attributes.description: The current status of the settlement process for this delivery interval. Tracks progression from preliminary ISO/RTO settlement through final invoice and payment.
attributes.references: NAESB WEQ-012 - Settlement and Billing Standards

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: The name of the source system that provided this delivery record. Typically OpenLink Endur for ETRM position management, ISO settlement files, or meter data management (MDM) systems.

attributes.name: source_system_record_code
attributes.description: The unique identifier of this delivery record in the source system. Used for data reconciliation and traceability back to the operational system of record.

products.name: market_bid
products.description: Unified market participation record covering the complete ISO/RTO market lifecycle from bid submission through clearing award, physical energy scheduling, and ancillary service procurement. Captures DAM and RTM bid/offer submissions to ISO/RTO markets (CAISO, MISO, PJM, ERCOT, NYISO, ISO-NE) including bid type (energy, ancillary service, capacity), resource ID, PNode, bid quantity (MW), bid price ($/MWh), bid curve segments, market interval, and submission timestamp. Tracks award phase: awarded MW, clearing price (LMP), ISO confirmation reference, award interval, and market type (DAM/RTM). Tracks scheduling phase: e-Tag reference number, source/sink PNodes, transmission path, scheduled MW by interval, curtailment instructions, schedule status (submitted, confirmed, curtailed, expired), and NAESB e-Tag compliance. Covers ancillary service procurement: service type (regulation up/down, spinning reserve, non-spinning reserve, supplemental), resource ID, procured MW, procurement price ($/MW-hr), ISO award reference, and cost allocation to transmission or distribution tariff. Supports FERC EQR reporting, NAESB e-Tag compliance, ancillary service cost reporting, and complete market participation audit trail. SSOT for all ISO/RTO market participation data in the trading domain.
products.reference: ISO/RTO Market Bid Submission

attributes.name: awarded_mw

attributes.name: ferc_eqr_reported_flag

attributes.name: iso_award_reference

attributes.name: iso_confirmation_reference

attributes.name: iso_rto_code
attributes.business_glossary_term: Independent System Operator (ISO) / Regional Transmission Organization (RTO) Code
attributes.description: The ISO or RTO market to which this bid was submitted. Identifies the wholesale electricity market operator. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: CAISO|MISO|PJM|ERCOT|NYISO|ISONE|SPP — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: market_interval_end
attributes.description: The end timestamp of the market interval for which this bid applies. Together with market_interval_start, defines the delivery window.
attributes.references: NAESB WEQ Standards, ISO/RTO Market Rules

attributes.name: market_interval_start
attributes.description: The start timestamp of the market interval (typically hourly or sub-hourly) for which this bid applies. Defines the delivery period.
attributes.references: NAESB WEQ Standards, ISO/RTO Market Rules

attributes.name: market_type
attributes.description: The market timeframe for this bid. Day-Ahead Market (DAM) clears one day prior to delivery; Real-Time Market (RTM) clears closer to the operating hour.

attributes.name: modified_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this market bid record was last modified. Tracks updates to bid status, awards, schedules, or settlement data.

attributes.name: naesb_compliant_flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this bid and associated scheduling comply with NAESB WEQ standards for wholesale energy transactions and e-Tag requirements.

attributes.name: pnode_code
attributes.description: The pricing node or location at which energy is being bid or delivered. PNodes are the granular pricing locations within the ISO/RTO market used to calculate Locational Marginal Prices (LMP).

attributes.name: procured_mw
attributes.description: The quantity of ancillary service capacity procured through this bid, measured in megawatts. Represents the reserved capacity for grid support.

attributes.name: procurement_price_per_mw_hr

attributes.name: rec_tracking_number

attributes.references: State RPS Regulations, REC Tracking Systems

attributes.name: schedule_status

attributes.name: scheduled_mw_by_interval
attributes.description: JSON or delimited representation of scheduled MW quantities for each sub-interval within the market interval. Captures granular scheduling data for real-time dispatch.
attributes.references: NAESB WEQ Standards, ISO/RTO Market Rules

attributes.name: settlement_amount
attributes.description: The total financial settlement amount for this bid after market clearing and final settlement calculations. Includes energy payments, ancillary service payments, and any adjustments.

attributes.name: settlement_date
attributes.description: The date on which financial settlement for this bid was completed by the ISO/RTO or counterparty.

attributes.name: sink_pnode
attributes.description: The sink PNode for the scheduled energy transaction. Identifies the load or withdrawal point for the physical energy flow.
attributes.references: ISO/RTO Market Rules, NAESB WEQ Standards

attributes.name: source_pnode

attributes.references: ISO/RTO Market Rules, NAESB WEQ Standards

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: The name of the source system from which this bid record originated, typically OpenLink Endur ETRM or ISO/RTO market interface systems.

attributes.name: submission_timestamp
attributes.description: The exact timestamp when the bid was submitted to the ISO/RTO market. Critical for compliance with market submission deadlines and audit trails.
attributes.references: NAESB WEQ Standards, ISO/RTO Market Rules

attributes.name: transmission_path
attributes.description: The transmission path or corridor used for the scheduled energy delivery. May reference a named path or a set of transmission facilities.

attributes.name: award_status

attributes.name: award_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the ISO/RTO issued this market award confirmation. Represents the official award notification time.

attributes.name: award_version

attributes.name: awarded_quantity_mw

attributes.name: clearing_price_per_mwh
attributes.description: Locational Marginal Price (LMP) or market clearing price at which the award was made, expressed in currency per MWh. Determines settlement value.

attributes.name: created_timestamp

attributes.name: currency_code

attributes.name: dispute_flag

attributes.name: interval_duration_minutes

attributes.name: no_load_cost

attributes.name: ramp_rate_mw_per_minute

attributes.name: self_schedule_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this award resulted from a self-schedule (price-taker) bid rather than an economic (price-setter) bid. True = self-schedule, False = economic bid.

attributes.name: settlement_amount
attributes.description: Total financial settlement amount for this award, calculated as awarded_quantity_mwh multiplied by clearing_price_per_mwh. Represents the revenue or cost obligation.

attributes.name: settlement_run_type
attributes.description: Type of settlement calculation run that produced this award record. INITIAL = first settlement, FINAL = final settlement after meter data, RESETTLEMENT = correction run, TRUE_UP = annual reconciliation.

attributes.name: shadow_price
attributes.description: Shadow price of the binding constraint that limited the award quantity. Represents the marginal value of relaxing the constraint.

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: Name of the source system from which this award record originated. Typically the ETRM system (e.g., OpenLink Endur) or ISO/RTO interface.

attributes.name: startup_cost
attributes.description: Startup cost in currency units associated with this award if the resource was committed from an offline state. Used for make-whole payments.

attributes.name: trading_date
attributes.description: The operating day for which the energy or ancillary service was awarded. Represents the physical delivery date.

attributes.references: FERC Order 888, ISO/RTO Market Settlement Rules

attributes.name: load_forecast_mw
attributes.description: Forecasted load in megawatts (MW) at this pricing node for the market interval. Used for day-ahead market clearing and price formation analysis.

attributes.name: location_type
attributes.description: Type of location for which the LMP is calculated. GENERATOR = generation resource, LOAD = load zone, HUB = trading hub, ZONE = pricing zone, INTERFACE = transmission interface, AGGREGATE = aggregated pricing point.

attributes.name: marginal_loss_factor
attributes.description: Marginal loss factor at the pricing node. Represents the incremental transmission losses per unit of power injected or withdrawn at this location.

attributes.name: market_date
attributes.description: The calendar date for which the LMP applies. Used for day-level aggregation and reporting.

attributes.name: market_hour
attributes.description: The hour of the day (0-23) for which the LMP applies. Used for hourly market analysis and reporting.

attributes.name: market_interval_end_timestamp
attributes.description: End timestamp of the market interval for which the LMP applies. Represents the conclusion of the trading interval.

attributes.name: market_interval_start_timestamp
attributes.description: Start timestamp of the market interval for which the LMP applies. Represents the beginning of the trading interval (typically 5-minute or hourly intervals depending on ISO/RTO).

attributes.name: market_run_type
attributes.description: Type of market run. INITIAL = first published results, RESETTLEMENT = revised settlement, FINAL = final binding settlement after all adjustments.

attributes.name: market_type
attributes.description: Type of energy market for which the LMP is published. DAM = Day-Ahead Market, RTM = Real-Time Market, FMM = Fifteen-Minute Market, IDM = Intra-Day Market.

attributes.name: price_unit_of_measure
attributes.description: Unit of measure for the LMP price. Standard is dollars per megawatt-hour ($/MWh).

attributes.name: pricing_zone_code
attributes.description: Code identifying the pricing zone or load zone to which the pricing node belongs. Used for zonal price aggregation.

attributes.name: publication_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the LMP data was published by the ISO/RTO. Used to track data latency and timeliness of market information.

attributes.name: record_effective_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this LMP record became effective in the data warehouse. Used for temporal tracking and historical analysis.

attributes.name: record_end_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this LMP record was superseded or expired. Null for current records. Used for slowly changing dimension Type 2 tracking.

attributes.name: reference_bus_name
attributes.description: Name of the reference bus used for LMP calculation. The reference bus is the baseline location against which congestion and loss components are measured.

attributes.name: scarcity_pricing_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether scarcity pricing or operating reserve demand curve pricing was applied during this market interval. Used to identify periods of tight supply conditions.

attributes.name: source_system_code
attributes.description: Code identifying the source system from which the LMP data was extracted. Typically the ISO/RTO market data feed or ETRM system identifier.

attributes.name: trading_hub_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this pricing node is a designated trading hub. Trading hubs are commonly used reference points for bilateral contracts and financial hedging.

attributes.name: voltage_level_kv
attributes.description: Voltage level in kilovolts (kV) at which the pricing node is located. Used for transmission planning and loss analysis.

products.name: scheduling_coordinator
products.description: Scheduling coordinator (SC) entity registered with an ISO/RTO to submit energy schedules, market bids, and settlement on behalf of the utility's generation and load resources. Captures SC ID, ISO/RTO affiliation, registered resource list, SC type (generator, load-serving entity, marketer), OATT compliance status, NAESB scheduling certification, FERC market-based rate authorization reference, contact information, and active/inactive status. Required for ISO market participation eligibility and NAESB e-Tag scheduling authority.
products.reference: NAESB Scheduling Coordinator

attributes.name: scheduling_coordinator_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the scheduling coordinator entity registered with an ISO/RTO. Primary key for the scheduling coordinator product.

attributes.name: compliance_environmental_permit_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.environmental_permit. Business justification: Scheduling coordinators operating generation resources must hold environmental permits for air quality and water discharge. Compliance teams verify SC registrations align with permitted facilities to

attributes.name: ancillary_services_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this scheduling coordinator is authorized to bid and provide ancillary services (regulation, spinning reserve, non-spinning reserve, voltage support) in the ISO/RTO markets.

attributes.name: business_address_line1
attributes.description: The first line of the scheduling coordinator's registered business address (street number and name) on file with the ISO/RTO.

attributes.name: business_address_line2
attributes.description: The second line of the scheduling coordinator's registered business address (suite, floor, building) on file with the ISO/RTO.

attributes.name: business_city
attributes.description: The city of the scheduling coordinator's registered business address on file with the ISO/RTO.

attributes.name: business_country_code
attributes.description: The three-letter ISO country code of the scheduling coordinator's registered business address. Typically USA, CAN (Canada), or MEX (Mexico) for North American energy markets.

attributes.name: business_postal_code
attributes.description: The postal code or ZIP code of the scheduling coordinator's registered business address on file with the ISO/RTO.

attributes.name: business_state_province
attributes.description: The state or province of the scheduling coordinator's registered business address on file with the ISO/RTO.

attributes.name: collateral_posted_usd
attributes.description: The total amount of financial collateral (cash, letter of credit, surety bond) posted by the scheduling coordinator with the ISO/RTO to secure market obligations and credit exposure.
attributes.references: ISO/RTO Credit Policy and Collateral Requirements

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this scheduling coordinator record was first created in the data system. Used for data lineage and audit trail purposes.

attributes.name: credit_limit_usd
attributes.description: The maximum credit exposure limit in USD established by the ISO/RTO for this scheduling coordinator based on creditworthiness assessment. Determines the maximum unsecured market position the SC can hold.
attributes.references: ISO/RTO Credit Policy and Collateral Requirements

attributes.name: dam_participation_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this scheduling coordinator is authorized and actively participates in the ISO/RTO day-ahead energy market for forward scheduling and financial hedging.

attributes.name: duns_number
attributes.description: The nine-digit DUNS number assigned by Dun & Bradstreet to uniquely identify the scheduling coordinator entity for credit assessment and business verification purposes.

attributes.name: etrm_system_code
attributes.business_glossary_term: Energy Trading and Risk Management (ETRM) System Identifier
attributes.description: The internal identifier for this scheduling coordinator in the utility's ETRM system (e.g., OpenLink Endur). Used for linking ISO/RTO market positions to internal trading books and risk management.

attributes.name: ferc_mbr_authorization
attributes.business_glossary_term: Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) Market-Based Rate (MBR) Authorization
attributes.description: Reference to the FERC docket number or authorization identifier granting this scheduling coordinator market-based rate authority for wholesale energy sales. Required for entities selling energy at market rates rather than cost-based rates.

attributes.name: ftr_crr_eligibility_flag
attributes.business_glossary_term: Financial Transmission Right (FTR) / Congestion Revenue Right (CRR) Eligibility Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this scheduling coordinator is eligible to hold and trade financial transmission rights or congestion revenue rights for hedging transmission congestion costs.

attributes.name: iso_rto_affiliation
attributes.business_glossary_term: Independent System Operator (ISO) / Regional Transmission Organization (RTO) Affiliation
attributes.description: The ISO or RTO with which this scheduling coordinator is registered and authorized to submit schedules, bids, and participate in market operations. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: CAISO|ERCOT|MISO|PJM|SPP|NYISO|ISO_NE|other — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: last_audit_date
attributes.description: The date of the most recent compliance audit or review conducted by the ISO/RTO or internal audit team to verify scheduling coordinator adherence to market rules and OATT requirements.

attributes.name: last_audit_result
attributes.description: The outcome of the most recent compliance audit: passed (no issues), passed with findings (minor issues noted), failed (material non-compliance), or not applicable (no audit conducted).

attributes.name: naesb_certification_date
attributes.business_glossary_term: North American Energy Standards Board (NAESB) Certification Date
attributes.description: The date on which the scheduling coordinator received NAESB WEQ certification for electronic scheduling authority.
attributes.references: NAESB WEQ-001 Wholesale Electric Quadrant Standards

attributes.name: naesb_certification_status
attributes.business_glossary_term: North American Energy Standards Board (NAESB) Certification Status
attributes.description: Indicates whether the scheduling coordinator holds current NAESB WEQ certification for electronic scheduling (e-Tag) authority. Certified status is required for submitting NERC e-Tags for interchange transactions.
attributes.references: NAESB WEQ-001 Wholesale Electric Quadrant Standards

attributes.name: nerc_company_code
attributes.business_glossary_term: North American Electric Reliability Corporation (NERC) Company Identifier
attributes.description: The unique company identifier assigned by NERC for compliance reporting and reliability coordination. Used for linking scheduling coordinator activities to NERC CIP and operational standards.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-form text field for capturing additional information, special conditions, operational notes, or historical context related to this scheduling coordinator registration and market participation.

attributes.name: oatt_compliance_status
attributes.business_glossary_term: Open Access Transmission Tariff (OATT) Compliance Status
attributes.description: Indicates whether the scheduling coordinator is in compliance with FERC-mandated Open Access Transmission Tariff requirements for non-discriminatory transmission access and scheduling practices.
attributes.references: FERC Order 888 Open Access Transmission Tariff

attributes.name: primary_contact_email
attributes.description: The primary email address for the scheduling coordinator contact used for ISO/RTO market notices, settlement statements, and operational communications.

attributes.name: primary_contact_name
attributes.description: The full name of the primary business contact person responsible for scheduling coordinator operations and ISO/RTO communications.

attributes.name: primary_contact_phone
attributes.description: The primary telephone number for the scheduling coordinator contact used for urgent market operations and real-time coordination with the ISO/RTO.

attributes.name: registered_resource_count
attributes.description: The total number of generation and/or load resources currently registered under this scheduling coordinator for market participation and settlement purposes.

attributes.name: registration_date
attributes.description: The date on which the scheduling coordinator was officially registered and authorized by the ISO/RTO to participate in wholesale energy markets.

attributes.name: registration_expiration_date
attributes.description: The date on which the scheduling coordinator registration expires and must be renewed. Null if registration is perpetual subject to compliance.

attributes.name: registration_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the scheduling coordinator registration with the ISO/RTO. Active indicates full market participation authority; inactive indicates voluntary withdrawal; suspended indicates temporary restriction; pending_approval indicates application under review; revoked indicates termination by ISO/RTO.

attributes.name: rtm_participation_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this scheduling coordinator is authorized and actively participates in the ISO/RTO real-time energy market for balancing and spot transactions.

attributes.name: sc_code
attributes.description: The externally-known unique alphanumeric code assigned by the ISO/RTO to identify this scheduling coordinator in market operations, e-Tag submissions, and settlement processes.

attributes.name: sc_name
attributes.description: The legal business name of the scheduling coordinator entity as registered with the ISO/RTO.
attributes.references: FERC Order 888 Open Access Transmission Tariff

attributes.name: sc_type
attributes.description: Classification of the scheduling coordinator based on the primary role in the wholesale energy market: generator (represents generation resources), load-serving entity (represents load), marketer (third-party intermediary), trader (financial participant), aggregator (pools multiple resources), or hybrid (multiple roles).

attributes.name: scheduling_contact_email
attributes.description: The email address for the scheduling contact used for schedule confirmations, e-Tag notifications, and market bid acknowledgments.

attributes.name: scheduling_contact_name
attributes.description: The full name of the designated contact person responsible for submitting energy schedules, e-Tags, and day-ahead/real-time market bids on behalf of the scheduling coordinator.

attributes.name: scheduling_contact_phone
attributes.description: The telephone number for the scheduling contact used for real-time schedule adjustments, curtailment notifications, and emergency coordination.

attributes.name: settlement_contact_email
attributes.description: The email address for the settlement contact used for receiving settlement statements, invoices, and payment notifications from the ISO/RTO.

attributes.name: settlement_contact_name
attributes.description: The full name of the designated contact person responsible for reviewing market settlement statements, invoice reconciliation, and financial dispute resolution.

attributes.name: settlement_contact_phone
attributes.description: The telephone number for the settlement contact used for resolving billing disputes, payment coordination, and financial reconciliation inquiries.

attributes.name: tax_identification_number
attributes.description: The federal tax identification number (EIN for US entities, Business Number for Canadian entities) used for tax reporting and financial settlement with the ISO/RTO.

attributes.name: total_registered_capacity_mw
attributes.description: The aggregate nameplate capacity in megawatts (MW) of all generation resources registered under this scheduling coordinator. Used for market monitoring and concentration analysis.

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this scheduling coordinator record was last modified in the data system. Used for tracking data currency and change management.

products.name: energy_schedule
products.description: Physical energy delivery schedule (e-Tag) submitted to ISO/RTO and counterparties for bilateral and market transactions. Captures schedule ID, source/sink PNodes, transmission path, scheduled MW by interval, e-Tag reference number, curtailment instructions, and schedule status (submitted, confirmed, curtailed, expired). Supports NAESB e-Tag compliance and real-time dispatch coordination.
products.reference: NAESB e-Tag Energy Schedule

attributes.name: energy_schedule_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the energy schedule record. Primary key for the energy schedule entity.

attributes.name: counterparty_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the counterparty entity involved in this energy schedule transaction. May be a bilateral trading partner, ISO/RTO, or scheduling coordinator.

attributes.name: dr_event_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to demand.dr_event. Business justification: Energy schedules must account for DR event curtailments. Real business process: transmission scheduling and balancing where DR events create load deviations requiring e-Tag adjustments and imbalance s

attributes.name: energy_scheduling_coordinator_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the scheduling coordinator responsible for submitting and managing this schedule with the ISO/RTO. The SC acts as the interface between market participants and the system operator.

attributes.name: event_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to outage.outage_event. Business justification: Energy schedules (e-Tags) are curtailed or modified when transmission/generation outages occur. NERC/NAESB coordination requires tracking which outage event caused schedule adjustments. Essential for

attributes.name: forecast_generation_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to forecast.forecast_generation. Business justification: E-tags and transmission schedules are created based on generation forecasts. Scheduling coordinators use generation forecasts to submit balanced schedules to ISOs/RTOs and avoid imbalance penalties. L

attributes.name: load_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to forecast.load. Business justification: Transmission schedules must account for load forecasts at sink points to ensure adequate delivery and avoid congestion. Schedulers link schedules to load forecasts to optimize transmission path select

attributes.name: market_participant_id
attributes.description: The unique identifier assigned to the market participant by the ISO/RTO for this energy schedule. Used for market settlement and reporting.

attributes.name: planned_outage_window_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to outage.planned_outage_window. Business justification: Schedulers coordinate energy schedules with planned transmission/generation maintenance windows to avoid scheduling through de-energized facilities. Required for OASIS posting compliance and day-ahead

attributes.name: scheduling_coordinator_id
attributes.description: FK to trading.scheduling_coordinator.scheduling_coordinator_id — Energy schedules (e-Tags) are submitted by scheduling coordinators. This FK is required for NAESB compliance and schedule authorization tracking.

attributes.name: trade_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier linking this schedule to the underlying energy trading transaction in the Energy Trading and Risk Management (ETRM) system. References the deal or position in OpenLink Endur.

attributes.name: trading_position_id
attributes.description: Identifier linking this schedule to a Financial Transmission Right (FTR) position that hedges congestion risk between the source and sink nodes.

attributes.name: transmission_path_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the transmission path or corridor used for this energy schedule. Links to the transmission network topology and Available Transfer Capability (ATC) calculations.

attributes.name: transmission_service_agreement_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the transmission service agreement under which this schedule is executed. References the OATT-compliant service reservation.

attributes.name: ancillary_service_type
attributes.description: The type of ancillary service being scheduled, if applicable. Ancillary services support grid reliability and include regulation, reserves, and voltage support.

attributes.name: balancing_authority_code
attributes.description: The four-letter code identifying the NERC-registered Balancing Authority responsible for maintaining load-resource balance for this energy schedule.

attributes.name: comments
attributes.description: Free-text field for operational notes, special instructions, or additional context related to this energy schedule.

attributes.name: confirmation_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this energy schedule was confirmed by the ISO/RTO or counterparty, indicating acceptance and readiness for execution.

attributes.name: congestion_charge_usd
attributes.description: The congestion charge in US dollars associated with this energy schedule, calculated based on Locational Marginal Pricing (LMP) differences between source and sink nodes.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this energy schedule record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and data lineage.

attributes.name: curtailment_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this energy schedule has been subject to curtailment instructions from the transmission operator or ISO/RTO due to system constraints or reliability concerns.

attributes.name: curtailment_mw
attributes.description: The megawatt amount by which this schedule has been curtailed. Represents the reduction from the originally scheduled MW due to transmission constraints or reliability directives.

attributes.name: curtailment_reason
attributes.description: Textual explanation of the reason for schedule curtailment, such as transmission congestion, system emergency, or reliability constraint.

attributes.name: curtailment_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when the curtailment instruction was issued for this energy schedule.

attributes.name: dynamic_schedule_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this is a dynamic schedule that allows real-time adjustments to scheduled MW values based on actual generation or load conditions, as opposed to a static schedule with fixed intervals.

attributes.name: etag_reference_number
attributes.description: Unique electronic tag identifier assigned to this energy schedule for transmission system coordination and NERC compliance. The e-Tag is the industry-standard mechanism for scheduling energy transactions across transmission systems.

attributes.name: interval_duration_minutes
attributes.description: The duration of each scheduling interval in minutes. Common values are 15, 30, or 60 minutes depending on ISO/RTO market rules.

attributes.name: iso_rto_code
attributes.business_glossary_term: Independent System Operator (ISO) / Regional Transmission Organization (RTO) Code
attributes.description: The code identifying the ISO or RTO jurisdiction where this energy schedule is executed. Major North American ISOs/RTOs include CAISO, ERCOT, MISO, PJM, NYISO, ISO-NE, and SPP. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: CAISO|ERCOT|MISO|PJM|NYISO|ISO_NE|SPP — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: loss_factor
attributes.description: The percentage factor representing energy losses during transmission from source to sink. Used to adjust scheduled quantities for line losses.

attributes.name: modified_by
attributes.description: The username or identifier of the system user who last modified this energy schedule record.

attributes.name: modified_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this energy schedule record was last modified in the system. Used for audit trail and change tracking.

attributes.name: number_of_intervals
attributes.description: The total count of scheduling intervals covered by this energy schedule. Calculated based on schedule duration and interval length.

attributes.name: priority_code
attributes.description: The priority classification of this energy schedule under OATT rules. Firm schedules have higher priority than non-firm during curtailment events.

attributes.name: rec_quantity
attributes.description: The quantity of Renewable Energy Certificates (RECs) in MWh associated with this energy schedule, if applicable. Used for renewable portfolio standard (RPS) compliance.
attributes.references: EPA RPS Standards, State RPS Programs

attributes.name: rec_tracking_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this energy schedule is associated with renewable energy generation and requires Renewable Energy Certificate (REC) tracking for compliance or trading purposes.
attributes.references: EPA RPS Standards, State RPS Programs

attributes.name: schedule_end_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when the scheduled energy delivery ends. Marks the end of the last interval in the schedule.

attributes.name: schedule_start_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when the scheduled energy delivery begins. Marks the start of the first interval in the schedule.

attributes.name: schedule_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the energy schedule indicating its operational state in the scheduling workflow. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: draft|submitted|confirmed|approved|active|curtailed|expired|cancelled|rejected — 9 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: schedule_type
attributes.description: Classification of the energy schedule indicating the nature of the transaction: bilateral contract, day-ahead market (DAM), real-time market (RTM), ancillary services, wheel-through transmission, or dynamic schedule.

attributes.name: scheduled_mw
attributes.description: The total megawatt capacity scheduled for delivery in this energy schedule. Represents the aggregate power flow across all intervals.

attributes.name: scheduled_mwh
attributes.description: The total energy quantity in megawatt-hours scheduled for delivery across the entire schedule period. Calculated as the sum of interval-level MWh values.

attributes.name: scheduling_fee_usd
attributes.description: The administrative fee in US dollars charged by the ISO/RTO or scheduling coordinator for processing and managing this energy schedule.

attributes.name: settlement_period
attributes.description: The year-month period (YYYY-MM format) for which this energy schedule will be financially settled by the ISO/RTO or counterparty.

attributes.name: settlement_status
attributes.description: The current status of financial settlement for this energy schedule. Tracks progression from preliminary to final settlement and any disputes or adjustments.

attributes.name: sink_pnode
attributes.description: The pricing node or location identifier where energy is delivered or withdrawn from the transmission system. Used for Locational Marginal Pricing (LMP) calculations.

attributes.name: source_pnode
attributes.description: The pricing node or location identifier where energy is sourced or injected into the transmission system. Used for Locational Marginal Pricing (LMP) calculations.

attributes.name: submission_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this energy schedule was submitted to the ISO/RTO or counterparty for approval and coordination.

attributes.name: transmission_charge_usd
attributes.description: The transmission service charge in US dollars for using the transmission system to deliver energy under this schedule. Based on OATT rates.

attributes.name: created_by
attributes.description: The username or identifier of the system user who created this energy schedule record in the ETRM system.

products.name: market_settlement
products.description: Unified settlement record for all wholesale energy transaction types within the trading domain: ISO/RTO market settlements (DAM/RTM energy and ancillary services), bilateral OTC trade settlements, PPA contract settlements, FTR congestion revenue settlements, and capacity market settlements. Captures settlement type discriminator, settlement amount ($), quantity (MWh), settlement price, energy imbalance charges, ancillary service charges, congestion charges, loss charges, uplift charges, netting adjustments, payment due date, payment status, settlement interval, ISO statement reference or counterparty invoice reference, dispute status, dispute resolution date, and cumulative P&L tracking. For FTR settlements: congestion revenue earned/owed based on LMP differential, settlement period, and P&L against acquisition cost. Reconciled in OpenLink Endur and feeds accounts receivable/payable. SSOT for all settlement data in the trading domain. Supports FERC market reporting, bilateral contract compliance, and settlement dispute management.
products.reference: ISO/RTO Settlement Statement

attributes.name: market_settlement_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the market settlement record. Primary key for all wholesale energy transaction settlements across ISO/RTO markets, bilateral OTC trades, PPA contracts, FTR congestion revenue, and capacity markets.

attributes.name: contract_id
attributes.description: Reference to the underlying contract or agreement governing this settlement. Applicable for PPA settlements, bilateral contract settlements, and FTR holdings. Null for spot market settlements.

attributes.name: cost_center_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.cost_center. Business justification: ISO/RTO settlements must be allocated to cost centers for cost recovery tracking and variance analysis. Real business process: monthly settlement reconciliation requires cost center assignment for acc

attributes.name: counterparty_id
attributes.description: Reference to the counterparty entity involved in the settlement. For ISO/RTO settlements, this is the ISO/RTO organization; for bilateral trades, this is the trading counterparty; for PPA settlements, this is the power purchase agreement counterparty.

attributes.name: dr_event_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to demand.dr_event. Business justification: Market settlements reconcile DR event performance payments. Real business process: ISO settlement statements allocating energy and capacity payments for DR dispatch, requiring event linkage for paymen

attributes.name: energy_price_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to forecast.energy_price. Business justification: Settlement price reconciliation compares actual LMPs to forecasted prices for variance analysis and dispute resolution. Settlement analysts link settlements to the price forecasts used for budgeting a

attributes.name: ftr_holding_id
attributes.description: FK to trading.ftr_holding.ftr_holding_id — FTR congestion revenue settlements (now in unified market_settlement) must link to the FTR holding for P&L calculation against acquisition cost.

attributes.name: gl_account_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.gl_account. Business justification: Every settlement transaction must post to a specific GL account for financial statement preparation. Real business process: daily settlement posting to general ledger requires GL account mapping for e

attributes.name: market_award_id
attributes.description: FK to trading.market_award.market_award_id — Settlements reconcile awarded quantities against actuals. The settlement→award FK is required for the settlement reconciliation process and dispute resolution.

attributes.name: market_bid_id
attributes.description: FK to trading.market_bid.market_bid_id — ISO/RTO market settlements must link to the originating market bid/award for settlement verification and dispute resolution. Essential for DAM/RTM settlement reconciliation.

attributes.name: market_participant_id
attributes.description: The unique identifier assigned by the ISO/RTO to the market participant (scheduling coordinator or qualified scheduling entity) for this settlement. Used for ISO/RTO market reconciliation.

attributes.name: market_trade_id
attributes.description: FK to trading.trade.trade_id — Settlement records must reference the trade they settle for reconciliation, P&L tracking, and audit trail. This is the core settlement→trade linkage in any ETRM system.

attributes.name: ppa_id
attributes.description: FK to trading.ppa.ppa_id — PPA settlements (now unified in market_settlement) must link back to the PPA contract for delivery reconciliation and invoice generation.

attributes.name: profit_center_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.profit_center. Business justification: Market settlements impact profit center P&L and must be tracked for segment reporting. Real business process: FERC Form 1 and state regulatory filings require profit center-level settlement data for j

attributes.name: regulatory_filing_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.regulatory_filing. Business justification: Market settlements with disputes or unusual charges trigger regulatory filings including FERC complaints, tariff interpretation requests, and cost recovery proceedings. Regulatory affairs references s

attributes.name: trade_id
attributes.description: FK to trading.trade.trade_id — Settlements must trace back to the originating trade for reconciliation, dispute resolution, and audit trail. This is the fundamental transaction→settlement link.

attributes.name: transaction_trade_id
attributes.description: Reference to the underlying energy transaction or trade record in the ETRM system that generated this settlement. Links settlement to the originating position or deal.

attributes.name: vendor_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to supply.vendor. Business justification: ISO/RTO market settlements with generation owners or transmission providers who are registered vendors. Links market clearing charges/payments to vendor master for accounts payable processing and cash

attributes.name: accounting_period
attributes.description: The financial accounting period (e.g., 2024-Q1, 2024-03) to which this settlement is allocated for financial reporting purposes. Used for revenue recognition and accounts receivable/payable posting.

attributes.name: ancillary_service_charge_amount
attributes.description: The total charges for ancillary services procured in conjunction with the energy settlement. Includes regulation, spinning reserve, non-spinning reserve, and voltage support charges as applicable.

attributes.name: capacity_charge_amount
attributes.description: Charges for capacity obligations or capacity market settlements. Represents the cost of securing generation capacity to meet future demand, separate from energy commodity charges.

attributes.name: congestion_charge_amount
attributes.description: The congestion component of the locational marginal price settlement. Represents the cost of transmission congestion between the generation source and the delivery point. May be positive (charge) or negative (credit).

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this settlement record was first created in the system. Audit trail field for data lineage and compliance.

attributes.name: cumulative_profit_loss_amount
attributes.description: The running cumulative profit or loss for this trading position or contract through this settlement date. Calculated by summing all settlement amounts for the position from inception to current settlement. Used for mark-to-market valuation and position tracking.

attributes.name: currency_code
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for all monetary amounts in this settlement. Typically USD for US markets or CAD for Canadian markets.

attributes.name: delivery_end_timestamp
attributes.description: The precise date and time when energy delivery ended for the transaction being settled. For interval-based settlements, this marks the end of the settlement interval.

attributes.name: delivery_start_timestamp
attributes.description: The precise date and time when energy delivery began for the transaction being settled. For interval-based settlements, this marks the beginning of the settlement interval.

attributes.name: dispute_flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator of whether this settlement is currently under dispute. True indicates an active dispute has been raised by either party; false indicates no dispute.

attributes.name: dispute_raised_date
attributes.description: The date on which the settlement dispute was formally raised. Null if no dispute exists.

attributes.name: dispute_reason
attributes.description: Free-text description of the reason for the settlement dispute. Captures the business justification for challenging the settlement calculation or amount. Null if no dispute exists.

attributes.name: dispute_resolution_date
attributes.description: The date on which the settlement dispute was resolved and closed. Null if dispute is still open or if no dispute exists.

attributes.name: energy_charge_amount
attributes.description: The base energy charge calculated as settlement quantity multiplied by settlement price. Represents the core energy commodity cost before adjustments for ancillary services, congestion, losses, or uplift.

attributes.name: ftr_congestion_revenue_amount
attributes.business_glossary_term: Financial Transmission Right (FTR) Congestion Revenue Amount (USD)
attributes.description: Revenue earned or owed from financial transmission right holdings based on the locational marginal price differential between source and sink nodes. Hedges congestion cost exposure in ISO/RTO markets.

attributes.name: gl_posting_date

attributes.name: modified_by_user

attributes.name: netting_adjustment_amount

attributes.name: payment_due_date

attributes.name: payment_status

attributes.name: pnode_code

attributes.name: settlement_date

attributes.name: settlement_interval_minutes

attributes.name: settlement_price_per_mwh

attributes.name: settlement_quantity_mwh

attributes.name: settlement_reference_number

attributes.name: settlement_status

attributes.name: regulatory_filing_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.regulatory_filing. Regulatory affairs reports FTR positions in market-based rate triennial filings and transmissio

attributes.name: sink_pnode_id
attributes.description: The ISO/RTO pricing node identifier representing the sink (withdrawal) point of the FTR path. Used to calculate Locational Marginal Price (LMP) differences for congestion revenue.

attributes.name: source_pnode_id
attributes.description: The ISO/RTO pricing node identifier representing the source (injection) point of the FTR path. Used to calculate Locational Marginal Price (LMP) differences for congestion revenue.

attributes.description: The financial accounting method applied to this FTR holding. Hedge accounting defers gains/losses to match hedged items; mark-to-market recognizes fair value changes immediately; accrual recognizes revenue as earned.

attributes.name: accumulated_payout
attributes.description: The cumulative congestion revenue (or charge for obligations) in USD received from the ISO/RTO since the FTR became effective. Positive values indicate net revenue; negative values indicate net charges.

attributes.name: acquisition_price_per_mw
attributes.description: The price paid per MW in the FTR auction to acquire this holding, expressed in USD per MW. Used to calculate total acquisition cost and evaluate hedging effectiveness.

attributes.name: auction_date
attributes.description: The date on which the FTR auction was conducted and this holding was acquired. Critical for tracking acquisition timing and market conditions.

attributes.name: auction_period
attributes.description: The time period identifier for which this FTR was auctioned, typically in format YYYY-MM or YYYY for annual auctions. Defines the delivery period for the hedging instrument.

attributes.name: auction_type
attributes.description: Classification of the ISO/RTO auction through which this FTR was acquired. Annual and monthly are standard forward auctions; long-term covers multi-year; reconfiguration allows secondary market adjustments.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this FTR holding record was first created in the ETRM system. Used for audit trails and data lineage tracking.

attributes.name: credit_requirement_amount
attributes.description: The collateral or credit amount in USD required by the ISO/RTO to maintain this FTR position. Based on market exposure and counterparty credit rating.

attributes.name: current_market_value
attributes.description: The current estimated market value in USD of this FTR holding based on recent auction clearing prices or secondary market transactions. Updated periodically for mark-to-market valuation.

attributes.name: effective_end_date
attributes.description: The date when this FTR holding expires and stops accruing congestion revenue or charges. Marks the end of the delivery period.

attributes.name: effective_start_date
attributes.description: The date when this FTR holding becomes effective and begins accruing congestion revenue or charges. Marks the beginning of the delivery period.

attributes.name: ftr_class
attributes.description: Time-of-use classification defining when the FTR is effective. On-peak covers high-demand hours, off-peak covers low-demand hours, 24-hour covers all hours.

attributes.name: ftr_contract_number
attributes.description: The externally-known unique contract identifier assigned by the ISO/RTO for this FTR holding. Used for market settlement reconciliation and regulatory reporting.

attributes.name: ftr_in_book

attributes.name: ftr_type
attributes.description: Classification of the FTR instrument. Obligation FTRs pay or charge based on congestion price differences; Option FTRs only pay when positive. Critical for risk management and hedging strategy.

attributes.name: hedge_effectiveness_ratio
attributes.description: A calculated metric (0 to 1) representing how effectively this FTR hedges the underlying congestion exposure. Values near 1 indicate highly effective hedges; values near 0 indicate poor correlation.

attributes.name: holding_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the FTR holding. Active holdings are accruing revenue; expired holdings have passed their end date; transferred holdings have been sold or reassigned; terminated holdings were cancelled before expiration.

attributes.name: iso_registration_reference
attributes.description: The ISO/RTO system reference number or registration ID linking this FTR holding to the market operators records. Used for settlement reconciliation and dispute resolution.

attributes.name: iso_rto_code
