products.name: depreciation_schedule
products.description: Asset depreciation schedule defining the financial depreciation profile for each utility asset or asset class. Captures depreciation method (straight-line, declining balance, units of production), useful life (years), salvage value, annual depreciation charge, accumulated depreciation, net book value, regulatory depreciation rate (as approved by PUC), and RAB depreciation treatment. Supports CAPEX/OPEX planning, regulatory asset base (RAB) valuation, and SOX-compliant financial reporting. Sourced from SAP S/4HANA Fixed Asset Accounting (FI-AA).
products.reference: SAP S/4HANA FI-AA — Asset Depreciation Area / IAS 16 Property Plant Equipment

attributes.name: depreciation_schedule_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the depreciation schedule record. Primary key for the depreciation schedule entity.

attributes.name: asset_class_id
attributes.description: FK to asset.asset_class.asset_class_id — Depreciation methods and useful life defaults are driven by asset class. This FK enables class-level depreciation policy inheritance.

attributes.name: asset_registry_id
attributes.description: FK to asset.asset_registry.asset_registry_id — Depreciation schedules are defined per asset. Without this FK, depreciation charges cannot be allocated to specific assets for RAB valuation and financial reporting.

attributes.name: class_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to asset.asset_class. Business justification: depreciation_schedule has both asset_registry_id (for asset-specific schedules) and asset_class_code (STRING) for class-level depreciation schedules. The asset_class_code should be normalized to FK as

attributes.name: employee_id
attributes.description: User ID of the person or system account that created this depreciation schedule record.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404 Internal Controls; SAP S/4HANA Audit Trail

attributes.name: last_modified_by_user_employee_id
attributes.description: User ID of the person or system account that last modified this depreciation schedule record.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404 Internal Controls; SAP S/4HANA Audit Trail

attributes.name: registry_id
attributes.description: Reference to the utility asset (generation unit, transformer, transmission tower, distribution pole, switchgear, protection relay, substation equipment, fleet vehicle, or facility) to which this depreciation schedule applies.

attributes.name: accounting_period
attributes.description: Accounting period (month) within the fiscal year to which this depreciation schedule record applies. Typically 1-12.

attributes.name: accumulated_depreciation
attributes.description: Total depreciation expense recognized to date since the asset was placed in service. Increases each period by the depreciation charge.
attributes.references: GAAP ASC 360; SAP S/4HANA Fixed Asset Accounting (FI-AA)

attributes.name: accumulated_depreciation_gl_account_code
attributes.business_glossary_term: Accumulated Depreciation General Ledger (GL) Account Code
attributes.description: General ledger account code for the accumulated depreciation contra-asset account on the balance sheet.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA Financial Accounting (FI); GAAP ASC 360

attributes.name: acquisition_date
attributes.description: Date the asset was acquired or placed in service. Marks the start of the depreciation period.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA Fixed Asset Accounting (FI-AA); GAAP ASC 360

attributes.name: annual_depreciation_charge
attributes.description: Annual depreciation expense allocated to the asset under the selected depreciation method. For straight-line: depreciable base divided by useful life years.
attributes.references: GAAP ASC 360; FERC Uniform System of Accounts

attributes.name: business_area_code
attributes.description: Business area or operating segment (e.g., generation, transmission, distribution, retail) to which this asset and its depreciation expense are allocated.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA Financial Accounting (FI); FERC Uniform System of Accounts

attributes.name: capex_opex_classification
attributes.description: Classification of the asset as capital expenditure (CAPEX) or operational expenditure (OPEX) for financial planning and regulatory reporting purposes. CAPEX assets are capitalized and depreciated; OPEX items are expensed immediately.
attributes.references: GAAP ASC 360; FERC Uniform System of Accounts

attributes.name: company_code
attributes.description: Company code or legal entity to which this depreciation schedule belongs. Supports multi-entity utility holding companies.

attributes.name: cost_center_code
attributes.description: Cost center to which depreciation expense is allocated for internal management accounting and OPEX tracking.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this depreciation schedule record was first created in the source system.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404 Internal Controls; SAP S/4HANA Audit Trail

attributes.name: currency_code
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for all monetary amounts in this depreciation schedule (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP).

attributes.name: depreciable_base
attributes.description: Amount subject to depreciation, calculated as original cost minus salvage value. Used as the basis for annual depreciation charge calculation.

attributes.name: depreciation_area_code
attributes.description: Code identifying the depreciation area or ledger (e.g., book depreciation, tax depreciation, regulatory depreciation) to which this schedule applies. Utilities often maintain parallel depreciation schedules for different reporting purposes.

attributes.name: depreciation_asset
attributes.description: FK to asset.asset_registry.asset_registry_id — Depreciation schedules must reference the asset being depreciated. Required for RAB valuation and financial reporting.

attributes.name: depreciation_end_date
attributes.description: Date on which depreciation calculation ends for this asset. Typically the date the asset is fully depreciated, retired, or disposed of.
attributes.references: GAAP ASC 360; FERC Uniform System of Accounts

attributes.name: depreciation_method
attributes.description: Method used to calculate depreciation expense over the asset's useful life. Straight-line is most common for utility assets; units of production may be used for generation equipment; regulatory composite may be mandated by PUC for rate-regulated assets.
attributes.references: GAAP ASC 360 Property Plant and Equipment; FERC Uniform System of Accounts

attributes.name: depreciation_start_date
attributes.description: Date on which depreciation calculation begins for this asset. Typically the placed-in-service date or the first day of the following month.

attributes.name: depreciation_status
attributes.description: Current status of the depreciation schedule. Active indicates ongoing depreciation; fully depreciated indicates the asset has reached its salvage value; suspended indicates temporary halt; retired/disposed indicates asset is no longer in service.

attributes.name: depreciation_to_asset
attributes.description: FK to asset.asset_registry.asset_registry_id — Each depreciation schedule is assigned to a specific asset for financial reporting, RAB valuation, and SOX compliance. This is a mandatory FK for fixed asset accounting.

attributes.name: fiscal_year
attributes.description: Fiscal year to which this depreciation schedule record applies. Enables year-over-year tracking of depreciation expense and accumulated depreciation.

attributes.name: functional_area_code
attributes.description: Functional area (e.g., operations, maintenance, administration) to which depreciation expense is allocated for cost analysis.

attributes.name: gl_account_code
attributes.description: General ledger account code to which depreciation expense is posted. Typically a depreciation expense account in the income statement.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA Financial Accounting (FI); FERC Uniform System of Accounts

attributes.name: impairment_indicator_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the asset has been identified as potentially impaired (carrying value may exceed recoverable amount). Triggers impairment testing under GAAP ASC 360.

attributes.name: last_depreciation_run_date
attributes.description: Date of the most recent depreciation calculation run for this asset. Used to track depreciation processing and ensure timely financial close.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this depreciation schedule record was last modified in the source system.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404 Internal Controls; SAP S/4HANA Audit Trail

attributes.name: net_book_value
attributes.description: Current carrying value of the asset on the balance sheet, calculated as original cost minus accumulated depreciation. Also known as book value or carrying amount.
attributes.references: GAAP ASC 360; SOX Section 404 Internal Controls

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text notes or comments regarding this depreciation schedule, including adjustments, regulatory guidance, or special circumstances.

attributes.name: original_cost
attributes.description: Original acquisition or construction cost of the asset, including capitalized installation, engineering, and AFUDC (Allowance for Funds Used During Construction). Basis for depreciation calculation.
attributes.references: GAAP ASC 360; FERC Uniform System of Accounts Part 101

attributes.name: placed_in_service_date
attributes.description: Date the asset was placed into operational service and began generating revenue or providing utility function. Depreciation typically begins on this date.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; IRS Publication 946

attributes.name: rab_depreciation_treatment
attributes.description: Treatment of this asset's depreciation in the Regulatory Asset Base (RAB) for rate-making purposes. Determines whether depreciation expense is recoverable through customer rates.
attributes.references: PUC Rate Case Orders; FERC Uniform System of Accounts

attributes.name: rab_inclusion_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this asset is included in the Regulatory Asset Base (RAB) for rate-making purposes. True if included; false if excluded.
attributes.references: PUC Rate Case Orders; FERC Uniform System of Accounts

attributes.name: regulatory_depreciation_rate_percent
attributes.description: Depreciation rate (as a percentage of original cost) approved by the Public Utility Commission (PUC) for rate-making purposes. May differ from book depreciation rate.
attributes.references: PUC Rate Case Orders; FERC Uniform System of Accounts

attributes.name: remaining_useful_life_years
attributes.description: Estimated remaining useful life of the asset in years as of the current reporting period. Calculated as original useful life minus elapsed time since placed in service.
attributes.references: GAAP ASC 360; PUC Depreciation Study Guidelines

attributes.name: salvage_value
attributes.description: Estimated residual value of the asset at the end of its useful life. Subtracted from original cost to determine depreciable base.
attributes.references: GAAP ASC 360; FERC Uniform System of Accounts

attributes.name: source_system_code
attributes.description: Code identifying the source system from which this depreciation schedule record originated (e.g., SAP_S4HANA, VENTYX_ASSET_SUITE).

attributes.name: source_system_record_code
attributes.description: Unique identifier of this depreciation schedule record in the source system. Enables traceability and reconciliation.

attributes.name: tax_depreciation_method
attributes.description: Depreciation method used for tax reporting purposes. May differ from book depreciation method. MACRS (Modified Accelerated Cost Recovery System) is common in the US.

attributes.name: tax_useful_life_years
attributes.description: Useful life of the asset for tax depreciation purposes, as defined by tax regulations. May differ from book useful life.

attributes.name: useful_life_years
attributes.description: Expected useful life of the asset in years, as determined by engineering assessment and regulatory guidance. Used to calculate annual depreciation charge under straight-line or declining balance methods.
attributes.references: GAAP ASC 360; FERC Uniform System of Accounts; PUC Depreciation Study Guidelines

products.name: spare_parts_inventory
products.description: Inventory management for spare parts, consumables, and critical spares held for utility asset maintenance and emergency restoration. Captures material master data (number, description, asset class applicability, criticality classification), stocking details (location, quantity on hand, min stock, reorder point, lead time), valuation (unit cost, total inventory value), and supplier references. Also records material issue and return transactions against work orders including issue date, quantity, receiving technician, and cost allocation. Supports O&M material cost tracking, inventory replenishment triggers, and critical spare availability assurance. Sourced from Ventyx Asset Suite Inventory module and SAP S/4HANA Materials Management (MM).
products.reference: Ventyx Asset Suite — Inventory / SAP MM Material Master

attributes.name: spare_parts_inventory_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the spare parts inventory record. Primary key for the spare parts inventory product.

attributes.name: asset_class_id
attributes.description: FK to asset.asset_class.asset_class_id — Spare parts are stocked for specific asset classes (e.g., bushings for 132kV transformers). This FK enables parts applicability lookup during work order planning.

attributes.name: class_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to asset.asset_class. Business justification: spare_parts_inventory has asset_class_applicability (STRING) which appears to store which asset class(es) the spare part is applicable to. This should be normalized to FK asset_class_id → asset_class.

attributes.name: direct_load_control_device_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Direct Load Control Device Id (Foreign Key)
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to demand.direct_load_control_device. Business justification: Spare parts inventory for DLC devices (communication modules, control relays, thermostats) supports DR program reliability. Warehouse management links spare parts to device models for reorder point ca

attributes.name: primary_spare_employee_id
attributes.description: System user identifier of the person who created the spare parts inventory record in the enterprise asset management system.

attributes.name: abc_classification
attributes.description: Inventory classification based on value and usage frequency. A items are high-value or high-usage requiring tight control and frequent review, B items are moderate-value with standard controls, C items are low-value with minimal controls. Used for cycle counting frequency and inventory management prioritization.

attributes.name: bin_location
attributes.description: Specific bin, shelf, or rack location within the stocking location where the material is stored. Supports warehouse picking and cycle counting operations.
attributes.references: Ventyx Asset Suite Inventory Module Standard

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the spare parts inventory record was first created in the system. Supports audit trail and data lineage requirements.

attributes.name: criticality_classification
attributes.description: Business criticality rating of the spare part based on impact to operations if unavailable. Critical items are essential for emergency restoration and grid reliability, high items support major assets, medium items are standard maintenance spares, and low items are non-essential consumables.

attributes.name: currency_code
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the unit cost valuation (e.g., USD, CAD, EUR, GBP).

attributes.name: hazardous_material_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the material is classified as hazardous and requires special handling, storage, and disposal procedures per OSHA and EPA regulations. True if hazardous, False if non-hazardous.
attributes.references: OSHA Hazard Communication Standard (HCS) and EPA RCRA

attributes.name: last_issue_date
attributes.description: Date when the material was most recently issued from inventory to a work order or maintenance activity. Used for inventory turnover analysis and obsolescence management.
attributes.references: Ventyx Asset Suite Material Issue Tracking

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the spare parts inventory record was most recently updated. Supports change tracking and audit compliance.

attributes.name: last_physical_count_date
attributes.description: Date when the last physical cycle count or annual inventory audit was performed for this material at this stocking location. Supports inventory accuracy and SOX compliance requirements.

attributes.name: last_purchase_date
attributes.description: Date when the material was most recently purchased via a purchase order. Used for inventory aging analysis and procurement pattern tracking.

attributes.name: last_purchase_order_number
attributes.description: Most recent purchase order number used to procure this material. Provides audit trail and reference for pricing, lead time, and supplier performance analysis.

attributes.name: lead_time_days
attributes.description: Expected number of calendar days from purchase order placement to material receipt at the stocking location. Used for reorder point calculation and emergency procurement planning.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA Purchasing Lead Time Standard

attributes.name: manufacturer_name
attributes.description: Name of the original equipment manufacturer (OEM) or supplier who produces the spare part. Used for warranty tracking, quality management, and supplier performance analysis.
attributes.references: Ventyx Asset Suite Supplier Management Standard

attributes.name: manufacturer_part_number
attributes.description: Original equipment manufacturer's part number or catalog number for the spare part. Used for cross-referencing, procurement, and ensuring correct part substitution.

attributes.name: material_description
attributes.description: Detailed textual description of the spare part or consumable item including technical specifications, manufacturer details, and usage context.
attributes.references: Ventyx Asset Suite Inventory Module Standard

attributes.name: material_group_code
attributes.description: Hierarchical classification code grouping similar materials for procurement, reporting, and spend analysis. Examples include electrical components, mechanical parts, safety equipment, or consumables.

attributes.name: material_number
attributes.description: Unique material master identifier assigned to the spare part or consumable item in the enterprise asset management system. This is the externally-known business identifier used across procurement, inventory, and maintenance operations.

attributes.name: material_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the material master record. Active materials are available for procurement and issue, inactive materials are temporarily blocked, obsolete materials are phased out, pending approval materials are under review, and discontinued materials are no longer supported by the manufacturer.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA Material Master Status Management

attributes.name: material_type
attributes.description: Classification of the inventory item by usage category. Spare parts are replaceable components for assets, consumables are items used up during maintenance, critical spares are high-value low-turnover items essential for emergency restoration, tools are reusable equipment, safety equipment includes PPE and protective gear, and bulk materials are commodities purchased in volume.
attributes.references: Ventyx Asset Suite Material Classification Standard

attributes.name: maximum_stock_level
attributes.description: Maximum inventory quantity threshold to avoid overstocking and excess capital tied up in inventory. Used for inventory optimization and storage capacity planning.
attributes.references: Ventyx Asset Suite Inventory Optimization Standard

attributes.name: minimum_stock_level
attributes.description: Minimum inventory quantity threshold below which replenishment should be triggered. Set based on lead time, usage rate, and criticality to ensure availability for planned and emergency maintenance.
attributes.references: Ventyx Asset Suite Inventory Replenishment Standard

attributes.name: obsolete_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the material has been marked as obsolete and should no longer be procured or issued. True if obsolete, False if active. Obsolete materials may still have on-hand inventory for legacy asset support.
attributes.references: Ventyx Asset Suite Material Master Lifecycle Management

attributes.name: plant_code
attributes.description: Identifier for the organizational plant or business unit to which this inventory record belongs. Used for multi-site inventory management and cost allocation across generation, transmission, and distribution operations.

attributes.name: preferred_supplier_code
attributes.description: Identifier for the preferred or primary supplier from whom this material should be procured. Links to vendor master data in the enterprise resource planning system.

attributes.name: quantity_on_hand
attributes.description: Current physical inventory quantity available in stock at the stocking location. Measured in the material's unit of measure.

attributes.name: reorder_point
attributes.description: Inventory level at which a purchase requisition or replenishment order should be automatically generated. Calculated based on lead time demand plus safety stock.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA Materials Management Reorder Point Planning

attributes.name: serial_number_tracking_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether individual units of this material are tracked by unique serial numbers for warranty, calibration, or asset lifecycle management. True if serial-tracked, False if batch-tracked or non-serialized.
attributes.references: Ventyx Asset Suite Serial Number Management

attributes.name: shelf_life_months
attributes.description: Maximum number of months the material can be stored before it expires or degrades and must be disposed of. Applicable to consumables, lubricants, chemicals, and time-sensitive spare parts. Null for non-perishable items.

attributes.name: source_system_code
attributes.description: Identifier for the operational system of record from which this inventory data originated. VENTYX for Ventyx Asset Suite Inventory module, SAP_MM for SAP S/4HANA Materials Management, SAP_PM for SAP Plant Maintenance, MANUAL for manually entered records.

attributes.name: source_system_record_code
attributes.description: Unique identifier or primary key of this inventory record in the source operational system. Used for data lineage, reconciliation, and bidirectional synchronization.

attributes.name: spare_part_applicability
attributes.description: FK to asset.asset_class.asset_class_id — Spare parts are stocked for specific asset classes. This FK enables identification of which parts serve which equipment types for inventory optimization.

attributes.name: spare_parts_to_asset_class
attributes.description: FK to asset.asset_class.asset_class_id — Spare parts are stocked for specific asset classes (e.g., transformer bushings for 132kV power transformers). This FK enables bill-of-materials resolution and critical spare identification.

attributes.name: stocking_location_code
attributes.description: Identifier for the warehouse, storeroom, or facility where the spare part inventory is physically held. May reference central warehouses, regional depots, or substation storerooms.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA Plant and Storage Location Standard

attributes.name: stocking_location_name
attributes.description: Human-readable name of the warehouse or storeroom where the inventory is held.

attributes.name: storage_condition_code
attributes.description: Required environmental storage conditions for the material. Ambient for standard warehouse conditions, climate controlled for temperature and humidity sensitive items, refrigerated for cold storage, outdoor for weather-resistant bulk materials, and hazmat storage for hazardous materials requiring special containment.

attributes.name: total_inventory_value
attributes.description: Total monetary value of the on-hand inventory calculated as quantity on hand multiplied by unit cost. Used for Regulatory Asset Base (RAB) valuation, financial reporting, and Capital Expenditure (CAPEX) / Operational Expenditure (OPEX) tracking.
attributes.references: SOX Financial Reporting and Internal Controls

attributes.name: unit_cost
attributes.description: Standard or moving average cost per unit of measure for the material. Used for inventory valuation, work order costing, and Operations and Maintenance (O&M) expense tracking.

attributes.name: unit_of_measure
attributes.description: Standard unit in which the material quantity is tracked and issued. EA=each, FT=feet, M=meters, KG=kilograms, LB=pounds, GAL=gallons, L=liters, BOX=box, ROLL=roll, SET=set. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: EA|FT|M|KG|LB|GAL|L|BOX|ROLL|SET — 10 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: valuation_class
attributes.description: Accounting classification code used to assign inventory value to specific general ledger accounts for financial reporting. Links material inventory to chart of accounts for CAPEX, OPEX, and balance sheet reporting.

attributes.name: warranty_months
attributes.description: Number of months of manufacturer warranty coverage from the date of purchase or installation. Used for warranty claim management and total cost of ownership analysis. Null if no warranty applies.

products.name: inspection
products.description: Periodic, event-driven, or regulatory-mandated evaluation of utility asset condition encompassing routine patrol inspections (visual, post-storm, vegetation management), scheduled condition assessments, and advanced diagnostic tests (thermographic survey, dissolved gas analysis, partial discharge test, oil sampling, vibration analysis, ultrasonic testing). Records inspection/assessment date, method/type, inspector or assessor identity, overall condition score (1-5 scale per IEEE/IEC standards), individual test results with pass/fail thresholds, defects identified with severity classification (critical, major, minor), recommended follow-up actions (repair, replace, monitor, no action), estimated remediation cost, next assessment due date, and regulatory compliance flags (e.g., NERC FAC-003 vegetation management, OSHA confined space). Feeds asset health indices, risk-based maintenance prioritization, reliability-centered maintenance analysis, and condition-based maintenance triggers. SSOT for all asset condition evaluation data. Sourced from Ventyx Asset Suite Condition Monitoring, field inspection mobile apps, and SCADA-integrated online monitoring systems.
products.reference: Ventyx Asset Suite — Inspection / NERC FAC-003 Transmission Vegetation Management

attributes.name: ambient_temperature_c
attributes.description: Ambient temperature in degrees Celsius at the time of inspection, relevant for temperature-sensitive diagnostic tests (e.g., thermography, oil analysis).

attributes.name: approval_timestamp

attributes.name: defect_description

attributes.name: estimated_remediation_cost

products.name: valuation
products.description: Periodic valuation record for utility assets supporting RAB (Regulatory Asset Base) determination, insurance valuation, and fair value assessment. products.name: asset_risk_assessment
products.description: Risk-based assessment record for utility assets evaluating probability of failure (PoF), consequence of failure (CoF), and overall asset risk score using industry-standard methodologies. Captures assessment date, risk methodology (risk matrix, Monte Carlo simulation, Weibull analysis), probability of failure rating based on age, condition, loading, and environment, consequence categories (safety, environment, reliability/SAIDI-SAIFI impact, financial, regulatory/compliance), overall risk score, risk band (critical, high, medium, low), recommended intervention (replace, refurbish, increase monitoring, accept risk), cost-benefit analysis of intervention, and risk-informed maintenance priority ranking. Supports risk-based asset management (RBAM) per ISO 55000, IRP investment justification, and PUC prudency review evidence. Sourced from Ventyx Asset Suite Risk module and enterprise risk management systems.

products.name: work_order_material_issue
products.description: This association product represents the Material Issue Transaction between work_order and spare_parts_inventory. It captures the consumption of spare parts, materials, and consumables against maintenance work orders in utility asset management operations. Each record links one work order to one spare part inventory item with transactional attributes including quantities issued and returned, costs at time of issue, timestamps, material document references, and cost allocation codes. This is a core operational entity in EAM/CMMS systems (Ventyx Asset Suite, SAP PM, Maximo) that enables material cost tracking, inventory consumption analysis, and work order cost rollup.. Existence Justification: In utility asset management operations, maintenance work orders consume multiple spare parts and materials (transformers, insulators, cables, tools, consumables), and each spare part in inventory is issued to multiple work orders over its lifecycle. Material issue transactions are actively created by storeroom clerks and technicians during work execution, with each transaction recording quantities, costs, timestamps, and document references. This is a recognized operational entity in EAM systems called Material Issue, Parts Consumption, or Material Document.

Each enrollment has distinct capacity commitments, performance metrics, baseline methodologies, and settlement rates that are managed independently by the demand response operations team.

It captures the compliance status, verification history, and evidence management for each asset-obligation pair. Each record links one asset to one regulatory obligation with attributes that track compliance verification dates, responsible parties, and audit evidence specific to that asset's compliance with that particular obligation.. Existence Justification: In energy utilities operations, individual physical assets (transformers, transmission towers, substations, protection relays) are each subject to multiple regulatory obligations from different governing bodies (NERC CIP cybersecurity standards, EPA emissions limits, OSHA safety mandates, FERC reliability requirements). Simultaneously, each regulatory obligation applies to many assets across the utility's asset base based on asset characteristics like voltage class, criticality score, and operational function. Compliance teams actively manage this many-to-many relationship by tracking verification dates, collecting evidence, assigning responsible parties, and preparing for audits on each asset-obligation pair.

products.name: ppa_allocation
products.description: This association product represents the allocation relationship between physical generation assets and renewable power purchase agreement contracts. It captures the contractual assignment of specific assets (or portions thereof) to PPA contracts for renewable attribute tracking, settlement, and RPS compliance. Each record links one asset to one PPA contract with allocation percentage, contracted capacity, pricing terms, and effective dates that exist only in the context of this specific asset-contract pairing.. Existence Justification: In utility-scale renewable energy procurement, portfolio PPAs routinely allocate generation from multiple physical assets (e.g., individual wind turbines, solar array sections, or entire generation facilities) to a single contract to aggregate capacity and meet volume commitments. Conversely, a single asset can participate in multiple PPAs simultaneously through time-slicing (baseload energy sold to one contract, renewable attributes to another), partial capacity allocation, or sequential contract assignments. The allocation relationship itself carries critical operational data including allocation percentage, asset-specific pricing, effective dates, and settlement meter assignments that belong to neither the asset nor the PPA alone.

products.name: impact_assessment
products.description: This association product represents the technical impact assessment between a utility asset and an interconnection application. It captures the engineering analysis of how a proposed distributed energy resource (DER) interconnection affects specific grid assets, including thermal loading, voltage regulation, protection coordination, and required upgrades. Each record links one asset to one interconnection application with impact-specific attributes that exist only in the context of this relationship. This is the foundation for cluster study formation, cost allocation, and queue management under FERC Order 2023 and state interconnection rules.. Existence Justification: In utility interconnection operations, a single interconnection application routinely impacts multiple grid assets (transformer, feeder, substation, protection devices) that must be analyzed for thermal, voltage, and protection impacts. Conversely, a single asset can be affected by multiple pending interconnection applications in the queue, requiring coordinated analysis to determine cumulative impacts and shared upgrade costs. Utilities actively manage these asset-application impact assessments as part of the technical review process, tracking impact type, severity, upgrade requirements, and cost allocation for each asset-application combination.

products.name: der_connection
products.description: This association product represents the physical electrical connection between a utility asset and a distributed energy resource (DER) system. It captures the technical configuration, protection coordination, metering arrangement, and operational status of each connection point. Each record links one asset_registry entry to one der_system with attributes that exist only in the context of this specific interconnection configuration. Essential for distribution operations, protection coordination, outage management, and maintenance planning of DER-integrated grid infrastructure.. Existence Justification: In utility distribution operations, a single DER system (solar PV, battery storage, EV charger) physically connects to multiple utility assets at the point of interconnection - typically a service transformer, revenue meter, utility-accessible disconnect switch, and protection relay. Conversely, a single utility asset such as a distribution transformer or secondary service panel can serve multiple DER systems installed at different customer premises or even multiple DER systems at the same location. Each connection has unique technical attributes including metering configuration, protection coordination settings, connection capacity limits, and operational status that belong to the specific DER-asset pairing, not to either entity alone.

Each record links one capital project to one environmental permit with attributes that exist only in the context of this regulatory compliance relationship.. Existence Justification: Capital projects in energy utilities require multiple environmental permits (EPA Title V air permits, NPDES water discharge permits, wetlands permits, endangered species authorizations) depending on project scope and location. Each permit applies to multiple projects over its validity period. Environmental compliance officers actively manage project-permit relationships by tracking compliance with specific permit conditions, conducting verification activities, documenting mitigation measures, and coordinating regulatory inspections for each project-permit combination.
products.reference: Internal - M:N Association

attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the environmental permit governing this project

attributes.name: compliance_status

attributes.name: environmental_permit_number

This attribute should be removed from capital_project as the relationship is properly modeled through the project_permit association, which can link to multiple permits and track permit-specific compliance details.]

attributes.name: mitigation_measure_description
attributes.description: Description of specific mitigation measures, controls, or corrective actions implemented for this project to comply with this permit condition. May include engineering controls, monitoring protocols, or operational restrictions.

attributes.name: next_inspection_date
attributes.description: Scheduled date for the next regulatory inspection or compliance verification for this project-permit combination.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Additional notes, comments, or documentation references related to permit compliance for this specific project.

attributes.name: permit_application_date

attributes.name: permit_approval_date

attributes.name: permit_condition_number
attributes.description: Specific permit condition number or reference that applies to this capital project. Each permit may have multiple conditions, and projects must track compliance with specific applicable conditions.

attributes.name: responsible_party
attributes.description: Name or identifier of the individual or team responsible for ensuring compliance with this permit condition for this specific project. May be project manager, environmental coordinator, or compliance officer.

attributes.name: verification_date
attributes.description: Date when compliance with this permit condition was last verified by environmental compliance staff or regulatory inspectors.

domains.name: renewable
domains.description: Renewable energy resource management including utility-scale wind farms, solar arrays, battery storage, and hydroelectric facilities. Manages DER registration, DERMS integration, REC issuance and retirement, RPS compliance portfolios, renewable generation forecasting, curtailment management, BTM generation tracking, NEM credits, and VPP aggregation configurations. Supports state renewable portfolio standards and clean energy mandates.
domains.references: FERC Order 2222, RPS State Mandates, NERC BAL, DERMS

products.name: der_registry
products.description: Master registry of all Distributed Energy Resources (DERs) registered within the utility service territory. Captures DER type (solar PV, battery storage, small wind, fuel cell), nameplate capacity (kW/MW), technology class, interconnection point (POI), DERMS system identifier, commissioning date, operational status, ownership structure (customer-owned, third-party, utility), and geographic coordinates. SSOT for all distributed generation and storage assets participating in utility programs including NEM, VPP, demand response, and storage incentives. Excludes utility-scale generation facilities mastered in the generation domain and customer-level interconnection applications managed in the interconnection domain.
products.reference: DERMS DER Registry / NERC Generator Registration

attributes.name: der_registry_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the DER registration record. Primary key for the DER registry.
attributes.references: IEEE 1547 - Standard for Interconnecting Distributed Resources with Electric Power Systems

attributes.name: commissioning_technician_employee_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: DER commissioning requires licensed electricians to perform final inspections, sign-off, and permission-to-operate certification. Tracks responsible technician for regulatory compliance, warranty clai

attributes.name: control_area_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to grid.control_area. Business justification: DERs operate within specific control areas for balancing authority coordination, ACE calculation, frequency regulation, and interchange scheduling. Control area operators need visibility of all DER ca

attributes.name: distribution_substation_id
attributes.description: Distribution substation identifier serving the DER location. Used for substation-level DER aggregation, capacity planning, and grid impact analysis.

attributes.name: ems_node_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to grid.ems_node. Business justification: Large DERs (>1MW typically) modeled as EMS nodes for state estimation, power flow analysis, and contingency analysis. Required for grid operators to include DER generation in real-time network models

attributes.name: feeder_id
attributes.description: Distribution feeder circuit identifier where the DER is interconnected. Used for hosting capacity analysis, voltage regulation studies, and feeder-level DER penetration tracking.

attributes.name: fixed_asset_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.fixed_asset. Business justification: Utility-owned DER installations (solar, storage) are capitalized fixed assets requiring FERC account assignment, depreciation, and rate base inclusion; core link for renewable asset accounting and reg

attributes.name: forecast_zone_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to forecast.zone. Business justification: DER assets are geographically assigned to forecast zones for aggregated load and generation forecasting, resource adequacy assessments, and distribution planning. Essential for modeling DER impact on

attributes.name: material_master_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to supply.material_master. Business justification: DER equipment (inverters, batteries, solar panels) are procured materials with part numbers, specifications, and warranty tracking. Real business process: asset lifecycle management, spare parts plann

attributes.name: btm_generation_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the DER is a behind-the-meter installation serving on-site load. True for customer-sited resources that offset premise consumption. False for front-of-meter or utility-scale resources that export all generation to the grid.

attributes.name: commissioning_date
attributes.description: Date when the DER completed all interconnection requirements and was authorized to begin commercial operation. Used for Renewable Energy Certificate (REC) vintage determination, incentive eligibility, and asset age tracking.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this DER registry record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking.
attributes.references: SOX Internal Controls - Audit Trail Requirements

attributes.name: curtailment_capable_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the DER can be remotely curtailed by the utility or aggregator. True if the resource has communication and control infrastructure for dispatch down commands. False if the resource operates autonomously without remote control capability.
attributes.references: IEEE 2030.5 - Demand Response and Load Control

attributes.name: data_source_system
attributes.description: Name of the source system or application that provided this DER registration data. Examples include interconnection application systems, DERMS platforms, or manual registration portals. Used for data lineage and reconciliation.

attributes.name: decommissioning_date
attributes.description: Date when the DER was permanently removed from service and disconnected from the grid. Null for active resources. Used for asset lifecycle tracking and capacity planning.
attributes.references: State Public Utility Commission Decommissioning Requirements

attributes.name: demand_response_eligible_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the DER is eligible to participate in utility demand response programs. True if the resource has controllable load or dispatchable generation/storage capability. False if ineligible due to size, technology, or operational constraints.

attributes.name: der_name
attributes.description: Business name or designation of the distributed energy resource installation.

attributes.name: der_to_enrollment
attributes.description: FK to renewable.renewable_der_enrollment.renewable_der_enrollment_id — DER enrollment records must reference the specific DER they enroll. This is the fundamental master-to-transaction link for DER program management.

attributes.name: der_type
attributes.description: Classification of the DER technology. Solar PV includes rooftop and ground-mount photovoltaic systems. Battery storage includes lithium-ion, flow batteries, and other electrochemical storage. Wind includes small-scale turbines under 1 MW. Fuel cell includes hydrogen and natural gas fuel cells. Combined heat and power (CHP) includes cogeneration systems. Microturbine includes small combustion turbines.
attributes.references: FERC Order 2222 - Participation of Distributed Energy Resource Aggregations in Markets

attributes.name: derms_system_code
attributes.business_glossary_term: Distributed Energy Resource Management System (DERMS) System ID
attributes.description: External system identifier used by the DERMS platform to monitor and control this DER. Enables real-time dispatch, curtailment commands, and telemetry integration. Null for DERs not enrolled in DERMS programs.
attributes.references: IEEE 2030.5 - Smart Energy Profile Application Protocol

attributes.name: export_limit_kw
attributes.description: Maximum power export limit in kilowatts (kW) allowed by the interconnection agreement. May be less than nameplate capacity due to grid constraints, NEM program rules, or hosting capacity limitations. Null if no export limit applies.

attributes.name: forecast_provider
attributes.description: Name of the third-party or internal system providing generation forecasts for this DER. Used for solar and wind resources requiring day-ahead and real-time production forecasting. Null for non-variable resources.

attributes.name: incentive_program_code
attributes.description: Code identifying the utility or state incentive program under which the DER was installed. Examples include solar rebate programs, storage incentives, or federal Investment Tax Credit (ITC) tracking. Null if no incentive was claimed.
attributes.references: State and Federal Renewable Energy Incentive Programs

attributes.name: installation_cost_usd
attributes.description: Total installed cost of the DER in US dollars including equipment, labor, permitting, and interconnection fees. Business-confidential. Used for incentive program cost-effectiveness analysis and LCOE calculations.

attributes.name: interconnection_agreement_number
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the executed interconnection agreement governing the DERs connection to the utility grid. References the legal contract specifying technical requirements, liability, and operational protocols.

attributes.name: last_inspection_date
attributes.description: Date of the most recent utility or third-party inspection of the DER installation. Used for compliance verification, safety audit tracking, and periodic re-certification requirements.
attributes.references: OSHA and State Electrical Inspection Requirements

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this DER registry record was most recently updated. Used for change tracking, data quality monitoring, and audit trail purposes.
attributes.references: SOX Internal Controls - Audit Trail Requirements

attributes.name: latitude
attributes.description: Geographic latitude coordinate of the DER installation in decimal degrees. Used for GIS mapping, solar irradiance modeling, weather correlation, and grid topology analysis.

attributes.name: longitude
attributes.description: Geographic longitude coordinate of the DER installation in decimal degrees. Used for GIS mapping, solar irradiance modeling, weather correlation, and grid topology analysis.

attributes.name: meter_number
attributes.description: Utility meter identifier associated with the DER interconnection point. References the revenue meter or production meter used for NEM credit calculation, billing, and generation tracking. May reference a dedicated production meter or the premise service meter.

attributes.name: nameplate_capacity_kw
attributes.description: Maximum rated power output or storage capacity of the DER in kilowatts (kW). For generation resources, this is the AC output rating. For battery storage, this is the maximum discharge rate. Critical for grid planning, interconnection studies, and program eligibility determination.

attributes.name: nem_eligible_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the DER is eligible for Net Energy Metering (NEM) programs. True if the resource meets size, technology, and jurisdictional requirements for NEM credit generation. False if ineligible or enrolled in alternative compensation mechanisms.

attributes.name: next_inspection_due_date
attributes.description: Scheduled date for the next required inspection or compliance verification. Null if no periodic inspection is required. Used for proactive maintenance scheduling and regulatory compliance tracking.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for additional comments, special conditions, or operational notes related to the DER registration. May include interconnection study findings, operational restrictions, or program-specific requirements.

attributes.name: operational_status
attributes.description: Current operational state of the DER. Commissioned indicates the resource has completed interconnection and is authorized to operate. Operational indicates active generation or storage capability. Offline indicates temporary non-operation due to maintenance or technical issues. Decommissioned indicates permanent removal from service. Suspended indicates administrative hold. Testing indicates pre-commissioning validation phase.

attributes.name: owner_name
attributes.description: Legal name of the entity that owns the DER asset. May be a residential customer, commercial entity, or third-party developer. Business-confidential for competitive and privacy reasons.

attributes.name: ownership_structure
attributes.description: Legal ownership model of the DER. Customer-owned indicates the premise owner owns the asset. Third-party-owned indicates a solar lease, PPA, or other third-party financing arrangement. Utility-owned indicates utility-scale BTM assets. Community-shared indicates community solar or shared renewable programs.

attributes.name: poi_identifier
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the physical point where the DER connects to the utility distribution system. References the specific transformer, service panel, or substation bus where interconnection occurs. Critical for grid modeling, outage management, and voltage regulation analysis.
attributes.references: IEEE 1547 - Point of Common Coupling Requirements

attributes.name: rec_eligible_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the DER is eligible to generate Renewable Energy Certificates (RECs). True if the resource is a qualifying renewable technology under state RPS rules. False if ineligible due to technology type, vintage, or jurisdictional requirements.

attributes.name: registration_date
attributes.description: Date when the DER was first registered in the utility DER registry. Represents the initial record creation date, which may precede commissioning. Used for audit trail and registration workflow tracking.

attributes.name: rps_compliance_tier
attributes.description: RPS tier classification for the DER under state renewable portfolio standards. Tiers typically differentiate by technology type, vintage, or geographic location. Examples include Tier 1 (new renewables), Tier 2 (existing renewables), Solar Carve-Out, or Distributed Generation tier. Null if not RPS-eligible.

attributes.name: service_territory
attributes.description: Utility service territory or operating company jurisdiction where the DER is located. Used for regulatory reporting, RPS compliance tracking, and jurisdictional analysis.

attributes.name: smart_inverter_capable_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the DER is equipped with IEEE 1547-2018 compliant smart inverter functionality. True if the inverter supports advanced grid support functions including volt-VAR, frequency-watt, and dynamic reactive power control. False for legacy inverters without advanced functions.

attributes.name: storage_capacity_kwh
attributes.description: Total energy storage capacity in kilowatt-hours (kWh) for battery storage and other energy storage systems. Null for non-storage DER types. Used for Virtual Power Plant (VPP) aggregation and demand response program sizing.
attributes.references: FERC Order 841 - Electric Storage Participation in Markets

attributes.name: technology_class
attributes.description: Detailed technology classification including manufacturer model, inverter type, panel efficiency class, or battery chemistry. Provides granular technical categorization beyond the primary DER type.
attributes.references: IEC 61850 - Communication Networks and Systems for Power Utility Automation

products.name: renewable_rec_certificate
products.description: Renewable Energy Certificate (REC) issuance and retirement record. Each REC represents 1 MWh of renewable electricity generated and injected into the grid. Captures certificate serial number, generation source facility or DER, generation period, technology type, vintage year, issuing registry (WREGIS, M-RETS, PJM-GATS, NAR), certificate status (issued, transferred, retired, expired), retirement reason (RPS compliance, voluntary, export), and associated RPS obligation period. SSOT for REC inventory, lifecycle tracking, and compliance retirement within the renewable domain.
products.reference: WREGIS / M-RETS / NERC GATS REC Certificate

attributes.name: renewable_rec_certificate_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the renewable energy certificate record. Primary key.

attributes.name: attestation_document_id
attributes.description: Reference identifier for the supporting documentation or attestation filed with the registry to verify generation and REC issuance. Used for audit and compliance verification.

attributes.name: der_registry_id
attributes.description: FK to renewable.der_registry.der_registry_id — Each REC must trace back to the generation source (DER or facility) that produced the 1 MWh of renewable electricity. This is a regulatory requirement for REC validity.

attributes.name: irp_scenario_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to forecast.irp_scenario. Business justification: IRP scenarios project REC generation and retirement to model RPS compliance pathways, renewable attribute tracking, and ACP exposure. Essential for long-term renewable procurement planning.

attributes.name: journal_entry_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.journal_entry. Business justification: REC issuance, transfer, and retirement trigger GL entries for inventory valuation, revenue recognition, and compliance cost accounting; direct link automates posting and provides audit trail for renew

attributes.name: meter_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to metering.meter. Business justification: REC issuance requires validated metered generation data from specific revenue-quality meters for attestation. REC audit trail and compliance verification link certificate to source meter for data line

attributes.name: obligation_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.obligation. Business justification: RECs must be tracked against specific RPS compliance obligations for regulatory reporting. Utilities track which RPS mandate each REC satisfies. Critical for RPS compliance verification and obligation

attributes.name: power_plant_id
attributes.description: Reference to the renewable generation facility or distributed energy resource (DER) that produced the electricity represented by this REC.

attributes.name: registry_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to asset.asset_registry. Business justification: RECs issued from utility-owned renewable assets require asset linkage for RPS compliance audits, vintage tracking, and double-counting prevention. Complements existing power_plant_id for non-plant ren

attributes.name: rps_obligation_id
attributes.description: FK to renewable.rps_obligation.rps_obligation_id — RECs are retired to satisfy RPS obligations. This is the core compliance linkage — every REC retirement for RPS compliance must reference the specific obligation period it satisfies. Production-critic

attributes.name: vpp_configuration_id
attributes.description: Reference to the virtual power plant (VPP) or DER aggregation program if this REC was generated by a facility participating in aggregated dispatch. Null for standalone facilities.

attributes.name: certificate_serial_number
attributes.description: Unique serial number assigned by the issuing registry to this REC. This is the externally-known identifier used for tracking, trading, and retirement across registries and market participants.
attributes.references: WREGIS, M-RETS, PJM-GATS, NAR Registry Standards

attributes.name: certificate_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the REC. Issued: newly created; Active: available for trading; Transferred: ownership changed; Retired: used for compliance or voluntary claim; Expired: past validity period; Cancelled: invalidated; Suspended: temporarily held. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: issued|active|transferred|retired|expired|cancelled|suspended — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: NERC, FERC, State PUC REC Tracking Standards

attributes.name: compliance_year
attributes.description: Calendar year for which this REC was retired to meet RPS compliance obligations. May differ from vintage year due to banking or forward compliance rules.
attributes.references: State PUC RPS Compliance Reporting Standards

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this REC record was first created in the internal system. Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking.

attributes.name: curtailment_mwh
attributes.description: Amount of renewable generation that was curtailed (not delivered to grid) during the generation period due to grid constraints or economic dispatch. Subtracted from gross generation to determine net REC-eligible generation.

attributes.name: data_source_system
attributes.description: Name of the source system or registry API from which this REC data was ingested. Examples: WREGIS API, M-RETS API, manual entry, internal generation system.

attributes.name: eligibility_flags
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of eligibility attributes for this REC, such as tier classification (Tier I, Tier II), solar carve-out eligibility, new facility status, or other state-specific program qualifications.

attributes.name: expiration_date
attributes.description: Date after which the REC can no longer be used for compliance or voluntary claims. Typically 3-5 years from vintage year depending on state rules.

attributes.name: facility_commercial_operation_date
attributes.description: Date when the generation facility began commercial operation. Used to determine new vs. existing facility status for RPS tier classification.
attributes.references: FERC, State PUC Facility Registration Standards

attributes.name: facility_county
attributes.description: County or equivalent administrative region where the generation facility is located. Used for local content and economic development tracking.

attributes.name: facility_state
attributes.description: Two-letter US state code or three-letter country code where the generation facility is located. Used for determining RPS eligibility and geographic tracking.
attributes.references: ISO 3166-1 Alpha-2/3, State RPS Geographic Eligibility Rules

attributes.name: generation_end_date
attributes.description: End date of the generation period during which the renewable electricity represented by this REC was produced.

attributes.name: generation_mwh
attributes.description: Quantity of renewable electricity generation represented by this REC, measured in megawatt-hours. Each REC typically represents 1 MWh of renewable generation injected into the grid.

attributes.name: generation_start_date
attributes.description: Start date of the generation period during which the renewable electricity represented by this REC was produced.

attributes.name: grid_injection_point
attributes.description: Point of interconnection (POI) identifier where the renewable generation was injected into the transmission or distribution grid. Used for locational tracking and grid impact analysis.

attributes.name: issuance_date
attributes.description: Date on which the REC was officially issued by the registry and became available for trading or retirement.

attributes.name: issuing_registry
attributes.description: Name of the regional or national registry that issued and tracks this REC. WREGIS: Western Renewable Energy Generation Information System; M-RETS: Midwest Renewable Energy Tracking System; PJM-GATS: PJM Generation Attribute Tracking System; NAR: North American Renewables Registry; NEPOOL-GIS: New England Power Pool Generation Information System; ERCOT: Electric Reliability Council of Texas; MIRECS: Michigan Renewable Energy Certification System. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: WREGIS|M-RETS|PJM-GATS|NAR|NEPOOL-GIS|ERCOT|MIRECS — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this REC record was last updated in the internal system. Used for audit trail and change tracking.

attributes.name: market_value_usd
attributes.description: Estimated or actual market value of this REC in US dollars at the time of issuance or most recent valuation. Used for financial reporting and portfolio valuation.
attributes.references: GAAP, FASB ASC 820 Fair Value Measurement

attributes.name: nameplate_capacity_mw
attributes.description: Maximum rated electrical output capacity of the generation facility in megawatts at the time of REC issuance. Used for facility classification and program eligibility.

attributes.name: net_metering_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the generation represented by this REC came from a behind-the-meter (BTM) net metering facility. True if NEM generation; False if utility-scale or non-NEM DER.
attributes.references: State NEM Program Rules, PURPA Standards

attributes.name: retirement_date
attributes.description: Date on which the REC was retired and removed from circulation. Null if the REC has not been retired.
attributes.references: State PUC RPS Compliance Reporting Standards

attributes.name: retirement_reason
attributes.description: Business reason for retiring the REC. RPS Compliance: used to meet state renewable portfolio standard obligations; Voluntary Green Power: customer voluntary renewable energy program; Export Compliance: retired for out-of-state RPS; Corporate Sustainability: retired for corporate renewable energy goals; Carbon Offset: retired for carbon neutrality claims.
attributes.references: State RPS Compliance Standards, EPA Green Power Partnership

attributes.name: rps_obligation_period
attributes.description: The compliance period (typically a calendar year or program year) for which this REC is being applied toward RPS obligations. Format: YYYY or YYYY-YYYY for multi-year periods.
attributes.references: State PUC RPS Compliance Reporting Standards

attributes.name: technology_type
attributes.description: Type of renewable energy technology used to generate the electricity. Solar PV: photovoltaic solar; Wind: onshore or offshore wind turbines; Hydroelectric: run-of-river or reservoir hydro; Biomass: organic material combustion; Geothermal: earth heat; Landfill Gas: methane capture.
attributes.references: EPA Renewable Energy Standards, State RPS Definitions

attributes.name: trading_platform
attributes.description: Name of the electronic trading platform or bilateral agreement mechanism through which this REC was last traded. Examples: Marex Spectron, Evolution Markets, bilateral OTC.

attributes.name: transfer_history_count
attributes.description: Number of times this REC has been transferred between accounts since issuance. Used for audit trail and market activity analysis.

attributes.name: vintage_year
attributes.description: Calendar year in which the renewable electricity was generated. Used for RPS compliance tracking and market valuation, as some programs require current or recent vintage RECs.

products.name: rps_obligation
products.description: Renewable Portfolio Standard (RPS) compliance obligation and running position record per compliance period and state jurisdiction. Captures the regulatory target (obligated retail sales MWh, required renewable percentage, technology-specific carve-outs for solar/offshore wind/storage, ACP rate) and the running compliance position against that target (RECs retired to date, RECs in inventory, projected shortfall or surplus MWh, compliance percentage achieved, last reconciliation timestamp). Includes compliance deadline, filing status, and alternative compliance payment exposure. SSOT for RPS obligation targets AND compliance position tracking within the renewable domain — no separate position product exists. Feeds regulatory filings to state PUCs and internal compliance dashboards.
products.reference: State PUC RPS Compliance Filing / FERC RPS Reporting

attributes.name: rps_obligation_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the RPS compliance obligation record. Primary key for the RPS obligation entity.

attributes.name: irp_scenario_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to forecast.irp_scenario. Business justification: RPS compliance obligations drive renewable capacity targets in IRP scenarios. Scenarios model pathways to meet RPS requirements, including capacity additions, REC procurement, and ACP exposure.

attributes.name: obligation_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.obligation. Business justification: RPS obligations are regulatory compliance obligations under state renewable portfolio standards. Links RPS-specific tracking to enterprise compliance framework. Essential for integrated compliance man

attributes.name: regulatory_asset_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.regulatory_asset. Business justification: RPS compliance costs (ACP payments, REC procurement above market) create regulatory assets for future rate recovery; link supports rate case filings, FERC Form 1 reporting, and amortization tracking.

attributes.name: acp_exposure_amount
attributes.description: Total financial exposure in dollars for Alternative Compliance Payments based on projected shortfall multiplied by ACP rate. Represents potential penalty cost if shortfall is not remedied.

attributes.name: acp_paid_amount
attributes.description: Actual Alternative Compliance Payment amount in dollars paid to the state for this compliance period. Null if no ACP has been paid.

attributes.name: acp_rate_per_mwh
attributes.business_glossary_term: Alternative Compliance Payment (ACP) Rate per Megawatt-Hour (MWh)
attributes.description: Regulatory penalty rate per MWh for shortfall, expressed in dollars per MWh. This is the Alternative Compliance Payment rate that the utility must pay for each MWh of unmet RPS obligation.

attributes.name: compliance_deadline_date
attributes.description: Regulatory deadline by which the utility must demonstrate full compliance with the RPS obligation for this period. Typically 3-6 months after the compliance period end date.

attributes.name: compliance_percentage_achieved
attributes.description: Current compliance percentage achieved based on RECs retired to date divided by required renewable MWh, expressed as a percentage. Indicates progress toward meeting the RPS obligation.

attributes.name: compliance_period_end_date
attributes.description: End date of the compliance period for this RPS obligation. Typically December 31 of the compliance year.

attributes.name: compliance_period_start_date
attributes.description: Start date of the compliance period for this RPS obligation. Typically January 1 of the compliance year.

attributes.name: compliance_period_year
attributes.description: Calendar year for which this RPS obligation applies. RPS compliance is typically measured annually or over multi-year periods.

attributes.name: compliance_status
attributes.description: Current status of the RPS obligation compliance. In_progress indicates the compliance period is active; compliant indicates full compliance achieved; shortfall indicates projected or actual deficit; surplus indicates excess compliance; filed indicates compliance report submitted; under_review indicates regulatory review in progress.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this RPS obligation record was first created in the system. Audit field for data lineage.

attributes.name: filing_status
attributes.description: Status of the regulatory compliance filing to the state PUC. Not_filed indicates no filing yet; draft indicates filing in preparation; submitted indicates filing delivered to regulator; accepted indicates regulator approval; rejected indicates regulator rejection; amended indicates revised filing submitted.

attributes.name: filing_submission_date
attributes.description: Date on which the RPS compliance filing was submitted to the state PUC. Null if not yet filed.

attributes.name: jurisdiction_code
attributes.description: Two-letter state code identifying the regulatory jurisdiction imposing the RPS obligation (e.g., CA for California, NY for New York, MA for Massachusetts).

attributes.name: last_reconciliation_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent reconciliation of the RPS compliance position. Indicates when RECs retired, inventory, and shortfall/surplus calculations were last updated.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text notes capturing additional context, assumptions, or special circumstances related to this RPS obligation. May include details on carve-out strategies, banking decisions, or regulatory correspondence.

attributes.name: obligated_retail_sales_mwh
attributes.description: Total retail electricity sales in MWh subject to the RPS obligation for this compliance period. This is the base quantity against which the renewable percentage requirement is applied.

attributes.name: offshore_wind_carveout_mwh
attributes.description: Absolute quantity of offshore wind energy in MWh required to meet the offshore wind carve-out. Null if no offshore wind carve-out applies.

attributes.name: offshore_wind_carveout_percentage
attributes.description: Technology-specific carve-out percentage requiring a minimum portion of the RPS obligation to be met with offshore wind generation. Null if no offshore wind carve-out applies.

attributes.name: projected_shortfall_mwh
attributes.description: Projected shortfall in MWh between the required renewable MWh and the sum of RECs retired plus RECs in inventory. Positive value indicates a deficit; null or zero indicates compliance is on track or surplus exists.

attributes.name: projected_surplus_mwh
attributes.description: Projected surplus in MWh beyond the required renewable MWh. Positive value indicates excess RECs available for banking or future compliance periods; null or zero indicates no surplus.

attributes.name: reconciliation_frequency
attributes.description: Frequency at which the RPS compliance position is reconciled and updated. Indicates how often the running position is refreshed.

attributes.name: recs_inventory_mwh
attributes.description: Quantity of RECs in MWh currently held in inventory and available for retirement toward this compliance period. Represents banked RECs not yet applied.

attributes.name: recs_retired_mwh
attributes.description: Total quantity of RECs in MWh that have been retired to date for this compliance period. This is the running compliance position representing actual compliance achieved.
