products.name: workforce_crew_dispatch
products.description: This association product represents the operational dispatch event linking field crews to outage restoration work. Each record captures a single dispatch assignment of one crew to one outage event, including dispatch timing, arrival, work execution windows, crew status transitions, priority, and field notes. This is the authoritative SSOT for crew deployment history, response time tracking, restoration labor allocation, and post-storm after-action analysis. Crew dispatches are created by OMS dispatchers, updated by field supervisors via mobile devices, and consumed by workforce analytics, FEMA reimbursement reporting, and reliability performance measurement systems.. Existence Justification: Crew dispatch to outage events is a canonical M:N operational relationship in utility outage management. A single major outage event (e.g., transmission line failure, storm damage) routinely requires multiple crews dispatched sequentially or simultaneously for damage assessment, isolation, repair, and restoration. Conversely, a single crew responds to multiple distinct outage events during a shift, storm period, or mutual aid deployment. Each dispatch is an operational business event actively managed by OMS dispatchers with rich lifecycle data including dispatch timing, arrival, work execution windows, status transitions, priority, and field notes.
products.reference: Internal - M:N Association

attributes.name: dispatch_source

attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the crew dispatch assignment. Transitions tracked in OMS for real-time crew location awareness and restoration progress monitoring. products.name: project_assignment
products.description: This association product represents the Assignment between employee and capex_project. It captures the allocation of utility personnel to capital expenditure projects with role, time allocation, labor rates, and assignment lifecycle dates. Each record links one employee to one capex_project with attributes that exist only in the context of this specific project assignment. Supports capital cost tracking, labor capitalization, FERC reporting of labor costs by project, and resource planning across the capital portfolio.. Existence Justification: In utility capital project operations, employees are routinely assigned to multiple capital projects simultaneously with different roles and time allocations (e.g., a senior engineer at 30% on substation upgrade, 40% on transmission line replacement, 30% on distribution automation). Conversely, capital projects require cross-functional teams with multiple employees across disciplines (project managers, engineers, technicians, planners, safety officers). The business actively manages these assignments with specific roles, allocation percentages, labor rates, and approval workflows for capital cost tracking and FERC reporting.

products.name: scenario_participation
products.description: This association product represents the participation relationship between employees and IRP scenarios. It captures the role-based contribution of utility personnel (analysts, engineers, economists, managers) in developing, reviewing, and approving Integrated Resource Plan scenarios. Each record links one employee to one IRP scenario with attributes that document their specific role, contribution type, approval authority, and participation timeline. This data is critical for regulatory documentation, cross-examination preparation in PUC proceedings, and tracking accountability for scenario assumptions and modeling decisions.. Existence Justification: IRP scenario development is a collaborative multi-disciplinary process where multiple employees (analysts, engineers, economists, managers) contribute to each scenario in different roles, and each employee typically works on multiple scenarios within an IRP filing (base case, high growth, low carbon, etc.). The utility must track who participated in each scenario, their specific role and contribution type, approval authority level, and participation timeline for regulatory documentation and cross-examination preparation in PUC proceedings.

domains.name: compliance
domains.description: Regulatory compliance management including NERC CIP audits, FERC reporting, PUC rate cases, environmental permits, emissions reporting to EPA, reliability standards documentation, SOX controls, and CPCN applications. Manages compliance obligations, audit trails, regulatory filings, evidence collection, enforcement action records, and regulatory correspondence. Serves as SSOT for compliance posture reporting to the Board and external regulators.
domains.references: NERC CIP, FERC Form 1, EPA CAMD, SOX, PUC

products.name: obligation
products.description: Master registry of all regulatory compliance obligations applicable to the utility, including NERC CIP standards, FERC tariff requirements, PUC service territory rules, EPA emissions limits, OSHA safety mandates, SOX internal controls, CPCN conditions, and NERC reliability standard sub-requirements. Each obligation record captures the governing body, regulatory citation, effective dates, applicability scope (generation, transmission, distribution, trading), compliance frequency, responsible organizational unit, violation risk factor (VRF), violation severity level (VSL) where applicable, and current compliance status. Serves as the SSOT for what the utility is required to do and by when, and drives audit preparation, evidence collection workflows, risk assessment prioritization, and regulatory filing schedules.

products.name: regulatory_filing
products.description: Transactional record of every formal submission made to a regulatory body, encompassing routine periodic filings, regulatory proceeding applications, market transaction reports, proactive self-disclosures, rate case proceedings, and long-term resource planning filings. Covers FERC Form 1, FERC EQR, FERC Form 552, FERC market-based rate tariff filings, NERC reliability standard audit submissions, PUC general and transmission rate case filings (including test year, revenue requirement, proposed rate changes, intervenor parties, procedural milestones, settlement status, and commission orders), CPCN applications for major capital projects (including project description, capital cost, environmental review, and certificate conditions), IRP filings (including planning horizon, load forecast, resource scenarios, and commission approval), EPA emissions reports, RPS compliance filings, self-reported potential violations (SPVs), FERC voluntary disclosures, and EPA self-disclosure submissions. Captures filing type, docket number, regulatory agency, submission date, filing period, filing status, responsible preparer, and filing-type-specific detail attributes. SSOT for all outbound regulatory submissions, regulatory proceeding lifecycle tracking, proactive disclosure management, rate case management, and resource planning filings.

products.name: audit_finding
products.description: Individual compliance deficiency, exception, gap, or near-miss record identified through formal audit, internal monitoring, control testing, self-assessment, or operational review. Covers NERC CIP potential violations (PVs), FERC market rule violations, PUC service quality deficiencies, SOX control deficiencies, internally discovered compliance exceptions, and proactive near-miss identifications. Captures finding reference number, associated audit (if audit-originated), violated standard or rule citation, severity classification, discovery method (external audit, internal audit, self-monitoring, employee report, control testing), finding description, root cause category, risk severity, business unit responsible, remediation due date, and escalation status (including whether self-reporting is warranted). Serves as the single register for all compliance deficiencies regardless of discovery channel — from formal audit findings to internally identified exceptions. Drives the enforcement and corrective action workflow, and feeds the self-report filing process when internal findings warrant proactive disclosure.
products.reference: NERC Violation Risk Factor / Violation Severity Level Matrix; FERC Enforcement Advisory

attributes.description: Identifier of the environmental compliance officer responsible for managing this permit and ensuring ongoing compliance with permit conditions.

attributes.name: environmental_obligation_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.obligation. Business justification: Each environmental permit fulfills a specific regulatory obligation (e.g., EPA Title V air permit, NPDES water discharge permit). Many permits can fulfill one obligation (1:N). Adding obligation_id FK

attributes.name: obligation_id
attributes.description: FK to compliance.obligation.obligation_id — Environmental permits create compliance obligations (permit conditions become obligations). Links permit portfolio to the obligation registry.

attributes.name: power_plant_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the generation, transmission, or distribution facility covered by this environmental permit. Links permit to the physical asset location where environmental compliance is enforced.

attributes.name: appeal_status
attributes.description: Status of any administrative or judicial appeal of permit conditions. Appeals can delay permit effectiveness or result in modified conditions.
attributes.references: EPA Administrative Appeals Process, Environmental Appeals Board

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this permit record was first created in the compliance management system. Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking.

attributes.name: data_source_system
attributes.description: Name of the source system from which this permit record was ingested (e.g., SAP EHS, environmental compliance database, regulatory agency portal). Used for data lineage and reconciliation.

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: The date the environmental permit becomes legally binding and enforceable. May differ from issuance date if permit includes a delayed effective date provision.

attributes.name: enforcement_action_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this permit is currently subject to an active enforcement action, consent decree, or compliance order from the regulatory agency.
attributes.references: EPA Enforcement and Compliance History Online (ECHO)

attributes.name: expiration_date
attributes.description: The date the environmental permit expires and must be renewed. Operating beyond expiration without renewal constitutes a violation subject to enforcement action and penalties.
attributes.references: EPA Permit Renewal Requirements, Clean Air Act Section 502(b)(5)

attributes.name: facility_epa_code
attributes.business_glossary_term: Facility EPA (Environmental Protection Agency) Identification Number
attributes.description: The unique EPA facility identification number assigned to the permitted facility. Used for all federal environmental reporting including emissions inventories and discharge monitoring reports.

attributes.name: facility_name
attributes.description: Name of the utility facility covered by this environmental permit. Typically a power generation plant, substation, or operations center subject to environmental regulation.

attributes.name: issuance_date
attributes.description: The date the environmental permit was officially issued by the regulatory agency. Marks the beginning of the permit term and the effective date for permit conditions.

attributes.name: issuing_agency
attributes.description: Name of the federal, state, or local regulatory agency that issued the environmental permit. Typically EPA for federal permits or state environmental protection agency for state-delegated programs.
attributes.references: EPA Regional Offices, State Environmental Protection Agencies

attributes.name: issuing_agency_jurisdiction
attributes.description: The governmental jurisdiction level of the issuing agency. Determines the regulatory authority hierarchy and appeal process for permit conditions.
attributes.references: EPA Jurisdictional Framework, State Environmental Law

attributes.name: last_inspection_date
attributes.description: Date of the most recent regulatory agency inspection of the permitted facility for compliance with permit conditions. Inspections may be routine or triggered by complaints or violations.

attributes.name: last_inspection_result
attributes.description: Outcome of the most recent regulatory inspection. Major violations may result in enforcement actions, penalties, or permit modifications.

attributes.name: last_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this permit record was last modified. Tracks changes to permit status, conditions, or administrative data for compliance audit purposes.

attributes.name: monitoring_frequency
attributes.description: Required frequency for monitoring and reporting emissions or discharges under this permit. Determines compliance testing schedule and data submission deadlines to regulatory agencies.
attributes.references: EPA Continuous Emission Monitoring (CEM) Requirements, 40 CFR Part 60

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for additional notes, special circumstances, or historical context related to this permit. Used for internal compliance management and knowledge transfer.

attributes.name: permit_conditions_summary
attributes.description: High-level summary of key permit conditions, operational restrictions, and compliance obligations. Detailed conditions are maintained in permit documentation repository.

attributes.name: permit_document_url
attributes.description: URL or file path to the official permit document in the document management system. Provides access to full permit text, conditions, and attachments.

attributes.name: permit_fee_amount
attributes.description: Annual or one-time fee paid to the regulatory agency for permit issuance, renewal, or maintenance. Fee structure varies by permit type and jurisdiction.
attributes.references: EPA Permit Fee Schedule, State Environmental Fee Regulations

attributes.name: permit_fee_currency
attributes.description: Currency code for permit fees. Typically USD for US-based utility operations.

attributes.name: permit_number
attributes.description: The official permit number issued by the regulatory agency. This is the externally-known unique identifier used in all regulatory correspondence and compliance reporting.
attributes.references: EPA Title V Operating Permit Program, NPDES Permit Program

attributes.name: permit_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the environmental permit. Active permits authorize operations; expired or suspended permits require immediate remediation to avoid enforcement action.
attributes.references: EPA Permit Compliance Framework, State Environmental Agency Standards

attributes.name: permit_type
attributes.description: Classification of the environmental permit based on the regulatory program and environmental media regulated. Determines applicable compliance requirements and reporting obligations.
attributes.references: EPA Environmental Permit Classification, Clean Air Act, Clean Water Act, RCRA

attributes.name: permitted_discharge_limit_gallons_per_day
attributes.description: Maximum allowable daily water discharge volume in gallons per day under NPDES or state water discharge permit. Applies to cooling water, process water, and stormwater discharges.
attributes.references: NPDES Permit Program, Clean Water Act Section 402

attributes.name: permitted_emission_limit_tons_per_year
attributes.description: Maximum allowable annual emissions in tons per year for regulated air pollutants under this permit. Exceeding this limit constitutes a permit violation and triggers enforcement action.
attributes.references: EPA Title V Operating Permit, Clean Air Act Section 112

attributes.name: public_comment_period_end_date
attributes.description: Date the public comment period closed for this permit. After this date, the permit becomes final unless appealed.

attributes.name: public_notice_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this permit was subject to public notice and comment period as required for major permits under EPA regulations. Public participation is required for Title V and major NPDES permits.
attributes.references: EPA Public Participation Requirements, 40 CFR Part 124

attributes.name: regulated_pollutants
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of specific pollutants regulated under this permit (e.g., SO2, NOx, PM2.5, mercury, lead, benzene). Each pollutant may have individual emission or discharge limits and monitoring requirements.
attributes.references: EPA National Ambient Air Quality Standards (NAAQS), Clean Water Act Effluent Guidelines

attributes.name: renewal_application_date
attributes.description: The date the permit renewal application was submitted to the regulatory agency. Must typically be submitted 6-18 months before expiration depending on permit type and jurisdiction.
attributes.references: EPA Permit Renewal Timelines, 40 CFR Part 70

attributes.name: renewal_status
attributes.description: Current status of the permit renewal process. Tracks whether renewal application has been submitted and the agencys decision status. Critical for avoiding permit lapses.
attributes.references: EPA Permit Renewal Process, State Permit Program Requirements

attributes.name: reporting_frequency
attributes.description: Required frequency for submitting compliance reports to the regulatory agency. Missed reporting deadlines can result in notices of violation and penalties.
attributes.references: EPA Compliance Reporting Requirements, State Environmental Reporting Standards

attributes.name: responsible_party_email
attributes.description: Email address of the responsible official for regulatory correspondence and compliance notifications related to this permit.

attributes.name: responsible_party_name
attributes.description: Name of the individual or role designated as the responsible official for this permit as reported to the regulatory agency. This person certifies compliance reports and permit applications.

attributes.name: responsible_party_phone
attributes.description: Phone number of the responsible official for urgent regulatory communications and compliance inquiries.

attributes.name: responsible_party_title
attributes.description: Job title of the responsible official for this permit. Typically a senior operations or environmental manager with authority to certify compliance.

attributes.name: special_conditions_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this permit includes special or non-standard conditions beyond typical permit requirements. Special conditions often require enhanced monitoring or operational controls.

attributes.name: violation_count
attributes.description: Total number of documented violations of this permit since issuance. High violation counts may trigger enhanced oversight or permit revocation proceedings.

products.name: compliance_rec_certificate
products.description: Renewable Energy Certificate (REC) record tracking the generation, registration, transfer, retirement, and compliance use of RECs for Renewable Portfolio Standard (RPS) compliance. Captures REC serial number, generating facility, generation technology type, vintage period, MWh quantity, registry (WREGIS, NEPOOL GIS, PJM GATS, M-RETS), current owner, transfer history, retirement date, and associated RPS compliance obligation. SSOT for RPS certificate inventory, retirement tracking, and RPS compliance demonstration to state PUCs.
products.reference: WREGIS; NEPOOL GIS; PJM GATS; State RPS Regulations

attributes.name: compliance_rec_certificate_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Compliance Renewable Energy Certificate (REC) Certificate ID
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the REC certificate record. Primary key for the compliance REC certificate entity.

attributes.name: attestation_document_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the attestation or verification document supporting this REC issuance. Used for audit trail and compliance verification purposes.

attributes.name: obligation_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.obligation. Business justification: REC certificates fulfill renewable portfolio standard (RPS) obligations. Many RECs can fulfill one obligation (1:N). Adding obligation_id FK links the REC to the RPS obligation it satisfies. The rps_j

attributes.name: ppa_contract_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the Power Purchase Agreement (PPA) or REC purchase contract under which this REC was acquired. Links to contract management system for terms and conditions.

attributes.name: primary_compliance_power_plant_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the renewable energy generation facility that produced the energy for which this REC was issued. Links to the generation asset registry.

attributes.name: certificate_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the REC certificate. Active certificates are available for trading or retirement; retired certificates have been used for compliance; transferred certificates have changed ownership; cancelled certificates are voided.

attributes.name: compliance_credit_mwh
attributes.description: Effective compliance credit value after applying any multipliers. Calculated as energy_quantity_mwh × rec_multiplier. This is the value counted toward RPS obligation fulfillment.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this REC certificate record was first created in the internal compliance tracking system. Used for audit trail and data lineage purposes.

attributes.name: current_owner_name
attributes.description: Name of the current legal owner of this REC certificate. Ownership may transfer multiple times before retirement. Confidential business information.

attributes.name: data_source_system
attributes.description: Name of the source system or registry from which this REC data was ingested (e.g., WREGIS API, M-RETS feed, manual entry). Used for data lineage and reconciliation.

attributes.name: eligibility_flags
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of special eligibility attributes or certifications for this REC (e.g., in-state, new facility, low-impact hydro, community solar). Used to match RECs to specific compliance requirements.

attributes.name: emissions_avoided_co2_tons
attributes.description: Estimated tons of CO2 emissions avoided by the renewable generation represented by this REC, calculated using regional grid emission factors. Used for environmental impact reporting.

attributes.name: energy_quantity_mwh
attributes.description: Quantity of renewable energy represented by this REC certificate, measured in megawatt-hours. Typically one REC equals one MWh of renewable generation, though some programs use different ratios.

attributes.name: expiration_date
attributes.description: Date after which this REC can no longer be used for compliance purposes in the applicable jurisdiction. Many RPS programs impose vintage limits (e.g., RECs must be used within 3 years of generation).

attributes.name: facility_location_country
attributes.description: Country where the generating facility is located. Most U.S. state RPS programs only accept RECs from facilities in the U.S. or specific Canadian provinces.

attributes.name: facility_location_state
attributes.description: U.S. state or Canadian province where the generating facility is located. Geographic location affects RPS eligibility in many jurisdictions.
attributes.references: EIA-860, State RPS Geographic Eligibility Rules

attributes.name: generation_end_date
attributes.description: End date of the generation period for which this REC was issued. Defines the end of the time window during which the renewable energy was produced.

attributes.name: generation_start_date
attributes.description: Start date of the generation period for which this REC was issued. Defines the beginning of the time window during which the renewable energy was produced.

attributes.name: generation_technology_type
attributes.description: Type of renewable energy technology used to generate the electricity represented by this REC. Critical for RPS compliance as many states have technology-specific requirements or multipliers. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: solar|wind|hydro|biomass|geothermal|landfill gas|tidal|wave — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: generation_vintage_month
attributes.description: Calendar month (1-12) in which the renewable energy was generated. Provides granular vintage tracking for compliance and trading purposes.

attributes.name: generation_vintage_year
attributes.description: Calendar year in which the renewable energy was generated. Vintage year determines eligibility for compliance periods under state RPS programs.

attributes.name: issuance_date
attributes.description: Date on which this REC certificate was issued by the registry. Issuance typically occurs after generation data is verified and submitted to the registry.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this REC certificate record was last updated in the internal compliance tracking system. Tracks data currency and change history.

attributes.name: last_transfer_date
attributes.description: Date of the most recent ownership transfer of this REC. Null if the REC has never been transferred from the original owner.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text notes or comments regarding this REC certificate, including special handling instructions, compliance considerations, or audit findings. Used for operational coordination and compliance documentation.

attributes.name: original_owner_name
attributes.description: Name of the original owner to whom this REC was first issued, typically the generator or the entity with contractual rights to the RECs from the generation facility.

attributes.name: purchase_currency_code
attributes.description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for the purchase price. Typically USD for U.S. REC markets.

attributes.name: purchase_price_per_rec
attributes.description: Price paid per REC certificate in the most recent transaction, typically in USD. Confidential commercial information used for cost tracking and portfolio valuation.

attributes.name: rec_multiplier
attributes.description: Multiplier applied to the energy quantity for compliance credit calculation. Some state RPS programs provide enhanced credit (e.g., 1.5x or 2.0x) for certain technologies, in-state generation, or other policy objectives.

attributes.name: rec_serial_number
attributes.description: Unique serial number assigned by the registry to this REC certificate. This is the externally-known business identifier used for tracking, trading, and retirement of the certificate across registries and market participants.
attributes.references: WREGIS, NEPOOL GIS, PJM GATS, M-RETS Registry Standards

attributes.name: registry_name
attributes.description: Name of the registry system where this REC is registered and tracked. Registries provide independent verification and tracking of renewable energy generation and certificate lifecycle. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: WREGIS|NEPOOL GIS|PJM GATS|M-RETS|NAR|ERCOT|MIRECS — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: retirement_date
attributes.description: Date on which this REC was retired for compliance or voluntary purposes. Retired RECs cannot be traded or reused. Null if the REC has not been retired.

attributes.name: retirement_reason
attributes.description: Reason for retiring this REC certificate. RPS compliance retirements are used to meet state renewable portfolio standards; voluntary retirements support corporate sustainability goals or green marketing claims.

attributes.name: rps_compliance_year
attributes.description: Compliance year for which this REC was retired to meet RPS obligations. Null if not retired for RPS compliance. Critical for demonstrating compliance to state PUCs.

attributes.name: rps_tier
attributes.description: RPS tier or category classification for this REC under the applicable state program. Many states have tiered structures with different technology eligibility and compliance requirements for each tier.

attributes.name: transfer_count
attributes.description: Number of times this REC has been transferred between owners since issuance. Provides insight into market activity and trading liquidity.

products.name: rate_case
products.description: Master record for each PUC or FERC rate case proceeding initiated by or involving the utility, including general rate cases, transmission rate cases (FERC OATT), distribution rate cases, fuel adjustment clause proceedings, and decoupling mechanism filings. Captures docket number, filing jurisdiction, case type, test year, filed revenue requirement, proposed rate changes, intervenor parties, procedural schedule milestones (pre-hearing conference, evidentiary hearings, briefs, proposed decision), settlement status, and final commission order. Tracks the full proceeding lifecycle from initial filing through final order and any rehearing requests. SSOT for rate case lifecycle management.
products.reference: PUC Docket Management; FERC eTariff; OATT Rate Case

attributes.name: rate_case_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the rate case proceeding. Primary key for the rate case entity.

attributes.name: lead_attorney_employee_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: Rate cases require employee lead attorney accountability for case strategy and testimony. Replaces text field with FK to enable legal workload tracking, case portfolio management, and expertise alloca

attributes.name: load_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Test Year Load Forecast Id (Foreign Key)
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to forecast.load. Business justification: Rate cases use load forecasts for test year to justify revenue requirements and rate base. Load forecast drives capacity cost allocation, energy sales projections, and rate design - foundational to ra

attributes.name: peak_demand_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to forecast.peak_demand. Business justification: Rate cases cite peak demand forecasts for capacity cost allocation and demand charge rate structure design. Peak demand determines generation and transmission capacity costs recovered through rates.

attributes.name: administrative_law_judge
attributes.description: Name of the administrative law judge or hearing officer assigned to preside over the evidentiary hearing and issue a proposed decision. Null if not applicable in this jurisdiction.

attributes.name: approved_rate_increase_percent
attributes.description: Overall percentage increase in customer rates approved by the commission in the final order. Expressed as a percentage. Null until final order is issued.

attributes.name: case_description
attributes.description: Narrative description of the rate case purpose, scope, and key issues. Includes summary of major cost drivers, policy issues, and contested matters.

attributes.name: case_status
attributes.description: Current procedural status of the rate case in its regulatory lifecycle. Tracks progression from initial filing through final commission order and any post-order proceedings. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: draft|filed|pending|hearing_scheduled|hearing_complete|settlement_negotiation|commission_deliberation|final_order_issued|rehearing_requested|closed — 10 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: State PUC Procedural Rules; FERC Rules of Practice and Procedure

attributes.name: case_type
attributes.description: Classification of the rate case proceeding by its regulatory purpose and scope. General rate cases address overall revenue requirements; transmission rate cases address FERC OATT rates; distribution rate cases address local delivery rates; fuel adjustment clauses address fuel cost recovery; decoupling mechanisms address revenue decoupling from sales volume; formula rates address automatic rate adjustment mechanisms.
attributes.references: FERC Order 888 (OATT); State PUC Rate Case Procedures

attributes.name: commission_staff_analyst
attributes.description: Name of the primary commission staff analyst assigned to review and analyze the rate case filing.

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: Date the new rates approved in the final order become effective for customer billing. May differ from final order date due to suspension periods, phase-in schedules, or tariff filing requirements.
attributes.references: State PUC Rate Implementation Rules; FERC Tariff Filing Requirements

attributes.name: evidentiary_hearing_end_date
attributes.description: Date the evidentiary hearing concluded. Null if case settled before hearing or hearing not yet completed.
attributes.references: State PUC Procedural Rules; FERC Rules of Practice and Procedure

attributes.name: evidentiary_hearing_start_date
attributes.description: Date the evidentiary hearing commenced, where witnesses present testimony and are subject to cross-examination. Null if case settled before hearing or hearing not yet scheduled.
attributes.references: State PUC Procedural Rules; FERC Rules of Practice and Procedure

attributes.name: filed_with_agency
attributes.description: FK to compliance.regulatory_agency.regulatory_agency_id — Rate cases are filed with specific PUCs or FERC. Essential FK for jurisdictional tracking.

attributes.name: filing_date
attributes.description: Date the utility formally filed the rate case application with the regulatory commission. This date triggers statutory review timelines and procedural schedules.
attributes.references: State PUC Filing Requirements; FERC Section 205 Filing Procedures

attributes.name: filing_jurisdiction
attributes.description: Regulatory jurisdiction where the rate case is filed. Use state abbreviation for state PUC filings (e.g., CA, TX, NY) or FERC for Federal Energy Regulatory Commission filings.
attributes.references: FERC Jurisdiction; State PUC Jurisdictional Authority

attributes.name: final_order_date
attributes.description: Date the commission issued its final order deciding the rate case. This date establishes the effective date for new rates (subject to any suspension or phase-in provisions).
attributes.references: State PUC Procedural Rules; FERC Rules of Practice and Procedure

attributes.name: initial_brief_due_date
attributes.description: Deadline for parties to file initial post-hearing briefs summarizing their positions and legal arguments. Null if case settled or procedural schedule not yet established.
attributes.references: State PUC Procedural Rules; FERC Rules of Practice and Procedure

attributes.name: intervenor_count
attributes.description: Number of parties granted intervenor status in the rate case proceeding, including consumer advocates, industrial customer groups, environmental organizations, and other stakeholders.
attributes.references: State PUC Procedural Rules; FERC Rules of Practice and Procedure

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-form text field for additional notes, observations, or context regarding the rate case proceeding that do not fit structured fields.

attributes.name: prehearing_conference_date
attributes.description: Date of the prehearing conference where procedural schedule, discovery protocols, and hearing logistics are established. Null if not yet scheduled or if case settled before hearing.
attributes.references: State PUC Procedural Rules; FERC Rules of Practice and Procedure

attributes.name: proposed_decision_date
attributes.description: Date the administrative law judge or hearing officer issued a proposed decision recommending findings and conclusions to the commission. Null if not applicable in this jurisdiction or if case settled.

attributes.name: proposed_rate_increase_percent
attributes.description: Overall percentage increase in customer rates proposed by the utility in the initial filing, calculated as the change in revenue requirement divided by current revenues. Expressed as a percentage. Negative values indicate a rate decrease.

attributes.name: record_created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this rate case record was first created in the system.

attributes.name: record_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this rate case record was last modified in the system.

attributes.name: regulatory_affairs_manager
attributes.description: Name of the regulatory affairs manager responsible for coordinating the utility's rate case strategy, filings, and stakeholder engagement.

attributes.name: rehearing_decision_date
attributes.description: Date the commission issued its decision on the rehearing petition. Null if no rehearing was requested or decision not yet issued.
attributes.references: State PUC Procedural Rules; FERC Rules of Practice and Procedure

attributes.name: rehearing_request_date
attributes.description: Date the petition for rehearing was filed. Null if no rehearing was requested.
attributes.references: State PUC Procedural Rules; FERC Rules of Practice and Procedure

attributes.name: rehearing_requested_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether any party filed a petition for rehearing or reconsideration of the final commission order (True) or not (False).
attributes.references: State PUC Procedural Rules; FERC Rules of Practice and Procedure

attributes.name: reply_brief_due_date
attributes.description: Deadline for parties to file reply briefs responding to initial briefs. Null if case settled or procedural schedule not yet established.
attributes.references: State PUC Procedural Rules; FERC Rules of Practice and Procedure

attributes.name: settlement_date
attributes.description: Date the settlement agreement was executed by the parties. Null if the case was not settled.
attributes.references: State PUC Settlement Procedures; FERC Settlement Policy

attributes.name: settlement_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the rate case was resolved through a settlement agreement among the utility, commission staff, and intervenor parties (True) or proceeded to a fully litigated commission decision (False).
attributes.references: State PUC Settlement Procedures; FERC Settlement Policy

attributes.name: suspension_period_days
attributes.description: Number of days the commission suspended the proposed rate effective date to allow time for review and hearing. Statutory suspension periods vary by jurisdiction (e.g., 5 months for FERC, varies by state PUC).
attributes.references: Federal Power Act Section 205; State PUC Statutes

attributes.name: test_year_end_date
attributes.description: Ending date of the test year period used to establish the revenue requirement and cost of service.
attributes.references: State PUC Rate Case Standards; FERC Cost of Service Methodology

attributes.name: test_year_start_date
attributes.description: Beginning date of the test year period used to establish the revenue requirement and cost of service. Test year may be historical, future, or a hybrid period depending on jurisdiction.
attributes.references: State PUC Rate Case Standards; FERC Cost of Service Methodology

products.name: sox_control
products.description: Master record for each Sarbanes-Oxley (SOX) internal control over financial reporting (ICFR) applicable to the utility, including controls over revenue recognition, regulatory asset accounting, fuel cost recovery, and capital expenditure authorization, along with the complete testing history for each control. Captures control ID, control objective, control type (preventive/detective), control frequency, process owner, IT or manual classification, associated financial statement assertion, and design effectiveness rating. For each test execution: test period, testing methodology (inquiry, observation, inspection, re-performance), sample size, test results (effective/ineffective), deficiency classification (control deficiency, significant deficiency, material weakness), tester identity, and external auditor reliance flag. SSOT for SOX control inventory, test execution records, and testing results supporting management's annual SOX 404 assessment and external auditor reliance.
products.reference: SOX Section 302/404; PCAOB AS 2201; COSO Framework

attributes.name: sox_control_id
attributes.description: Primary key for sox_control

attributes.name: process_owner_employee_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: SOX controls require employee process ownership for accountability per COSO framework. Replaces text field with FK to enable segregation of duties analysis, control testing assignment, and audit trail

attributes.name: program_id
attributes.description: FK to compliance.program.program_id — SOX controls operate under the SOX Compliance Program. Links control inventory to program structure.

attributes.name: sox_program_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.program. Business justification: SOX controls are managed within a compliance program (e.g., SOX ICFR Compliance Program). Many controls can be part of one program (1:N). Adding program_id FK links the SOX control to its governing pr

attributes.name: affected_account
attributes.description: The primary general ledger account or account range that this control impacts (e.g., '4000-Revenue', '1500-Regulatory Assets', '6100-Fuel Costs', '1800-Property Plant and Equipment'). May reference multiple accounts separated by semicolons.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404 - Management Assessment of Internal Controls

attributes.name: control_documentation_reference
attributes.description: Reference to the detailed control documentation, such as a document management system identifier, SharePoint location, or process narrative document number where the full control description, procedures, and evidence requirements are maintained.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404 - Management Assessment of Internal Controls

attributes.name: control_frequency
attributes.description: How often the control is performed or executed (e.g., daily reconciliation, monthly review, quarterly certification, annually for rate case filings, or event-driven for specific transactions).

attributes.name: control_nature
attributes.description: Classification indicating whether the control is performed manually by personnel, fully automated by IT systems, or a manual control that depends on IT-generated reports or data (IT-dependent manual control).
attributes.references: PCAOB AS 2201 - Audit of Internal Control

attributes.name: control_number
attributes.description: Business identifier for the SOX control, typically following a hierarchical numbering scheme (e.g., FIN-01, REV-02, CAPEX-03). Used in audit documentation and external auditor workpapers.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404 - Management Assessment of Internal Controls

attributes.name: control_objective
attributes.description: Detailed statement of the control's purpose and what risk it is designed to mitigate (e.g., 'To ensure that revenue is recognized in accordance with GAAP and regulatory accounting principles', 'To ensure that capital expenditures are properly authorized and capitalized').

attributes.name: control_owner_name
attributes.description: Name of the individual or role responsible for executing or overseeing the control activity (may differ from process owner; e.g., 'Senior Accountant - Revenue', 'Regulatory Compliance Manager').

attributes.name: control_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the control: active (in operation), inactive (temporarily suspended), retired (no longer applicable), or under remediation (deficiency identified and being corrected).
attributes.references: SOX Section 404 - Management Assessment of Internal Controls

attributes.name: control_title
attributes.description: Short descriptive title of the SOX control (e.g., 'Revenue Recognition Review', 'Capital Expenditure Authorization', 'Regulatory Asset Reconciliation').
attributes.references: SOX Section 404 - Management Assessment of Internal Controls

attributes.name: control_type
attributes.description: Classification of the control based on its timing and purpose: preventive (stops errors before they occur), detective (identifies errors after they occur), or corrective (remediates identified errors).

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this control record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and data lineage purposes.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404 - Management Assessment of Internal Controls

attributes.name: deficiency_classification
attributes.description: Classification of any identified control deficiency: none (no deficiency), control deficiency (minor issue unlikely to result in misstatement), significant deficiency (important enough to merit attention by those charged with governance), or material weakness (reasonable possibility of material misstatement not being prevented or detected).
attributes.references: PCAOB AS 2201 - Audit of Internal Control

attributes.name: deficiency_description
attributes.description: Detailed description of any identified control deficiency, including the nature of the issue, root cause, and potential impact on financial reporting. Null if no deficiency exists.
attributes.references: PCAOB AS 2201 - Audit of Internal Control

attributes.name: design_effectiveness_rating
attributes.description: Assessment of whether the control, as designed, is capable of preventing or detecting material misstatements if it operates as prescribed. Evaluated during control documentation and walkthroughs.
attributes.references: PCAOB AS 2201 - Audit of Internal Control

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: The date on which this control became effective and operational. Used to track control lifecycle and determine when testing should commence.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404 - Management Assessment of Internal Controls

attributes.name: entity_level_control_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this is an entity-level control (True) that operates across the entire organization (e.g., code of conduct, whistleblower hotline, board oversight) or a process-level control (False) specific to a particular business process.

attributes.name: external_auditor_reliance_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the external auditor plans to rely on this control (True) as part of their financial statement audit, or will perform substantive testing instead (False). Reliance typically requires more rigorous internal testing.
attributes.references: PCAOB AS 2201 - Audit of Internal Control

attributes.name: external_auditor_test_date
attributes.description: The date on which the external auditor last tested this control as part of their integrated audit. Null if the auditor has not tested this control or does not plan to rely on it.
attributes.references: PCAOB AS 2201 - Audit of Internal Control

attributes.name: external_auditor_test_result
attributes.description: The external auditor's assessment of the control's operating effectiveness based on their independent testing. Not tested indicates the auditor did not evaluate this control.
attributes.references: PCAOB AS 2201 - Audit of Internal Control

attributes.name: financial_statement_assertion
attributes.description: The primary financial statement assertion that this control addresses: existence (transactions occurred), completeness (all transactions recorded), accuracy (amounts correct), valuation (assets/liabilities properly valued), rights and obligations (entity has legal rights), or presentation and disclosure (proper classification and disclosure).
attributes.references: PCAOB AS 2201 - Audit of Internal Control

attributes.name: it_application
attributes.description: The primary IT system or application that supports this control (e.g., 'SAP S/4HANA', 'Oracle CC&B', 'SAP IS-U'). Relevant for automated controls and IT-dependent manual controls. Null for purely manual controls.

attributes.name: it_general_control_dependency
attributes.description: Description of any IT General Controls (ITGCs) that this control depends on, such as access controls, change management, or data backup procedures. Critical for assessing the reliability of automated and IT-dependent manual controls.

attributes.name: key_control_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this is a key control (True) or a supporting/secondary control (False). Key controls are those that directly address significant risks to financial reporting and are subject to more rigorous testing.
attributes.references: PCAOB AS 2201 - Audit of Internal Control

attributes.name: last_modified_by
attributes.description: The name or user ID of the individual who last modified this control record. Used for accountability and change tracking.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404 - Management Assessment of Internal Controls

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this control record was last updated. Used to track changes to control design, ownership, or testing results.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404 - Management Assessment of Internal Controls

attributes.name: last_test_date
attributes.description: The most recent date on which this control was tested for operating effectiveness. Used to track testing currency and plan future test cycles.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404 - Management Assessment of Internal Controls

attributes.name: last_test_methodology
attributes.description: The testing approach used in the most recent test: inquiry (asking control performers), observation (watching control execution), inspection (examining evidence), re-performance (independently executing the control), or a combination of methods.
attributes.references: PCAOB AS 2201 - Audit of Internal Control

attributes.name: last_test_period
attributes.description: The fiscal period or date range covered by the most recent test (e.g., 'Q1 2024', 'January 2024', 'FY2023'). Indicates the scope of the testing performed.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404 - Management Assessment of Internal Controls

attributes.name: last_test_result
attributes.description: The outcome of the most recent control test: effective (control operated as designed with no exceptions), ineffective (control failed or had exceptions), or not applicable (control was not in operation during test period).
attributes.references: PCAOB AS 2201 - Audit of Internal Control

attributes.name: last_test_sample_size
attributes.description: The number of items or instances tested during the most recent control test. Sample size is determined based on control frequency, risk rating, and testing standards.
attributes.references: PCAOB AS 2201 - Audit of Internal Control

attributes.name: last_tester_name
attributes.description: Name of the individual who performed the most recent control test. Used for accountability and to ensure independence (tester should not be the control performer).
attributes.references: SOX Section 404 - Management Assessment of Internal Controls

attributes.name: operating_effectiveness_rating
attributes.description: Assessment of whether the control is operating as designed and is being performed consistently throughout the period. Determined through testing activities (inquiry, observation, inspection, re-performance).
attributes.references: PCAOB AS 2201 - Audit of Internal Control

attributes.name: regulatory_relevance
attributes.description: Description of how this control supports regulatory compliance beyond SOX, such as FERC reporting requirements, PUC rate case filings, NERC CIP standards, or EPA emissions reporting. Null if the control is purely SOX-driven.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts, State PUC Regulations

attributes.name: remediation_plan
attributes.description: Description of the corrective action plan to address an identified deficiency, including specific steps, responsible parties, and timeline. Null if no deficiency exists or remediation is complete.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404 - Management Assessment of Internal Controls

attributes.name: remediation_target_date
attributes.description: The target date by which the remediation plan is expected to be completed and the control deficiency resolved. Null if no active remediation is in progress.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404 - Management Assessment of Internal Controls

attributes.name: retirement_date
attributes.description: The date on which this control was retired or deactivated, typically due to process changes, system implementations, or risk reassessment. Null for active controls.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404 - Management Assessment of Internal Controls

attributes.name: risk_rating
attributes.description: Assessment of the inherent risk level associated with the process or account that this control mitigates. High-risk controls typically receive more frequent testing and external auditor attention.

attributes.name: scoping_rationale
attributes.description: Explanation of why this control was included in the SOX control inventory, including the materiality assessment, risk evaluation, and linkage to significant accounts or disclosures. Used to support scoping decisions with external auditors.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404 - Management Assessment of Internal Controls

products.name: sox_control_test
products.description: Transactional record of each SOX control test execution performed during quarterly and annual ICFR assessments, capturing the tested control, test period, testing methodology (inquiry, observation, inspection, re-performance), sample size, test results (effective/ineffective), deficiency classification (control deficiency, significant deficiency, material weakness), and external auditor reliance flag. Supports management's annual SOX 404 assessment and external auditor testing.
products.reference: SOX Section 404; PCAOB AS 2201; COSO Internal Control Framework

attributes.name: sox_control_test_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the SOX control test execution record. Primary key for the sox_control_test product.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404 - Management Assessment of Internal Controls

attributes.name: audit_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.audit. Business justification: SOX control tests can be part of an audit (e.g., annual SOX audit, quarterly ICFR review). Many tests can be part of one audit (1:N). Adding audit_id FK links the control test to the audit engagement.

attributes.name: remediation_plan_id
attributes.description: Reference to the formal remediation plan developed to address the identified deficiency. Links to the remediation tracking system for monitoring corrective action completion.

attributes.name: sox_control_id
attributes.description: Reference to the specific SOX control being tested. Links to the control registry that defines the control objective, control activities, and control owner.

attributes.name: account_code
attributes.description: The general ledger account code(s) to which this control applies. For utilities, typically includes accounts such as plant in service (101), accumulated depreciation (108), accounts receivable (142), revenue accounts (400-series), and operating expense accounts (500-900 series) per FERC Uniform System of Accounts.

attributes.name: active_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this control test record is active and current. False indicates the record has been superseded, voided, or is no longer relevant for current period reporting. Used for filtering current-period test results.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404 - Management Assessment of Internal Controls

attributes.name: business_process
attributes.description: The business process or cycle to which this control belongs (e.g., Revenue and Receivables, Procurement to Pay, Payroll, Fixed Assets, Financial Close and Reporting, Treasury, Regulatory Reporting). Used for organizing controls by process area and assigning process owners.

attributes.name: control_automation_level
attributes.description: The degree of automation in the control execution. Fully automated controls are system-enforced with no manual intervention; semi-automated controls combine system and manual steps; manual controls are entirely human-performed. Automation level affects sample size and testing methodology.
attributes.references: PCAOB AS 2201 - Audit of Internal Control Over Financial Reporting

attributes.name: control_frequency
attributes.description: The designed operating frequency of the control being tested. Determines the expected population size and testing approach. Daily and weekly controls typically require larger sample sizes than quarterly or annual controls.

attributes.name: control_type
attributes.description: The nature of the control being tested. Preventive controls stop errors before they occur; detective controls identify errors after they occur; corrective controls remediate identified errors. Classification affects testing approach and reliance strategy.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this control test record was first created in the system. Audit trail field for record lifecycle tracking.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404 - Management Assessment of Internal Controls

attributes.name: deficiency_classification
attributes.description: The severity classification of any identified control deficiency. Control deficiency is a shortcoming that does not rise to significant deficiency. Significant deficiency is important enough to merit attention by those charged with governance. Material weakness is a deficiency such that there is a reasonable possibility of material misstatement. Classification follows PCAOB definitions.
attributes.references: PCAOB AS 2201 - Audit of Internal Control Over Financial Reporting

attributes.name: deficiency_description
attributes.description: Detailed narrative description of the control deficiency identified during testing, including the nature of the exception, the root cause, and the potential impact on financial reporting. Required when test_result is ineffective.

attributes.name: entity_level_control_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this is an entity-level control (e.g., tone at the top, code of conduct, risk assessment process, board oversight) as opposed to a transaction-level or process-level control. Entity-level controls have a pervasive effect on internal control over financial reporting.

attributes.name: exceptions_identified_count
attributes.description: The number of sample items that did not meet the control criteria or where the control did not operate as designed. Zero exceptions indicates effective control operation for the sample tested.

attributes.name: external_auditor_firm_name
attributes.description: The name of the external audit firm (e.g., Deloitte, PwC, EY, KPMG, or other registered public accounting firm) that reviewed or relied upon this test. Required for publicly traded utilities subject to SOX 404(b) external auditor attestation.

attributes.name: external_auditor_reliance_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the external auditor (Big 4 or other registered public accounting firm) intends to rely on this management test as part of their integrated audit of internal controls over financial reporting. True means the auditor will not re-perform the test; false means the auditor will perform their own independent test.
attributes.references: PCAOB AS 2201 - Audit of Internal Control Over Financial Reporting

attributes.name: external_auditor_review_date
attributes.description: The date on which the external auditor reviewed this management test for purposes of determining reliance. Populated only when external_auditor_reliance_flag is true.
attributes.references: PCAOB AS 2201 - Audit of Internal Control Over Financial Reporting

attributes.name: financial_statement_assertion
attributes.description: The primary financial statement assertion addressed by the control being tested. Existence confirms assets/liabilities exist; completeness confirms all transactions are recorded; accuracy confirms amounts are correct; valuation confirms proper measurement; rights_and_obligations confirms ownership; presentation_and_disclosure confirms proper classification and disclosure. Multiple assertions may apply; this field captures the primary assertion. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: existence|completeness|accuracy|valuation|rights_and_obligations|presentation_and_disclosure|cutoff|classification — promote to reference product]

attributes.name: fiscal_quarter
attributes.description: The fiscal quarter for which this control test was performed. Q1, Q2, Q3, or Q4. Used for quarterly SOX assessment and interim financial reporting.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404 - Management Assessment of Internal Controls

attributes.name: fiscal_year
attributes.description: The fiscal year for which this control test was performed, typically matching the test period end date fiscal year. Used for annual SOX 404 assessment aggregation and multi-year trend analysis.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404 - Management Assessment of Internal Controls

attributes.name: information_technology_general_control_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this is an IT general control (e.g., access controls, change management, backup and recovery, IT operations) that supports the operating effectiveness of automated application controls. ITGC deficiencies can cascade to application control failures.
attributes.references: PCAOB AS 2201 - Audit of Internal Control Over Financial Reporting

attributes.name: key_control_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this is a key control that management and external auditors rely upon to prevent or detect material misstatements. Key controls require annual testing; non-key controls may be tested on a rotational basis.
attributes.references: PCAOB AS 2201 - Audit of Internal Control Over Financial Reporting

attributes.name: last_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this control test record was most recently modified. Audit trail field for change tracking and data quality monitoring.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404 - Management Assessment of Internal Controls

attributes.name: remediation_required_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether management action is required to remediate the identified deficiency. True for significant deficiencies and material weaknesses; may be true for control deficiencies depending on risk assessment.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404 - Management Assessment of Internal Controls

attributes.name: review_date
attributes.description: The date on which the test results were reviewed and approved by the reviewer. Must be on or after the test execution date.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404 - Management Assessment of Internal Controls

attributes.name: reviewer_name
attributes.description: The name of the individual who reviewed and approved the test results and conclusion. Typically a senior internal auditor, SOX manager, or Chief Audit Executive. Required for quality assurance and segregation of duties.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404 - Management Assessment of Internal Controls

attributes.name: risk_rating
attributes.description: The inherent risk rating of the control based on the magnitude and likelihood of potential misstatement if the control fails. Critical and high-risk controls require more rigorous testing (larger samples, more frequent testing) than medium or low-risk controls.

attributes.name: sample_selection_method
attributes.description: The approach used to select the sample from the population. Random uses statistical sampling; systematic selects every nth item; haphazard is non-statistical but unbiased; judgmental targets high-risk items; all_items tests the entire population.

attributes.name: sample_size
attributes.description: The number of items or transactions selected for testing. For automated controls, may be 1 (test of configuration). For manual controls, typically 25+ items per PCAOB guidance for key controls.
attributes.references: PCAOB AS 2201 - Audit of Internal Control Over Financial Reporting

attributes.name: test_evidence_location
attributes.description: The file path, document management system reference, or physical location where the test workpapers and supporting evidence are stored. Required for audit trail and external auditor review. Typically a network path or document management system URL.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404 - Management Assessment of Internal Controls

attributes.name: test_execution_date
attributes.description: The date on which the control test was actually performed by the tester. This is the principal business event timestamp for the test execution.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404 - Management Assessment of Internal Controls

attributes.name: test_methodology
attributes.description: The audit testing technique applied to evaluate control effectiveness. Inquiry involves asking questions; observation involves watching the control in action; inspection involves examining documents; reperformance involves independently executing the control; analytical procedure involves data analysis; walkthrough involves tracing a transaction through the process.
attributes.references: PCAOB AS 2201 - Audit of Internal Control Over Financial Reporting

attributes.name: test_notes
attributes.description: Additional narrative notes, observations, or context about the test execution, results, or follow-up actions. May include tester commentary on control design improvements, process changes during the test period, or coordination with external auditors.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404 - Management Assessment of Internal Controls

attributes.name: test_number
attributes.description: Business identifier for the control test execution, typically formatted as control-code-year-sequence (e.g., FIN-2024-001). Used for audit trail and external auditor reference.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404 - Management Assessment of Internal Controls

attributes.name: test_period_end_date
attributes.description: The ending date of the period for which the control effectiveness is being tested. For quarterly assessments, typically the last day of the fiscal quarter.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404 - Management Assessment of Internal Controls

attributes.name: test_period_start_date
attributes.description: The beginning date of the period for which the control effectiveness is being tested. For quarterly assessments, typically the first day of the fiscal quarter.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404 - Management Assessment of Internal Controls

attributes.name: test_result
attributes.description: The overall conclusion on control effectiveness based on the test evidence. Effective means the control operated as designed with no or immaterial exceptions. Ineffective means the control did not operate as designed or had material exceptions. This is the principal outcome of the test execution.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404 - Management Assessment of Internal Controls

attributes.name: tester_name
attributes.description: The name of the individual who performed the control test. Typically an internal audit team member, SOX compliance analyst, or process owner. Required for audit trail and accountability.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404 - Management Assessment of Internal Controls

attributes.name: tester_role
attributes.description: The organizational role or function of the individual who performed the test. Distinguishes between management testing (internal audit, SOX compliance, process owner) and external auditor testing.
attributes.references: PCAOB AS 2201 - Audit of Internal Control Over Financial Reporting

attributes.name: updated_by_user
attributes.description: The user ID or name of the individual who last modified this control test record. Required for audit trail and accountability in SOX compliance documentation.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404 - Management Assessment of Internal Controls

products.name: program
products.description: Master record for each formal compliance program maintained by the utility, including the NERC CIP Compliance Program, FERC Standards of Conduct Program, Environmental Compliance Program, SOX Compliance Program, and OSHA Safety Compliance Program. Captures program name, governing regulatory framework, program owner, program charter date, scope of applicability, associated policies and procedures, and program effectiveness metrics. Includes the full training management lifecycle: training course catalog, training delivery methods, training assignments, and for each personnel training completion: assigned personnel role, training course, delivery method, assigned date, completion date, assessment score, pass/fail status, and certification expiry date. Provides the organizational structure for compliance management and serves as SSOT for compliance program inventory and all compliance training evidence required under NERC CIP-004, FERC Standards of Conduct, OSHA, and other regulatory training mandates.
products.reference: NERC CMEP; FERC Standards of Conduct; EPA Compliance Assurance

attributes.name: program_id

attributes.name: owner_org_unit_id

attributes.name: assessment_required_flag

attributes.name: associated_policies_count
attributes.description: The number of formal policies that are part of this compliance program.

attributes.name: associated_procedures_count
attributes.description: The number of formal procedures that implement this compliance program.

attributes.name: audit_frequency

attributes.name: board_reporting_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this compliance program status and metrics are reported to the Board of Directors (True/False).

attributes.name: board_reporting_frequency
attributes.description: The frequency at which compliance program status is reported to the Board of Directors.

attributes.name: budget_usd
attributes.description: The annual budget allocated to this compliance program in United States Dollars, including personnel, training, technology, and external audit costs.

attributes.name: certification_issued_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether a formal certification is issued upon successful completion of training (True/False).

attributes.name: certification_validity_period_months
attributes.description: The number of months for which a training certification remains valid before recertification is required. Null if certification does not expire.

attributes.name: charter_date
attributes.description: The date on which the compliance program was formally chartered and approved by executive leadership or the Board.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this compliance program record was first created in the system.

attributes.name: document_repository_location
attributes.description: The system or location where compliance program documentation, policies, procedures, and evidence are stored (e.g., SharePoint site, document management system path).

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: The date on which the compliance program became operationally effective and binding on the organization.

attributes.name: effectiveness_rating
attributes.description: Qualitative assessment of the compliance programs effectiveness in achieving its objectives and managing compliance risk.

attributes.name: evidence_retention_period_years
attributes.description: The number of years that compliance evidence and training records must be retained to satisfy regulatory and audit requirements.
attributes.references: NERC CIP-004, FERC, SOX, State PUC

attributes.name: expiration_date
attributes.description: The date on which the compliance program is scheduled to expire or be reviewed for renewal. Null for perpetual programs.

attributes.name: external_auditor_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this compliance program is subject to external auditor review (True/False).

attributes.name: governing_regulatory_framework
attributes.description: The primary regulatory framework or standard that mandates this compliance program (e.g., NERC CIP-001 through CIP-014, FERC Order 2000, EPA Clean Air Act, SOX Section 404, OSHA 29 CFR 1910).

attributes.name: issuing_regulatory_body
attributes.description: The governing body or regulatory agency that issued the compliance mandate (e.g., NERC, FERC, EPA, SEC, OSHA, State PUC).
attributes.references: NERC, FERC, EPA, SEC, OSHA, State PUC

attributes.name: last_audit_date
attributes.description: The date of the most recent internal or external audit of this compliance program.
attributes.references: NERC, FERC, SOX, Internal Audit Standards

attributes.name: last_audit_result
attributes.description: The outcome of the most recent audit of this compliance program.
attributes.references: NERC, FERC, SOX, Internal Audit Standards

attributes.name: last_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this compliance program record was most recently modified.

attributes.name: minimum_passing_score_pct
attributes.description: The minimum assessment score required to pass training and achieve compliance (e.g., 80.00 for NERC CIP training assessments).

attributes.name: next_audit_date
attributes.description: The scheduled date for the next internal or external audit of this compliance program.
attributes.references: NERC, FERC, SOX, Internal Audit Standards

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-form notes capturing additional context, special considerations, or historical information about the compliance program.

attributes.name: owner_title
attributes.description: Job title of the program owner (e.g., Chief Compliance Officer, VP Regulatory Affairs, Director Environmental Compliance).

attributes.name: program_code
attributes.description: Unique business identifier code for the compliance program (e.g., NERC-CIP, FERC-SOC, EPA-EMIS, SOX-FIN, OSHA-SAF).

attributes.name: program_description
attributes.description: Comprehensive narrative description of the compliance program objectives, scope, key activities, and deliverables.

attributes.name: program_name
attributes.description: Full official name of the compliance program (e.g., NERC CIP Compliance Program, FERC Standards of Conduct Program, Environmental Compliance Program, SOX Compliance Program, OSHA Safety Compliance Program).

attributes.name: program_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the compliance program.

attributes.name: program_type
attributes.description: Classification of the compliance program by its origin and binding nature.

attributes.name: risk_rating
attributes.description: The assessed risk level associated with non-compliance under this program, considering both likelihood and impact.

attributes.name: scope_of_applicability
attributes.description: Detailed description of the organizational scope to which this compliance program applies (e.g., all generation facilities, all transmission assets rated above 100kV, all employees with access to BES Cyber Systems, all financial reporting personnel).

attributes.name: training_completion_threshold_pct
attributes.description: The minimum percentage of assigned personnel who must complete training for the program to be considered compliant (e.g., 100.00 for NERC CIP, 95.00 for internal programs).

attributes.name: training_frequency
attributes.description: The required frequency at which training must be completed or refreshed for this compliance program.
attributes.references: NERC CIP-004, FERC Standards of Conduct, OSHA

attributes.name: training_required_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether formal training is mandated for personnel under this compliance program (True/False).
attributes.references: NERC CIP-004, FERC Standards of Conduct, OSHA

attributes.name: updated_by_user
attributes.description: The user ID or name of the person who last updated this compliance program record.

products.name: training_record

Captures training course, assigned personnel role, training delivery method, assigned date, completion date, assessment score, and certification expiry. Supports NERC CIP-004 personnel training evidence requirements.

attributes.name: training_program_id

products.name: audit_scope
products.description: This association product represents the scoping relationship between organizational units and compliance audits. It captures which organizational units are included in each audit's scope, along with audit-specific metrics for that unit including findings count, audit effort hours, and the specific scope description for that unit. Each record links one org_unit to one audit with attributes that exist only in the context of this scoping relationship.. Existence Justification: In energy utility compliance operations, audits routinely scope multiple organizational units (e.g., a NERC CIP audit may cover Generation, Transmission, and Distribution units), and each organizational unit undergoes multiple audits annually from different regulatory bodies (NERC, FERC, PUC, EPA, SOX). The scoping relationship is actively managed by audit coordinators who track findings, audit hours, and scope descriptions specific to each org_unit-audit combination.

attributes.description: Size of the document file in bytes.

attributes.name: filing_deadline

attributes.name: filing_status
attributes.description: Current status of the regulatory filing process.

attributes.name: is_archived

attributes.name: issue_date

attributes.name: owner_department

attributes.name: regulatory_body

attributes.name: retention_period_days

attributes.name: revision_date
attributes.description: Date of the most recent amendment or version update.

attributes.name: status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the document.

attributes.name: storage_path
attributes.description: File system or object store location where the document file resides.

attributes.name: title
attributes.description: Human‑readable title of the compliance document.

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to the document record.

attributes.name: version_number
attributes.description: Incremental version identifier for the document.

attributes.name: superseded_compliance_document_id
