attributes.name: forecasted_wind_speed_m_per_s
attributes.business_glossary_term: Forecasted Wind Speed Meters per Second (m/s)
attributes.description: The predicted wind speed in meters per second at hub height for wind generation assets. Critical meteorological input for wind generation forecasting. Null for non-wind assets.

attributes.name: grid_constraint_flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator of whether transmission or distribution grid constraints are expected to limit renewable generation dispatch during this interval. True indicates constraints are forecasted, False indicates no constraints expected.

attributes.name: interval_duration_minutes
attributes.description: The duration of the forecast interval in minutes. Common values include 5, 15, 30, or 60 minutes depending on operational requirements and forecast granularity.

attributes.name: locational_marginal_price_usd_per_mwh
attributes.business_glossary_term: Locational Marginal Price (LMP) United States Dollar (USD) per Megawatt-Hour (MWh)
attributes.description: The forecasted locational marginal price at the renewable asset point of interconnection in USD per MWh. Reflects local grid congestion and transmission constraints. Used for economic dispatch optimization.

attributes.name: market_clearing_price_usd_per_mwh
attributes.business_glossary_term: Market Clearing Price United States Dollar (USD) per Megawatt-Hour (MWh)
attributes.description: The forecasted or actual wholesale electricity market price in USD per MWh for this interval. Used to calculate expected revenue and inform economic curtailment decisions. May be null for non-market forecasts.

attributes.name: net_generation_mw
attributes.description: The predicted net generation output after accounting for curtailment. Calculated as forecasted_generation_mw minus forecasted_curtailment_mw. Represents the actual expected dispatch to the grid.

attributes.name: persistence_forecast_mw
attributes.description: A simple baseline forecast assuming current generation continues unchanged. Used as a benchmark to evaluate the skill and value-add of advanced forecasting models.

attributes.name: ramp_rate_mw_per_minute
attributes.description: The predicted rate of change in generation output in megawatts per minute from the previous interval. Critical for grid stability analysis and reserve requirement calculations. Positive values indicate increasing generation, negative values indicate decreasing generation.

attributes.name: renewable_interval_to_renewable_forecast
attributes.description: FK to forecast.renewable_forecast.renewable_forecast_id — Every renewable forecast interval MUST reference its parent renewable forecast. Required for real-time renewable integration and grid balancing.

attributes.name: renewable_technology_type
attributes.description: The type of renewable generation technology for which this forecast applies. Different technologies require different forecasting methodologies and meteorological inputs.

attributes.name: weather_data_source
attributes.description: The name or identifier of the meteorological data provider used as input for this forecast (e.g., NOAA, ECMWF, proprietary weather service). Critical for forecast quality assessment and vendor management.

products.name: peak_demand
products.description: Master entity capturing seasonal and annual peak demand forecasts used for resource adequacy planning, transmission planning, and IRP. Records forecasted system peak MW, coincident peak date/time window, temperature sensitivity assumptions, demand response reduction credits, and reserve margin calculations. Submitted to RTO/ISO for capacity planning and NERC reliability assessments. Supports CAPEX investment decisions for T&D infrastructure.
products.reference: NERC Long-Term Reliability Assessment; IRP Peak Demand

attributes.name: peak_demand_id
attributes.description: Primary key for peak_demand

attributes.name: control_area_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to grid.control_area. Business justification: Peak demand forecasts drive control area capacity planning, reserve margin calculations, and resource adequacy assessments. Balancing authorities use peak forecasts for transmission planning and gener

attributes.name: forecast_model_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to forecast.model. Business justification: Peak demand forecasts are produced by registered forecasting models. The model table is the authoritative registry for model metadata, versioning, and accuracy metrics. Adding forecast_model_id FK all

attributes.name: peak_forecast_zone_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to forecast.zone. Business justification: Peak demand forecasts are spatially scoped to forecast zones. The zone table defines geographic boundaries and aggregation levels. Adding forecast_zone_id FK allows retrieval of zone_code, zone_name,

attributes.name: peak_zone_id
attributes.description: FK to forecast.zone.zone_id — Peak demand forecasts are scoped to system or zone level. FK enables zone-level capacity planning.

attributes.name: planning_assumption_id
attributes.description: FK to forecast.planning_assumption.planning_assumption_id — Peak demand forecasts use planning assumptions (load growth rates, EV adoption, DR credits). FK enables assumption traceability.

attributes.name: approved_by
attributes.description: User ID or name of the person who approved this peak demand forecast for use in resource adequacy and capacity planning.

attributes.name: approved_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this peak demand forecast was approved by planning or management for use in resource adequacy and capacity planning.

attributes.name: btm_solar_reduction_mw
attributes.description: Forecasted behind-the-meter (BTM) solar generation reduction credit in megawatts (MW) that will reduce the net peak demand seen by the grid.
attributes.references: FERC Net Energy Metering (NEM) Standards, IEEE 1547 Interconnection Standards

attributes.name: capex_trigger_flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this forecast triggers capital expenditure (CAPEX) investment decisions for transmission and distribution (T&D) infrastructure (True if triggers investment, False otherwise).

attributes.name: confidence_level_percent
attributes.description: Statistical confidence level of the forecast expressed as a percentage (e.g., 90.0 for 90% confidence interval). Indicates forecast reliability.
attributes.references: Statistical Forecasting Standards, NERC Planning Standards

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this peak demand forecast record was first created in the system.

attributes.name: dr_reduction_mw
attributes.description: Forecasted demand response (DR) program reduction credit in megawatts (MW) that will reduce the gross peak demand. Used for resource adequacy calculations.
attributes.references: FERC Order 2222, NERC Resource Adequacy Standards

attributes.name: energy_efficiency_reduction_mw
attributes.description: Forecasted energy efficiency program reduction credit in megawatts (MW) that will reduce the gross peak demand due to efficiency measures.
attributes.references: DOE Energy Efficiency Standards, State PUC Efficiency Mandates

attributes.name: forecast_error_mw
attributes.description: Expected forecast error or uncertainty range in megawatts (MW). Represents the plus/minus range around the forecasted peak demand.

attributes.name: forecast_horizon
attributes.description: Time horizon classification for the forecast (short-term operational, seasonal, annual, multi-year, or long-term capacity planning).

attributes.name: forecast_name
attributes.description: Business-friendly name or label for this peak demand forecast (e.g., 'Summer 2024 System Peak', 'Winter 2025 Coincident Peak').

attributes.name: forecast_notes
attributes.description: Free-text notes, assumptions, or commentary related to this peak demand forecast. May include special conditions, data quality issues, or planning considerations.

attributes.name: forecast_scenario
attributes.description: Planning scenario or case assumption underlying this forecast (base case, high growth, low growth, extreme weather, conservation, electrification).

attributes.name: forecast_season
attributes.description: Seasonal period for which the peak demand is forecasted (summer, winter, spring, fall, or annual).

attributes.name: forecast_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the peak demand forecast (draft, submitted to RTO/ISO, approved by planning, revised, or archived).

attributes.name: forecast_type
attributes.description: Classification of the peak demand forecast by scope and aggregation level (system-wide, coincident across zones, non-coincident, zonal, substation-level, or feeder-level).

attributes.name: forecast_year
attributes.description: Calendar year for which the peak demand is forecasted.

attributes.name: forecasted_temperature
attributes.description: Forecasted temperature (in degrees Fahrenheit or Celsius) at the time of peak demand. Used for weather-correlated load forecasting.

attributes.name: irp_filing_date
attributes.description: Date on which the IRP containing this forecast was filed with the state Public Utility Commission.

attributes.name: irp_filing_flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this forecast is included in an Integrated Resource Plan (IRP) filing to the state Public Utility Commission (True if included, False otherwise).

attributes.name: modified_by
attributes.description: User ID or name of the person or system that last modified this peak demand forecast record.

attributes.name: modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this peak demand forecast record was last modified or updated.

attributes.name: mw
attributes.description: Forecasted system peak demand in megawatts (MW). This is the principal quantitative value representing the maximum expected load.
attributes.references: NERC Glossary of Terms, IEEE Power Systems Standards

attributes.name: net_peak_demand_mw
attributes.description: Net forecasted peak demand in megawatts (MW) after applying all reduction credits (demand response, BTM solar, energy efficiency). This is the load the utility must serve.

attributes.name: normal_temperature
attributes.description: Normal or baseline temperature assumption (in degrees Fahrenheit or Celsius) used as the reference point for temperature sensitivity calculations.

attributes.name: peak_date
attributes.description: Forecasted date on which the peak demand is expected to occur.

attributes.name: peak_hour_end
attributes.description: Ending hour (0-23) of the forecasted peak demand window. Used for operational dispatch planning.

attributes.name: peak_hour_start
attributes.description: Starting hour (0-23) of the forecasted peak demand window. Used for operational dispatch planning.

attributes.name: required_capacity_mw
attributes.description: Total required generation capacity in megawatts (MW) calculated as net peak demand plus reserve margin. Used for resource adequacy and capacity procurement planning.
attributes.references: NERC Resource Adequacy Standards, RTO/ISO Capacity Market Rules

attributes.name: reserve_margin_percent
attributes.description: Planning reserve margin percentage applied to the net peak demand to determine required generation capacity. Expressed as a percentage (e.g., 15.0 for 15%).
attributes.references: NERC Resource Adequacy Standards, RTO/ISO Planning Criteria

attributes.name: rto_iso_submission_date
attributes.business_glossary_term: Regional Transmission Organization (RTO) / Independent System Operator (ISO) Submission Date
attributes.description: Date on which this forecast was submitted to the RTO/ISO for capacity planning and reliability assessments.
attributes.references: NERC Reliability Standards, RTO/ISO Reporting Requirements

attributes.name: rto_iso_submission_flag
attributes.business_glossary_term: Regional Transmission Organization (RTO) / Independent System Operator (ISO) Submission Flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this forecast has been submitted to the RTO/ISO for capacity planning and reliability assessments (True if submitted, False otherwise).
attributes.references: NERC Reliability Standards, RTO/ISO Reporting Requirements

attributes.name: temperature_sensitivity_mw_per_degree
attributes.description: Temperature sensitivity coefficient representing the change in peak demand (MW) per degree Fahrenheit or Celsius change from normal. Used for weather-adjusted forecasting.
attributes.references: NOAA Weather Correlation Standards, NERC Load Forecasting Guidelines

attributes.name: temperature_unit
attributes.description: Unit of measure for temperature sensitivity (Fahrenheit or Celsius).

attributes.name: weather_station_code
attributes.description: Identifier of the weather station or meteorological data source used for temperature and weather correlation in this forecast.

attributes.name: created_by
attributes.description: User ID or name of the person or system that created this peak demand forecast record.

products.name: weather_input
products.description: Weather forecast data ingested from NWP providers (GFS, ECMWF, NAM) as primary inputs to load, generation, and renewable forecasting models. Stores temperature, humidity, wind speed/direction, cloud cover, precipitation, solar irradiance, and dew point at zone or weather station level. Tracks NWP model source, forecast issue time, and validity period. Critical driver for all forecast accuracy and the primary exogenous variable in energy demand and renewable output prediction.
products.reference: NWP Weather Model; NOAA NWS Forecast

attributes.name: weather_input_id
attributes.description: Primary key for weather_input

attributes.name: forecast_zone_id
attributes.description: Identifier for the geographic zone or service territory to which this weather forecast applies. Links to the zone definition used in load and generation forecasting models.

attributes.name: atmospheric_pressure_hpa
attributes.description: Forecasted atmospheric pressure at sea level in hectopascals (hPa). Used in advanced weather correlation models and can influence wind patterns and storm tracking.

attributes.name: cloud_cover_percent
attributes.description: Forecasted total cloud cover as a percentage (0-100). Primary driver of solar irradiance reduction and solar generation output forecasting.

attributes.name: data_quality_flag
attributes.description: Quality assurance flag indicating the reliability of this forecast record. Values include valid (passed all checks), suspect (anomaly detected), missing (data gap), interpolated (filled from adjacent data), estimated (model-derived).

attributes.name: dew_point_c
attributes.description: Forecasted dew point temperature in degrees Celsius. Used to calculate humidity and assess cooling load and comfort index impacts on energy demand.

attributes.name: ensemble_member_number
attributes.description: Identifier for the ensemble member or scenario within an ensemble forecast system (e.g., ECMWF EPS member 1, 2, 3). Null for deterministic forecasts. Enables probabilistic forecasting and uncertainty quantification.

attributes.name: forecast_confidence_score
attributes.description: Numerical confidence or quality score assigned to this forecast record by the NWP provider or internal validation process. Higher scores indicate greater reliability. Used to weight ensemble forecasts.

attributes.name: forecast_issue_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when the NWP model run was issued or published by the provider. This is the model initialization time, critical for tracking forecast vintage and lead time.

attributes.name: forecast_lead_time_hours
attributes.description: The number of hours between the forecast issue time and the valid time. Indicates forecast horizon and is a key driver of forecast accuracy degradation.

attributes.name: forecast_type
attributes.description: Classification of the forecast methodology: deterministic (single outcome), ensemble (multiple scenarios), probabilistic (distribution-based), or nowcast (very short-term, 0-6 hours).

attributes.name: forecast_update_cycle
attributes.description: The NWP model run cycle identifier (e.g., 00Z, 06Z, 12Z, 18Z for GFS). Indicates which daily model run produced this forecast, critical for tracking model version and update frequency.

attributes.name: forecast_valid_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time for which this forecast is valid. Represents the target hour or interval that the weather variables predict. Used to align weather inputs with load and generation forecast horizons.

attributes.name: ingestion_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this weather forecast record was ingested into the lakehouse from the external NWP provider or data feed. Used for data lineage and latency tracking.

attributes.name: is_historical_reforecast
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this record is a historical reforecast (hindcast) used for model training and validation, rather than a real-time operational forecast.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for additional context, anomalies, or special conditions associated with this forecast record (e.g., model outage, data correction, extreme weather event).

attributes.name: nwp_model_source
attributes.description: The numerical weather prediction model provider or system that generated this forecast data (e.g., GFS, ECMWF, NAM, HRRR, WRF). Critical for model performance tracking and ensemble forecasting.
attributes.references: NOAA NWP Standards, ECMWF Model Documentation

attributes.name: precipitation_mm
attributes.description: Forecasted precipitation accumulation in millimeters for the forecast interval. Impacts hydro generation availability, solar output, and load patterns during storm events.

attributes.name: precipitation_probability_percent
attributes.description: Forecasted probability of precipitation occurrence as a percentage (0-100). Used in probabilistic forecasting and risk assessment for renewable generation and load variability.

attributes.name: relative_humidity_percent
attributes.description: Forecasted relative humidity as a percentage (0-100). Influences cooling load, HVAC efficiency, and customer comfort-driven energy consumption.

attributes.name: snow_depth_cm
attributes.description: Forecasted snow depth on the ground in centimeters. Relevant for winter peak load forecasting, transmission line loading, and hydro reservoir inflow modeling.

attributes.name: solar_irradiance_w_per_m2
attributes.description: Forecasted global horizontal irradiance (GHI) in watts per square meter. Direct input to solar photovoltaic generation forecasting models and renewable energy integration planning.
attributes.references: WMO GRIB2 Code Table 4.2, NREL Solar Radiation Standards

attributes.name: source_file_name
attributes.description: The name of the source file or data feed from which this forecast record was extracted (e.g., GRIB2 file name, API endpoint). Supports data lineage and troubleshooting.

attributes.name: spatial_resolution_km
attributes.description: The spatial grid resolution of the NWP model in kilometers (e.g., GFS 13km, ECMWF 9km). Indicates the granularity of the forecast and impacts accuracy for localized weather phenomena.

attributes.name: temperature_c
attributes.description: Forecasted air temperature in degrees Celsius at the zone or station level. Primary driver of heating and cooling load in energy demand forecasting.

attributes.name: temporal_resolution_minutes
attributes.description: The time interval between consecutive forecast data points in minutes (e.g., 60 for hourly, 15 for sub-hourly). Defines the granularity of the forecast time series.

attributes.name: visibility_km
attributes.description: Forecasted horizontal visibility in kilometers. May be used in operational safety assessments and can correlate with fog-related load patterns.

attributes.name: weather_station_code
attributes.description: Identifier for the weather station or observation point from which this forecast data is sourced or interpolated.

attributes.name: wind_direction_degrees
attributes.description: Forecasted wind direction in degrees (0-360, where 0/360 is North, 90 is East, 180 is South, 270 is West). Used in wind farm output modeling and turbine-level generation forecasting.

attributes.name: wind_gust_speed_mps
attributes.description: Forecasted maximum wind gust speed in meters per second. Important for wind turbine curtailment decisions and grid stability planning during high-wind events.

attributes.name: wind_speed_mps
attributes.description: Forecasted wind speed in meters per second at the zone or station level. Critical input for wind generation forecasting and renewable intermittency prediction.

products.name: model
products.description: Master entity representing a registered forecasting model configuration used to produce load, generation, or renewable forecasts. Captures model type (statistical regression, neural network, ensemble, persistence), model version, training data period, input feature set, hyperparameters, calibration date, and owning team. Provides model governance and lineage for all forecast runs. Supports model comparison and champion/challenger evaluation workflows.
products.reference: Forecast Model Registry; MLOps Model Catalog

attributes.name: model_id
attributes.description: Primary key for model

attributes.name: accuracy_metric_mae
attributes.description: Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of the model on validation data. Measures average forecast error magnitude.

attributes.name: accuracy_metric_mape
attributes.business_glossary_term: Accuracy Metric Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE)
attributes.description: Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) of the model on validation data. Primary accuracy metric for forecast quality assessment.

attributes.name: accuracy_metric_rmse
attributes.business_glossary_term: Accuracy Metric Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE)
attributes.description: Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE) of the model on validation data. Measures forecast deviation in absolute units (MW, MWh, etc.).

attributes.name: approval_date
attributes.description: Date when the model was formally approved for production use by the model governance committee or designated authority.

attributes.name: calibration_date
attributes.description: Date when the model was last calibrated or re-trained with updated historical data. Critical for model performance tracking and refresh scheduling.

attributes.name: champion_challenger_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this model is part of a champion/challenger evaluation workflow. True if the model is being compared against an incumbent champion model.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the model record was first created in the registry. Used for audit trail and model lifecycle tracking.

attributes.name: deployment_environment
attributes.description: Environment where the model is currently deployed: development, staging, production, or sandbox. Used for change management and release control.

attributes.name: documentation_url
attributes.description: URL or file path to detailed model documentation including methodology, assumptions, validation results, and usage guidelines.

attributes.name: execution_frequency
attributes.description: Scheduled frequency at which the model generates forecasts: real-time, hourly, daily, weekly, monthly, or on-demand.

attributes.name: forecast_category
attributes.description: Primary category of forecast output produced by this model: load forecasting, generation forecasting, renewable intermittency, demand response, price forecasting, or capacity planning.

attributes.name: forecast_horizon
attributes.description: Temporal scope of the forecast: real-time (minutes), short-term (hours to days), day-ahead, medium-term (weeks to months), seasonal, or long-term (years) for IRP planning.

attributes.name: framework
attributes.description: Software framework or library used to implement the model (e.g., TensorFlow, PyTorch, scikit-learn, R forecast package, proprietary EMS module).

attributes.name: geographic_scope
attributes.description: Geographic coverage of the forecast model (e.g., service territory, balancing authority area, RTO region, specific substation, or renewable site).

attributes.name: hyperparameters
attributes.description: JSON or text representation of model hyperparameters (e.g., learning rate, number of layers, regularization coefficients, ensemble weights). Used for model reproducibility and tuning.

attributes.name: input_feature_set
attributes.description: Comma-separated list or description of input features used by the model (e.g., temperature, humidity, day-of-week, historical load, wind speed, solar irradiance).

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the model record was last updated. Tracks configuration changes, recalibration, or metadata updates.

attributes.name: model_code
attributes.description: Business identifier code for the forecast model used in operational references and reporting. Unique across all registered models.

attributes.name: model_description
attributes.description: Detailed textual description of the model purpose, methodology, use cases, and key assumptions. Provides business context for model selection and interpretation.

attributes.name: model_name
attributes.description: Human-readable name of the forecast model describing its purpose and scope (e.g., 'Summer Peak Load LSTM', 'Wind Generation Ensemble').

attributes.name: model_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the model: development (under construction), testing (validation phase), champion (production model), challenger (competing alternative), retired, or deprecated.

attributes.name: model_type
attributes.description: Classification of the forecasting algorithm or methodology used (statistical regression, neural network, ensemble, persistence, ARIMA, LSTM, random forest). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: statistical_regression|neural_network|ensemble|persistence|arima|lstm|random_forest — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: output_granularity
attributes.description: Temporal resolution of the forecast output: 5-minute, 15-minute, hourly, daily, monthly, or annual intervals.

attributes.name: owner_email
attributes.description: Email address of the model owner for operational communication and governance escalation.

attributes.name: owner_name
attributes.description: Full name of the individual responsible for the model. Primary point of contact for model questions and governance.

attributes.name: owning_team
attributes.description: Name of the business unit or team responsible for developing, maintaining, and governing this forecast model (e.g., Load Forecasting, Renewable Analytics, Grid Operations).

attributes.name: regulatory_compliance_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this model is used for regulatory reporting or compliance purposes (e.g., NERC resource adequacy, FERC market reporting, IRP filings). True if regulatory-critical.

attributes.name: retirement_date
attributes.description: Date when the model was retired from active use. Null for active models.

attributes.name: training_end_date
attributes.description: End date of the historical data period used to train the model. Defines the conclusion of the training window.

attributes.name: training_start_date
attributes.description: Start date of the historical data period used to train the model. Defines the beginning of the training window.

attributes.name: validation_period_end_date
attributes.description: End date of the out-of-sample validation period used to assess model accuracy.

attributes.name: validation_period_start_date
attributes.description: Start date of the out-of-sample validation period used to assess model accuracy. Distinct from training period.

attributes.name: version
attributes.description: Version identifier for the model configuration following semantic versioning (e.g., v1.2.0). Incremented when model structure, hyperparameters, or training data change.

attributes.name: weather_data_source
attributes.description: Name of the weather data provider or service used as input to the model (e.g., NOAA, Weather Underground, proprietary SCADA sensors).

products.name: accuracy
products.description: Transactional entity capturing post-hoc forecast accuracy measurements comparing forecasted values against actuals for a completed forecast run. Stores MAPE (Mean Absolute Percentage Error), MAE (Mean Absolute Error), RMSE, bias, and peak error metrics at system, zone, and interval levels. Tracks accuracy by forecast horizon, season, and weather regime. Used for model performance governance, regulatory reporting, and continuous improvement of forecasting processes.
products.reference: NERC Forecast Accuracy Reporting; IRP Forecast Validation

attributes.name: accuracy_id
attributes.description: Primary key for accuracy

attributes.name: accuracy_forecast_model_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to forecast.model. Business justification: Forecast accuracy records measure the performance of registered forecasting models. The model table is the authoritative registry for model configuration, hyperparameters, and baseline accuracy metric

attributes.name: accuracy_model_id
attributes.description: FK to forecast.model.model_id — Accuracy records measure performance of a specific forecast model. FK enables model performance governance and champion/challenger comparison.

attributes.name: forecast_run_id
attributes.description: Reference to the specific forecast run being evaluated for accuracy. Links to the forecast execution that produced the predictions being measured.

attributes.name: meter_point_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to metering.meter_point. Business justification: Forecast accuracy records track performance at specific service points or aggregations. Forecasters identify which meter points drive forecast errors to refine models. Real business process: granular

attributes.name: zone_id
attributes.description: Reference to the specific transmission or distribution zone for which accuracy is measured. Null for system-level measurements.

attributes.name: absolute_error_mw
attributes.description: The absolute difference between forecasted and actual values, calculated as |forecasted_value_mw - actual_value_mw|. Used in Mean Absolute Error (MAE) calculations.

attributes.name: actual_value_mw
attributes.description: The actual observed value for the interval, measured in megawatts. This is the realized load, generation, or other metric that occurred and is used as ground truth for accuracy calculation.

attributes.name: benchmark_comparison
attributes.description: Comparison of the forecast accuracy against a benchmark model or target threshold. Indicates whether the forecast performed better, worse, or equivalent to the benchmark.

attributes.name: bias_mw
attributes.description: The signed difference between forecasted and actual values, calculated as forecasted_value_mw - actual_value_mw. Positive bias indicates over-forecasting, negative bias indicates under-forecasting.

attributes.name: confidence_interval_lower
attributes.description: The lower bound of the confidence interval for the accuracy metric. Provides statistical confidence range for the measured accuracy.

attributes.name: confidence_interval_upper
attributes.description: The upper bound of the confidence interval for the accuracy metric. Provides statistical confidence range for the measured accuracy.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this accuracy record was first created in the system. Used for data lineage and audit trail purposes.

attributes.name: data_quality_flag
attributes.description: Indicator of the quality of the actual data used for accuracy calculation. Flags whether the actual values were validated, suspect, estimated through VEE (Validation Estimation and Editing), or missing.

attributes.name: day_type
attributes.description: Classification of the day as weekday, weekend, or holiday. Used to segment accuracy analysis by day-of-week patterns that affect load profiles.

attributes.name: for_run
attributes.description: FK to forecast.run.run_id — Accuracy records are computed for a specific forecast run. FK enables traceability from accuracy metrics to the exact run and input data.

attributes.name: forecast_horizon_hours
attributes.description: The time horizon of the forecast being evaluated, measured in hours from the forecast issuance time. Common values include 1-hour ahead, 24-hour ahead, 168-hour ahead (weekly), etc.

attributes.name: forecast_type
attributes.description: The category of forecast being evaluated. Indicates whether this accuracy measurement applies to load forecasting, generation forecasting, renewable intermittency prediction, demand response, price forecasting, or reserve requirements.

attributes.name: forecasted_value_mw
attributes.description: The predicted value from the forecast model, measured in megawatts. This is the value that was forecasted for the interval and is being compared against actuals.

attributes.name: granularity_level
attributes.description: The geographic or organizational level at which the forecast accuracy is measured. System-level represents total utility territory, zone represents transmission zones, substation and feeder represent distribution levels.

attributes.name: improvement_opportunity_flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator flagging forecast intervals or conditions where significant accuracy improvement opportunities exist. Used to prioritize model tuning and enhancement efforts.

attributes.name: interval_end_timestamp
attributes.description: The ending timestamp of the forecast interval being evaluated. Represents the end of the period for which the forecast was made and is now being measured against actuals.

attributes.name: interval_start_timestamp
attributes.description: The beginning timestamp of the forecast interval being evaluated. Represents the start of the period for which the forecast was made and is now being measured against actuals.

attributes.name: mae_mw
attributes.description: The Mean Absolute Error for the forecast interval or aggregation period, measured in megawatts. Represents the average magnitude of forecast errors in absolute terms.

attributes.name: mape
attributes.description: The Mean Absolute Percentage Error for the forecast interval or aggregation period. Represents the average magnitude of forecast errors as a percentage of actual values. Industry standard accuracy metric for forecast performance.

attributes.name: measurement_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when the forecast accuracy measurement was calculated and recorded. Represents when actuals were compared against forecasted values.

attributes.name: model_version
attributes.description: The version identifier of the forecasting model that produced the forecast being evaluated. Enables tracking of model performance across versions and model updates.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for capturing contextual information about the accuracy measurement, including explanations for anomalies, data quality issues, or special conditions affecting the forecast.

attributes.name: peak_error_mw
attributes.description: The maximum absolute error observed during the forecast period. Critical for evaluating forecast performance during peak demand or generation periods.

attributes.name: peak_error_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when the peak error occurred. Identifies the specific interval with the largest forecast deviation.

attributes.name: percentage_error
attributes.description: The error expressed as a percentage of the actual value, calculated as ((forecasted_value_mw - actual_value_mw) / actual_value_mw) * 100. Used in Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) calculations.

attributes.name: regulatory_threshold_met
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether the forecast accuracy met regulatory or contractual accuracy thresholds. Used for compliance reporting to FERC, NERC, or RTO/ISO requirements.

attributes.name: rmse_mw
attributes.business_glossary_term: Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE) in Megawatts (MW)
attributes.description: The Root Mean Squared Error for the forecast interval or aggregation period, measured in megawatts. Penalizes larger errors more heavily than MAE and is sensitive to outliers.

attributes.name: sample_size
attributes.description: The number of individual forecast intervals included in the accuracy calculation. Relevant when accuracy metrics are aggregated across multiple intervals or data points.

attributes.name: season
attributes.description: The meteorological season during which the forecast interval occurred. Used to track accuracy performance by seasonal patterns and weather regimes.

attributes.name: squared_error
attributes.description: The square of the difference between forecasted and actual values, calculated as (forecasted_value_mw - actual_value_mw)^2. Used in Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE) calculations.

attributes.name: time_of_day_category
attributes.description: Classification of the forecast interval by time-of-day load pattern. Used to evaluate accuracy during different daily load shapes and operational conditions.

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this accuracy record was last modified. Used for tracking changes to accuracy measurements as actuals are revised or data quality improves.

attributes.name: weather_regime
attributes.description: The weather condition classification during the forecast interval. Used to evaluate forecast accuracy under different weather scenarios that impact load and renewable generation.

products.name: irp_scenario
products.description: Master record for an Integrated Resource Plan scenario and its year-by-year planning data used in long-term capacity planning and resource adequacy analysis. Captures scenario parameters (load growth, fuel price trajectory, carbon policy, renewable targets, DR credits, retirement schedule) at the header level. Stores annual planning data for each year within the scenario including forecasted peak demand (MW), annual energy requirement (GWh), planned capacity additions/retirements (MW by resource type), reserve margin (%), renewable percentage, and CO2 emissions projection. Multiple scenarios per IRP filing (base, high growth, low carbon). Enables year-by-year resource adequacy gap analysis and investment planning. Submitted to state PUC as part of regulatory IRP process.
products.reference: IRP (Integrated Resource Plan); PUC IRP Filing

attributes.name: irp_scenario_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the IRP scenario. Primary key for the irp_scenario product.

attributes.name: control_area_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to grid.control_area. Business justification: IRP scenarios model future control area configurations, load growth, generation mix, and transmission expansion. Utilities plan generation and transmission investments within control area operational

attributes.name: irp_filing_id
attributes.description: Reference to the parent IRP filing submission to the state Public Utility Commission (PUC). Links this scenario to the regulatory filing docket.

attributes.name: owning_org_unit_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to workforce.org_unit. Business justification: IRP scenarios are developed and owned by specific planning departments/organizational units for territorial and functional accountability. Required for regulatory filings (PUC dockets) to identify res

attributes.name: parent_scenario_irp_scenario_id
attributes.description: Reference to the parent scenario if this is a sensitivity or variant scenario. Links sensitivity scenarios back to their base case for comparison. Null for base case scenarios.

attributes.name: planning_assumption_id
attributes.description: FK to forecast.load_growth_assumption.load_growth_assumption_id — IRP scenarios are built on specific planning assumptions (load growth, fuel price). Must link for scenario reproducibility.

attributes.name: approved_by
attributes.description: Name or identifier of the executive or committee that approved this scenario for inclusion in the IRP filing. Provides accountability and governance trail.

attributes.name: approved_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this scenario was formally approved for inclusion in the IRP filing. Marks transition from draft to official status.

attributes.name: battery_storage_capacity_mw
attributes.description: Total planned battery energy storage system (BESS) capacity additions over the planning horizon for this scenario, measured in megawatts (MW). Critical for renewable integration and grid flexibility.
attributes.references: FERC Order 841, State Energy Storage Mandates

attributes.name: capacity_market_assumption
attributes.description: Assumed market structure for capacity procurement. None means vertically integrated utility; energy_only means no separate capacity payments; capacity_market means RTO/ISO capacity auction; hybrid means mixed approach.
attributes.references: RTO Market Rules, FERC Capacity Market Orders

attributes.name: carbon_policy_assumption
attributes.description: Carbon emissions policy framework assumed in this scenario. None means no carbon constraint; state_target follows state renewable portfolio standard (RPS) or clean energy goals; federal_mandate assumes national policy; carbon_tax models explicit carbon pricing; cap_and_trade models emissions trading system.
attributes.references: State RPS Legislation, EPA Clean Power Plan

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this scenario record was first created in the system. Audit trail for scenario development lifecycle.

attributes.name: demand_response_credit_mw
attributes.description: Assumed demand response (DR) program capacity credit in megawatts (MW) that can be counted toward resource adequacy. Represents load reduction capability from DR programs during peak periods.

attributes.name: discount_rate_pct
attributes.description: Weighted average cost of capital (WACC) or discount rate used for net present value (NPV) calculations in this scenario, expressed as a percentage. Reflects utility cost of capital for investment analysis.
attributes.references: Utility Financial Planning, State PUC Rate Case Orders

attributes.name: distributed_energy_resource_penetration_pct
attributes.description: Assumed penetration of distributed energy resources (rooftop solar, battery storage, microgrids) as a percentage of total capacity by end of planning horizon. Impacts load forecast and grid planning.
attributes.references: State Net Energy Metering (NEM) Policies, DERMS Planning

attributes.name: economic_growth_assumption
attributes.description: Assumed economic growth trajectory for the service territory. Low assumes slow GDP growth; reference uses consensus forecasts; high assumes robust expansion; recession models economic downturn impacts on load.

attributes.name: electrification_assumption
attributes.description: Assumed rate of transportation and building electrification (electric vehicles, heat pumps) over the planning horizon. Low assumes slow adoption; reference uses market forecasts; high assumes policy-driven acceleration.
attributes.references: EIA Annual Energy Outlook, State Climate Action Plans

attributes.name: energy_efficiency_savings_gwh
attributes.description: Cumulative annual energy savings from energy efficiency programs by the end of the planning horizon, measured in gigawatt-hours (GWh). Reduces forecasted energy requirements.

attributes.name: filed_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the IRP containing this scenario was filed with the state Public Utility Commission (PUC). Establishes regulatory record date.

attributes.name: fossil_capacity_retirement_mw
attributes.description: Total planned fossil fuel generation capacity retirements (coal, natural gas, oil) over the planning horizon for this scenario, measured in megawatts (MW). Reflects decarbonization strategy and asset lifecycle management.
attributes.references: Asset Management Lifecycle Plans, EPA Emissions Standards

attributes.name: irp_uses_peak_demand
attributes.description: FK to forecast.peak_demand_forecast.peak_demand_forecast_id — IRP scenarios reference peak demand forecasts for capacity planning. Critical for resource adequacy analysis.

attributes.name: load_growth_assumption_pct
attributes.description: Average annual load growth rate assumption for this scenario expressed as a percentage (e.g., 1.50 for 1.5% annual growth). Key driver for capacity planning and resource adequacy analysis.

attributes.name: modeling_software
attributes.description: Name and version of the capacity expansion or production cost modeling software used to develop this scenario (e.g., PLEXOS, Aurora, PROMOD, Encompass). Important for model transparency and reproducibility.

attributes.name: modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this scenario record was last modified. Tracks iterative refinement during IRP development process.

attributes.name: natural_gas_price_trajectory
attributes.description: Assumed natural gas price path over the planning horizon. Low assumes sustained low prices; reference uses EIA or market consensus; high assumes supply constraints or carbon pricing; volatile models price uncertainty.

attributes.name: peak_demand_growth_assumption_pct
attributes.description: Average annual peak demand (MW) growth rate assumption for this scenario expressed as a percentage. May differ from energy growth due to load shape changes, electrification, or demand response programs.

attributes.name: planning_horizon_end_year
attributes.description: Final year of the planning horizon covered by this scenario (typically 10-20 years from start). Four-digit year (e.g., 2043).

attributes.name: planning_horizon_start_year
attributes.description: First year of the planning horizon covered by this scenario (typically current year or next year). Four-digit year (e.g., 2024).

attributes.name: puc_docket_number
attributes.description: State PUC docket or case number assigned to the IRP filing containing this scenario. Links scenario to regulatory proceeding for tracking and reference.

attributes.name: reliability_metric_lole
attributes.business_glossary_term: Loss of Load Expectation (LOLE) Reliability Metric
attributes.description: Loss of Load Expectation (LOLE) reliability metric for this scenario, typically measured in days per year. Industry standard is 0.1 days/year (one day in ten years). Demonstrates resource adequacy.

attributes.name: renewable_capacity_addition_mw
attributes.description: Total planned renewable generation capacity additions (solar, wind, hydro, biomass) over the planning horizon for this scenario, measured in megawatts (MW). Key metric for tracking renewable energy integration.

attributes.name: renewable_target_pct
attributes.description: Target renewable energy percentage of total generation by the end of the planning horizon. Reflects state RPS requirements or utility commitments (e.g., 50.00 for 50% renewable by 2030).

attributes.name: reserve_margin_target_pct
attributes.description: Planning reserve margin target for resource adequacy expressed as a percentage above forecasted peak demand (e.g., 15.00 for 15% reserve margin). Ensures sufficient capacity to meet reliability standards.
attributes.references: NERC Resource Adequacy Standards, RTO Planning Criteria

attributes.name: retirement_schedule_assumption
attributes.description: Assumed retirement schedule for existing generation assets. Baseline follows planned retirements; accelerated models early coal/gas plant closures; delayed extends asset life; policy_driven reflects regulatory mandates.

attributes.name: scenario_code
attributes.description: Business identifier code for the scenario (e.g., BASE_2024, HIGH_GROWTH_2024, LOW_CARBON_2024). Used in regulatory filings and internal planning documents.

attributes.name: scenario_description
attributes.description: Detailed narrative description of the scenario including key assumptions, strategic rationale, and how it differs from other scenarios in the IRP. Used in regulatory filings and stakeholder presentations.

attributes.name: scenario_name
attributes.description: Descriptive name of the IRP scenario (e.g., Base Case, High Load Growth, Accelerated Decarbonization, Low Gas Price). Human-readable label for reports and presentations.

attributes.name: scenario_notes
attributes.description: Additional notes, caveats, or technical details about the scenario that do not fit in other structured fields. Used for model documentation and knowledge transfer.

attributes.name: scenario_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the scenario. Draft indicates work in progress; under_review means internal stakeholder review; approved means executive sign-off; filed means submitted to PUC; archived means superseded by newer IRP.

attributes.name: scenario_type
attributes.description: Classification of the scenario within the IRP framework. Base represents the most likely case; sensitivity tests single variable changes; alternative explores different strategic paths; stress_test examines extreme conditions; bookend defines planning boundaries.

attributes.name: sensitivity_variable
attributes.description: For sensitivity scenarios, identifies the specific variable being tested (e.g., natural gas price, load growth, carbon price, technology cost). Null for base case scenarios.

attributes.name: stakeholder_feedback_summary
attributes.description: Summary of stakeholder comments and feedback received on this scenario during public comment periods or technical conferences. Documents stakeholder engagement process required by many state PUCs.

attributes.name: technology_cost_assumption
attributes.description: Assumed capital cost trajectory for new generation technologies (solar, wind, battery storage, gas turbines). Low assumes rapid cost declines; reference uses industry consensus; high assumes slower learning curves.
attributes.references: NREL Annual Technology Baseline, Lazard LCOE

attributes.name: total_co2_emissions_million_tons
attributes.business_glossary_term: Total Carbon Dioxide (CO2) Emissions Million Tons
attributes.description: Cumulative CO2 emissions over the planning horizon for this scenario, measured in million metric tons. Key environmental metric for comparing scenarios and demonstrating compliance with carbon reduction goals.
attributes.references: EPA Greenhouse Gas Reporting, State Climate Action Plans

attributes.name: total_resource_cost_npv_million
attributes.business_glossary_term: Total Resource Cost Net Present Value (NPV) Million Dollars
attributes.description: Net present value of total resource costs (capital, fixed O&M, variable O&M, fuel) over the planning horizon for this scenario, in millions of dollars. Key metric for comparing scenario economics.

attributes.name: transmission_expansion_assumption
attributes.description: Assumed level of transmission system expansion over the planning horizon. None means no new transmission; limited means targeted upgrades; moderate means regional expansion; aggressive means major interstate projects.
attributes.references: RTO Transmission Planning Process, FERC Order 1000

attributes.name: weather_normalization_method
attributes.description: Method used to normalize weather impacts in load forecasting. Historical_average uses 10-30 year average; climate_adjusted incorporates climate change projections; extreme_weather models increased frequency of heat waves and cold snaps.
attributes.references: NOAA Climate Data, Utility Load Forecasting Best Practices

products.name: irp_scenario_year
products.description: Transactional entity capturing annual planning data for each year within an IRP scenario. Stores year-specific forecasted peak demand (MW), annual energy requirement (GWh), planned capacity additions (MW by resource type), planned retirements (MW), reserve margin (%), renewable percentage, and CO2 emissions projection. Enables year-by-year resource adequacy gap analysis and investment planning across the IRP planning horizon.
products.reference: IRP Annual Planning Data; NERC Resource Adequacy

attributes.name: irp_scenario_year_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Integrated Resource Plan (IRP) Scenario Year ID
attributes.description: Unique identifier for each annual planning data record within an IRP scenario. Primary key for the irp_scenario_year entity.

attributes.name: meter_point_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to metering.meter_point. Business justification: IRP scenario projections are grounded in historical consumption patterns at service points. Planners trace meter points to validate load growth assumptions and customer class trends. Real business pro

attributes.name: primary_irp_scenario_id
attributes.description: Reference to the parent IRP scenario that this annual planning record belongs to. Links to the irp_scenario master entity.

attributes.name: approval_status
attributes.description: Current approval status of this planning year data within the IRP scenario workflow. Tracks progression through planning review and approval process.

attributes.name: approved_by
attributes.description: Username or identifier of the planning authority who approved this planning year data. Null if not yet approved.

attributes.name: approved_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this planning year data was approved. Null if not yet approved. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.

attributes.name: average_lcoe_usd_per_mwh
attributes.business_glossary_term: Average Levelized Cost of Energy (LCOE) in USD per MWh
attributes.description: Weighted average levelized cost of energy in US dollars per megawatt-hour across the generation portfolio for this planning year. Represents all-in cost of generation.
attributes.references: DOE Energy Information Administration (EIA) LCOE Methodology

attributes.name: capacity_factor_percent
attributes.description: Weighted average capacity factor as a percentage across the generation portfolio for this planning year. Represents actual generation relative to maximum potential generation.

attributes.name: co2_emissions_projection_tons
attributes.description: Projected annual carbon dioxide emissions in metric tons for this planning year. Critical for environmental compliance, carbon pricing analysis, and sustainability reporting.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this planning year record was first created in the system. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.

attributes.name: demand_response_capacity_mw
attributes.description: Total demand response capacity in megawatts (MW) planned for this year. Represents load reduction capability from DR programs and customer participation.

attributes.name: der_capacity_mw
attributes.description: Total distributed energy resource capacity in megawatts (MW) planned for this year. Includes behind-the-meter solar, microgrids, and customer-sited generation.

attributes.name: distribution_investment_usd
attributes.description: Planned distribution infrastructure investment in US dollars for this planning year. Includes distribution system upgrades, smart grid, and DER integration investments.

attributes.name: emissions_intensity_kg_per_mwh
attributes.description: Projected carbon emissions intensity in kilograms of CO2 per megawatt-hour of generation. Measures carbon efficiency of the generation portfolio.

attributes.name: energy_storage_capacity_mw
attributes.description: Total energy storage capacity in megawatts (MW) planned for this year. Includes battery storage, pumped hydro, and other storage technologies.

attributes.name: forecasted_annual_energy_gwh
attributes.description: Projected total annual energy requirement in gigawatt-hours (GWh) for this planning year. Represents total electricity consumption across all customer classes.
attributes.references: FERC Form 714 - Annual Electric Balancing Authority Area and Planning Area Report

attributes.name: forecasted_peak_demand_mw
attributes.description: Projected system peak demand in megawatts (MW) for this planning year. Critical metric for resource adequacy planning and capacity expansion decisions.

attributes.name: fossil_capacity_mw
attributes.description: Total fossil fuel generation capacity in megawatts (MW) planned for this year. Includes coal, natural gas, and oil-fired generation.

attributes.name: fuel_cost_projection_usd
attributes.description: Projected total fuel costs in US dollars for fossil fuel and nuclear generation in this planning year. Based on forward fuel price curves and generation dispatch forecasts.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this planning year record was last updated. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.

attributes.name: loss_of_load_probability
attributes.description: Calculated probability of loss of load events for this planning year. Reliability metric indicating likelihood of supply shortfall. Target typically <0.1 (one day in ten years).

attributes.name: modified_by
attributes.description: Username or identifier of the user who last modified this planning year record. Supports audit trail and change tracking.

attributes.name: net_capacity_change_mw
attributes.description: Net change in generation capacity (additions minus retirements) in megawatts (MW) for this planning year. Positive values indicate capacity growth, negative indicate reduction.

attributes.name: nuclear_capacity_mw
attributes.description: Total nuclear generation capacity in megawatts (MW) planned for this year. Represents baseload nuclear power generation assets.

attributes.name: planned_capacity_additions_mw
attributes.description: Total planned generation capacity additions in megawatts (MW) for this planning year across all resource types. Includes new builds, expansions, and acquisitions.
attributes.references: FERC Form 1 - Annual Report of Major Electric Utilities

attributes.name: planned_retirements_mw
attributes.description: Total planned generation capacity retirements in megawatts (MW) for this planning year. Includes decommissioning, mothballing, and asset sales.
attributes.references: FERC Form 1 - Annual Report of Major Electric Utilities

attributes.name: planning_reserve_margin_percent
attributes.description: Target planning reserve margin percentage for this year as defined by regional transmission organization or internal planning criteria. Differs from actual reserve margin.

attributes.name: planning_year
attributes.description: The calendar year for which this planning data applies within the IRP scenario horizon. Typically ranges from current year to 20-30 years forward.

attributes.name: renewable_capacity_mw
attributes.description: Total renewable generation capacity in megawatts (MW) planned for this year. Includes solar, wind, hydro, biomass, and other renewable sources.

attributes.name: renewable_percentage
attributes.description: Percentage of total generation capacity from renewable sources for this planning year. Used to track compliance with state RPS mandates and corporate sustainability goals.

attributes.name: reserve_margin_percent
attributes.description: Planned reserve margin as a percentage of peak demand for this planning year. Represents excess capacity above peak demand to ensure reliability. Typically 15-20% per NERC standards.

attributes.name: scenario_notes
attributes.description: Free-text notes documenting key assumptions, constraints, or special considerations for this planning year within the scenario. Captures planner commentary and decision rationale.

attributes.name: total_capital_expenditure_usd
attributes.description: Total planned capital expenditure in US dollars for generation capacity additions, upgrades, and infrastructure investments in this planning year.

attributes.name: total_operational_expenditure_usd
attributes.description: Total planned operational expenditure in US dollars for generation operations, maintenance, and fuel costs in this planning year.

attributes.name: transmission_investment_usd
attributes.description: Planned transmission infrastructure investment in US dollars for this planning year. Includes new lines, substations, and grid upgrades to support generation additions.

attributes.name: year_sequence
attributes.description: Sequential ordering of this year within the IRP scenario planning horizon (1 for first year, 2 for second year, etc.). Enables chronological analysis.

products.name: capacity_requirement
products.description: Master entity defining resource adequacy capacity requirements and reliability targets for a planning period. Captures installed capacity reserve margin targets, planning reserve margin (PRM), net qualifying capacity (NQC) by resource type, and RTO/ISO-mandated capacity obligations (e.g., PJM RPM, MISO PRA). Stores NERC reliability standard thresholds including loss-of-load probability (LOLP) targets and expected unserved energy (EUE) limits. Drives capacity procurement triggers, deficiency penalties, and IRP resource selection. Updated annually per RTO/ISO capacity auction results.
products.reference: NERC Resource Adequacy; RTO Capacity Market Obligation

attributes.name: capacity_requirement_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the capacity requirement record. Primary key for the capacity requirement entity.

attributes.name: capacity_irp_scenario_id
attributes.description: Reference to the IRP scenario or planning case that generated this capacity requirement. Links capacity planning to long-term resource strategy.
attributes.references: IRP Filing Requirements, State Energy Planning Standards

attributes.name: control_area_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to grid.control_area. Business justification: Capacity requirements are calculated per control area for resource adequacy, planning reserve margin compliance, and NERC reliability standards. Control area operators use capacity requirements to ens

attributes.name: planning_period_id
attributes.description: Reference to the planning period for which this capacity requirement applies (e.g., annual IRP cycle, multi-year planning horizon).

attributes.name: primary_irp_scenario_id
attributes.description: FK to forecast.irp_scenario.irp_scenario_id — Capacity requirements are derived from IRP scenarios. FK enables traceability from capacity obligations back to planning assumptions.

attributes.name: rto_iso_zone_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Regional Transmission Organization (RTO) / Independent System Operator (ISO) Zone ID
attributes.description: Reference to the RTO or ISO zone for which this capacity requirement is defined (e.g., PJM, MISO, CAISO, ERCOT, NYISO, ISO-NE).

attributes.name: approval_date
attributes.description: Date when this capacity requirement was formally approved by the regulatory authority (PUC, FERC) or RTO/ISO governing body.
attributes.references: FERC Filing Requirements, State PUC Orders

attributes.name: approved_by
attributes.description: Name of the regulatory authority, commission, or governing body that approved this capacity requirement (e.g., 'FERC', 'California PUC', 'PJM Board').

attributes.name: capacity_auction_clearing_price_per_mw_day
attributes.description: Market clearing price from the most recent capacity auction in dollars per megawatt-day ($/MW-day). Used for capacity procurement cost forecasting and budget planning.
attributes.references: RTO/ISO Capacity Market Results (PJM RPM, MISO PRA)

attributes.name: capacity_deficiency_mw
attributes.description: Calculated capacity deficiency in megawatts (MW), representing the shortfall between the capacity requirement and available capacity. Positive values indicate a need for additional procurement.

attributes.name: capacity_export_limit_mw
attributes.description: Maximum capacity in megawatts (MW) that can be exported to external zones or regions, representing surplus capacity available for sale in external markets.
attributes.references: RTO/ISO Interconnection Studies, NERC MOD Standards

attributes.name: capacity_import_limit_mw
attributes.description: Maximum capacity in megawatts (MW) that can be imported from external zones or regions to meet the local capacity requirement, based on transmission interface limits.
attributes.references: RTO/ISO Interconnection Studies, NERC MOD Standards

attributes.name: capacity_surplus_mw
attributes.description: Calculated capacity surplus in megawatts (MW), representing the excess capacity above the requirement. Positive values indicate over-procurement or reserve margin cushion.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this capacity requirement record was first created in the system.

attributes.name: deficiency_penalty_rate_per_mw_day
attributes.description: Penalty rate assessed for capacity deficiency in dollars per megawatt-day ($/MW-day). Applied when a load-serving entity fails to meet its capacity obligation.

attributes.name: demand_response_capacity_requirement_mw
attributes.description: Capacity requirement allocated to demand response programs in megawatts (MW), representing load reduction capability that can be dispatched during peak periods.
attributes.references: FERC Order 745, RTO/ISO Demand Response Rules

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: Date when this capacity requirement becomes effective and binding for planning and procurement activities.

attributes.name: energy_storage_capacity_requirement_mw
attributes.description: Capacity requirement allocated to energy storage resources (battery, pumped hydro, compressed air) in megawatts (MW). Supports grid flexibility and renewable integration.
attributes.references: FERC Order 841, State Energy Storage Mandates

attributes.name: expected_unserved_energy_mwh
attributes.description: Expected unserved energy limit in megawatt-hours (MWh), representing the maximum acceptable amount of load that may not be served due to capacity shortfalls. NERC reliability metric.

attributes.name: expiration_date
attributes.description: Date when this capacity requirement expires or is superseded by a subsequent requirement. Null for open-ended requirements.

attributes.name: filing_reference_number
attributes.description: Regulatory filing reference number or docket number associated with the approval of this capacity requirement (e.g., FERC docket number, PUC case number).
attributes.references: FERC eFiling System, State PUC Filing Standards

attributes.name: flexible_capacity_requirement_mw
attributes.description: Capacity requirement in megawatts (MW) for flexible ramping resources capable of responding to rapid load changes and renewable intermittency. Supports grid flexibility needs.
attributes.references: CAISO Flexible Capacity Framework, FERC Order 764

attributes.name: forecast_confidence_level_percent
attributes.description: Statistical confidence level for the peak demand forecast expressed as a percentage (e.g., 90.0% confidence interval). Indicates the reliability of the forecast used to set the capacity requirement.

attributes.name: installed_capacity_requirement_mw
attributes.description: Total installed capacity requirement in megawatts (MW) calculated as peak demand plus planning reserve margin. This is the target capacity that must be procured or available.
attributes.references: NERC BAL-502, RTO/ISO Capacity Market Rules

attributes.name: last_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this capacity requirement record was last modified or updated.

attributes.name: local_capacity_requirement_mw
attributes.description: Capacity requirement in megawatts (MW) that must be met by resources located within a specific local reliability area or load pocket, due to transmission constraints.
attributes.references: CAISO Local Capacity Technical Study, RTO/ISO Local Reliability Rules

attributes.name: loss_of_load_probability_target
attributes.description: Target loss of load probability expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.1 represents one day in ten years). NERC reliability standard threshold for acceptable risk of load shedding.

attributes.name: net_qualifying_capacity_mw
attributes.description: Net qualifying capacity in megawatts (MW) representing the effective capacity contribution of resources after applying derating factors for availability, intermittency, and transmission constraints.
attributes.references: CAISO Tariff, CPUC Resource Adequacy Rules

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text notes providing additional context, assumptions, or special considerations for this capacity requirement (e.g., policy drivers, market conditions, planning assumptions).

attributes.name: peak_demand_forecast_mw
attributes.description: Forecasted peak demand in megawatts (MW) for the planning period, representing the maximum expected load that must be served.

attributes.name: planning_reserve_margin_percent
attributes.description: Planning reserve margin expressed as a percentage above peak demand, representing the target capacity cushion to ensure reliability (e.g., 15.0% means capacity must be 115% of peak demand).

attributes.name: renewable_capacity_requirement_mw
attributes.description: Capacity requirement allocated to renewable energy resources (wind, solar, hydro, biomass) in megawatts (MW). Driven by Renewable Portfolio Standard (RPS) mandates and clean energy targets.
attributes.references: State RPS Regulations, IRP Clean Energy Standards

attributes.name: requirement_name
attributes.description: Business name or label for this capacity requirement (e.g., '2025 Summer Peak Capacity Requirement', 'PJM RPM 2024/2025').

attributes.name: requirement_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the capacity requirement: draft (under development), proposed (submitted for approval), approved (authorized by regulator), active (in effect), superseded (replaced by newer requirement), or archived (historical record).

attributes.name: requirement_type
attributes.description: Classification of the capacity requirement type: installed capacity (ICAP), planning reserve margin (PRM), net qualifying capacity (NQC), resource adequacy (RA), or reliability must-run (RMR).

attributes.name: thermal_capacity_requirement_mw
attributes.description: Capacity requirement allocated to thermal generation resources (coal, natural gas, nuclear) in megawatts (MW). Used for resource mix planning and diversification analysis.

attributes.name: transmission_constraint_adjustment_mw
attributes.description: Capacity adjustment in megawatts (MW) to account for transmission system constraints that limit the deliverability of generation capacity to load centers.

attributes.name: unforced_capacity_requirement_mw
attributes.description: Unforced capacity requirement in megawatts (MW), representing capacity adjusted for expected forced outage rates. Used in PJM and other markets to account for resource reliability.
attributes.references: PJM RPM Rules, NERC Generating Availability Data System (GADS)

attributes.name: weather_normalization_applied_flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether weather normalization adjustments were applied to the peak demand forecast (True) or not (False). Weather normalization removes extreme weather variability.

products.name: energy_price

Stores forecasted LMP by pricing node at the header level with fuel price trajectories, carbon price assumptions, and capacity price forecasts. Includes interval-level LMP ($/MWh) by PNode with energy, congestion, and loss components, forward natural gas price ($/MMBtu), and capacity price ($/MW-day) at configurable resolution. Supports LCOE calculations, economic dispatch optimization, hedging strategy development, bilateral contract valuation, and market participation decisions.
products.reference: LMP Forward Curve; FERC Market Price Forecast; LCOE Analysis

attributes.name: employee_id
attributes.description: Reference to the user or analyst who approved this forecast for publication and operational use. Supports accountability and governance.

attributes.name: energy_forecast_zone_id

attributes.name: energy_zone_id

attributes.name: pricing_node_id

attributes.references: FERC Order 888 - Open Access Transmission Tariff (OATT)

attributes.name: superseded_by_forecast_energy_price_id
attributes.description: Reference to the newer forecast that supersedes this one. Nullable if this is the current active forecast. Supports forecast version lineage.

attributes.name: ancillary_services_price_usd_per_mwh
attributes.description: Forecasted price for ancillary services (regulation, spinning reserves, non-spinning reserves) in US dollars per megawatt-hour. Supports grid stability and frequency control cost modeling.

attributes.name: approved_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this forecast was approved by an authorized user. Distinct lifecycle event from creation and modification.

attributes.name: capacity_price_usd_per_mw_day
attributes.description: Forecasted capacity price in US dollars per megawatt-day. Represents the cost of ensuring resource adequacy and grid reliability through capacity markets.

attributes.name: carbon_price_usd_per_ton
attributes.description: Forecasted carbon price or carbon tax in US dollars per ton of CO2 equivalent. Used for environmental compliance cost modeling and Renewable Portfolio Standard (RPS) analysis.
attributes.references: EPA Clean Air Act - Emissions Trading

attributes.name: coal_price_usd_per_ton
attributes.description: Forecasted coal price in US dollars per ton. Used for modeling generation costs for coal-fired power plants.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this forecast record was first created in the system. Audit trail for data lineage and compliance.

attributes.name: currency_code
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for all monetary values in this forecast (e.g., USD, CAD, EUR). Supports multi-currency operations for international utilities.

attributes.name: forecast_confidence_level_percent
attributes.description: Statistical confidence level of the forecast expressed as a percentage (e.g., 80%, 90%, 95%). Indicates the probability that actual prices will fall within the forecasted range.

attributes.name: forecast_effective_end_date
attributes.description: The last date for which this forecast is applicable. Defines the end of the forecast validity period. Nullable for open-ended forecasts.

attributes.name: forecast_effective_start_date
attributes.description: The first date for which this forecast is applicable. Defines the beginning of the forecast validity period.

attributes.name: forecast_identifier
attributes.description: Business-readable identifier or code for this forecast run, used for tracking and referencing in reports and analysis.

attributes.name: forecast_interval_end_timestamp
attributes.description: The precise end timestamp of the interval for which this price forecast applies. Defines the interval boundary for time-series price data.

attributes.name: forecast_interval_start_timestamp
attributes.description: The precise start timestamp of the interval for which this price forecast applies. Used for interval-level LMP forecasting at hourly or sub-hourly resolution.

attributes.name: forecast_methodology
attributes.description: The methodology used to generate this forecast: fundamental (supply-demand modeling), statistical (time-series analysis), machine learning (AI/ML models), hybrid (combination), or expert judgment (analyst-driven).

attributes.name: forecast_notes
attributes.description: Free-text notes or commentary from analysts regarding assumptions, limitations, or special considerations for this forecast. Supports transparency and decision-making context.

attributes.name: forecast_source_system
attributes.description: Name or identifier of the source system that generated this forecast (e.g., OpenLink Endur, proprietary forecasting tool, third-party vendor). Supports data lineage and audit.

attributes.name: forecast_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the forecast: draft (under development), approved (validated by analysts), published (released for operational use), superseded (replaced by newer forecast), or archived (historical record).

attributes.name: forecast_type
attributes.description: Classification of the forecast horizon: short-term (hours to days), mid-term (weeks to months), long-term (years), day-ahead market (DAM), real-time market (RTM), or seasonal planning.
attributes.references: NAESB WEQ Standards - Wholesale Electric Quadrant

attributes.name: hedging_strategy_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this forecast is used for developing hedging strategies and risk management in energy trading. True if used for hedging, False otherwise.

attributes.name: interval_duration_minutes
attributes.description: The duration of the forecast interval in minutes (e.g., 5, 15, 60). Supports configurable resolution for different market and planning needs.

attributes.name: iso_rto_code
attributes.business_glossary_term: Independent System Operator (ISO) / Regional Transmission Organization (RTO) Code
attributes.description: Code identifying the ISO or RTO market region for this forecast (e.g., CAISO, PJM, ERCOT, MISO, NYISO, ISO-NE, SPP). Critical for market-specific price modeling.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this forecast record was last updated or modified. Supports change tracking and audit requirements.

attributes.name: lcoe_calculation_flag
attributes.business_glossary_term: Levelized Cost of Energy (LCOE) Calculation Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this forecast is used for LCOE calculations and generation asset economic analysis. True if used for LCOE, False otherwise.

attributes.name: lmp_congestion_component_usd_per_mwh
attributes.business_glossary_term: Locational Marginal Price (LMP) Congestion Component (USD per MWh)
attributes.description: Forecasted congestion component of the LMP in US dollars per megawatt-hour. Reflects transmission constraints and grid congestion costs at this pricing node.

attributes.name: lmp_energy_component_usd_per_mwh
attributes.business_glossary_term: Locational Marginal Price (LMP) Energy Component (USD per MWh)
attributes.description: Forecasted energy component of the Locational Marginal Price in US dollars per megawatt-hour. Represents the marginal cost of serving the next increment of load at this location.

attributes.name: lmp_loss_component_usd_per_mwh
attributes.business_glossary_term: Locational Marginal Price (LMP) Loss Component (USD per MWh)
attributes.description: Forecasted loss component of the LMP in US dollars per megawatt-hour. Accounts for electrical losses in transmission from generation to load.

attributes.name: lmp_total_usd_per_mwh
